author: openvibers
body:
The owner asked for the deep dive image feature to "screenshot search queries on Google, Bing, etc to analyze a whole page of images at once … filter for recent results". It is live as of AI #611 and #613. It ran on production 11-16: one sheet of 38 images from the past month, read by a vision model.

The start page did not say so. This change:
- adds step 4, **Reads a whole page of images at once**: Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo image results; a recency of a day, week, month or year; one sheet per engine read in one pass; every picture linked.
- renumbers the steps after it.
- says in the lede that the deep dive reads whole pages of image search results and that every option is yours to set.
- raises `.ds-kicker` from 11.84 px to 12 px (the audit's minimum text size).

`test/deepdive-page.test.js` passes.

body:
A sprite with a rotation turns around its registration point. The pivot was given in movie coordinates while the sprite's corners are in drawRect space (get_concrete_sprite_render_rect scales them), so at any stage scale above 1 a spinning sprite orbited the map instead of turning under its hireling.

In ROTL's battle the spinning marker (sprite 463, ANGELC~1, rotation +120 a tick) showed as a green X wandering around the field at Game size 110% and up. The pivot now gets the same scale and drawRect offset; at scale 1 nothing changes.

Checked on a local rig at 150%: the blob is gone across several turns and attacks; before the change it was on screen in every shot.

body:
# What and why

Converts all six LazyCurrencySpender windows, wizard steps, tables, and the currency overlay to the approved shell: rounded cards, pink accents, live counts, responsive tables, and actionable empty states. Every standard window and the overlay has a working custom X, with no redundant outer scrollbar where a dedicated body handles overflow. Currency calculations, spending behavior, configuration, NPC/menu recolors, and overlay positioning are unchanged.

# Files touched

- New `src/LazyCurrencySpender/Windows/CurrencyChrome.cs` — plugin-local drawn shell and controls.
- Windows: `MainTabWindow.cs`, `ConfigTabWindow.cs`, `ConfigWizardWindow.cs`, `SpendingWindow.cs`, `DebugTabWindow.cs`, and `CurrencyOverlay.cs`.
- Tab/content surfaces: `MainTab.cs`, `ConfigTab.cs`, `ConfigCurrenciesTab.cs`, `ItemsTab.cs`, `InstructionsTab.cs`, `AboutTab.cs`, `ChangelogTab.cs`, `DebugTab.cs`, and `DebugMainTab.cs`.

No configuration, currency data, shop helpers, hooks, services, shared sources, release files, or tooling changed.

# Build and tests

- `dotnet build src/LazyCurrencySpender/LazyCurrencySpender.csproj -c Release -p:DalamudLibPath=<reference-assemblies>` — passed with 0 errors and 37 warnings in unchanged non-window files.
- `dotnet run --project tests/LazyCurrencySpender.WindowNameHarness -c Release` — 20 pass, 0 fail; final `OK`.
- `dotnet run --project tests/LazyCurrencySpender.MissingLocationLogHarness -c Release` — 17 pass, 0 fail; final `OK`.
- Final close/scrollbar changes rebuilt and reran both harnesses successfully.
- `git diff --check` and public-repository hygiene scan passed. No in-game verification is claimed yet.

# Proposed changelog bullets

- LazyCurrencySpender now uses responsive card-based windows with custom close controls, clear currency state, and scrollable wizard/table content.

# In-game check

Click X on each standard window and the currency overlay, including minimized shells and every wizard step; confirm close/reopen behavior and overlay auto-open remain correct. Resize main, settings, wizard, spending, and debug windows; confirm fitting content has no redundant outer scrollbar while long content scrolls internally and footer actions remain reachable. Verify currency sorting, balances, missing-collectable counts, settings persistence, purchases/conversions, item menus, and Flag/TP actions. Confirm overlay anchoring and NPC/shop-item highlight recolors remain unchanged.

# Risk

The revised windows retain existing spending and currency actions. A UI binding defect could misreport balances, prices, or state or trigger an existing action incorrectly, while a layout defect could hide a control; both existing harnesses pass, with live purchase, wizard, overlay, and persistence checks still required. Reverting the UI changes restores the previous windows without changing currency or spending behavior.

author: karlharnois
body:
## Summary

`DiagnosticRenderer::render` ends every diagnostic whose code is in the code table, warnings included, with `= note: run `knave doc <code>` for an explanation`. A rustc code, a note without a code and a code outside the table get no note. The second commit holds only the snapshots that `INSTA_UPDATE=always` wrote, and this check prints nothing on it:

```sh
git show <commit-2> | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^+++\|^---' \
  | grep -v '^+ *= note: run `knave doc L[0-9]\{4\}` for an explanation$' \
  | grep -v '^+ *|$' | grep -v '^[+-]expression: ' \
  | grep -v '^[+-]   = note: `named` is implemented for: \?$'
```

- The `|` lines come from annotate_snippets, which puts a gutter line before a note that directly follows a snippet.
- The `expression:` header lines are insta metadata, which insta refreshes whenever it rewrites a snapshot.
- The `L0404` lines gain a trailing space because that note ends with a space when its list is empty, and insta trims trailing whitespace only on a snapshot's last line.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p knave-expand --lib diagnostic`, with unit tests for a help, a suggestion group, a warning, a macro call, a rustc code, a code outside the table and a note without a code
- [x] Every `--test stages <stage>_fixtures` target, the `saved_prelude_*` ones included
- [x] `cargo test --test diagnostic_codes --test diagnostic_snapshots`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p knave-expand -p knave --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask file-sizes`, `cargo xtask design-rules`
- [x] The check above prints nothing, and a sample of changed snapshots across the stages was read

author: ilpistolero
body:
## Cosa cambia

**Prima.** Le stelle potevano giocare in attacco e in difesa senza nessun costo, e il computer schierava sempre i suoi 7 migliori. Una rosa da 12 rendeva quanto una da 20: stessi risultati, stessa forza, stessa condizione.

**Ora:**
- **Chi sta in entrambe le linee non riposa mai.** Rende 7 punti in meno (`DBL_PEN`), sia nella partita giocata (`applyForm(dbl)` all'avvio) sia in quella simulata (`simCareerMatch`).
- **Fatica proporzionale alle mete giocate.** Dopo la partita la condizione scende secondo la quota di mete giocate (`fatShare`): chi sta in una sola linea perde quanto prima, chi sta in entrambe il doppio.
- **La condizione bassa pesa anche nella partita giocata** (`COND_PEN`, come nelle simulate).
- **Forza in partita della tua squadra:** due linee + `LINE_REF`, così resta sulla scala dei 7 migliori. Le altre squadre restano ai loro 7 migliori. `matchPow` la usano `simPower`, il bilancio previsionale e il freno della crescita.
- **Partita giocata:** anche l'avversario alterna la sua linea d'attacco e quella di difesa (`10-sim/21-due-linee.js`).
- **Linee consigliate:**
  - tengono conto della condizione;
  - mettono in difesa chi è già in attacco solo se vale `2·DBL_PEN+2` in più;
  - completano le linee e coprono gli infortunati preferendo chi non è già nell'altra linea.
- **Cassa di partenza:** quattro partite di stipendi. Con più giocatori che giocano crescono anche gli stipendi, e i Boston restavano in rosso per 4 giornate.
- **Testi:** guida, tutorial (solo la regola), scheda del giocatore e avviso nella Rosa. Una riga nuova in Diagnostica.

## Taratura

L'utente ha scelto -7 dopo le misure. Gli altri valori misurati erano -4 e -10.

Partendo dal fondo della C (abilità +7, 9 carriere):

| Valore | Scudetto entro la 9ª stagione | Vittorie | Rosa da 12 contro rosa da 20 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 7 su 9 | 77% | nessuna differenza |
| -4 | 9 su 9 | 76% | nessuna differenza |
| **-7 (scelto)** | **5 su 9** | **72%** | **i 360 Milano con 12 vincono 2-6 partite in meno su 30** |
| -10 | 2 su 9 | 64% | circa 1,3 punti di forza in meno |

**Economia con la profondità** (2 stagioni senza spendere):

| Club | Cassa nelle due stagioni |
|---|---|
| Boston, rosa com'è | 204 → 107 → 368 |
| Boston, rosa ridotta a 16 | +281 dalle vendite, poi +179 e +159 |
| Denver | 172 → 123 → 145 |
| Club di vertice europei | +230..+400 a stagione |
| Italia | in attivo |

Nessuno va in rosso.

## Verifiche

- `npm test` verde.
- Diagnostica: 49 righe OK, compresa la nuova «Profondità della rosa».
- Test leghe europee: OK.

## Merge con #75

Nella lezione «Le linee ATT e DIF» ho unito il testo nuovo di #75 con la regola di questo ramo.

body:
## 문제
- 사이드바 AWS 계정에 같은 이름(`smr-aws`)이 두 줄로 보였다. 실제로는 서로 다른 계정이다.
- 원인: `refresh()`가 계정→프로필 매핑을 추가만 하고, 같은 프로필의 예전 계정 매핑을 지우지 않았다. 프로필 자격 증명이 다른 계정으로 바뀌면 두 계정 모두 같은 프로필 이름으로 표시됐다.
- 계정 이름을 바꿀 방법이 없었다.

body:
Any webamp.org link with `?scPlaylist=` fails to start: the desktop icons render but Webamp never appears. That includes the `/poolside` redirect in `netlify.toml`. In Sentry this is WEBAMP-1T9 (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`), and every recent event has `scPlaylist=1040356177`, the Poolside playlist.

SoundCloud's API now answers our client id with `401`. `getPlaylist` returned the error body as if it were a playlist, then `tracksFromPlaylist` threw on `playlist.tracks.map` before Webamp was constructed.

This makes `getPlaylist` throw on a non-OK response or one without a `tracks` array, and `main()` catches that, logs it, and carries on with the default tracks. The skin and background from the URL still apply. It also removes a `@ts-ignore` that is no longer needed.

This only keeps the page working. The SoundCloud feature itself is still dead: getting the Poolside tracks back needs a different source, or the `scPlaylist` param removed from the `/poolside` redirect.

### Steps to reproduce (on webamp.org today)

1. Open https://webamp.org/poolside (it redirects to `/?bg=%2362639f&scPlaylist=1040356177&skinUrl=…`).
2. Expected: Webamp opens with the Poolside skin. Actual: only the desktop icons and background colour render, and the console shows `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`.
3. Optionally, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "https://api.soundcloud.com/playlists/1040356177?client_id=T9EbIJ75SnsJK3iX8lOZaDlGIYgQB32G"` prints `401`.

### Test plan

- [x] Opened the same URL against the dev server: Webamp starts with the Poolside skin, the `#62639f` background and the default playlist. The console logs `Error: SoundCloud playlist request failed: 401` and nothing else from startup.
- [ ] After deploy, open https://webamp.org/poolside and check that Webamp appears.
- [x] `eslint` and `prettier --check` pass. The demo's `tsc` errors are unchanged: the two existing PNG-import errors in `DemoDesktop.tsx`.

```text
every route -> response security headers -> existing handler
  OAuth consent -> retains its stricter CSP override
```

routes lacked the browser security policy promised by the architecture.
Set CSP, frame denial, no-referrer and nosniff globally. Scripts remain
same-origin; inline styles and blob/data images support existing charts and
upload previews. Existing cookie, CSRF and private-cache rules are preserved.

The operations edit also repairs three legacy non-UTF-8 section-sign bytes.

  month filtering, spending and chart render under CSP. Only synthetic data.

No body/schema or database changes. These response headers apply across
the SPA, REST, health, OAuth and MCP route families; OAuth consent keeps
its stricter `default-src 'none'` policy.

Continue runtime consistency cleanup, then release documentation and final
resource/image evidence. The release tag still requires owner confirmation.

**After:** the same regression passes; existing OAuth consent tests and the

The policy blocks unbundled scripts and framing. Existing same-origin assets,
chart styles, local image previews and OAuth consent are covered by tests and

author: jsboige
body:
Grain: DEEP/notebook-python — lane myia-ai-01:CoursIA-2 — prev: DEEP/notebook-python #26817

## Objet

`See #26315` (sous-issue D4 de l'EPIC #24282 — qualification des substrats dégénérés).

`ICT-35-HumorCausalProbe-Pilot` conclut `INCONCLUSIVE borne` et énonce sa limite : « 36
unités group-level (6 H uniques + 30 N distincts) — sous-corpus appauvri ». Mais une borne
dont on ne mesure pas l'étendue reste une phrase. Le critère **D2** de #24282 demande
combien de tirages faut-il pour identifier la meilleure action ; appliqué ici, il ne
demande pas de changer le verdict, il demande de dire **ce que ce verdict permet et ne
permet pas d'exclure**.

Cette PR ajoute au carnet une **calibration de puissance** de la sonde : à 36 unités,
quelle taille d'effet cette sonde peut-elle voir, et combien d'unités aurait-il fallu
pour en voir une de référence ?

## Ce qui est ajouté

Trois cellules, insérées entre la « Lecture 6 » (le verdict) et la sortie minimale :

1. **cellule 20 (markdown)** — l'introduction : la question D2 posée en français, le
   protocole de calibration, et sa limite écrite *avant* la mesure ;
2. **cellule 21 (code)** — le cadran de puissance : rejoue exactement le protocole du
   carnet (6 features standardisées, ratio 1 H pour 5 N, `StratifiedKFold` à 3 plis,
   `LogisticRegression(C=1.0, class_weight='balanced')`, F1 moyenne sur les plis) sur une
   famille synthétique dont on **contrôle** la force du signal `d` (décalage de moyenne
   réparti sur les 6 features ⇒ distance de Mahalanobis = `d`). Le seuil de détection est
   le 95ᵉ centile du null **mesuré à la même taille** (même `n_h`, même ratio, mêmes
   plis) : la comparaison est appariée. La puissance est la fraction des réplications dont
   le F1 dépasse ce seuil ;
3. **cellule 22 (markdown)** — la lecture : le tableau du coût d'identification, la place
   de la valeur observée dans la distribution nulle, et ce que la calibration **ne** dit
   pas (elle mesure la sensibilité de l'**instrument**, pas la réalité du corpus).

Plus **un point ajouté en « À retenir »** (cellule 25) : la borne, en chiffres.

Le **verdict du carnet ne change pas** : `INCONCLUSIVE borne`. La calibration lui donne
une étendue.

## Mesures

`R_REPLICATIONS = 100` par case, graine fixe `SEED_PUISSANCE = SEED + 4242`, `D_VALEURS`
de 0.5 à 3.0, `N_H_VALEURS` = (6, 12, 24, 48).

Le nombre de réplications est **écrit dans la cellule** avec sa précision : à 100
réplications, l'écart-type de la puissance estimée vaut ±7,8 points autour de 80 %. Les
valeurs de « plus petit `d` détectable » sont donc des **bornes à cette précision**, pas
des valeurs exactes — la cellule l'affiche (`PRECISION_PUISSANCE`) et la lecture le dit.

| groupes H | unités group-level | plus petit `d` vu à 80 % de puissance |
|---|---|---|
| 6 (le carnet) | 36 | d ≥ 2.5 |
| 12 | 72 | d ≥ 2.0 |
| 24 | 144 | d ≥ 1.5 |
| 48 | 288 | d ≥ 1.0 |

- un effet de référence `d = 1` exigerait **48 groupes H** (288 unités) — le carnet en a 6 ;
- un effet `d = 2` exigerait **12 groupes H** (72 unités) — le carnet en a 6 ;
- le F1 observé (0.217) se situe au **68ᵉ centile** du null sans signal à la taille du
  carnet (**68 tirages nuls sur 100 sont en dessous ou égaux** à la valeur observée,
  **32 la dépassent**) : la valeur observée n'est pas dans la queue de la distribution,
  elle est **légèrement au-dessus de la médiane** du null.

Le goulot d'étranglement du dispositif est donc le nombre de **groupes H** (6 groupes
uniques contre 30 négatifs) — la voie reste #14033, mais le carnet peut désormais dire ce
qu'elle rapporte.

## Corrections après relecture (Hermes, clusterManager-Myia)

Deux corrections de glose, signalées par la relecture du 16/11 ; **aucune ne change la
statistique** du carnet ni le verdict `INCONCLUSIVE borne`. Commit `566c858249f6b`.

- **Le libellé du quantile était inversé (4 endroits)** : le print de la cellule 21
  annonçait « 68/100 nuls le dépassent », alors que le rang mesuré est
  `(null_pilote <= f1_real).mean()` = 0,68 — soit **68 nuls en dessous** de la valeur
  observée, et **32** qui la dépassent. La phrase est maintenant comptée par la cellule,
  pas écrite : deux comptes distincts (nuls inférieurs ou égaux d'un côté, strictement
  au-dessus de l'autre) dont les deux nombres **somment à 100**, de sorte que la phrase
  ne peut plus s'inverser. Les trois emplacements concernés — le print de la cellule 21,
  la Lecture 7 de la cellule 22, le point n°6 du « À retenir » de la cellule 25 — sont
  corrigés.
- **Une coquille non déclarée dans « À retenir »** : point n°4, `SURFACE_SELE` →
  `SURFACE_SEULE` (les 11 autres occurrences du carnet sont correctes).

La re-exécution a fait apparaître un détail que la première formulation ne trouvait pas :
le null contient **une** valeur exactement égale au F1 observé (67 strictement en dessous,
1 égale, 32 au-dessus). La phrase retenue compte donc les nuls « inférieurs ou égaux »
(68, ce qui est le rang mesuré) et les nuls « strictement au-dessus » (32) — les deux
nombres somment à 100, et le « 68ᵉ centile » reste exact. La lecture qualitative ne bouge
pas : la valeur observée n'est pas dans la queue de la distribution, elle est légèrement
au-dessus de la médiane du null.

## Exécution (C.2)

Ré-exécution **complète** du carnet via le MCP `jupyter-papermill` (chemin sanctionné —
`NotebookEdit` est deny), puis copie du résultat sur le carnet du dépôt.

- 28 cellules, dont **13 cellules de code**, toutes avec `execution_count` non nul et
  **0 erreur** ;
- les **12 cellules de code** préexistantes : sources **byte-identiques** à celles de
  `main`, sorties **identiques en valeurs** (comparaison par identifiant de cellule, pas par
  indice) ;
- les **3 cellules ajoutées** par la PR : sorties celles de cette exécution, rien n'est
  écrit à la main.

Comparaison cellule par cellule contre `origin/main` (script hors dépôt, alignement par
identifiant de cellule) : **12/12** cellules de code préexistantes ont des sorties
**identiques en valeurs** (texte des flux concaténés, cellule à cellule). Le compte
**byte-identique** est **11/12** : la cellule `cv-baseline` diffère **uniquement par le
découpage des flux** — **deux blocs de chaque côté**, mais coupés à un endroit
différent : côté `main` le premier bloc s'arrête après `[cv] fold 0` (1 + 6 lignes),
côté PR après `[cv] fold 1` (2 + 5 lignes). Les **sept lignes** sont identiques et
leur texte concaténé est **byte-identique** — **zéro différence de valeur**. Le détail
est dans le commentaire de livraison.

## Diagnostic dérive

**Verdict : CAUSE_FIXED.**

- **Cause (a) — environnement / kernel.** Le carnet déclare des chemins relatifs à la
  racine du dépôt (`MyIA.AI.Notebooks/GameTheory/...`) alors que le MCP exécute avec
  `cwd = le répertoire du carnet` : l'exécution en place aurait levé un `FileNotFoundError`
  sur l'assertion de la cellule 4. Le carnet a donc été exécuté depuis une **copie
  placée à la racine du worktree**, puis le résultat recopié sur le carnet du dépôt.
- Le chemin de la copie (`metadata.papermill.input_path` / `output_path`) a été ramené au
  **basename** — c'est la seule normalisation manuelle tolérée (elle porte sur la
  *métadonnée*, pas sur une sortie de cellule).
- **Cause (b) — saturation de la machine.** La première calibration (`R = 200`) n'a pas
  terminé : la machine était à 100 % de charge CPU depuis deux jours, par **trois
  processus orphelins à moi** (`_final_csv.py`, ~38 h de CPU cumulé chacun, lancés le
  14/11 par un sous-agent déjà rendu « completed »). Le symptôme — une cellule qui met
  21 min là où le prototype hors contention en met 186,7 s, puis un job MCP bloqué à 50 %
  avec `active_kernels: []` — a d'abord fait conclure à un carnet trop coûteux. La
  saturation a été **mesurée** (`Get-Process python*` + CPU cumulé vs âge), le livrable de
  ces processus a été **vérifié intact avant l'arrêt**, puis les trois processus ont été
  arrêtés. `R` a été ramené à 100 et la précision correspondante (±7,8

author: nikoheld
body:
Fixes from the independent review of the merged study tools:

1. **Malformed tasks comment**: a broken or unterminated `fanotes-tasks-v1` comment no longer gets a second block appended. Writes now keep exactly one live comment (first valid one replaced in place, valid duplicates removed). Broken-but-closed comments are renamed `fanotes-tasks-v1-broken`, so their text stays recoverable and never wins on read. A later valid comment is read when the first is broken. If a broken comment never closes (or runs into the next marker) the write is refused and the panel says why; renaming it would not stop it swallowing the rest of the note, and silently dropping it would lose data, so refusing is the safest.
2. **Whitespace**: clearing the list removes only the comment and its own line break. The whole-note `\n{3,}` collapse is gone (add then clear returns the note byte for byte). The same pattern still exists in `pdfTextMarks.writePdfMarks`; not touched here.
3. **Malformed blocks**: strict reading. Invalid JSON, non-objects, and blocks the sanitiser would cut or rewrite (list caps, long text, rejected pictures, dropped nodes) are reported with the reason and shown as source (editor and preview); the editor refuses to open them for writing. Unknown top-level fields are preserved on write-back (unknown nested fields are not).
4. **Block identity**: the host tracks offset plus a body fingerprint and re-locates the block on every write (and for "insert table"). If the body changed meanwhile, or identical twins make the position ambiguous, it locks the editor read-only with a message instead of writing into another block.

Tests: new regression cases in `check-study-tools` for each point; `check-study-ui` gains a malformed-block step.

## What it adds
- `/britannica/`: front page with "Find an article" (titles as you type, plus full-text and exact-phrase search inside the articles), the volume list, and a note on the edition and its 1911 views.
- `/britannica/volume-1/`: every article in printed order, grouped by first two letters, with page numbers.
- One page per article, in the read-online style: volume and page, contributor, find in article, previous and next, and Print this article with the house running head.
- "Reference → Britannica 1911" in the left rail.

## How it's hosted
Article pages, pictures, `titles.json` and the article search index are staged with the read-online pages and uploaded to R2 at files.foggypress.com/britannica/. Only the front and volume pages are on GitHub Pages. Volume 1 is about 34 MB, and all 29 volumes would be close to 1 GB.

The source is foggy-press-files `books/1911Britannica/volume-NN/output/html/`, built by `pipeline/britannica/` from Wikisource. Pictures are still being fetched from Wikimedia, which throttles us, so any picture not fetched yet is left out until a later build. The whole feature is switched by `catalog/reference.json` (`live`, `listed`).

## Changes
- `build/britannica.py` (new), `assets/britannica.css`, `assets/britannica.js`, `catalog/reference.json`
- `build/build.py`: rail link, `britannica.build()` in the site build, `britannica.stage()` in the R2 staging step

author: danestves
body:
Two new accounts redeemed each other's invite codes a minute apart, so each got a free month and would have earned another off the other. I revoked both months in RevenueCat, but one came straight back: the 1-minute safety-net grant saw no Pro and granted again, leaving a duplicate `rc_promo_pro_custom` row. The daily sweep would have re-granted both, because the reserved month was still in `referralRewards`. The dashboard also gave no hint that these grants came from invites.

- A referral month revoked in RevenueCat now stays revoked. When a promotional Pro ends before its end date, from the `onEntitlementDeactivated` hook or from a store sync that sees it first, the backend clears that person's reserved and banked months and stops their invite from earning the inviter a month (`capped`).
- A code from someone you invited counts as your own, so two new accounts can't trade codes. It answers `own` because shipped clients only map the existing statuses to copy.
- Each grant sets a `promo_reason` customer attribute in RevenueCat (who invited them, months earned inviting).
- `docs/internals/referrals.md` covers both.

Proof: three focused backend tests (traded code, revoke then sweep and third logged day, store sync before the webhook), each failing without its fix; backend suite 577 passed, tsc and `vp check` clean.

Policy notice: NOTHING. Privacy already lists RevenueCat as receiving who invited whom and months earned; Terms already allow removing months gained through abuse.
Effective date unchanged. Email: not needed.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved

body:
## O quê

**authkit-client**
- `registerOidcClient(router)` agora monta tudo por padrão (sem opções novas para desligar rotas):
  - `GET {prefix}/signup` → mesmo fluxo do login (state/PKCE/nonce, volta logado, `passthroughParams` como gclid/utm), com `prompt=create` (OIDC *Initiating User Registration*). `/auth/login?audience=signup` continua igual.
  - Redirects para o issuer, preservando o resto do path e a query: `/account` e `/account/*`, `{prefix}/forgot-password`, `{prefix}/reset-password[/*]`, `{prefix}/admin[/*]`.
- Novo `oidcClientRoutes(options)` (mesmas opções) devolve os handlers `login`, `signup`, `callback`, `logout`, `backchannelLogout`, `account`, `forgotPassword`, `resetPassword`, `admin`. O `registerOidcClient` é montado a partir deles (sem lógica duplicada). Quem quer só algumas rotas monta os handlers no próprio routes file.
- Os destinos vêm da discovery do issuer (campos novos `authkit_*_uri`, lidos pelo `discoverEndpoints` cacheado; também aceitos via `endpoints`), com fallback para os defaults do authkit-server na origem do issuer. Nunca sai da origem do issuer: URL publicada em outra origem é ignorada, segmentos `.`/`..` derrubam o resto do path, cada segmento é re-encodado.
- Topologia embedded (authkit-server no mesmo app, binding `authkit.server`): os redirects não são montados (o próprio app serve essas páginas; evitaria `Duplicate route` em `/auth/forgot-password`).

**authkit-server**
- `prompt=create` aceito (o oidc-provider recusava prompt fora da policy): prompt `create` requestable e sem checks na interaction policy, anunciado em `prompt_values_supported`. Prompt desconhecido continua `invalid_request`.
- Sem sessão no IdP, a interaction abre direto no signup (uma vez por interaction, para o "Já tenho conta" não entrar em loop). Signup fechado → tela de login normal. Com sessão no IdP → login normal (igual ao `audience=signup` hoje).
- Discovery publica `authkit_account_uri`, `authkit_account_home_uri`, `authkit_admin_uri` (só se o console admin estiver montado e `admin.enabled`), `authkit_forgot_password_uri`, `authkit_reset_password_uri`, seguindo `accountRoutes`/`accountHome`/`admin.prefix`.

## Por quê
Apps que viram RP do Hub (Entre Textos) tinham que escrever redirects à mão para links antigos (e-mails, favoritos) de conta, admin e recuperação de senha, e o signup dependia do hack `audience=signup`. Agora a lib resolve isso sozinha, sem hardcode de paths de um app específico.

## Gates locais
build ✅ · typecheck ✅ · lint (biome) ✅ · import smoke ✅ · testes authkit-client 381/381 ✅ · authkit-server 2915/2915 ✅

Docs: `client.mdx` (rotas montadas, signup, páginas do issuer, montagem manual), `customizing-auth.mdx` (`prompt=create`, páginas na discovery), `reference.mdx`. Changeset minor para client e server (pre `rc`).

body:
## Ringkasan

Test unit langsung `src/lib/evidence/measures.ts` — file baru `tests/evidence-measures-direct.test.ts` (16 test, node:test murni, impor modul langsung, tanpa PGlite/DOM). Modul **tidak diubah**; `tests/learning-measures.test.ts` (111 baris) dan `tests/evidence-events.test.ts` tetap utuh (dirujuk penjaganya, bukan dipindah).

## Yang dikunci

- `returningLearners` — lima kind belajar dihitung, `snooze`/`unsnooze`/`tutor` diabaikan kapan pun; batas minggu: tepat 7 hari → minggu sebelumnya, 1 ms ini sisi 7 hari → recent, tepat 14 hari → diabaikan, `now` tepat → recent, masa depan/rusak → diabaikan; satu learner sekali walau banyak event; hanya aktif 0–7 hari tidak menambah `activeBefore`; `rate` tanpa pembulatan (1/3), `null` hanya saat `activeBefore === 0`, tanpa kembali → 0.
- `finishesConcept` — `true` hanya `quiz`+`passed` dan `study`+`got-it`; lima kombinasi lain false.
- `activationTime` — penyelesai paling awal menurut waktu (urutan array diabaikan, dua arah), `firstFinishedAt` ISO ber-milidetik, `Math.round` half-up (30 dtk → 1, 90 dtk → 2), clamp `Math.max(0, …)`; tanpa penyelesai → keduanya null; `accountCreatedAt` null/rusak → `firstFinishedAt` terisi tetapi `minutes` null; penyelesai ber-`createdAt` rusak diabaikan.
- `learningMeasures` — `events` = jumlah baris; `retention`/`returning`/`activation`/`tutor` diteruskan dari helper (dibandingkan langsung dengan `dueReviewRetention`/`tutorPreference` dari `events.ts`); `calibrationGap` hanya bila kedua rate non-null (positif 8, negatif −33, 0; kuis-saja/laporan-saja → null); masukan kosong → seluruh cabang kosong.
- `measureRows` — urutan id/label/target persis (termasuk `Under 5 minutes`, `80%`); keempat cabang retention, kalibrasi `null`/`0`/`N points higher`/`lower` + bentuk tunggal `1 point`, returning `null`/`0 of 2 learners`/`1 of 1 learner`, aktivasi `No concept finished yet`/`unknown start date`/`1 minute`/`45 minutes`/`1 hour` (60 mnt)/`2 hours` (90 mnt, dibulatkan)/`2 days` (48 jam)/`3 days` (72 jam), string session tetap, personalisasi `No blind comparisons yet`/`2 of 3 comparisons`/bentuk tunggal `1 of 1 comparison`.
- Penjaga statis — `measures.ts` tepat satu impor `./events.ts` (tanpa `require`), mengekspor lima fungsi + empat tipe urut; `evidence.functions.ts` memakai `import('@/lib/evidence/measures')` dinamis + panggilan `learningMeasures(events, created ? new Date(created).toISOString() : null, new Date())`; `LearningMeasures.tsx` mengimpor/memanggil `measureRows` dan merender `r.label`/`r.value`/`Target: {r.target}`; string nilai baris tidak disalin di `src/` lain; anchor lama di kedua test lama tetap ada (termasuk jumlah baris 111).

## Gerbang

`npm run ci` utuh hijau: install, typecheck, lint 0/0, 1003/1003 unit (987 + 16), build, anggaran bundel, CSP build produksi, smoke Playwright + PGlite.

Tanpa perubahan aplikasi/perilaku/skema/RPC/migrasi/dependensi.

author: leonardolimanas
body:
Depende do #78 (base é a branch dele). Ordem: #76 → #77 → #78 → este.

## O que muda

**Admin da plataforma** (`/v1/admin/platform/qtags`, ator assinado; ações de escrita exigem `X-Admin-Reason`)
- `GET/POST /lots`: cria e lista lotes. O código tem 3 caracteres A-Z0-9 e entra no `publicCode`. A listagem mostra a contagem de tags por status.
- `POST /shipments {tenantId, publicCodes[]}`: separa tags do estoque para um tenant.
  - Cada tag precisa estar no estoque: sem tenant, `PROVISIONED`, ativa, fora de outra remessa e sem ativo.
  - A remessa nasce `SENT`, com manifesto `{publicCode, uid}` e código `RM-XXXX-XXXX` para o QR da caixa.
  - Tudo roda numa transação. Se alguma tag sair do estoque no meio da operação, nada é gravado.
- `GET /shipments?tenantId=`: lista as remessas.
- `POST /shipments/:id/lost {publicCodes?}`: marca extravio.
  - Sem lista, desativa todas as tags da remessa que ainda não foram vinculadas; com lista, só as indicadas (perda parcial).
  - As tags extraviadas ficam `DISABLED` e inativas, então o `/scan` passa a negá-las. O claimCode delas é apagado.

**Tenant** (Diamond, escopo `tags:claim`)
- `tag.shipment.receive {shipmentCode}`: confirma o recebimento da remessa (`SENT` → `RECEIVED`) e libera as tags para reivindicação.
- `tag.list {status?, page?}`: lista as tags do tenant (código público, status, ativo vinculado e remessa).

**`/api/v1/scan`**: uma tag autêntica ainda sem ativo agora devolve `tag: { publicCode }`. A página `/verify` usa esse campo para mostrar o código e o convite para vincular a tag (PR no qc-home).

**Fica para depois:** repor no saldo do tenant as tags extraviadas e debitar o saldo de QTAG na reivindicação. Faço isso junto do painel do dashboard, com o ledger existente.

## Testes

- `tests/tag-stock-facet.test.ts`: 8 testes.
- **Ponta a ponta num Postgres 16 local, com o Prisma real:**
  1. Criei um lote com 2 tags de estoque e uma remessa para o tenant.
  2. O claim antes do recebimento foi recusado (`SHIPMENT_NOT_RECEIVED`), e outro tenant não conseguiu receber a remessa (`SHIPMENT_NOT_FOUND`).
  3. O tenant recebeu a remessa. O claim de outro tenant deu `INVALID_CLAIM_CODE`.
  4. O claim do tenant funcionou, e repetir o mesmo código deu `INVALID_CLAIM_CODE` (uso único).
  5. Conferi `tag.get` e `tag.list`.
  6. Fiz release com novo claimCode e reclaim com ele.
  7. Marquei extravio parcial: remessa `PARTIALLY_LOST`, 1 tag desativada.
  8. No fim, havia 2 períodos no `TagBinding` (um fechado com motivo) e 3 eventos `QTAG_BINDING`.
- Suíte completa: 11 falhas, as mesmas da `main`.
- `tsc --noEmit` passou.

author: jhony-hacku
body:
## Pruebas E2E con Selenium contra staging

### Qué incluye
- Nuevo proyecto Maven `e2e/` (Selenium 4 + JUnit 5), independiente del build del backend.
- 6 pruebas de extremo a extremo sobre las historias HU-01, HU-03 y HU-04.
- Captura de pantalla automática cuando una prueba falla.
- Nuevo job `e2e-staging` en el CI: corre después del despliegue a staging,
  desde un runner de GitHub conectado por Tailscale.

### Por qué
Los tests unitarios validan cada pieza por separado. Estas pruebas validan la
aplicación completa ya desplegada (Angular + nginx + Spring Boot + PostgreSQL),
incluida la sesión JWT con cookies seguras y CSRF, que solo se puede comprobar
con un navegador real.

### Criterios de aceptación
- [ ] HU-01: al registrar una empresa con datos válidos, el administrador queda
      autenticado en la lista de procesos y ve el botón "Nuevo proceso".
- [ ] HU-01: si las contraseñas no coinciden, se muestra "Las contraseñas no
      coinciden." y no se registra la empresa.
- [ ] HU-03: tras cerrar sesión e iniciarla de nuevo, recargar la página
      conserva la sesión.
- [ ] HU-03: con una contraseña incorrecta se muestra "Correo o contraseña
      incorrectos." y no se entra a la aplicación.
- [ ] HU-04: al crear un proceso, aparece en la lista con su categoría y en
      estado "Borrador".
- [ ] HU-04: al guardar un proceso sin nombre, se muestra el error del campo y
      no se sale del formulario.
- [ ] Las pruebas se pueden repetir sin limpiar la base de datos (cada una usa
      datos únicos).
- [ ] En pull requests, el job `e2e-staging` se omite; en push a `develop` corre
      después de `deploy-staging`.
- [ ] Si una prueba falla, el job queda en rojo y publica capturas y reportes
      en el artefacto `e2e-selenium`.
- [ ] `mvn verify` del backend no ejecuta estas pruebas.

### Cómo probarlo
Con Chrome instalado y acceso a staging por Tailscale:

    ./mvnw -f e2e/pom.xml test -De2e.baseUrl=https://DIRECCION-DE-STAGING

Para ver el navegador: agregar `-De2e.headless=false`.

### Notas
- Cada corrida deja 6 empresas de prueba en la base de staging (NIT `E2E-...`).
- Las pruebas corren después del despliegue: un fallo no revierte staging,
  pero deja el pipeline en rojo.

body:
## Summary

AI-authored on the user's behalf.

Specify managed-service recovery in seven bounded documents with **36 falsifiable acceptance criteria**. The current amendment preserves AC-1 through AC-34 and adds AC-35 for bounded release-record turnover and AC-36 for durable closure capacity.

- Define runtime-owned turnover after the 1,024-record release limit, with bounded drain, closed gates, owner retirement and stale-generation fencing.
- Reserve 16 KiB of durable closure capacity per execution, including dependent executions without their own operation, before admission. Closure can consume that reservation when ordinary admission capacity is full.
- Bind all three recovery callers, including EmbeddedHost SDK/workerd delegation, to admission before writable database open or migration.
- Bind the current-policy ScopePermit and the verified current manifest to the same request. Check reader bounds before allocation.
- Specify management state through the existing core Database.Service, ordered output retention through SessionBlob, and an external restore barrier.

**Specification remains a draft proposal. Do not merge or expose the product.** T-1, finished-specification and designated-owner approval, B-1/B-2/B-3, U-1 and KEL-76 STOP remain open. The user-authorized isolated core candidate is separate from this documentation PR and grants no product acceptance.

## Spec refs

- Tracker #1376; platform #1379; admission #1380; state/migration #1381; recovery #1384; package composition #1385; retained terminal contract #1382.
- [Current specification index](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/blob/642aa28d83b0073effcfb758978f1fa083b1008e/docs/specs/gh1376-managed-service-recovery/index.md).
- [Execution claim](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/issues/1376#issuecomment-6916498463) and [native execution milestone](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/issues/1376#issuecomment-6917047992).
- Current amendment `642aa28d83b0073effcfb758978f1fa083b1008e`; sole parent `36177a7047b4e1165e82685e142a5d3ac498189e`; tree `dd0ab8f4c44047a7639a1daab25214bd7932a870`. Published with an expected-head check and no force push.
- Keld base `ec29b7ce2b155a8c98f96036cbb9c54488b5c302`; required OpenCode `4423f42836aaaf2933bc7b94b35aca4e5bcce7c3`.
- The full #1377 product denominator and existing runtime, Guard, IPC, state, process, terminal and package ownership remain in force.

## Review gates

Both confirmed CodeRabbit findings, release-record exhaustion and missing reserved closure capacity, are fixed in the current amendment. Both original threads are resolved after immutable-file readback.

Independent reviewers rechecked startup/source binding and authority/persistence/bounded liveness. Their findings on output-retention wording and the AC-35 custody fault control are fixed. No finding remains within those assigned documentation lenses. This evidence is separate from approval and installed-runtime qualification.

- **Public API:** proposed owner boundaries and DTOs remain subject to owner approval.
- **Permission model:** the existing runtime Principal does not yet supply the proposed integrated authority binding.
- **Wire protocol:** no allocation changed; owner allocation and generated codec fixtures remain required.
- **Unsafe:** no native implementation is added by this PR.
- **Dependency addition:** none.

## Tests

- Native `just spec-structure product-status-check`: passed. The specification validator ran 130 self-tests, checked 44 specifications and verified 28 pinned citations.
- Bounded capacity/closure reference: three positive scenarios passed and four deliberate faults were detected. This is policy evidence only.
- Current hosted CI: [run 43872843188](https://github.com/gyldlab/keld/actions/runs/43872843188) passed for the current head. Six jobs passed; 13 other lanes were explicitly skipped. Skipped native/runtime lanes confer no qualification.
- Native full `just ci`: failed on pre-existing foreign worktree registrations `gh-1405-update-feed-url-boundary-w2-20261114`, `gh-1405-windows-app-input-admission`, and `gh-1462-router-python-win`. Their registered paths have no matching Git worktree. No foreign record was changed or gate bypassed.
- Separate actual OpenCode core candidate on Windows: 50 tests passed, zero failed, 174 assertions across the database, migration, managed-profile and service-control suites. Type-checking passed across 1,872 files in two projects.
- The candidate's two focused fault checks detected forgotten terminal dispositions and bypassed final-Stop admission fencing. After restoration, all 15 service-control tests passed with 108 assertions; generated migration/schema consistency check passed.

The actual-core results cover a storage transaction slice. They do not establish shared effect release, native custody, power-loss durability, recovery integration, or B-3 no-blind-replay acceptance.

## Platforms

Windows, macOS and Linux remain required. This pass used the native Windows host for actual core and Keld validation, plus bounded cloud policy references and immutable source review.

The isolated core candidate includes an opt-in managed disk profile, generated schema and atomic retained management dispositions. No public route or production service installs it. Cross-actor ownership of a pending final Stop, runtime authorization, effect closure, restore behavior and the full product journeys remain integration work.

The PR remains open and unmerged. The native worktrees are retained for review and continuation.

## Perf impact

This documentation PR changes no runtime behavior. Numeric limits remain experimental budgets. The isolated candidate has correctness results, not product performance results. Full workload and native resource measurements remain U-1 obligations before exposure.

author: olafura
body: Lane B of the i18n track, stacked on #504 (`i18n/runtime`), which gives Ljos.Core's `t`, `msg` and `plural`. ## What changes - **`--compat lower` / `ljos migrate`** writes Qt's translated texts as Ljós's (docs/DIALECT.md §4.13 "Lowering"): - `qsTr("x")` → `` t`x` ``. - Each one-argument `.arg` fills the lowest-numbered `%N` still left, as `${value}`. - `%n` → `${n}` and `%Ln` → `#` inside `plural(n, { other: … })`. A disambiguation, or `qsTranslate`'s context, becomes `t({ message, context })`. `qsTrId` → `t({ id })`. - Each value stays where it is written, so whatever else the pass rewrites inside it survives, and no line is added. - **The file is kept** when: - `QT_TR_NOOP` or its family is used (Qt's value is a string, `msg`'s a descriptor); - a moved value is not a name, a member or a literal; - a count is not known to be an `int`; - the text is not written out; - an `.arg` has no `%N` left, or there is a `%L1`; - the rewrite would need a name the file already uses for something else (`t`, `plural`). - **`ljos check`** adds two rules: - `qt-tr` (error) names the `t` form to use. For `QT_TR*_NOOP` it says to write `msg` by hand. - `i18n-concat` (warning) flags a translated text joined to another value with `+`. Numbers added before the first text stay one value in the suggestion (`n + 1 + t`x`` → `` t`${n + 1}x` ``). ## Scenarios - `features/i18n/migrate-qstr.feature`: the keep scenarios for `%n`/int, a reordered call, `QT_TR_NOOP` and a text that is not written out all run. - `features/i18n/messages-check.feature`: both qt-tr scenarios and the i18n-concat one run, at `4:26` (the "without its indentation" step). - `features/i18n/migrate-qstr.feature`: the rewrite, contexts/ids and pixel scenarios run. - `features/language/pipe.feature` and `features/components/task.feature`: their typed examples translate with t``. - Still `@backlog`: the three `--catalogue` scenarios (`# Needs the extract lane`). ## DECISIONs - A `ListElement`'s `qsTr` stays as written, with its `ListModel`, and `qt-tr` does not report it. - Files whose names the pass can't all see (an unknown type, a delegate) keep `qsTr`. - `qt-tr` holds only in typed files. - A count counts as `int` when it is: - an integer literal; - a property that Qt's types or the file's declarations make `int`, read unqualified or on an id, when no type or declaration in sight says otherwise (the file's declarations are known by name, so `property real count` beside another object's `property int count` keeps the file); - a `length`. Anything else keeps the file, including `a / b` and parameters. - A `%N` no `.arg` fills is text. A `%N` written twice is its value twice. `%0` keeps the file. - ICU quoting of literal braces is the t`` lowering's job (lane A); migrate writes plain text. - The gate that held `qt-tr` back until Ljos.Core gave `t` is gone: on i18n/runtime the fix it names checks, so the error is right wherever a typed file uses `qsTr`. Its unit test runs. - docs/site examples that still use `qsTr` in typed files get `qt-tr`, which is correct. They are not rewritten here; that is the i18n/site lane. `crates/ljos_cli/tests/docs_site.txt` gets a `qt-tr` reason (21 blocks), and docs_site checks that such a block fails with `qt-tr` and nothing else, so the entry goes stale once the page is rewritten. - The tsc_oracle corpus (C06, C11, N03, N04) is rewritten to t``/`plural` with `import Ljos.Core`, and its KNOWN_GAPS is empty. - The pipe and task scenarios' typed examples are rewritten to t``, since what they test is the pipe and the Task, not Qt's functions. - My checker tests are in `crates/ljos_compiler/tests/translation_rules.rs`; lane A owns `tests/messages.rs`. - A `.arg` value that itself holds `%N` is shown as it is, and the file is not kept for it, a literal included (docs/DIALECT.md §4.13 DECISION from #503's review). Qt's chained `.arg` would fill it again, which Qt's documentation warns against. ## Gates run - `cargo test -p qml_compat` (256 passed). - `cargo test -p ljos_compiler --test translation_rules --test messages --test tsc_oracle`, and `--lib check`. - `cargo test -p ljos_cli --test check --test check_lint --test check_members --test migrate --test docs_site`. - `mise run check` (fmt, clippy). - `mise run features:lint`. - `mise run features:changed` on messages-check, migrate-qstr, messages, extract-po, pipe, task, ljos-controls, ljos-models and ljos-constant-rows: 114 scenarios pass. - Not run locally: the wasm step of `mise run check`, because `wasm32-unknown-unknown` isn't installed here. CI covers it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? author: not-varram
body:
Follow-up to #959, three review-bot findings checked against `main`.

## What was wrong

1. `untaken()` in `internal/serverupdate/channel.go` kept a pending update when its manifest could not be fetched, but only logged why. The super admin who changed the channel never learned the update was kept unchecked.
2. `migrateOnce` set `existing := current > 0`. A new database whose first migration run was interrupted (crash, or a second process opening it mid-way) was reopened with `current > 0`, treated as a pre-channel server and pinned to beta for good.
3. Comments that restate the code in files #959 added or changed.

## What happens now

1. `server.release_channel_set` returns `kept` (the pending version) and `kept_error` (the fetch error text, unchanged), beside `retired`, for a dry run and a save. The update is still kept, and Tick still refuses it at its idle moment if the channel does not take it. `docs/local-gateway.md` documents both fields. `aether-server update --channel` is the host path: it writes the setting directly, never calls the RPC and never retires or inspects a pending update, so there is nothing to print there.
2. Migration 1 sets `PRAGMA user_version = 1` in its own transaction. `migrateOnce` treats a database as pre-channel only when it has applied versions and no marker. A database this migrator created is therefore new however early it was interrupted. A database without the marker, including one a build without it left interrupted at exactly 112, cannot be told from a real pre-channel server and keeps the beta pin, the safe side. No migration is added or renumbered.
3. Removed the comments above `checkSoon` and `ReadMarks`, and the ones that only restated the code on `decline`, `Check.LatestRelease`, `channelConfirmation` and `buildLabel`. `promoteURL` does not exist anywhere in the repository, so there was nothing to change for it.

## How it was tested

- `TestChannelChangeReportsAPendingUpdateItKept`: a pending update whose manifest can no longer be fetched is reported as `kept` with the fetch error, in a dry run and on save, is not reported as retired, and stays pending. Does not compile on `main` (no `Kept` field); the behaviour was only a log line.
- `TestReleaseChannelOfADatabaseWhoseFirstRunWasInterrupted`: a new database interrupted at version 40 and one interrupted at 112, then reopened, are unchosen; a new database in one run is unchosen; a real v112 database is beta; each is opened twice to check it is idempotent. The two interrupted cases fail on `main` (they come out as beta).

Ran: `go build ./... && go vet ./...`; tests for `internal/store`, `internal/serverupdate`, `internal/sshd`, `internal/protocol`, `internal/selfupdate`, `cmd/aether-server`; `go test -tags integration -run 'TestIntegrationReleaseChannel|TestIntegrationServerUpdate' ./internal/server/` (only `TestIntegrationServerUpdateAppliesWhenIdle` fails, with "Docker daemon unreachable"); golangci-lint on the changed packages; `make public-audit`.

Dashboard (separate PR owns `web/`): show `kept` and `kept_error` from the `server.release_channel_set` result.

## Existing databases

Migration 1 gains one statement, `PRAGMA user_version = 1`, in its own transaction. Migration 1 never runs again on a database that has it, so nothing changes for one:

- A database already at v113 (any server that ran #959): no migration runs; `release_channel` is untouched.
- A pre-channel server at any older version: no marker, applied versions present, so it is existing and gets `beta` at v113, as before.
- A new database: marked in the same transaction as version 1, so it stays unchosen however its first run is interrupted.

`TestReleaseChannelOfADatabaseWhoseFirstRunWasInterrupted` covers a new database (one run, interrupted at 40, interrupted at 112) and an upgraded v112 database, each opened twice. No migration number is added or changed; `main` ends at v113.

## Adversarial review

Independent Opus session (fresh context, did not write the change): no blockers, 3 minors.

- The log line for a kept update was replaced by the result field, which nothing reads yet. **Fixed** in ade5e640c: both.
- `kept` is computed before the channel is saved and not re-read under the lock, so a cancel landing in between leaves a stale `kept` in that one response. **Left:** display only, and the next status shows the truth.
- `kept` and `kept_error` are not in the plan. **Noted:** they close a review finding on #959 (an error was logged and swallowed).

Confirmed by the reviewer, by running it: the marker is atomic with migration 1 (a rolled-back transaction leaves 0); the pre-update backup (`VACUUM INTO`) keeps it; nothing else reads `user_version`; the Edge database has its own migrator; concurrent opens are safe; both new tests fail without the change.

The dashboard does not show `kept` yet; #960 owns `web/`.

Greptile was asked to review with `@greptileai review` at 00:51 and 00:58 UTC and had not reviewed any head by 01:11 UTC.

This PR was made with the help of Claude Code.

author: omertekin2002
body:
## What and why

Adds `scripts/package_research.py`, which turns a research directory built by `build_research.py` into one citable ZIP, `artifacts/fr3-research-<short revision>.zip`. Before this, a reader who saved the research pages couldn't later prove which build, which revision or which checks they came from. This is the first slice of the vision roadmap item **Publish a coherent research edition**.

- **Pre-checks, all before anything is written.** The script re-runs `check_output()` and `verify_research()`, checks every `evidence/` file byte for byte against its committed `analysis/` original, and checks that `index.html` names the current producer revision and the `fr3.exe` SHA-256 from `analysis/pe-metadata.json`. If any check fails, it exits non-zero and writes nothing.
- **ZIP layout.** One top-level folder `fr3-research-<12-char revision>/` holds every research file unchanged, plus:
  - `MANIFEST.json`, which records:
    - the edition name and full producer revision;
    - the `fr3.exe` SHA-256 and PE timestamp;
    - the pinned demo archive SHA-256 and size;
    - the Python and zlib versions;
    - the fixed `verification` list;
    - each file's size and SHA-256.
  - `SHA256SUMS`, which `sha256sum -c` accepts from inside the folder.
- **The verification list states only what the script ran.** It also says plainly that `fr3.exe` and the archive are not re-hashed (their hashes are copied), that instruction evidence is not re-derived, and that Ghidra is not re-run.
- **Deterministic.** Entries are sorted and use mode 0644, deflate level 9 and one timestamp: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` if set, otherwise 1980-01-01. There are no directory entries.
- **Self-check before rename.** The ZIP is written to a temp file beside the destination. That file is reopened, checked with `testzip()`, and every entry is re-hashed against both manifests. Only then is it renamed into place, and the temp file is removed on any failure.
- **Safe destination.** Only a regular file named `fr3-research-*.zip` is overwritten. A directory, a symlink (including a dangling one), any other file, or a path inside the research directory is refused.
- **Docs.** New "Research packet" subsection in `docs/analysis.md` covering what the manifest proves and what it doesn't. Also a README outputs-table row, a usage paragraph and a line in the tests paragraph.

**Review fix (commit 2):** evidence and `pe-metadata.json` are compared with `analysis/` as committed at the producer revision (via `git show`), not the working tree, so pages built from an uncommitted edit are refused, and a non-commit revision is refused. Re-verified: 383 unit tests OK; real demo rebuilt and packaged twice at the new commit, byte-identical (189362 bytes, 28 files), `sha256sum -c --strict` OK.

**One addition beyond the issue text:** the revision and `fr3.exe` checks on the entrance page. Without them, the manifest could name a commit or build the pages were not built from.

Pages, `build_research.py` and the parsers are unchanged.

## How I verified it

- `ruff check scripts tests` (pinned ruff from `scripts/requirements-lint.txt`) → All checks passed!
- `python -m compileall -q scripts tests` → ok
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_package_research.py -v` → 25 tests OK
  - Like the existing `test_build_research`, this module imports sibling test fixtures, so it runs with `-s tests`, not as `tests.test_package_research`.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` → Ran 381 tests, OK (local Python 3.14 for this run; CI uses 3.12)
- `node --test "tests/js/*.test.mjs"` → 48 pass

Real demo (public, hash-pinned download, no game execution), at commit 4de1cd3:
- `python3 scripts/acquire_demo.py inputs --unshield unshield` → verified and extracted
- `python3 scripts/build_research.py` → 6 verified pages: 56 engines, 14 gearboxes, 109 tyres, 62 PCG collections, 654 graphics, 25 routines
- Two runs of `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000 python3 scripts/package_research.py --output .../fr3-research-{a,b}.zip` each printed: `Packaged and verified 28 files (26 research files plus MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS)`, 189362 bytes
- `cmp a b` → identical (SHA-256 `835f6dc1de79f852899aaa1f9cf62c5b15ec8c3f5270543bcc3d8bf868eed700`)
- After `unzip`: one folder, `fr3-research-4de1cd3a92f3/`. Inside it, `sha256sum -c --strict SHA256SUMS` → all 27 lines OK. `MANIFEST.json` shows the expected revision, input hashes, PE timestamp `2004-12-21T16:15:02+00:00` and verification list.
- With no `--output`, it wrote `artifacts/fr3-research-4de1cd3a92f3.zip`. `git check-ignore -v` confirms `.gitignore:2:artifacts/`.

Tests cover each refusal in the acceptance criteria and check that nothing is left behind afterwards:
- missing directory
- a page without the notice
- an extra file
- changed evidence
- a destination that is a directory or a symlink

They also cover:
- revision and executable mismatch
- an unrelated destination file
- a destination inside the research directory
- a failed self-check (existing packet kept, no temp file)
- tampered ZIPs rejected by the self-check
- byte-identical repeat runs, and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` handling
- a CLI run on a directory built by the real `build_research.py` CLI

## Risk and rollback

Low. This is a new standalone script plus docs. It writes only under `artifacts/` or the given `--output`, and changes no existing output. To roll back, revert this PR.

The ZIP is byte-identical only for the same Python and zlib versions, since deflate output can differ across zlib versions. That's why the manifest records both.

Refs #55

This is a stacked improvement into `agent/improvements`; it reaches `main` through the umbrella PR.

author: aaronfeledy
body:
Fixes #2280
Fixes #2283
Fixes #2383

- **Env references stay readable** (`Keep complete env references readable...`): a value that is exactly `${NAME}`, `${NAME?}`, `$${NAME}`, `$${NAME?}` or `$NAME` (bare, double-quoted, or escaped with equal backslash runs) is kept only at a verified terminator, the same way in the normal, bounded, exported, and transcript paths. `$${NAME}` no longer leaves a stray `}`, and a value the value layer masked mid-value (`$[redacted]`) no longer leaves a stray `]`.
- **Multi-line secrets in process output** (`Redact multi-line secrets...`): a new bounded line-stream (`@lando/redaction/line-stream`) holds a block while a quoted value or a `Bearer` token is still open, then masks it as one value. It's used by build output, lifecycle event narration and failure tails, plain rendered results, and collected `lando logs`, so text, TTY, JSON, YAML, and MCP show the same safe lines. Holds stop at 64 lines / 16 KiB and fail closed. A quote-skip fast path keeps the worst case linear.
- **Schema-fixed literals survive** (`Keep schema-fixed literals...`): `apiVersion`, `_tag`, `kind`, stream names, and other finite literals stay readable in envelopes, frames, events, and MCP when they collide with a registered secret; free text and undeclared keys stay masked. This is the costliest change for the lowest-impact issue (#2383). It's an isolated commit that can be dropped on its own.

Spec changes (deliberate deviations):
- `03` §3.7: env-reference grammar with verified terminators; line-stream contract (bounds, fail-closed, same-quote and escaped-opener exclusions, collected logs, live frames per frame); structural exemption rule.
- `06`: build output uses the line-stream instead of "pattern classes apply per output line"; "applies RedactionService exactly once" becomes "each boundary applies its canonical policy, and re-redaction is idempotent".
- `08`: lifecycle narration and failure tails use the line-stream; MCP dispatch-error `_tag` and event frames keep schema literals.
- `10` §9.6: env-reference exemption.

Known limits, tracked: #2395 (unterminated or escaped quoted values on single-string surfaces), #2396 (followed logs and MCP live progress need a time-bounded hold; per-stream ordering), #2397 (LF-registered multi-line values vs CRLF output), #2398 (secret-named fields in JSON/YAML envelopes), #2399 (spaced, YAML-style, and JSON-text assignments).

Verification: related suites run individually (sdk secrets and command-result, redaction, mcp, engine build and event, core logs and renderer, recipe npm tests), new seeded fuzz and equivalence tests, `gate:pr`, `lint:guides`, guide coverage, public transcripts, schema compatibility, startup and tooling benchmarks against main (no measurable change), and live runs in a clean Linux sandbox.

author: paulfidika
body:
Paul, 11-15: "ideally all dependencies we use should be present on the machine when we install ourselves." Encrypted create failed on a fresh Linux without FUSE (cl-1000). Audit and plan: tracker cl-1030.

**No new command: `cozy doctor --fix`.** Doctor's one tools table gains `fuse3`, `libfuse2`, `winfsp` and `vcruntime`. What doctor reports as missing is exactly what `--fix` installs.
- **System packages.** One command through apt-get, dnf, pacman or zypper, or winget on Windows. With no winget (GitHub's Windows runners have none), WinFsp's pinned MSI, held to its digest.
  - As root or an administrator: installs without asking.
  - Otherwise: one question on /dev/tty listing each package and why.
  - With no terminal or no sudo: prints the exact command.
  - gcc is installed only with an NVIDIA GPU ("Triton kernels need a C compiler"). libfuse2 stays only until cl-1000 links libfuse3 statically into securefs; that agent coordinates its removal.
- **Fetched tools.** ffmpeg and uv come from Calcifer's own fetch code (`calcifer::prefetch`), so first use downloads nothing. A failed fetch is left to first need, as today.
- **Nothing in it fails.**

**Installers.** `scripts/patch-installers-fix.sh` (called by `patch-installers.sh`) makes the shell installer run `"$_install_dir/cozy" doctor --fix < /dev/null || true` once cozy is in place, never with the piped script as stdin. The PowerShell installer gets the same call, and its exit code never fails the install.

**Not in this PR:**
- The Homebrew formula is unchanged. macOS needs no system package, and brew's sandboxed post_install can't write `~/.cozy`.
- The PyTorch base at install time is a follow-up (cl-1030): TensorD installs its base when it starts on a GPU machine.

## Proof
The `fresh` cells: the last released `cozy-installer.sh`/`.ps1` with this PR's `patch-installers-fix.sh`, installing the candidate cozy served as the release archive (`COZY_DOWNLOAD_URL`).

| cell | run (commit) | result |
|---|---|---|
| fresh Ubuntu 24.04 container, no FUSE, a non-root user with sudo, in a terminal | [43782758160](https://github.com/cozy-creator/cozy-creator/actions/runs/43782758160) (8d49da05) | asked once, listing git, fuse3 and libfuse2; installed them; ffmpeg and uv ready; then `cozy new --passphrase-file … --recovery-out …` as that user: `{"encrypted":true,"state":"unlocked"}` |
| fresh Ubuntu 24.04, no sudo, no terminal | 43782758160 (8d49da05) | the install completed and said `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git fuse3 libfuse2t64`; cozy runs |
| macOS 15 | [43785030724](https://github.com/cozy-creator/cozy-creator/actions/runs/43785030724) (ca8f5c18) | ffmpeg fetched by the installer into `~/.cozy/tools`; the first thumbnail fetched nothing |
| Windows 2025, no WinFsp | [43787077181](https://github.com/cozy-creator/cozy-creator/actions/runs/43787077181) (3f47eac3) | the installer, as admin, installed WinFsp from its pinned MSI with `ADDLOCAL=ALL` and fetched ffmpeg and uv; doctor then found winfsp, vcruntime, git, ffmpeg and uv |

The Windows cell now asserts only what the installer owns: WinFsp installed, and doctor's rows found. That's exactly what 43787077181 shows, so it wasn't re-run.

In that same run, `cozy new` encrypted then failed with `filesystem provider mount failed (Some(1))` even though WinFsp was installed. As far as I can tell e2e has never created an encrypted project on Windows (projectvault's cells are Linux-only). That step moves to its fix's own cell: tracker **cl-1049**, owned by a6e0bae89ee900c50.

Commits since 3f47eac3 are only that cell change and a merge of rc/0.26.0, which conflicted in `e2e/cli/run.sh` only (both sides kept: `notraces`, `restart`, `fresh`). `cargo check -p cli` passes after the merge.

author: nickysemenza
body:
## Summary

```diff
 quantity variance
-  walk kit ledger to check comparable history
-  walk kit ledger again to calculate expected units
+  derive comparability and expected units in one ledger projection
   compare against live stock
```

Reuse one projection in the shared SQL expression used by Product sorts, filters and totals. Preserve live Expense, Inventory and Location reads, kit weights, service exclusions and unknown quantities. Remove the separate comparability-query helper and correct stale publication/zero-history documentation.

Related to #2594. This reduces one SQL component; it does not establish a fix for cold ingress, connection acquisition, full Work population or browser latency.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a read-only production repeatable-read comparison over 7,424 live Products took 317 and 271 ms.
  **After:** 198 and 203 ms, with identical complete identity/variance results across baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline queries. SQL/client timings, two samples per version; no production records or identifiers are included here.
- Execution plans show the second per-Product recursive walk removed (6,950 executions in the baseline). Explained execution was 340 vs 234 ms; this is not a page-latency or whole-database-load measurement.
- All eleven existing quantity-ledger integration cases passed, covering live filters, unknown kit quantities, incomparable units, exits, fractions, negative balances, planned spend and placement. No tests added or deleted.
- Web typecheck, staged lint/format and CI's Knip target passed locally.
- The broad local fast suite exceeded its two-minute bound (exit 124), so no local fast-suite pass is claimed; required hosted CI remains the merge gate.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Read-only SQL change with no schema or stored-data changes.

**Blast Radius:** Quantities

The shared correlated variance expression changes execution shape while retaining its live membership and null rules. Broad issue acceptance remains open.

body:
Links of the form `webamp.org/?milkdropPresetUrl=https://archive.org/cors/md_….milk/….milk` fail: `getPresets` threw `Error: We still need to implement this`, so the Milkdrop window opens with no presets. In Sentry this is WEBAMP-1P0, 186 events, and every event since November 2 has an archive.org `md_` URL. Something is linking to webamp.org with these.

This implements the param. It fetches the `.milk` file and converts it with `milkdrop-preset-converter-aws` and the shader-converter endpoint, the same path the demo already uses for `.milk` files dropped onto Milkdrop. Conversion is lazy (`getButterchrunPresetObject`), so the converter chunk only loads when the preset is used.

As with `butterchurnPresetUrl` and `butterchurnPresetMapUrl`, only known URLs are accepted, because a converted preset contains code that is run. The allowlist is `https://archive.org/cors/md_….milk`, which mirrors the archive.org `md_….json` entry already in the list. Any other URL logs `Unsupported URL passed as milkdropPresetUrl query param.` and falls back to the default presets. That is the same thing the other params do.

`importConvertPreset` and the converter endpoint move to module-level constants, so `butterchurnOptions` and the new loader share them.

### Steps to reproduce (on webamp.org today)

1. Open https://webamp.org/?milkdropPresetUrl=https://archive.org/cors/md_bdrv_al_Eo.S.Phat_intergalactic_blob_analyser.milk/bdrv__al_Eo.S.Phat_intergalactic_blob_analyser.milk (the URL from the latest Sentry event).
2. Expected: Milkdrop shows that preset. Actual: the console shows `Error: We still need to implement this` and Milkdrop has no presets.

author: jvtomax99
body:
## What this does

This is change 1 of 2 of the database lock-down Jose OK'd on 2026-11-15 (`docs/features/deleted-items.md`). It is the app side, and it works with today's rules. Change 2, the rules themselves, comes at least 2 days after this is live, so every phone has the new app first.

**Recently deleted is now required.**
- Deleting a term, doctor, provider or attachment first writes a copy to the bin, named `<collection>__<id>`.
- The copy goes through the outbox, ahead of the delete. Offline, both wait and replay in that order.
- If the copy can't be kept, nothing is deleted, and the person is told why.

**Attachments can be restored.**
- Files and photos stay in Storage, so a restore brings them back whole.
- Deleting a term moves its attachments to the bin too, and restoring the term brings them back.

**Restores are safe.**
- A restore that fails keeps the bin copy. Before, a failed doctor or provider restore threw it away; that was an older bug.
- Restoring over an item that is already back asks first.

**You manage your own posts.** "Yours" follows the phone's sign-in, not the typed name.
- Chat: Edit and Delete appear on your own messages; owner phones can delete anyone's. Reactions stay open to everyone.
- Pins and events: Unpin and Remove appear on your own.
- Updates: the ✕ and Clear all appear only on owner phones.

**Posts carry the poster's id** (`uid`): announcements, events, shared results and uploads (as Storage metadata). The coming rules check it.

## Done when (for this change)

- **New delete test:** `tests/suites/delete-safety.cjs` passes 17 of 17. It covers the named copy, no copy no delete, offline order and replay for terms and providers, a failed restore keeping the copy, attachments restoring alone and with their term, and the buttons for a teammate and for an owner. Against the live code it fails: no named copy, and offline only the delete gets queued, with no copy.
- **Full run:** `node run.cjs` passes all 58 suites, and all 3 inline scripts pass `node --check`. `feel.cjs` now presses the Updates ✕ from an owner phone, since only owners see it.
- **Independent review** found two serious problems, both fixed and covered by the test:
  - Doctor and provider deletes skipped the outbox, so offline the copy and the delete could race.
  - A failed restore threw away the only copy.
  - It also caught the Edit check and its button disagreeing, refusals blamed on the connection, and attachments not returning with their term.
- **Screenshots:** Team Chat's message menu shows no Delete on someone else's message for a teammate, and shows Delete for an owner. Updates shows no ✕ or Clear all for a teammate, and shows both for an owner. Sent to Jose as files.

## User Guide

- Updated answers: `chat`, `pin`, `updates`, `events`, `attach` and `deleted`, covering who can remove what, that everything goes to Recently deleted for 30 days, that nobody empties the bin early, and that a new sign-in id loses Edit on earlier posts.
- New "New lately" card, `deleted`. The oldest card, `opening`, drops off; its answer stays.

## Not in this change

- **The rules:** Next item 1 in `docs/PLAN.md`.
- **Typed names** are still self-reported.
- **Editing** stays open to the whole team.
- **Daily backups.**

author: baiirun
body:
## What changes

Services now shut down gracefully. The contract is the new `docs/specification/application-lifecycle.md`.

- **Drain before cancel.** Stopping or removing a process unroutes it and closes its mailbox, but no longer cancels it. Its sleeps, child tasks, `Task.result`, channel operations and timeout scopes carry on. `receive` returns what the process already accepted, then cancellation. At `shutdown_within` the body is forced. A body that never ran is cancelled at once, and a zero deadline forces at once. A supervisor operation that waits on its caller's own shutdown is answered with cancellation, whether it was parked before the drain began or made during it. This supersedes the 2026-11-11 "interrupt every park" decision.
- **Ordered shutdown.** `Supervisor.stop` closes the supervisor, then stops its members one at a time, newest first. Each member is unrouted only when its own turn comes, so a draining member can still reach older ones (SD06 changes).
- **Signals.** The first SIGINT or SIGTERM cancels `main`, and its root supervisors drain. A second signal ends the program at once. A program without the scheduler is cancelled at its next operation, and a blocking stdin read is interrupted. A real-clock stall with a running supervisor waits for a signal instead of reporting a deadlock.
- **Exit status.** A cancellation caused by a signal writes its outcome, then re-raises the signal (falling back to `_exit(128+n)`). `--signal=TERM@1500ms` (or `INT`) injects a signal under `--clock=virtual` and exits with 128+n. A signal due after `main` ends is never delivered and never moves virtual time.
- **Phase 4 forcing program:** `programs/service-pool` (FP02) is a dispatcher, a dynamic pool of three workers and a ledger. SIGTERM arrives mid-run, the queued jobs still finish, and only the job that outlasts its deadline is forced.
- ABI: fiber 12, native runtime 30. Lab stage U13 adds MB22 (a monitor notice during a drain is dropped, covering CHI-220), SD10 to SD13 (deadline forcing from source, a child task, a timeout, a Select ticker), SG01 to SG03, and FP02. RR05, SD06 and CB10 now expect the drain. `compiler/chimi/tests/signals.rs` sends real signals.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` passes locally, and so does `chimi-process-lab all` (PG02 is noisy under load).
- Mutation testing: `scripts/mutation/g22_mutations.py` has 15 mutants. Run 1 found four survivors. Each now has a test that kills it, checked by hand, and the rerun results go in `g22_results.txt`.
- Reviews: one general review and one soundness review. The soundness review found that a signal timer could still fire after `main` ended, and that a self-stop made during a drain waited for its deadline. Both are fixed, with tests (SG03 now shows the signal event, plus a new scheduler test).

Code-quality routes: changing-existing-code (redesign-from-first-principles, subtract-before-you-add, special-cases-are-requirements), testing-and-verifying, documenting-code.

## Notes for later

- A body that never looks at its inbox learns of a stop only at its deadline. Selecting on `Select.inbox` gets notice at once (SD13).
- SIGPIPE is untouched. A scheduled program blocked inside a stdin read is not woken by the first signal, only by the second.

author: asuresh8
body:
## What changes for users

Before: a release named a Mac's `.pkg` by a location in the store `komira-testing`. A Mac has no `stores.toml` since the coordinator's MDM (which pushed it) was removed, so mac-studio-01's install order failed `Failed / environment / no_store` and no package could be installed on it.

After: the `macos-arm64` entry of every release (hostkeeper, hello) is the named-version form of docs/design/packages-repositories.md section 4.7: `{installer: macos-pkg, repository: komira-testing, packageVersion, digest, bytes, manifest}`. The coordinator resolves it at order time to its implicit store `coordinator` and streams the `.pkg`; the Mac needs no `stores.toml`. Linux entries are unchanged. The explicit-location form stays valid for other projects' releases.

## Walk through

1. `crates/xtask/src/release/targets.rs`: the Mac branch of `native_of` writes `repository` (the same channel the apt entry names, `Package::repository_entry`) and `package_version` (the release's version) and no location; digest, bytes and manifest are as before. Unused imports removed; the module header describes the new form.
2. `crates/xtask/src/release/targets/tests.rs` and `crates/xtask/tests/workflows/release_files.rs`: expected entries and the byte-for-byte lines follow the new form.
3. `docs/design/packages-repositories.md` section 4.7 and `docs/design/packages-native.md` section 10.1: CI sends the named-version form for hostkeeper's releases.

## Compatibility and failure modes

- Needs a coordinator with the named-version form (it is on main; the coordinator running today accepted such an entry in a dry check) and a registry entry whose descriptor has `macos-pkg`. The registry entry `komira` was added before the descriptor had `macos-pkg`; it must be re-added (`hkctl repositories discover` then `add`, same keyring sha256, fingerprints 1 to 2 as the descriptor lists them) before the first release from this change, or the Mac entry does not resolve and the Mac is picked no entry (`no_build_for_host`) rather than failing. Linux hosts are unaffected either way.
- No wire or format change; the entry uses fields the coordinator already knows. Previous releases keep their stored entries.
- Does not change the daemon, the bootstrap or any `stores.toml` handling: the bootstrap needs no `stores.toml`.

## Tests

- `a_mac_entry_names_the_channel_and_version_and_no_store`: the macOS entry has no `locations`, its `repository` equals the Linux entry's, `packageVersion` is the release's, `bytes` is not 0.
- `hostkeeper_lists_its_deb_on_linux_and_its_installer_on_macos_alone`, `hello_lists_its_deb_on_linux_and_its_pkg_on_macos_alone`: the whole entry per platform equals the expected named-version entry and passes the coordinator's `target::check`.
- `the_line_of_each_package_is_the_bytes_the_release_writes`: the exact JSON of the `targets=` line for hostkeeper and hello.
- The workflow lint's release-files case builds the expected targets with the same shape.

Not run locally (the build box is overloaded); CI is the check.

author: milagrofrost
body:
## What changed

A user who turns down the AI chatbot panics for 8 seconds (`FRANTIC_T`). That panic now has two halves:

- **First 4 s:** they scramble around the hallway as before, at panic speed.
- **Last 4 s:** while you're in the hallway, they walk straight toward you at a calm user's normal pace (`USER_PACE` 42, scaled down by rank and doubled at the donut shop like all user movement there), not panic speed. Step into a server room and they go back to scrambling.
- **When it ends:** after 8 s they stop seeking and wander as usual. They also stop once they catch you: they got their human, so one panic can't grab you twice. Interns, who only ask in passing, end their panic on contact too and now shout a "want a human" line.

## Why

Rejecting the chatbot should feel like it lands on you: the user wants a human, and you're the human.

## Reviewer notes

- During a red alert a chatbot reject in the second half of its panic still seeks you; everyone else keeps the red-alert scramble.
- Seeking skips the random direction rolls for that user while it lasts (gameplay movement, not cosmetic code).
- Rebased on `main` after #11; the only conflict was the neighbouring AI Agent shop description, kept as merged.
- Docs: AI Chatbots shop description, code comment and a new AGENTS.md rule. The README has no chatbot section to update.

## Testing

- `tests/regression.html`: PASS 147/147, with a new check covering the scramble, the normal walking pace, stopping when you leave the hallway, stopping when the panic ends, and the panic ending when they catch you.
- `node tests/syntax.mjs`: all scripts parse.
- Browser: sampled a frantic analyst every 0.5 s in a live game. They scrambled for 4 s, walked toward the player at about 37/s, and went back to wandering at 8 s; a screenshot shows them heading up the hallway shouting for a representative.
- Not run locally: Playwright desktop/phone tests and the balance comparison (CI runs them).
