body: Typing indicators for room chat (`convex/` only). ## New function | Function | Type | Args | Returns | |---|---|---|---| | `rooms.setTyping` | mutation | `{ roomId, userId }` | – | ## Details - **`rooms.setTyping`**: room members who haven't left, and only while the room is `live`; otherwise it throws a friendly `ConvexError`. It sets `typingUntil = Date.now() + 4000`. If the current indicator still has 2+ seconds left, it skips the write. That keeps it cheap when the app calls it on every keystroke, and each refresh still extends it by 4 seconds. - **`rooms.send`** clears the sender's `typingUntil`. - **`rooms.get`** includes `typingUntil` per member (`null` when not set). The app shows "typing…" while `typingUntil > Date.now()` on the phone. - **Schema**: `roomMembers.typingUntil` (optional number). A note on load: every typing write re-runs `rooms.get` for everyone watching the room. The skip-if-fresh check keeps that to at most one write per person every ~2 seconds. If it ever gets heavy, typing state could move to its own small table. ## Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit -p convex` passes. - Throwaway convex-test run (not committed): - Refused before the room was live. - The first call set +4 s. A call 1 s later was skipped (3 s left). A call 2.5 s after that refreshed it to +4 s. - `send` cleared it. - A member who had left was refused.

## Description

Lot F1c of the 100 % coverage plan, second half: the GitHub PR review handlers. `pr-handlers.ts` goes from 2 153 to 799 lines. The review runs move to `pr-review-run.ts`, the "is the review still current" checks to `pr-freshness.ts` and the review memory view to `pr-review-memory.ts`. These files, plus `pr-actions.ts`, `pr-review-post.ts`, `pr-ipc-guard.ts`, `utils.ts` and `import-handlers.ts`, are at 100 % of lines and branches (675 statements, 463 branches).

**Stacked on #1005** (itself on #991): this branch contains their commits. Merge it after them; its own change is the last commit, 85dbc275.

What the tests found, fixed with a regression test each:

- A failed review sent its error without the PR number, so the renderer could not tell which PR failed and the spinner kept turning.
- Cancelling a local review stopped only the runner, not the processes it started. The forced stop that should follow never fired.
- When a review of a PR was started again, the end of the previous run removed the new run's entry, so the new one could no longer be cancelled.
- The first review and the follow-up review were two copies of the same 100 lines. They now share one path, driven by a table of their differences.
- A check run that ended `timed_out` did not count as failing CI.
- A repository configured by its clone URL (`https://github.com/o/r.git`) produced invalid API paths. It is now normalized like the other places that read `GITHUB_REPO`.
- A PR comment went through a temp file in `.workpilot/` that two concurrent comments shared. The body now goes to `gh` on stdin. `gh` runs asynchronously (it blocked the main process) and has a 64 MB output buffer instead of 1 MB, which cut off large diffs.
- The IPC guard now checks the post options (`forceApprove` only), the memory view's `limit` (a positive integer, capped at 100) and the memory search's query. A memory index entry must name a positive PR number to be read.

body:
Hand-entry part of #27. The CSV importer itself is already merged (#106).

**What it does**
- A **"Type them in"** tab on the import page, beside zip / folder / files (`www/js/import-manual.js`, one tab and one script line on the page). Each row has a date, optional time, test, value, unit, range, flag and lab.
  - Test names are suggested from `lab-aliases.json`'s canonical names (`GET /api/lab-names`).
  - Rows can be added, removed and pasted from a spreadsheet. A pasted header row decides which column is which; without one, columns fill in from the field pasted into.
  - The server checks each row as you type. Under the row it shows the name the result will be charted as, the range it read and the flag, or why the row can't be saved.
  - Works under the strict CSP and at 375 px. Viewers don't get the tab, because the page only lists profiles you own or edit.
- **`POST /api/profiles/{pid}/manual`** (`server/routes_manual.py`; editor or owner, CSRF-checked):
  - Reads rows with the CSV importer's own row reader. I moved the per-row logic into a public `csv_labs.read_row` and made `build()` public; `parse` behaves exactly as before and its tests are unchanged.
  - So typed results get the same source keys, canonical names, ranges and flags as the same rows in a CSV. Only the source label on the points differs ("Typed in").
  - Runs the registry's `check()`, then saves one import (origin and format `manual`) with `records.store` in a transaction, logged as `import` with counts. Undo should cover it like any other import.
  - If any row can't be read, the request is refused with per-row reasons and nothing is saved.

**Choices worth a look**
- Dates like 03/04/2026 that could be read either way are refused, with a request to write them as YYYY-MM-DD. A CSV import would guess instead.
- At most 200 rows per request, to stay under nginx's 64 KB body limit.
- The disabled primary button on the import page had white text on a white background. It now has visible text.

**Tests**
- New `tests/test_manual.py`, added to CI:
  - typed rows appear in `/data` with ranges, flags and canonical names;
  - typing a CSV fixture's rows gives the same keys as importing that CSV;
  - bad rows are refused with their reasons and nothing is saved;
  - a viewer can't save, and a request without the CSRF header is refused.
- `tests/browser_check.py` types two results, tries a paste, saves, and finds both on Trends (107 checks pass locally).
- `test_api`, `test_uploads`, `test_jobs` and the importer tests all pass.

author: tripandcode
body:
**Origin:** Interactive session

Closes #1491. A first-time reader on Pulse learns what the numbers mean, every headline figure explains itself in place, and statistics-only columns wait behind one explicit setting.

## What changed

- **Meaning-first tour on Pulse.** The tour has three steps, written in plain words:
  - **Delay:** a departure delay at a stop, from the operator's own feed. Early departures count as negative.
  - **On time:** built from the actual on-time window. By default that is 1 min early to 5 min late, so leaving earlier than that is not on time. The rate itself lives on Routes and each route page.
  - **Scope:** what the scope sentence counts, and that clicking ▼ changes it.

  How it behaves:
  - It reuses `FirstRunTour`, mounts inside Pulse's figures so every anchor exists, and is remembered under `transit.pulseTourSeen` once dismissed.
  - OverviewTab holds the step and the "Later" state, so a refetch, including the scope change step 3 invites, neither restarts nor reopens it.
  - The Live controls tour is deleted, along with its anchors, keys, CSS and tests. It taught controls rather than meaning, used 種別, and Live isn't the persona's screen.
- **Inline definitions.** `MetricDefinition`, wrapping the ⓘ `InsightHint`, explains the average delay, each fact row and Routes to check, consistent with the manual and the backend computations.
  - Each has a "More in the user manual" link to an anchor, which `manualAnchors.test` ties to real headings.
  - The late-routes and routes-to-check definitions say that their base excludes what Routes leaves out by default.
- **One "Show statistics" setting.** It lives in `statisticsPref.ts`, is off by default, and is remembered per browser.
  - **What it hides:** the Routes table's Samples, the day-type reports' Samples, Why's p50/p90 and counts, headway CoV and Samples, weather Samples, the period-summary counts, and the snapshot equivalents.
  - **Few-data marks:** a count may only hide if the figure it qualifies then carries the few-data mark below `FEW_DATA_MIN_SAMPLES` (100, mirrored from `RANKING_MIN_SAMPLES` by a test), or below the server's own floor where one is echoed. Each count marks one figure, and a missing figure carries no mark.
  - **Where the toggle appears:** only where a table it changes is drawn.
  - **CSV:** keeps every column.
  - **Left out on purpose:** NetworkTab's CI and samples (the fairness-gate evidence), the council report, the notebook and the route page's stop table.
- **Day-group wording.** `dow=weekend` is Saturday and Sunday only (`api/range.py`), so Ask's filter bar uses the scope's 土日 keys. The notebook's service chip selects the 土日祝 timetable, so its English now says "Weekend/holiday". A glossary guard rejects 土日のみ.
- **Docs and manuals (ja/en):** cover the tour, the ⓘ definitions, the statistics setting and its rule. The screenshot script seeds the tour as seen.

## Verification

All checks ran at 14a82c7e, each with its own exit code:
- `typecheck`, `test:coverage` (4338 tests), `lint`, `lint:i18n`, `lint:i18n-strings`, `deadcode`, `test:check-entry-chunk`, `test:check-css-tokens`, `check:css-tokens`, `test:check-react-compiler`, `check:react-compiler`, and `build:bundle && check:entry-chunk` all exit 0.
- `node --test tests/frontend/user_manual_parity.test.mjs tests/frontend/i18n_glossary.test.mjs`: 4/4.
- **Mutation checks, all red:**
  - dismissal not written;
  - statistics on by default;
  - average-delay definition removed;
  - tour ignoring "Later";
  - tour step reset on remount;
  - the thin mark removed on dwell, on headway, and on day-type;
  - the null-figure guard removed;
  - the Routes toggle made unconditional.
- **Backend:** untouched.

## Review status

Standard tier: two `branch-reviewer` passes over the full diff at ab27baef.
- **Majors, fixed in 1de42b46:**
  - Hiding Samples removed the only thinness signal on dwell/running, headway and day-type. This led to the shared few-data rule.
  - The tour restarted at step 1 after a scope change. OverviewTab now owns the step.
- **Minors, fixed:**
  - stale `ask-tab.md` tour text;
  - the screenshot script would capture the tour;
  - weather Samples ignored the setting;
  - the Why toggle showed with nothing to change;
  - a hand-kept statistics list, now derived from the schemas, with the prop required;
  - storage read per snapshot, now cached;
  - comment and doc drift;
  - ja 分母 and the definitions' base;
  - test storage cleanup.
- **Re-review of the Major-owning group at 1de42b46:** all four Majors confirmed fixed, no new Major. Three Minors fixed in 14a82c7e:
  - one mark per count on headway;
  - no mark beside a missing figure;
  - toggles only where a table is drawn.

author: huamick
body:
Increment increment_7c40695b282c (arc arc_488f7ea6e8bf, ADR-1345 D1, D2): a contract can name **observability as proof**, and health reads such a contract from its newest live reading.

## What now works
- A contract's proof can be `{ by: "observability-as-proof", reason, freshness, watcher }`: the freshness is a whole number of hours or days (`36h`, `2d`), and the watcher is whatever records the readings. The schema refuses this proof without a freshness or watcher. It also refuses a freshness or watcher on any other proof (3.22).
- `HealthRecord.recordObserved(contract, "passing" | "failing", { machine, evidence })` records a live reading. It is written by the contract's watcher, and its note is `<evidence>, taken on <machine>`. The reading is kept in its own record (`health_<id>_observed`), next to the column that test runs write, so CI skipping a live-only test never overwrites it. A reading that turns red, or green again, is announced the same way a test verdict is (it tells the owner and releases waiting work). The writer refuses a contract that another proof proves, and an id that names no live contract (5.31).
- For such a contract, the verified state is its newest reading. It is passing while the reading is no older than the freshness. Once older, it reads not re-run with the old pass kept as `was`, so an old reading never counts as passing. It is failing when the reading saw a failure (5.31).
- A test run's pass or skip does not stand in for the reading. A test's fail still fails the contract. With no reading at all, the capability's reason is the new **no live reading**, which the map's panel shows as "observability as proof has no live reading of n of m contracts yet" (5.32, 4.12).
- `plan_contract` and `edit_plan` accept the new proof. `show_plan` says it in full: "proved by observability as proof, a live reading no older than 2 days recorded by <watcher>: <reason>" (9.42).

## How this sits with ADR-1320's "CI over local"
The live reading is its own check. It is not part of the gear's ordering. ADR-1320 D2 orders test runs only: the gear takes CI's newest test verdict over a local one, and the contract's `ci` copy still records what CI's tests saw. For a contract proved by observability, the verified state comes from the reading, ahead of every test run's pass or skip. The one exception is a failing test, which still shows through, so a red is never hidden.

## Reused shape
The reading follows the lag run's budget-contract verdicts: a verified entry by a named writer, with its evidence in the note (8.16). The freshness turns 8.19's two-day "not renewed, so not re-run" rule into a reading-time check, so a watcher that stops recording goes stale without having to mark itself. No self-hosted runner (ADR-1345 D4).

## Left for the arc's next increment
`recordObserved` is not on the Library facade yet. Adding it to `FROM_HEALTH` in `packages/library/src/api/library.ts` needs the Library API capability, which another session held during this work. This step is written on increment_8d3cffd02ca4 (the box's recorder) as its first job.

## Pieces without a test of their own
None named by the last review.

author: sephrael-lumbres
body:
## Summary

Adds a second mail transport that sends through Resend's HTTPS API,
for hosts that block outbound SMTP. `app.mail.transport` picks the
transport. SMTP stays the default and now points at Mailpit, so a
local run needs no mail settings.

## Changes

**Resend transport**
- `ResendMailTransport` posts each email to Resend's `/emails` endpoint
  with a Bearer key and a `User-Agent` (Resend refuses requests without
  one). It times out after 5 seconds to connect and 10 to answer, like
  the SMTP settings.
- A recipient list over Resend's limit of 50 goes out as several emails.
- A refused or failed call throws, and `EmailSender` logs it as a WARN,
  as it does for SMTP.

**Choosing the transport**
- `app.mail.transport=resend` creates the Resend transport. Otherwise
  `SmtpMailTransport` sends.
- With email on, the Resend transport refuses to start without
  `RESEND_API_KEY` and says so. With email off it starts without one.
- `ResendSettings` binds `app.mail.resend.*`. Its `toString()` leaves
  out the API key.

**Configuration**
- The Zoho SMTP host, port, credentials and TLS properties are replaced
  by `localhost:1025` (Mailpit). `MAIL_USERNAME` and `MAIL_PASSWORD` are
  no longer used, and the test profile drops its dummy values for them.

**Privacy policy**
- Names Resend as the email provider, keeping a copy of each email for
  up to 30 days.

## Verification

- Local (JDK 21): 297 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.
- CI on this branch: same result, green.
- `PrivacyPolicyPageTest`'s Resend check failed against the unfixed
  code first (red check).
- Local smoke test with an empty Postgres 18 container and Mailpit:
  - SMTP with no mail variables: the contact message reached Mailpit
    from `Issue Overflow <support@issueoverflow.app>`.
  - Resend pointed at a closed local port: the page said the message
    was sent, nothing reached Mailpit, and the WARN was logged once.
  - Resend with no key and email on: startup failed, naming
    `RESEND_API_KEY`.
  - Resend with no key and email off: the app started and logged that
    email is turned off.
  - No ERROR lines in the runs that started.

## Notes

- Not red-checked: `ResendMailTransportTest`,
  `MailTransportSelectionTest` and `ResendSettingsTest`, which use
  classes this branch adds.
- As with SMTP, all of a notification's recipients go in one `To` list
  (up to 50 per email), so members see each other's addresses, which
  the privacy policy already says members can see.
- The production profile that selects Resend comes with the deployment
  changes.

author: aniruthananth
body: This replaces "the top scorer who clears all five takes the pot" and "nobody clears all five, stakes go back" with the owner's new rule. ## The rule (`convex/lib/settlement.ts`) - Each week the pot is split evenly among the paid members tied for the **most slots cleared**, even when that is fewer than five. If everyone clears all five, everyone gets an equal share. Points no longer affect the split. - Unpaid members get no share. There is no refund case: if no paid member cleared a slot, the whole pot **rolls into next week**. It is recorded as a positive `rollover` ledger row, and the week that later shares it out writes the matching negative row. - League settlements take no fee now, because the rule splits the whole pot. A 1v1 versus keeps its own rule and fee. ## Escrow and cashout (`convex/whop.ts`) - When a week settles, each share is credited as a `winnings` ledger row. That row is the member's escrow balance, and no money moves on Whop at that point. - Cashout happens in the season's last week: every unsent share from the season's weeks goes out as one transfer per member. This also applies to "season" payout leagues and is safe to run again (`retryPayouts` still sends what Whop refused). A versus cashes out when it settles. - Schema: `ledger.kind` gains `"rollover"` (additive). `standings.pot` leaves rollover rows out of its payouts list. ## App - EscrowFlow's lower box reads "Split among top finishers" while the week is open. After settlement it reads "In escrow: $X each", or "Rolls into next week" when nobody won. The new open-week label repeats no figure that is already shown in the pot. - The projection (`lib/projection.ts`) forecasts the new rule: a member who doesn't finish counts with the slots they already have. ## Tests and docs - convex-test cases: everyone 5/5 splits evenly; when the top is four, the members with four split it; unpaid members are excluded; when nothing is cleared the pot rolls over and the next winner takes it; shares stay in escrow before the last week; cashout happens once at season end. Projection, leaderboards and escrow tests are updated to the new figures. docs/SCORING.md is rewritten. - Nothing was run against the deployment. YCCO-3 deploys.

## Summary
- **Ask deep**: answers a question about a selected passage from every tab plus the document's retained original source text (spec 08 §6.9). The extracted text is kept in a private local sidecar and is never rendered, synced or published (09 §4.4).
- **Ask deeper** (new): reads the same material, then uses the provider's web search (at most 3 searches), then the model's general knowledge. Anything from outside the document is marked, the badge is written by the app, and only pages the provider actually reported are listed, as plain text with no links (08 §6.10).
- "Deep ask" is renamed **Ask deep**. Ask, Ask deep and Ask deeper each show a small ⓘ and a tooltip on hover and focus. Shortcuts: Enter, Cmd+Enter, Cmd+Shift+Enter.
- **Android 0.5.0** (versionCode 4): Share a document as an `.html` file.

## Changes
- **LLM** (`src/main/llm`):

- **Library**: retained source text (`src/main/library/sources.ts`), with a merge union and sync privacy.
- **Docs**: spec 01, 02, 06–13, 16, `hooks.md`, the PRD, README (What's new v0.5.0, downloads), CLAUDE.md, `android/README.md` and the privacy page.
- **Version**: 0.5.0 in `package.json`, the lockfile, Android `versionName`/`versionCode` and `release-versions.test.ts`.
- **Fix**: `test/package/bundle.pkg.ts` expected the prompt paths from before the catalogue moved (`prompts/in-depth.md` → `prompts/default/…`).

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`: pass.
- `npm test`: 284 files, 4503 tests passing (1 skipped), after the final edits.
- `npm run check:spec`: 0 errors (denylist: 0 hits).
- `npm run check:hygiene -- --out out --package`: ok.
- `npm run test:e2e`:
  - 221 passed, 7 skipped.
  - 1 failure, `find.e2e.ts` ("switching the document tab re-runs the search"), which passed 6/6 on re-run. It's a flake that happened while a Gradle build was using the CPU.
- `npm run test:visual`:
  - 71 passed, 26 skipped.
  - 1 failure: `app.visual.ts` "sidebar: folder, Archive expanded, Trash count". The hover screenshot shows the row without its hover state, even though the `opacity: 1` hover assertion just before it passes. That points to the environment (likely the real mouse cursor over the Electron window). Nothing in this PR touches the sidebar or its baseline, and it passed in the implementation run. Worth a re-run on CI.
- `npm run test:package`: 14 passed, against the 0.5.0 DMG built with `scripts/build.sh`.
- Android `./gradlew lint testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleRelease`: pass (253 unit tests). `scripts/android-dist.sh`: signed with the release key, secret scan clean.
- **Real API**: one Ask deeper call against Claude (`claude-opus-5`): 2 web searches, 19 pages reported, 3 kept, outside information marked. It surfaced two bugs, both fixed here with regression tests: `<cite>` tags leaking into paragraphs, and a `general` badge that contradicted listed pages.

## Risk / rollout
- **Cost**: web search costs about $0.01 per search on top of tokens, at most 3 per Ask deeper.
- **Account setting**: web search must be enabled for the Claude org. If it isn't, the provider falls back to knowledge-only. The fallback matches a 400 whose message mentions web search; the exact wording is unverified.
- **OpenAI**: its web search path is verified offline only (SDK types).
- **Privacy**: search queries go to the provider's web search; see `docs/privacy`. Retained source text stays local.
- **Compatibility**: an older app reading a newer document drops `depth`, `reach` and `web` and shows a plain answer box (schema `.catch`), as the spec describes.

## Security scan
- No gitleaks or trufflehog installed. The repo's `check:hygiene` and `check:spec` denylist (from the private spec) both report 0 hits.
- Manual regex pass over all 190 outgoing files and the commit message, covering private keys, cloud and API tokens, JWTs, webhook URLs, `user:pass@` URLs, emails, private IPs, home paths and the internal terms from the local notes. The only hits were test placeholders (`example.com`/`example.org`, `/Users/someone/`, `user:pw@` inputs that test stripping) and the owner's public name in `package.json`. No real hits.

author: b-at-neu
body:
Closes #748

## Summary

- Adds `main/pipeline-state/`: a persisted per-repository store (`<userData>/pipeline-state.json`) of every ticket's stage, claim, gates, review-cycle count and history, and makes it the source of truth.
- One writer, `writeState`, replaces every pipeline `applyLabels` call. It checks the request's `expect.present`/`absent` against the **store**, commits the store (awaited atomic write), and only then mirrors the label diff through `applyLabels` with the label half of the precondition emptied. A failed mirror is `mirror-failed`; the store is never rolled back.
- Reads cut over at one seam: `reconcileRepository` takes the store's view and overrides `matchedKeys`, `stageHistory` and `reviewCycleCount`. Tick, repair, observation, dispatch and the renderer then read store state unchanged.
- The GitHub read fetches tracked items by number when the label sweep misses them, so a ticket with every label removed still exists for the app. Swept items the store does not track are dropped.
- A repository seeds from its labels the first time it loads (after the first projection, so no ticket changes stage). A missing, malformed or newer-version file loads empty and reseeds from labels.
- A terminal-owned repository bypasses the store (labels are its record) and reseeds once when the app takes it back.

## Changes

- `apps/desktop/src/main/pipeline-state/` (new): `model.ts` (pure), `store.ts` (only writer), `writer.ts`, `labels.ts`, `default.ts` (composition).
- `apps/desktop/src/types/pipeline-state.ts`, `types/writes.ts` (`state-unsaved`, `mirror-failed`, `stateMoved`, `WriteState`), `types/offload.ts`, `types/gate.ts` (`GateDeps` moved here), `types/dispatch.ts`.
- `main/github/{query,map,pipeline}.ts`: `buildTrackedItemsQuery`, tracked read, `closed` on the fetch.
- `main/state/{reconcile,watcher,read,sources}.ts` and `offload/engine.ts`: view, tracked refs, load wait, seeding, pruning.
- `main/actions/*`, `main/claim.ts`, `main/dispatch/*`, `main/ipc.ts`: `writeState` and the store-label reader in place of `applyLabels`; `actions/bound.ts` binds every action once; `actions/claim.ts` (a pass-through) is gone.
- `main/tick/plan.ts`: the cycle-cap gate reads `item.reviewCycleCount`.
- Renderer copy for the two new outcomes in `board`, `gate`, `decision`, `claim` and the audit model; `renderer/lib/mirror-reason.ts`.
- `scripts/checks/desktop-pipeline-state.ts` (new layer 1 rails), `desktop-actions.ts`/`desktop-gate.ts` repointed at `writeState`, `docs/ENGINEERING.md` module boundary.
- Tests for the model, store, writer, labels, tracked read, tracked query, reconcile view, watcher seeding, survivor test, plan cap and the new copy.

## Testing plan

- [ ] Adoption: with the app closed, delete `<userData>/pipeline-state.json`. Start the app on a repository with tickets at several stages. Every Board row shows the same phase as before, and the file now lists each one.
- [ ] Labels removed: on an app-owned repository, take a ticket at `plan review` and remove every pipeline label from it on GitHub. After the next poll it is still at Plan review on the Board. Approving the plan moves it to Plan approved and dispatches implementation.
- [ ] Labels added by hand: add `ready` on GitHub to a ticket the store does not track. Nothing dispatches, and it does not appear on the Board until Work on.
- [ ] Restart: quit while a ticket is Implementing, then relaunch. It resumes at Implementing (interrupted session offered as before), not at whatever its labels say.
- [ ] Corrupt file: write `{` into `pipeline-state.json` and start. The app starts, and the stage of every ticket comes back from its labels.
- [ ] Mirror failure: revoke `gh` write scope (or go offline after a read) and approve a plan. The Board shows the "moved … label couldn't be updated" row, and the ticket proceeds on the store's stage.
- [ ] Terminal-owned: hand a repository to the terminal cockpit. Its Board still follows the labels, and after taking it back the store reseeds without a stage change.
- [ ] Unsaved state: make `pipeline-state.json` unwritable and approve a plan. The Board shows "port couldn't save its pipeline state … Try again", and nothing changed on GitHub.
- [ ] Capture the states the harness cannot show: the Board Needs you row, the Approve plan / Unblock / Work on result lines for `state-unsaved` and `mirror-failed`.

## Screenshots

**Settings audit log with Not saved and Label not updated rows — light**

![Settings audit log with Not saved and Label not updated rows — light](https://github.com/b-at-neu/port/blob/b7bd88d2d9b310fbd7548701c9372a2ad416d7ca/issue-748/04a55be/settings-audit-light.png?raw=true)

**Settings audit log with Not saved and Label not updated rows — dark**

![Settings audit log with Not saved and Label not updated rows — dark](https://github.com/b-at-neu/port/blob/b7bd88d2d9b310fbd7548701c9372a2ad416d7ca/issue-748/04a55be/settings-audit-dark.png?raw=true)

The Board row, gate, decision and Work on result lines are transient outcomes the fixture harness has no scenario for; they are covered by unit tests and listed as manual steps above.

## Automated checks

- `node scripts/checks.ts` — 4302 checks passed.
- `pnpm --filter desktop typecheck` and `pnpm --filter desktop lint` — clean.
- `pnpm --filter desktop test` — passes, apart from two failures unrelated to this change: `sessions/adapter.test.ts` "live" reads this machine's real Claude transcripts, and `watcher.test.ts` "an unforced due read during a hung read still skips" does not inject a conditional transport, so its pre-check reaches the network from this sandbox. Neither touches code changed here.

## Notes

- **Review-cycle count**: the store keeps a high-water mark and the cap reads `max(store, GitHub reviews)`. That can only hold earlier than today, never later. Reviewers: say if the cap should stay on GitHub reviews alone.
- **Tracked read**: an alias GitHub reports `NOT_FOUND` is treated as closed (the item is gone), so a deleted or transferred ticket is pruned. Any other alias error fails the whole read, the same rule as the detail read.
- **Placement**: `applyLabels` is injected into the writer from `default.ts`, so `writer.ts` is the only caller and `default.ts` the only importer; the layer 1 rails say so. The store file's path is named only in `default.ts`.
- **Labels drift until #751**: the mirror write is the transition's own add/remove diff, so a hand-removed label is not restored until #751 writes full state. #750 renames the vocabulary, #753 adds the doc set and may supersede check (c).
- Store `actor` on a history row is `null` for app-made transitions; the audit log carries who acted.

body:
Verified organizers can publish and correct an event's structured programme, with up to 30 sessions, dates, local start/end times, descriptions and a named time zone. Readers get a semantic ordered text programme in the existing event card. The native form supports adding/removing sessions, restores saved fields for editing, requests publication consent again and preserves keyboard focus after saving.

The additive 0019 migration preserves existing events with empty programmes. Programme data is validated and written atomically with the event, under the existing current-claim/verified-owner publication boundary. Invalid dates/times/zones or out-of-range sessions fail without mutation. Older clients cannot erase nonempty programmes by omitting the fields.

Validation: SQLite publication/edit/withdrawal, ownership and malformed-data tests; real disposable Worker/D1 lifecycle with the new migration; historical upgrade; three-language markup and save/focus regression. Chrome keyboard QA on a local in-memory UI fixture verified add/remove, restored values, readable programme and focus on the saved message. This browser fixture is separate from the real Worker/D1 integration and is not physical NVDA acceptance. Full combined main-based checks are running. No production deployment.

body:
## What

Every visitor was downloading all four hero videos in the background: the desktop and the phone video, each as `.webm` and `.mp4`, about 18 MB. Nuxt adds a `<link rel="prefetch">` for every file the entry bundle refers to, videos included. A visitor plays one of the four at most.

The dev-server suite: the hints only exist in a built page.

author: szaher
body:
Real-memory measurement for the delta tiles merged in #23 (you asked for measured evidence before any performance claims).

`evidence/p1.1-delta-tiles/measure_delta_tiles.py` runs a real `weightlab start` on the pinned Qwen2.5 base/Instruct pairs. Results are in `results/delta_tiles_darwin.json` and summarized in the README.

| Pair | Tensor (BF16) | Bytes read (A+B) | Build | Peak server RSS | Exact tile vs NumPy |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 0.5B | embed_tokens 151936×896 | 519 MiB | 1.41 s | 104.8 MiB | max rel. 5.0e-8 |
| 0.5B | layers.0 down_proj | 16.6 MiB | 0.12 s | 100.3 MiB | 5.9e-8 |
| Math-1.5B | embed_tokens 151936×1536 | 890 MiB | 2.40 s | 100.9 MiB | 5.0e-8 |
| Math-1.5B | layers.0 down_proj | 52.5 MiB | 0.23 s | 98.5 MiB | 5.9e-8 |

Idle server RSS was 62 MiB. Direct L3 tiles took 53–88 ms.

**Limits:**
- The page cache was warm (the files are hashed first), so the wall times are not disk throughput.
- Only the server process's RSS is counted, sampled every 50 ms.
- One 36 GiB machine. **The 8 GiB laptop target remains unverified**, as do 7B+ and multi-shard pairs and the row-sampled path above `pyramid_exact_max_mib`.

The CHANGELOG links the evidence, and the blueprint and manifest were regenerated. No code changes.

body:
## 概要

gstack の setup は、フックを `$HOME` の絶対パス（ユーザー名を含む）で `claude/settings.json` に登録する。`~/` に直した項目も、次の setup（`prune-stale --repoint`）で絶対パスに書き戻す。アップグレードのたびに `~/` へ戻す仕組みと、gstack・プラグイン・crit の CLI をまとめて更新するタスクを足す。

## 変更

- `claude/scripts/settings-home-paths.py`: `~/.claude/settings.json` のリンク先で、`"command": "<HOME>/` を `"command": "~/` に書き換える。リンクは残し、変更がなければ書かない。
- `claude/scripts/update-skills.sh`（端末では `mise run claude:update` でも実行できる）: gstack-upgrade → 書き換え → マーケットプレイスと user スコープのプラグインの更新 → `brew upgrade crit` → cc-crit の profile テスト、の順に実行する。途中で失敗しても続け、最後に失敗した手順と `/sync-skill-docs` の案内を出す。
  - Claude Code からは `! /bin/bash ~/dotfiles/claude/scripts/update-skills.sh` で実行する。mise はリポジトリのルートの設定ファイルを自動で信頼して読み込み、ルートには sandbox から書けるため。
  - ホームに移ってから各コマンドを実行し、Python には `-I` を付ける。
  - `claude plugin update` に `-y` は付けない。
- `claude/setup.sh` と zsh の `gstack-upgrade` 関数でも、gstack の setup の後に書き換える。
- CI: 新しいテスト 2 つを、macOS のジョブ（本番と同じ `/bin/bash` 3.2）で実行する。
- 文書: claude/README.md、SKILL_INVENTORY.md、CLAUDE.md、`/sync-skill-docs`、zsh/README.md、作業計画。

## 検証

- `test-settings-home-paths.py`（5 件）、`test-update-skills.py`（7 件）、`check-repo.py`、`test-check-repo.py`、shellcheck、actionlint、`mise run claude:skills-check`、`zsh -n`: すべて成功。
- 実機: `! /bin/bash ~/dotfiles/claude/scripts/update-skills.sh` はすべての手順が成功した（どれもすでに最新で、書き換えは 0 件）。`/sync-skill-docs` は変化なし。
- `/review`（スペシャリスト 5、adversarial、Red Team）: CRITICAL 2 件（`python3 -c` がカレントディレクトリから import する、`! mise run` の入口がルートの設定ファイルを読む）を直した。
- Codex レビュー: 指摘なし。Crit: 承認。

## 未対応・後続

- mise を通すほかのタスク（`crit:profile-test`、`claude:skills-snapshot` など）にも、ルートの設定ファイルを読む同じ経路がある。範囲が広いので、別の作業にする。
- 書き換えが起きるとき（gstack のフックを残したとき）に、セッション中でも `~/.claude/settings.json` のリンクが残るかは、実機ではまだ確かめていない。
- `/gstack-upgrade`（スキル）で更新したときは、自動では書き換えない。

author: vitorpamplona
body:
## Summary

Step 3 of the composer design review: a composer is a task, not a place. It opens over the screen that launched it, and closing it takes you back there. It doesn't create a tab, a window or a history entry unless you ask for one.

**Where a composer opens**

- **Desktop windows** (a wide window with a mouse: `composersOpenAsDialogs()` = rail tier or wider **and** `AppPlatform.hasFinePointer`): a dialog over the screen that opened it, drawn by the navigation host in a new `ComposerDialog`.
  - Esc closes it.
  - A click outside does nothing, so a stray click never throws a draft away.
  - The emoji panel docks inside the dialog.
  - The tools sit in its bottom strip.
  - The reading-column width cap doesn't apply inside it.
- **Every touch screen** (phones, landscape phones, tablets): full screen, as before, through the same path as before.
  - The rail tier also covers a phone turned sideways, where a centered card would leave about 400 dp of height before the keyboard opens.
  - On a tablet, the on-screen keyboard covers the bottom of a centered card. The screen around it adds nothing, because the dialog blocks it.
  - `hasFinePointer` is true only on the desktop today, so Android behaves as it did before this PR. A Chromebook or DeX could get the dialog later, once Android reports an attached mouse there.
- **Tabs layout:** a composer is never a tab. It opens over the tab it was opened from (`TabsModel.overlays`) and shows while that tab is the active one (`overlaysOver`).
  - Back and Ctrl+W close the active tab's composer first, then the tab.
  - A link clicked inside a composer opens its tab in the background, so the composer stays in front.
  - When something outside activates another tab (a notification, a deep link), that tab covers the composer. The composer is still open, draft and all, and shows again when its tab is back.
  - When the composer's flow continues to its result (a created group or channel, `Kind.Replace`), the result opens as a tab beside the tab it was opened from.
  - Asking for a section or a drawer screen (`Kind.Section`, `Kind.Drawer`) from a composer closes it.
  - Ctrl+Shift+T reopens a closed composer, or shows the one already open for that route instead of opening a second copy.
- **Stack layout:** a composer is pushed as before. In a desktop window the host draws it as a dialog over the screen below it.
- **Windows layout:** unchanged. Composers keep opening as windows of their own.

**Resizing the dialog**

- Handles sit in a thin ring just outside the card, inside its margin, so they never cover anything the composer draws:
  - the left and right sides, the bottom, and the bottom-right corner;
  - the corner's grip is drawn outside the card's rounded curve.
  - The card grows evenly around its center, so the edge stays under the pointer.
  - It is kept between a 360×320 dp minimum and the window.
  - Desktop shows resize cursors.
- Each size class (Quick, Form, Document) keeps the size it was left at, so every New Post opens at the size the last one had. A double click on the corner grip goes back to the default.
- Where it's kept, through a new `AppPlatform.composerDialogSizes` port (`ComposerDialogSizes`):
  - the desktop saves it in `composer-dialog-sizes.properties`;
  - `DesktopComposerDialogSizes` is a thin adapter over `ScreenWindowSizes`, which gained `saved`, `forget` and `preload`;
  - the file is read off the UI thread at startup;
  - other platforms keep the size for as long as the app runs.

**Pop out**

- A button in the composer's top bar (`ActionTopBar`) moves it into a window of its own, from the Stack or the Tabs layout.
- It shows only where the platform has windows (`NavigationLayoutType.WINDOWS` in `navigationLayouts`, so the desktop) and only inside the dialog.
- The window opens at the existing composer default of 520×680 (`ScreenWindowSizes`).
- The draft goes with it. The main host keeps the screens of these windows in its retained list, and each window draws the host's own decorated entry (`Nav.hostedEntries`) instead of building a fresh one.
  - So a tab moved out to a window now keeps its ViewModels and scroll position too. Before, it started over.
  - The Windows layout's own windows are unchanged.
- In a popped-out composer, the next step of its flow stays in its window.
- Window › Move to tab on a popped-out composer puts it back over the active tab, never into the strip.

**Switching layouts keeps windows open**

- `NavBackStacks.changeArrangement` now hands the old layout's screen windows to the new one (`NavModel.adoptWindows`). That covers a popped-out composer (draft included), a tab moved out to a window, and a screen of the Windows layout.
- Before, a switch closed them. Leaving the Tabs layout already dropped moved-out tabs before this PR; that is fixed here too.

**Registration**

- `composer<Route>(size)` / `composerArgs<Route>(size)` sit beside `composableFromBottom`, so a composer is still a route: drafts, share intents, deep links and saved state keep working.
- The model learns which routes are composers from the destinations (`NavBackStacks.opensOver`).
- All 46 composers are registered:

| Size | Default dialog | Composers |
|---|---|---|
| Quick | 600 dp wide, up to 85% of the window (max 720 dp) tall | note, comment, hashtag, geo and URL posts, voice reply, poll, highlight, public message, private message, find log, forum topic |
| Form | 820 dp wide, up to 85% tall | product, calendar event and calendar, Marmot and Cordn groups, geocache and hunt, award badge, profile, goal, community, git repository, podcast show/episode/trailer, music track/playlist, Concord channel, chats, workout, list and pack settings |
| Document | 1100 dp wide, up to 92% tall | article |

- Full screen, each keeps the motion it had: from the bottom, or from the side for the ones that already slid in from the end.

**Other changes**

- `NewMediaView` (pictures and videos) and `NewBadgeDialog` aren't routes. They now wrap themselves in the same `ComposerDialog`, as Quick and Form.
  - On the desktop they used to cover the whole window.
  - On touch screens they stay full screen.
- Composers left open, and popped-out composers, are restored on restart.
- A composer open over a tab doesn't make tab switches animate.

New string: `composer_pop_out` ("Open in a separate window").

## Test plan

- [x] Ran `./gradlew spotlessApply`: the repo is formatted
- [x] The git pre-push hook passed with `PREPUSH_KMP_METADATA=1` on every push: tests, the KMP metadata compiles and `:amethyst:lintPlayDebug`
- [x] Compiled `:desktopApp` and ran it
- [x] `NavComposerTest`: 18 model tests, covering:
  - the Tabs overlay, back, reopen and dedup, and reopening while one is open
  - a link from a composer, the next step of its flow, and a section asked for from it
  - a tab activated from elsewhere covering the composer until its tab is back
  - Pop out from Tabs and from Stack, a popped-out composer's flow, and moving a popped-out composer back
  - a composer asked for from a moved-out tab
  - layout switches that keep the composer and a popped-out composer's window, and restart
- [x] `DesktopComposerDialogSizesTest`: 3 tests (a picked size survives a restart per size class, a reset forgets it, a damaged entry reads as the default)
- [ ] Manually exercised the change: **desktop only, not yet on an Android device**

Notes (Desktop: Linux under Xvfb, 1600×1000 screen, read-only login):

author: camshaft
body:
## Problem

DC-0005-010 (`dc/s2n-quic-dc/spec/rfcs/0005-endpoint/02-receive.toml`, line 37) says: "A receiver MUST NOT dispatch the frames of a packet whose packet number it has already accepted from the same sender, or whose packet number is too old for it to tell."

The tests that #796 adds in `dispatch/packet_number_tests.rs` cover an accepted packet number at the window's right edge and one past its left edge. They don't cover an accepted number inside the window that isn't the newest, the case where `SlidingWindow::check` finds the number's bit set below the right edge, which `Cache::may_accept_packet_number` relies on.

## Change

Adds `a_new_message_under_an_accepted_packet_number_below_the_newest_doesnt_reach_the_stream` to `dc/s2n-quic-dc/src/endpoint/dispatch/packet_number_tests.rs`, citing DC-0005-010 with `type=test` as the other three tests do: packet 0 carries message 0 and packet 1 carries message 1; a second packet 0 that carries message 2 is refused with `Error::Duplicate` and the stream doesn't receive message 2; packet 2 then carries message 2 to the stream. No other file changes.

## Stacking

This branch is stacked on #796 (head 212d9d65df7f58c90027e794c8932ecbf9e66e2a), whose `dispatch.rs`, `recv.rs` and `recv/dedup.rs` changes the test depends on. Until #796 merges, this pull request's diff holds #796's commits too; this pull request's own change is commit af17386be8fedf52f601e06ad4585da18f0fa739 over 212d9d65df7f58c90027e794c8932ecbf9e66e2a. Merge it after #796.

## Testing done

This pull request's CI builds and runs the test.

author: michaelcrosato
body:
A builder's game (an open-world RPG made by another model on v0.100.0) crashed with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in `Shell.back` when the Back button of its co-op setup screen ("Connect the players") was pressed. The engine was at fault: its own audio-offset calibration screen crashes the same way.

## The crash: a screen's own `back` that calls `shell.back()`
- The game's screen had `back: () => { setupMode = null; shell.back(); }`, and its Back button called `shell.back()` too.
- `shell.back()` hands cancel to the open screen's own `back` and returns without closing it. So `shell.back()` called the screen's `back`, which called `shell.back()`, and so on until the stack overflowed. A screen with its own `back` had no public way to close itself except `hide()`, which closes every screen.
- The engine's own audio-offset calibration used the same pattern: `close = () => { K.stop(); this.back(); }` was its `back`. Cancel or Escape on it overflowed the stack in any game that offers it.
- **Fixed:** while a screen's own `back` runs (a flag on its stack entry), `shell.back()` closes that screen. A `back` that asks first still keeps its screen. One that closes two screens still sends the second through the lower screen's own `back`. A `back` that throws leaves the flag reset.

## The focus: a screen shown again
- `shell.show(name)` on the open screen made a new stack entry. `_render` only keeps the focus when it redraws the same entry, so the focus went to the first button. The builder's setup screen is shown again each time a player gets ready or a controller connects, so a controller player's focus jumped to "Player 1: Change ready state" after every press.
- **Fixed:** when a screen is shown again it is updated in place (the same entry, its spec merged as before), and the focus stays. The entry also keeps its `back` flag, so a `back` that updates its own screen and then closes it works too.

## Checks
- In the builder's own page (headless Chromium), the original reproduces the reported stack trace line for line. With only these two functions replaced, Back and Escape return to Play Together, the focus stays on Back when the screen updates, and no errors are thrown.
- New checks:
  - contract-test: cancelling a screen whose own `back` calls `shell.back()`, including after it updates itself; the audio-offset calibration; a `back` that closes two screens; a `back` that asks first.
  - standard-test, in Chromium: Escape on such a screen; the focus kept when a screen updates.
  - On the engine before the fix, 3 contract checks fail (stack overflow) and 2 standard checks fail (stack overflow, and the focus on the first button).
- `npm run test:changed`. An engine change runs all 30 suites:
  - at `1f90675` (on v0.103.0): all passed, 63 min 48 s;
  - at `0a9c86a` (merged with v0.104.0): all passed, 63 min 27 s;
  - at `c1fd359` (merged with v0.104.3, as v0.104.4): all passed, 64 min 25 s.
- The head, `313847b`, merges main at v0.106.0 (#230 to #232: Mode 7 and the mga module; in the engine core they change only its version line) as v0.106.1. Re-checked there: version, syntax, doctrine, API docs, contract (741 checks) and standard (127 checks) all pass, and a rebuild changes nothing. The full `npm test` runs on main after the merge, per CLAUDE.md.
- Budgets: KART is at 216,491 of its 218,000 (D94, soft since D98). No decision was needed.

body:
T159: the stream's rendering and switching, from T103's SP-6 findings, profiled on the runner first (`docs/tasks/T159-stream-render/profile.md`).

- **A, a long streaming block in pieces**: each update reparsed and relaid the whole growing message (0.25 ms/KB; 634 ms per update at 1.15 M characters). While a message streams, streamdown gets our `parseMarkdownIntoBlocksFn`: blocks over 16 KB split at spaces, code blocks by lines with their fences, and only the tail after the settled pieces is split again. Once the item completes, streamdown's own split renders it whole, the DOM equal to an unsplit render.
- **B, an event's known member by its type**: `zEvent`'s and `zEventBody`'s known members become a `z.discriminatedUnion` on `type` with `zUnknownEvent` still the fallback, generated by `tools/gen-protocol-ts`; every fixture parses the same under the old and the new union (known, degraded, unknown, invalid). Zod took about 59 ms per switch to a session out of the LRU.
- Spike diagnostics for T103's scenarios: Chromium traces through the window's DevTools session (`SP6_TRACE=1`) and an unminified renderer (`SP6_UNMINIFIED=1`), off by default.

author: rachelsprague
body:
Two CLAUDE.md rules to cut down on commands that get refused in agent sessions.

A review of past sessions since Nov 12 found about 270 refused commands in this repo, with no one asking for them:

- **Worktree guard (about 180):** Claude Code refuses commands in a worktree session that it can't verify stay inside the worktree: `cd ..` before git, `git -C` into another worktree, appending to files with `cat >> file <<EOF`, subshells and chained commands.
- **Auto-mode classifier (about 15):** chained `git add ... && git commit -F - <<EOF` gets blocked.
- **Push hook (about 65):** the hook reads command text, so it refuses harmless greps and reads of its own source that mention push, `--no-verify`, `hooksPath` or `$'...'` quoting.

Changes, both in CLAUDE.md:

- Landing work: while in a worktree, run each git command on its own from the worktree root (no `cd`, no `git -C` into another checkout, no chains or subshells around git), write files with Write/Edit, and commit with `git commit -F <file>`. The `/pre-push` command that records the review is the one exception, and `git -C` from the main checkout (as `/pick` does) is still fine.
- Public repo: says exactly which harmless commands the push hook refuses, and to read the hook, its tests and `.githooks/` with Read/Grep, not Bash.

Docs only; no code or tests change.

author: pundarikakshntripathi
body:
`X86TTIImpl::getArithmeticInstrCost` aborts when it is asked about a scalable vector type:

- `mul` hits the vXi8 multiply special case, which compares `Ty->getPrimitiveSizeInBits()` with 64 and so converts a scalable `TypeSize` to an integer.
- `udiv`/`sdiv`/`urem`/`srem` reach the division throughput path, which calls `getVectorNumElements()` on a scalable MVT.

This can be hit from VectorCombine (`foldExtractExtract`) and from `print<cost-model>`.

X86 has no scalable vectors, so return an invalid cost for them at the top of the function, as `getVectorInstrCost` already does since #177705.

For the opcodes that didn't crash, the throughput cost was already invalid. Their code-size, latency and size-latency costs used to come from the generic fallback (e.g. 1 for `add`) and are now invalid too. The test uses `-cost-kind=all` so that is covered.

With the crash gone, the reproducer from the issue now gets through VectorCombine and is folded to `extractelement (mul %v, %v), 0`, i.e. lane 0 times lane 0 instead of lane 0 times lane 1. That is a separate, existing problem in `foldExtractExtract` with scalable vectors (current main does the same for `add`) and is not addressed here.

Fixes #241495

valdes-tresanco-ms
body:
Second round of the vHPC fault list (Slurm + Son of Grid Engine labs).

## What a campaign does now
| Fault | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Job held in the queue (`scontrol hold` / `qhold`) | "waiting in the queue" | "held in the queue, waiting to be released or canceled: JobHeldUser" |
| Grid Engine job in error (Eqw) | alive forever | "in error in the queue, waiting for its error to be cleared (qmod -cj) or for a cancel" |
| Node fails mid-run | untested | NODE_FAIL, queued again, resumed from the journal |
| Out of memory / time (OOM, TIMEOUT, SGE `failed 37`) | "left the queue" | end state + a hint to ask for more |
| `qdel` by hand on Son of Grid Engine | taken for a killed runner, sent again | canceled (`#$ -notify` + USR2 trap leave a `deleted` mark) |
| Full disk, before or mid-run | untested | clear ENOSPC error; once freed, the campaign completes and nothing failed for good |
| File system without locks (Lustre without flock, some NFS) | runner exited 0 doing nothing | clear error naming the file system |

Also: qacct is read whole before deciding (a Grid Engine with `deleted_by` prints `failed` first).

## Tests
- Unit suite green; new unit tests for the wait reasons, end states, `_alive_why` out of the queue, the lock-less journal.
- Lab: Slurm 27/27, SGE 20 passed + 7 Slurm-only skipped. New: held job, node down (Slurm), full disk before/mid-run, SGE hand qdel (no longer skipped).

Not covered: SQLite WAL on NFS (single writer, the runner), an Eqw on a real Grid Engine.

author: robmcdonald5
body:
## Why

One posting is listed many times: per location, per board, reposted. Each copy is its own row, and each row was embedded on its own, paying for the same text again. The active pool is about to be embedded in full and then kept current, so identical text should be paid for once.

## What changes

`embedNextPage` is the page body behind the backfill CLI, the inline embed in the Node ingest, and the drain. It now pays for a text once:

1. A job whose title and description match a stored job holding a vector of the embedder's model takes a copy of that vector and that row's tag. The copy is one server-side `UPDATE`; no vector crosses the wire. A page that is all copies makes no provider call.
2. The rest go to the provider with each distinct text once, and the vector is written to every job on the page with that text.

The page result now counts `embedded` (one per distinct text sent) and `reused` apart, and the backfill CLI prints both.

## The content signature is the lookup, not the key

`content_signature` is an md5 over the lowercased, whitespace-collapsed title + description. The vector is computed over the raw text. So two rows with one signature can differ in letter case, in the amount or kind of whitespace, and in where the title ends and the description starts. They cannot differ in any other character.

Copying on the signature alone would give some jobs a vector computed for slightly different text. The copy therefore finds candidates through the signature index and accepts one only when title and description are equal, which is exactly equal embedding text.

What exactness costs, on a 1-in-16 sample of whole signature groups (3,676 backlog jobs):

| key | provider inputs |
|---|---|
| signature | 3,436 |
| equal title + description | 3,448 |

That is 12 more inputs (0.3% of the jobs). 11 signatures held more than one text; in every one the descriptions had the same length, so the differences sit in the title or in same-length whitespace.

A blank-description job has no signature, so it never finds a stored source (35 such jobs in the backlog). It still shares within a page.

## Expected saving on today's backlog

Read-only production counts, 2026-11-16:

- 69,732 active jobs, 60,588 of them with no vector. 42,701 rows hold a voyage-4-large vector; none holds another model's.
- 1,455 backlog jobs share a signature with a stored vector, and 3,752 more share one with another backlog job. By signature that is 5,207 jobs (8.6%) needing no provider input.
- Requiring equal text keeps about 95% of that (228 of 240 in the sample): roughly 4,900 to 5,000 jobs, about 8% fewer embed inputs.
- The largest group is 75 jobs.

The saving is modest because today's pool is mostly one-off postings. No paid call was made for this PR.

## Cost of the lookup

One extra statement per page and no migration. The production plan does one `jobs_content_signature_idx` scan per job, stopping at the first match:

- the 64 newest backlog jobs: 76 ms in total, on cold pages;
- 64 jobs from the largest group: 0.028 ms per lookup.

## Worth scrutinising

- **How the page learns the model.** It calls the embedder with no texts and reads `model` from the result. The real `embed` returns at once for an empty input (an existing test pins that). An injected embedder that doesn't would make a request, or fail, on every page; the `EmbedFn` doc now states the requirement.
- **Another model's vectors are never copied.** After a model swap, jobs are embedded on the new model.
- **A job that changes mid-page.** The copy carries the same content-hash guard as the write, and Postgres re-checks it on the locked row. A job whose text changed after the page was read stays NULL and is picked up with its new text.
- **Counts.** Rows written per page are `embedded + reused`. The ingest's `embedded` counter keeps meaning "postings given a vector", so it adds the two. The Inngest drain reads `embedded` only and is left untouched: it is paused and being removed.

Embedding is off in production, so nothing runs differently until it is switched on.

## Tests

PGlite integration tests cover: five jobs with one text cost one provider input and end with the same vector and tag, on one page and across pages; a closed job is a valid source; another model's vector is not reused; a case or spacing variant with the same signature is embedded, not copied; a job whose text changes before the copy, or while the page is embedding, is not given a stale vector.

body:
- **Install size.** Removed generated output from `skills/hyperfigure/examples/` (the printable PDFs, the `-light.html` builds and the verify/stress builds): Hyperfigure goes from 27 MB to 6.5 MB, about 20 MB off the plugin. They are rebuilt from the sources that stay, with the scripts the skill documents; NOTICE.md records the removal.
- **Third-party skill text.** `scripts/audit_packs.py` scans every pack and bundled skill for places that deserve a person's eye (network calls, running programs, building code from text, installs, credential or home-folder reads, writing outside the project, hidden text) and writes `docs/pack-audit.md`. It is a pattern scan, not a review, and says so; nothing is executed, symlinks are not followed. 5 tests.
- **LibreOffice route of hs-convert.** It failed in the first build sandbox; on a later machine it works, so real conversions are now tests (html to pdf, csv to xlsx, txt to docx and pdf, pdf to png). The pandoc route stays untested (not installed here).
- **Windows and macOS.** The repository's GitHub Actions workflow has never run: every run of it since the repo began (including Dependabot's and before my changes) fails within about 3 seconds with no log, so hosted CI cannot be used to test other systems until that is fixed on the account side (the draft PR #43 is closed for that reason; its matrix job is kept in `ci.yml` for when Actions works). In the meantime: `hs_run` no longer assumes `killpg` and `start_new_session`, the hook commands find `python` as well as `python3`, and a new test checks that every POSIX-only call in the scripts is guarded and that core files open text as UTF-8. This is static, not a run on a real Windows or macOS machine, and the README and site now say exactly that.

body:
Stacked on #170, then #169 and #168. Final step of the Tasks hub plan in `docs/plans/tasks-hub.md`.

## Summary
Copy and labels only. No behaviour, data or route changes.

- **Rename:** the dashboard preset grid, titled "Tasks" until now (which clashed with the new Tasks page), is now **Quick log**. Its description reads "Log extra work in one tap. Complete listed tasks from To do." Logging from the grid doesn't count towards a listed task, so the copy steers people to To do.
- **Drawer and toasts:**
  - "Create new chore" becomes "Add to quick log", and the list headings and the "Manage quick log" control use quick-log wording.
  - Toasts become "Added to quick log", "Deleted from quick log" and so on.

- **Server error copy** in quick-log flows: "Preset not found" becomes "Quick log task not found", plus the reorder-validation messages. Un-sharing a task that's on the list now says "Cannot make this task personal while it is on the household task list".

  - "Tasks require a shared preset" and "Preset not found" in task-management errors.

author: noahstotland
body:
Closes #79

NH-79: [Mail voice commands](https://github.com/noahstotland/nohands/issues/79). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-15-nh-79-mail-commands-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-15-nh-79-mail-commands.md`.

## Summary
- New Mail pack (`com.apple.mail`) on the NH-76 mechanism: new message, reply, reply all, forward, send message, undo send, next/previous message, get new mail, mark read/unread, flag, archive, junk, delete message, show/hide mailboxes, inbox, sent, search mail, attach a file, close message.
- `send` takes two words or more ("send message", "send email"); bare "send" is not a phrase. Bare `delete`, `up`, `down`, `undo`, `find` keep their global meaning in Mail.
- Rows added to the per-app table in `docs/voice-commands.md` (the ticket says README; the table moved there in NH-119).

## Proof
- **Core table test, Mail in front and another app in front**: `MailPackTests.swift`.

  ```
  $ swift test --no-parallel
  ✔ Test run with 588 tests passed after 16.650 seconds.
  ```

  (A parallel run on a loaded machine, load average 34, flaked three timing tests in `TaskRunnerTests`; they pass alone and in the serial run.)
- **A submenu path never falls back to agent-desktop** (`menuItemFindsLastSegmentThenClicksAndRefusesDisabled` has the case), so "go to sent" cannot press "Use This Mailbox For > Sent".
- **Phrases resolve in Mail only**:

  ```
  $ nohands-cli parse "send message" --app com.apple.mail
  [pressKey(⇧⌘D)]
  $ nohands-cli parse "send" --app com.apple.mail
  no match -> LLM
  $ nohands-cli parse "reply all" --app com.apple.Safari
  no match -> LLM
  ```

Not proven:
- Manual check in Mail on macOS 14 (each phrase does what it says): needs Mail, a mailbox and a microphone, not run. The chords come from Apple's documented Mail shortcuts; Mail's menu file confirmed the titles but not the key equivalents.
- `go to sent` resolves `Mailbox > Go to Favorite Mailbox > Sent` by menu title; where Mail puts that item is built at runtime and was not checked live.

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)

## Release note
In Mail you can now say "new message", "reply", "reply all", "forward", "send message", "archive", "delete message", "next message" and more. "Send" needs two words so a stray word cannot send a draft; "undo send" takes it back during Mail's undo delay.

author: kimyounggwang
body:
## 문제
README대로 빈 DB에 `prisma migrate deploy`를 하면 스키마와 다른 DB가 만들어진다.
- **`ConversionEvent` 표**와 **`Post` 컬럼 6개**(`postCategory`, `algorithmicScore`, `algorithmicPass`, `algorithmicDimensions`, `algorithmicFixes`, `rewriteCount`)를 만드는 마이그레이션이 없다. 그래서 `Post`를 읽는 모든 쿼리가 P2022로 깨진다(발행 크론부터).
- 옛 마이그레이션이 만든 **표 6개**는 스키마에 모델이 없다. 그래서 다음 `migrate dev`가 DROP TABLE을 자동으로 만든다.
- `threadPartIds`의 NULL 허용 여부와 인덱스 이름이 스키마와 다르다.

원인:
- 스키마만 바꾸고 마이그레이션을 안 만든 커밋(32980d9)
- 스키마와 다른 손작성 마이그레이션(1730aea)
- 이를 잡을 장치가 없었다

운영 DB는 마이그레이션 밖(`db push` 등)에서 맞춰졌을 가능성이 높다(추측). 운영에는 접속하지 않았다.

## 변경
- `20261116000000_archive_orphan_tables`
  - 고아 표 6개를 지우지 않고 `archive` 스키마로 **옮긴다**.
  - 데이터는 그대로 남고, Prisma는 `public`만 보므로 데이터 유무와 상관없이 결과가 같다.
  - `Brand`로 가는 FK 3개(`ON DELETE CASCADE`)는 끊는다. 브랜드를 지울 때 보관 데이터가 같이 지워지지 않게 하려는 것이다.
- `20261116000100_reconcile_schema_drift`
  - `ConversionEvent` 표·인덱스·FK, `Post` 컬럼 6개, `threadPartIds` NULL→`'[]'` 백필 후 NOT NULL, 인덱스 정리.
  - 모든 문장이 "이미 있으면 건너뜀"이라 운영에서는 대부분 아무 일도 안 한다.
  - `Post` 변경은 맨 끝에 둬서 배타 락을 잡는 시간을 줄였다.
  - `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'`와 `statement_timeout = '60s'`를 걸었다. 크론과 겹치면 기다리지 않고 통째로 되돌린 뒤 실패한다.
- **재발 방지:** `.github/workflows/prisma-drift.yml`
  - `prisma/**`가 바뀐 PR마다 Postgres 서비스 컨테이너에 마이그레이션을 다시 쌓고, 결과를 스키마와 비교한다(`migrate diff --from-migrations … --exit-code`).
  - 운영 DB에는 붙지 않는다.
- `README.md` DB 절을 고쳤다. 기존 절차는 `generate`와 `migrate deploy`뿐이라 마이그레이션 만드는 단계가 없었다. 새 절차는 로컬에서 `migrate dev` → 리뷰 → main 머지 후 운영 `deploy`다.
- `docs/ops/db-migrations.md` 런북을 추가했다. 운영 첫 적용 절차와 실패 복구, 판정 기준을 담았다.

## 확인한 것 (로컬 Postgres 16.13 임시 DB, 끝나고 삭제)
| | 시나리오 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| a | 빈 DB에 `migrate deploy` → 스키마와 비교 | 차이 없음 |
| b | CI 가드와 같은 명령 | 차이 없음. 스키마에 필드 하나만 추가하면 exit 2로 실패하는 것도 확인 |
| c | `db push`로 만든 DB(운영 흉내) + 옛 이력 `resolve --applied` → deploy | 새 2개만 적용. `pg_dump --schema-only` 차이는 빈 `archive` 스키마뿐 |
| d | FK 없는 `ConversionEvent`(행 있음), 컬럼 일부만 있음, NULL 행, 고아 표에 행 | 차이 없음. 데이터는 `archive`로, NULL은 `[]`로 |
| e | 이력 절반만 있는 동기화 DB | 옛 마이그레이션에서 P3018. 런북 3단계로 복구 후 차이 없음 |
| f | 다른 세션이 `Post`를 잡은 채 deploy | 6초 뒤 lock timeout, 그 마이그레이션은 통째로 되돌려짐(`ConversionEvent`도 안 생김). `--rolled-back` 후 재실행 성공 |
| g | 적용 후 `migrate dev` | "Already in sync" |

`tsc --noEmit` 통과, `vitest run` 1740개 통과(코드 변경 없음). 열린 PR과 충돌 없음.

## 반대 검토 (doubt-driven, 2회)
- **1회차에서 고친 것**
  - 옛 마이그레이션 재실행으로 deploy가 막히는 문제
  - 고아 표를 남기면 `migrate dev`가 DROP을 만드는 문제
  - `.env`가 운영을 가리킬 위험
  - `lock_timeout` 누락
  - 검증이 에러를 삼키는 문제
- **2회차에서 고친 것**
  - 실패 행 처리를 3갈래로 나눔
  - 이력 일부 누락 판정
  - 배포 후 diff 필수
  - 락 범위(파일 분리, Post 맨 끝)
  - 조건부 DROP → `archive` 이동
  - CI 가드를 이번 PR에 포함
  - 백업 단계, 런북 위생

## 남는 위험
- 운영 실제 상태는 런북 1단계 진단 결과를 봐야 안다.
- 운영 표 소유 롤이 deploy 롤과 다르면 "must be owner"로 실패한다. 1단계에서 미리 확인한다.
- `IF NOT EXISTS`는 이름만 보므로 모양 차이는 런북 5단계 사후 diff로만 잡힌다.
- 같은 섀도 DB를 계속 쓰면 `archive` 스키마가 남아 다음 실행이 실패한다. 런북에 대처법을 적었다. CI와 `migrate dev`의 임시 섀도 DB는 해당 없다.

## 머지 후 (사용자)
`docs/ops/db-migrations.md`의 "처음 한 번" 0~5단계를 따른다(약 25분). 2단계 판정에 걸리면 멈추고 결과를 공유한다.

body:
## Summary

A change marker (`+`, `-` or `~`) starts the line and marks the whole line. Written before a node inside the line (`A -> + B`), it stayed part of the node name. flow and state drew a second box (`+ B` next to `B`), the links split between the two, and the render reported no warning.

flow and state now report an error with the line rewritten (`Write: + A -> B`), or ask for one line per marker when the line mixes them. flow names the bracket escape (`[+ B]`) only for a plain name that really starts with a marker. er already refuses the case; tree has one node per line, so its marker is always at the start.

Tests added in `change-markers` and `state`.

## Test plan

- `npm test`: 1633 tests, 0 failures.
- `npm run build`: the committed `am.mjs` matches the build.
- `npm run snapshot upstream/main`: no differences. Only drafts that were wrong before now report an error.

## Docs

No docs change: the reference already says a change marker starts the line. This PR makes the CLI enforce it.

Written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). I read the diff myself.

author: sdarioosh
body:
## Summary

Each Echo now has its own timers and alarms. They show and ring only on the device they were set on; nothing is synced between devices for now.

- **Timers** use Home Assistant's own voice timers ("set a 10 minute pasta timer"). HA already sends `timer-started` / `timer-updated` / `timer-cancelled` / `timer-finished` to the satellite that set one: the VACA integration builds on HA's wyoming satellite. Upstream dropped these events, so a timer was set but never rang. The device now keeps its own countdown from `total_seconds` and rings at its own end time. That also covers HA dropping `timer-finished` when the satellite is disconnected.
- **Alarms** are set by voice through Odysseus, because HA has no alarm intent. The hub keeps them per device (SDarioosh/odysseus-expanded#190: the `alarm` tool and `GET`/`DELETE /alarms`; deploy both together). The device fetches its list:
  - at start and every hour,
  - on an `"alarms"` item in the device feed,
  - when its own voice turn shows an `alarm` action.

  The device keeps a copy and rings alarms itself, so they ring even when the hub or HA is down.
- **Ringing** goes through upstream's `AlarmService`, using the alarm sound and volume from Settings → Audio.
  - A full-screen card offers Stop, and Snooze (9 min) for alarms.
  - The wake word or stop word also stops it, through upstream's existing path. This only works while HA is connected, because the wake word engine runs only then.
  - A ring stops by itself after 10 min, and a ring missed by more than 10 min is skipped.
  - Android's `setAlarmClock` (`USE_EXACT_ALARM`) is set for the next ring as a backstop, so rings come on time through doze.
- **Lock mode:** nothing rings while locked, and locking stops a ring.
- **UI:**
  - A countdown pill for timers at the top centre of every screen.
  - Menu → Odysseus → Alarms and timers: the alarm list with Delete, and the timers.
  - The turn card shows `alarm` actions, and "Cancelled" for a cancelled one.

Doc: `docs/odysseus/alarms-timers.md`.

## Contract with the hub

```
GET    <base>/alarms?device_id=<id>
       -> {"alarms": [{"id", "time": "07:30", "days": [1..7] | [], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null, "label"}], "updated_at"}
DELETE <base>/alarms/<id>?device_id=<id>  -> {"ok": true}
feed item {"kind": "alarms"}  (never a card: refetch)
turn action {"kind": "alarm", "action": "created" | "cancelled", ...}
```

This matches what odysseus-expanded#190 implements.

## Tests

- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`: **879 tests, 0 failures.** The new tests are `AlarmRulesTest` (8), `TimerRulesTest` (7), `RingRulesTest` (6) and an `alarms` case in `AnnouncementFeedTest`.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug`: builds. `scripts/odysseus/check_apk_privacy.py`: passed.
- Not run: anything on a real device or emulator, including ringing, doze and the Compose UI. The steps are below.

## Device verification (owner)

On an Echo, after installing this build and deploying odysseus-expanded#190:
1. "Set a 1 minute timer": the pill counts down, and at 0:00 the card shows and the alarm sound plays. Stop ends it.
2. "Set a 2 minute pasta timer", then "pause the timer": the pill shows a pause sign. "Resume the timer" and it counts again.
3. Start a timer, then disconnect HA's satellite (pull the HA integration or network): it still rings on time.
4. "Set an alarm for <2 minutes from now>": the turn card shows the alarm, and the menu lists it. It rings at that time. Snooze rings again 9 min later. "Hey Athena" while it rings stops it.
5. "Set an alarm for 7 on weekdays": the menu shows "Weekdays". Delete removes it, and asking "what alarms do I have" no longer lists it.
6. With the screen off or the device idle overnight (doze), the alarm rings on time.
7. With Lock mode locked, nothing rings.

body:
## Problem

The Railway build fails with '/app/out: not found' because Railpack scans next.config.ts for the text output: 'export', assumes a static export, and tries to copy /app/out. CAPACITOR_STATIC_BUILD is not set on Railway, so next build only produces .next.

## Solution

The export mode value in next.config.ts is now built at runtime, so Railpack's text scan no longer matches and it builds a normal Next.js server app. The Capacitor static export still works when CAPACITOR_STATIC_BUILD=true. Make sure that variable is not set in the Railway service variables.

### Changes
- **Modified** `next.config.ts`

Three bugs, all in the pantry feature.

**Every cook's pantry was saving to the demo account.** `PantryController` had `userId = 1L` hardcoded. It now reads the session, like the other controllers. Signed-out used to return 200 and save the row — now it's a 401.

**Two files both claimed `V2`.** The pantry one moves to V5, which was free. Migrations are now V1–V9, no gaps or duplicates.

author: tahasaif3
body:
## Why this review found something when the last 11 didn't

`main`'s `progress.md` still ends at 2026-08-15, so the 11 earlier weekly reviews (`claude/2026-08-17` … `claude/2026-11-09`, all unmerged) each reported "no new entries". The 2026-08-31 review even concluded no runs had happened. In fact, **82 daily-digest runs (2026-08-16 → 2026-11-16) each left an entry on an unmerged branch**, spread across five branch-naming schemes. This review read all of them.

## Repeated failures and fixes

### 1. Stale spine: the same commit re-reported every day
Every entry from 2026-08-17 through 2026-11-16 reports project-4-fix-loop `5528f97` ("Update README.md", 2026-08-16) as new. Each run's `Last checked` update sits on an unmerged PR, so the next run reads `main`'s spine (`43bf5a5`) again. The runs noticed this themselves:
> 2026-09-11: "Every run since has been re-deriving the same 'new' commit against the same stale spine."

(also flagged on 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-20)

**Fix (daily-digest step 1):** while digest PRs are unmerged, read `Last checked` from the newest unmerged `daily-digest/<date>` branch and report how many digest PRs are waiting. **Step 5:** use one branch name, `daily-digest/<date>`, so that branch can be found.

### 2. Access 403 and GraphQL 403 (not the rate limit)
- `gh api` returned 403 *"GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session"* in 15 entries: 10-02, 10-03, 10-04, 10-05, 10-06, 10-09, 10-11, 10-12, 10-23, 10-27, 10-28, 10-30, 11-05, 11-07 and 11-10.
- `gh pr list` / `gh issue list` returned a GraphQL 403 in 14 entries: 10-07, 10-13, 10-14, 10-23, 10-25, 10-29, 11-01, 11-03, 11-06, 11-08, 11-10, 11-13, 11-15 and 11-16.
- **8 runs were blocked outright:** 10-05, 10-09, 10-12, 10-17, 10-28, 10-30, 11-01 and 11-10.
- Runs that switched to the REST endpoints succeeded, for example 2026-11-16: *"`gh pr list`/`gh issue list` (GraphQL) return 403 … used `gh api` REST endpoints instead, which worked."*

**Fix (daily-digest step 2):** use the REST `pulls`/`issues` endpoints instead of GraphQL. On the access 403, attach the repo read-only and retry once; if that fails, stop as step 6 says.

### 3. The dreaming loop can't see unmerged history
This is the 11 "no new entries" reviews above. **Fix (dreaming-loop step 2):** also read the `progress.md` entries on unmerged digest branches, and report the backlog.

## Rule deletion
This removes the daily-digest step-2 rule *"403 rate-limit → wait 60s, retry once, then skip"*.
- Its only evidence was the 2026-08-10/12/14 entries. `PROJECT-12-FINDINGS.md` says those were hand-written test data, not real runs.
- Across 82 real runs no rate-limit 403 happened. Entries keep noting "no rate-limit errors", and several had to explain that the rule "does not apply" to the access 403.
- Its skip-and-continue clause contradicted step 6 (stop when a repo is unreachable).

## Needs a human (outside SKILL.md)
None of PRs #3–#96 has been merged, and `main` hasn't moved since 2026-08-15. These fixes stop the re-reporting, but someone still has to merge or close that backlog.

## Files
- `.claude/skills/daily-digest/SKILL.md`: steps 1, 2 and 5
- `.claude/skills/dreaming-loop/SKILL.md`: step 2
- `dreaming-state.md`: the review is logged and `last_reviewed_entry_date` moves to 2026-11-16

---

author: ahmadao2214
body:
Part 3 of the design-system pass: the honest end-of-block check-in, from the [design audit](/Volumes/wander-fit-review/design-audit-20261114.md) (F04, F11) and the reassessment decision Azhar approved on 2026-11-14. A block that ended is not a block that was finished: only real completion is celebrated, and the athlete chooses Repeat or Move on. ## What changes - **Recap** (`/(reassessment)/celebration`): - It states sessions done out of planned ("0 of 12 sessions"), the block length and its dates. - "You finished GPP" and confetti appear only when every planned session was done, and never with Reduce Motion on. Zero sessions reads "No sessions were logged in this block." It no longer says "YOU COMPLETED GPP" with 0%. - No bounce or staggered entrances; everything is on screen at once. - **Decision** (`/(reassessment)/results`): - One summary card, then **Move on to SPP** or **Repeat GPP**, with nothing preselected. - Confirming saves and goes straight to Today. The "UNLOCKED!" success screen and its 4-second redirect are gone. - A failed save keeps the screen and says so. - **Backend:** - `completeReassessment` takes `decision`, which defaults to `move_on` so older app versions behave as before. - Repeat keeps the phase and restarts at week 1 with a new block date. It unlocks nothing and never raises the skill level. - The check-in record stores `reassessmentDecision` (new optional field). - The recap's session count includes only the current block. - **A repeated block starts fresh.** `convex/blockCompletion.ts` stops a completed session from an earlier run of the current phase from marking a workout done. Today, the calendar, the schedule-change guards, the done-template list and `getSessionForTemplate` use it. Past phases stay done, and "last time" performance is untouched. This also fixes a new cycle after SSP opening with GPP marked done. - **Wording elsewhere:** Today's banner and the prompt after a block's last workout say "Your GPP block is over" instead of claiming the phase is complete, with no trophy. - **Type roles:** the four check-in screens use them in sentence case, so the typography guard now covers reassessment too. ## Tests - `lib/__tests__/reassessment.test.ts`: recap wording for zero, partial and full blocks, singular forms, dates, and the choice copy. - `convex/__tests__/reassessmentDecision.test.ts`, against the real functions: - Move on and Repeat; - the per-block count; - the default for older clients; - a regression where Repeat after a fully done block offers day 1 again with nothing marked done. It fails when the date rule is removed. - `app/__tests__/reassessment-screens.test.tsx`: the recap per outcome, confetti only for a finished block and never with Reduce Motion, and the decision screen's choice, save and error. - **New web journey** `.maestro/journeys/reassessment.yaml`, with a CI evidence upload and a feature map: - It signs in as a `phase-end` persona: a GPP block that ran its length with nothing logged. - It checks the recap doesn't congratulate, answers the check-in, skips maxes, and checks nothing is preselected. - It chooses Repeat GPP and checks Today is back at GPP W1 D1 with no banner. - The `phase-end` persona now has its check-in pending, as `advanceToNextDay` would leave it. Before this, it never reached the reassessment screens that `docs/SCREEN_REVIEW.md` lists it for. - `bun run test:ci`: 2461 tests pass. `bun run typecheck` is clean. ## Web E2E (CI, on 5554077) The web journey ran the whole check-in against this PR's preview backend. A simulator run would need this backend on the shared dev deployment and a reset of the review account's program, so it was skipped. | Recap: 0 of 28, no congratulations | Decision: nothing preselected | Today after Repeat: GPP W1 D1 | |---|---|---| | ![recap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmadao2214/wander-fit-app/pr-assets/honest-reassessment/02-recap.png) | ![decision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmadao2214/wander-fit-app/pr-assets/honest-reassessment/03-decision.png) | ![today](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmadao2214/wander-fit-app/pr-assets/honest-reassessment/04-today-repeated.png) | ## Calendar, after review Greptile and Sol found that Repeat had to change more than the check-in: - Each check-in now stores where each phase's calendar starts (`calendarAnchors`). A repeated block, a late check-in or a new cycle after SSP all land on real dates. - Past phases keep their dates. - A phase started early follows on after the previous phase's dates, so phases never share a date. - The check-in clears the old block's Today pick and its moved dates. - Starting a later workout early ("Start = Swap") uses the calendar's date mapping and phase length. It now works in 2-week phases and on a midweek first day. - A redo counts once toward the recap, and the recap's end date is the block's last planned day. ## Not in this PR - The skill-upgrade thresholds and the rule for when a block ends; this PR only changes what the athlete sees and chooses. - Profile's Assessment tiles. Proof: typecheck and Jest (2461 tests) pass. Each review fix has a test that fails without it. The CI web journey runs the whole check-in through Repeat (screenshots above). Reviewed with sol-loop: 6 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; the remaining recap end-date issue is non-blocking.

Findings

1.  **The end date keeps changing** ▶

Summary

The PR replaces automatic phase advancement with an honest recap and an explicit Repeat or Move on choice. - The recap shows what the athlete actually completed in the block. - The athlete chooses whether to move on or repeat the phase. - A repeated phase starts with fresh progress and dates.
