author: jaguilar4k
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"JAguilar4k"} -->
_Requested by **Julián** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FnkfVhnsbC6r5FMpWsJsj8?thread=cmsg_01FnkfVhnsbC6r5FMpWsJsj8JRTLQ1umKtjtCBXLP7wYbT)_

## Resumen

Depende del PR #305 (#126), que a su vez sale de #304 (#127): esta rama sale de la de #305, así que hasta que esos dos se fusionen el diff incluye sus commits. Integrar después de #304 y #305.

Un visitante explora la vitrina de una tienda con filtros, ve el detalle de cada perfume y pide una recomendación, sin iniciar sesión.

- **Encabezado de la tienda** (`StoreLayout`, `GET /tiendas/{tienda}`): nombre, logo y lugar de las citas (`lugar_cita`). Una tienda que no existe muestra "No encontrado".
- **Vitrina** (`/tiendas/:tienda`, `GET /tiendas/{tienda}/perfumes`): paginada, con filtros de texto, familia, nota, momento, clima, ocasión y precio máximo que quedan en la URL para compartir la búsqueda. Una búsqueda nueva empieza en la primera página, el enlace a la página siguiente conserva los filtros y un filtro que la API rechaza con 422 se marca en su campo.
- **Detalle** (`/tiendas/:tienda/perfumes/:perfume`): notas por capa, etiquetas (momento, clima y ocasión en español), presentaciones y decants disponibles con su precio. Un perfume inactivo o de otra tienda muestra "No encontrado".
- **Precios:** tal como los entrega la API, en colones enteros con separador de miles (`formatColones`, con `Intl.NumberFormat` de `es-CR`). El navegador no calcula ningún precio.
- **Recomendador** (`/tiendas/:tienda/recomendaciones`, `POST /tiendas/{tienda}/recomendaciones`): junto al campo avisa que el texto se envía a un proveedor externo de IA y que no conviene incluir datos personales (R51); muestra la espera y marca el botón con `aria-disabled`, así que un doble envío manda una sola solicitud; cada perfume trae su razón como texto plano (nunca HTML), sus precios y un enlace al detalle, con "Recomendado con IA" o "Recomendado por reglas" según `origen`. Un 429 dice en cuánto tiempo volver a intentar (#127).
- **Raíz:** `/` abre la tienda de `VITE_DEFAULT_BUSINESS_SLUG` (nueva variable en `.env.example`, con `archivumparfums`, la tienda piloto de los seeders). La vista de inicio provisional de #123 deja de usarse y se quita con sus dos pruebas.
- **Contrato:** `presentaciones` y `decants` de la vitrina salían en `openapi/v1.json` como listas de elementos sin tipo, porque los recursos los armaban con `array_map`. `ShowcaseVariantResource` y `ShowcaseDecantResource`, anidados con `::collection` como hace el repo guía, documentan sus campos; el JSON no cambia. El contrato y `src/api/schema.ts` van regenerados.
- Los ayudantes de pruebas `fakeApi`, `json` y `problem` pasan a `src/api/__tests__/fakeApi.ts` para que las funcionalidades los compartan.
- Agendar una prueba desde la recomendación queda para #122, como dice el issue.

### Accesibilidad (WCAG 2.2 AAA)

- **"Ayuda y glosario"** (`/ayuda`, enlazada desde el pie de cada página): explica cómo buscar y pedir una recomendación, y define las palabras de perfumería (decant, concentración, notas, familia olfativa, presentación, bajo pedido, ml, ₡...). Cada término tiene un id: una página enlaza `/ayuda#decant` y el foco va al término.
- **Abreviaturas:** `MlAmount` muestra `<abbr title="mililitros">ml</abbr>`, las concentraciones dicen su nombre completo ("Eau de Parfum (EDP)") y los botones leen "mililitros".
- **Vitrina:** cada campo de búsqueda tiene una pista ligada con `aria-describedby`; los enlaces de paginación dicen "Página anterior" y "Página siguiente", y al cambiar de página el foco va al título de la lista. El número de resultados está en una región `role="status"` que siempre existe.
- **Detalle:** ruta de enlaces (Vitrina › perfume) y un `h1` con el nombre del perfume, que también titula la pestaña.
- **Recomendador:** la pista y el aviso de privacidad van ligados al campo, y el estado de la recomendación se anuncia en una región `role="status"`.
- El encabezado de la tienda es una lista de enlaces dentro de un `nav`, y "No encontrado" y "Sin permiso" titulan la pestaña.

## Issues

Closes #128

## Comprobación

- [x] En `archivum-web/`: `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run type-check`, `npm run test` (18 archivos, 114 pruebas), `npm run build` y `npm run api:check` pasan en local (con Node.js 24; el job `Web` usa el 26 de `engines`).
- [x] Pruebas de componentes con la API simulada: filtros (desde la URL, hacia la URL, paginación y 422), detalle (notas, etiquetas, precios y 404), las dos respuestas del recomendador, la espera con doble envío, el 429 y el aviso de privacidad. Se comprobó que la prueba de la razón falla si se muestra como HTML.
- [x] API, con PHP 8.4 y PostgreSQL 18: `scramble:export` reproduce el contrato de `main` sin cambios antes del arreglo; después, las pruebas de Pest de `tests/Feature/Catalog`, `tests/Unit/Catalog`, `tests/Architecture` y `OpenApiContractTest` pasan (512) y Pint no reporta nada. Larastan y la suite completa corren en el job `Quality` de este PR.
- [x] Pruebas de la ayuda (términos, enlace desde el pie y foco en el término de la dirección), de las pistas, de la paginación con el foco en la lista y de los títulos de cada página.
- [x] Sobre la cadena completa hasta #308, la auditoría de axe-core (reglas A, AA y AAA de WCAG 2.0, 2.1 y 2.2, más buenas prácticas) con Playwright contra la API de demostración, más revisiones propias de objetivos de 44 px, interlineado, largo de línea, foco y encabezados, no deja hallazgos en la vitrina (con y sin resultados), el detalle, el recomendador (vacío y con resultados), "No encontrado" y "Ayuda y glosario". axe deja como "incompleto" el contraste del área de texto del recomendador, porque no puede medir un campo que se tapa a sí mismo; se midió a mano: #1c1b1f sobre blanco, cerca de 17:1.
- [x] Los commits son atómicos, siguen Conventional Commits y llevan `Refs: #128`.
- [x] El código y los comentarios están en inglés; los textos de la interfaz, en español.
- [x] `openapi/v1.json` está regenerado y `archivum-web` usa los tipos regenerados.
- [x] La sección "Uso de IA" del README tiene su fila.

author: dramanica
body:
Fixes #82, and the general rule Andrea asked for: **every isopleth that cannot be drawn is kept as a row**, with an empty geometry and an `NA` area, and a warning that says why and what to do.

**Merge order:** stacked on #95–#98, because #95 also changes `hr_tt_ud_iso()` and every PR touches NEWS. Merge it after #98 (#99 is independent). Its own change is the last commit.

## Changes

- **`hr_tt_ud_iso()`**, and `levels` in `hr_tt_kde()`, `hr_tt_dbbmm()`, `hr_tt_akde()` and `hr_tt_akde_pop()`: each UD has one row per level. `cud_isopleths()` records every level it cannot draw, with the reason:
  - the cells with the highest value hold more of the UD than the level (#82). The warning gives the smallest level that can be drawn, and suggests a finer grid (for `hr_tt_kde()`, a smaller `res` or a larger `h`);
  - a 0% level;
  - a UD without values (all `NA`), or with infinite values;
  - contour lines that fail, cannot be turned into polygons, or enclose no area.
- These replace the bare "No isopleths could be computed" warnings. A level left empty for any other reason is still reported.
- **One warning per call**, with one line per UD and reason. Long lists are cut after 10 lines. For example:
  ```
  Some isopleths cannot be drawn, so they are returned with an empty geometry and an NA area:
  * 'a', 50%: the cells with the highest value of the UD hold more of it than the level (the smallest level that can be drawn is 90.2%), so no cell is within the isopleth; use a UD estimated on a finer grid (for hr_tt_kde(), a smaller res or a larger h)
  ```
- **`hr_tt_mcp()` and `hr_tt_locoh()`** already returned empty polygons when the locations within a level are fewer than three, or on a line. These now get an `NA` area rather than 0, with the same warning. The test data `example_tt_2` has such a case: the 50% MCP of track c.
- **`hr_tt_dbbmm(levels = ...)`**: tracks with fewer locations than `window_size`, which move2utils skips, now get empty rows. Its table of UDs still leaves them out (see below).
- **Exact levels:** the contour lines are matched to the levels by value, so a level such as `1/3` is no longer rounded through `split()`.

An empty geometry does not break plotting with `geom_sf()`; a test builds such a plot. The issue's example no longer fails with the default binned KDE, because #94 spreads each location over four cells. The tests use the exact KDE and small rasters.

## Decided by Andrea (16 Nov)

- The table of UDs of `hr_tt_dbbmm()`, without `levels`, still leaves out the tracks too short for `window_size`.
- MCP and LoCoH groups with fewer than three locations, and KDE groups whose UD is 0 on the grid, still give an error.

## Checks

- The new tests fail on the old code, and pass now.
- These test files pass locally, with no warnings: `hr_tt_ud_iso`, `hr_tt_mcp`, `hr_tt_locoh`, `hr_tt_dbbmm`, `hr_tt_kde`, `hr_tt_akde`, `hr_tt_akde_pop`, `hr_tt_ud_overlap`, `autoplot_hr_ud_tbl`, `group_by_meta` and `kde_vs_adehabitat`.
- The examples of the home range functions give no new warnings.

author: lanepon224
body:
> **Unfinished and unowned.** This is an unfinished side project with no owner or maintainer: nobody is responsible for it, it gets no support, and it may stop at any time. Anyone is free to take it, fork it, finish it or merge any part of it upstream (MIT, like Horizon and the Java bridge). Not affiliated with Horizon, the Java bridge, Mojang or Microsoft.

Fixes found while getting real Fabric 26.3 modpacks (100-300 mods from Modrinth) to run plug-and-play through the bridge. Opened as a **draft** so you can pick what you want: every commit is self-contained with its own message, and most can be cherry-picked on their own. Happy to split this into smaller PRs if that's easier.

Based on `java-bridge` at 99e8ba8 (current head), so it applies cleanly. No game files, mod jars or mod assets are included.

## What it covers (90 commits)

- **Loading big packs:** leave out the largest content mods (and say so in chat) instead of none when a pack has more block states than a world holds; wider sprite arrays up to the GPU limit; unreadable mod recipes/advancements left out instead of failing the world load.
- **Plug and play in the launcher:** missing required mods downloaded from Modrinth when Play starts (also following Modrinth's own dependency links), version conflicts fixed before Play, left-out mods shown on the Java mods tab.
- **Mods' content:** BCLib world setup, block tints, Tom's Storage cable textures, jigsaw structures, mod fluids, mod block collision/outlines, legacy `.lang` files, multi-namespace mods (BuildCraft).
- **Mods' mobs, screens and HUD:** animated mod mobs, mod screens (click/scroll/keys), mod key bindings, HUD layers, entity render dispatcher before client reload (Kiwi), client reload order (Subtle Effects).
- **Multiplayer:** unreadable mod packets, Java mods' attacks/teleports/jumps/deaths on guests, held joins until load functions ran.
- **Speed:** warm start with 184 mods from 2+ min to ~60-70 s (Java started early beside content reading, block facts snapshot, mod files bundled, threaded reads); data pack selectors (`type=#tag` from memory, `nbt=` parsed once) and slow tick functions named in the log; 2 cores left free for the render thread with Java mods (300-mod flight 1% low 42-46 -> 65-69 fps).
- **Storage:** the content build's own inputs removed from the cache (2.2 -> 0.96 GB with 184 mods).

## Tested

77 automatic checks on real mod packs (8, 21 and 38 jars, plus a 184-mod pack): blocks, items, animated mobs, mod screens, machines (Farmer's Delight, Tom's Storage, Energized Power, CC: Tweaked), Biomes O' Plenty worldgen, Waystones, mixin-heavy mods (Xaero, JEI, Inventory Profiles Next...), save/reload, shader pack pick, and a new-player start-to-quit run. Windows 11, Ryzen 5 7600, RX 7600.

## Not done

Several of these touch Horizon code that upstream (horizon-rust/horizon) has since reorganised (`game.rs` split into `game/*.rs`); a merge with upstream's current main is in progress on my side.

body:

_Requested by **Cameron** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EHppawrimAYMwgdEKgxQqx?thread=cmsg_01EHppawrimAYMwgdEKgxQqxJZdXG5TtN4zCaNLMW2ZwKk)_

## Summary

ADR-152 (Editorial design language) retires sound. This removes the chalk soundscape: the Login provider, the chalk cue on sign-in and sign-up submit, the "Chalk sound" toggle under the form, the synthesis engine with its tests, and the Hagoromo sound sketches in Storybook. The three `login.chalkSound*` strings leave `en.ts`, `ja.ts` and all 77 generated catalogs. The golden learner journey now fails if any page constructs a Web Audio context, creates an audio element or plays media.

What the issue's criteria came to in this codebase:

- **No audio on any page.** `e2e/support/sound-probe.ts` wraps `AudioContext`, `webkitAudioContext`, `OfflineAudioContext`, `Audio`, `document.createElement("audio")` and `HTMLMediaElement.play` for every page of the journey's browser context; the journey asserts the list is empty and writes it to its evidence file. I checked the probe itself in Chromium: it reports all four kinds of use.
- **Settings and toggles.** The only sound control was the Login toggle. Account and the CMS settings had none, so nothing changes there.
- **Audio files and bundle size.** There were no audio files; every cue was synthesized. What leaves the bundle is the synthesis code, its stylesheet and the strings. From a local `vite build` of this branch and of `next` (b3851e9d): the Login chunk goes from 43,952 to 37,337 bytes of JS and from 18,994 to 17,275 bytes of CSS; all client JS and CSS together drop 15,612 bytes (about 5,950 gzipped).
- **Voice input and read-aloud** (`src/features/voice/`) are not touched.

A learner who had switched the toggle off keeps a harmless `localStorage` preference key that nothing reads now.

## Screenshots

Login at 1440 and 390, before and after, are in the project files under `overhaul/olm-3289/`. The only visible change is that the "Chalk sound · On" switch under the privacy note is gone.

## Scope contract

- Linear issue: OLM-3289 (epic OLM-3254)
- Owned problem domain: sound on the web client
- Non-goals: the rest of the Hagoromo Storybook preview and the Cocco material layers (OLM-3302), the full rewrite of `docs/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md` (OLM-3303), voice features
- Handwritten changed lines / source files: 1,733 / 32, of which about 1,650 lines are deletions of the soundscape modules and their tests
- Migrations: 0
- Runtime activation boundaries: 1 (client)
- Supersedes / replaced by: none
- Scope exception: yes. This is a removal. The engine, its provider, the toggle, their tests and every importer have to go in one change or the build breaks, so it cannot be split below the 25-file line. `scope:exception` is set for that reason.

## Checklist

- [x] **Base branch is `next`**
- [ ] `npm run check:full` passes locally: not run in full. Typecheck, ESLint on the changed files, 436 focused Vitest tests (Login, Account deletion, design-language, i18n), `check:styling`, `check:readability`, `check:comments` and `check:standards` pass locally. `check:refactoring` reports about 150 findings in the cloud container, none in a file this PR touches, so CI is the evidence for it. The golden journey needs Postgres and runs in CI.
- [x] Failure mode considered: a browser with no Web Audio support behaves the same as any other now.
- [x] No API changes
- [x] No `import` from `vendor/olms` under `src/`
- [x] No secrets or user-facing notes UI
- [x] **Coverage:** the removed code takes its tests with it; the new guard is the golden-journey assertion
- [x] **History hygiene:** generated catalogs lose only the three sound keys (removed directly, because `i18n:translate --offline` would also have dropped unrelated pending strings); `modules.index.json` and `styling.baseline.json` are regenerated
- [x] **Pre-work check done**

author: zany130
body:
### Problem
Currently, Redumper-GUI lists optical drives on Linux by their `/dev/sg*` device identifiers, as Redumper uses these paths for dumping.

The problem is that sg numbers are dynamically assigned and are not a reliable way of identifying a drive. This is fine on single-drive systems, but on systems with multiple optical drives, it can become confusing.


### Solution
This update adds a small downstream patch that reads the drive manufacturer and model information from Linux sysfs and displays it alongside the device path.

The patch changes two files:

- `src/drives.rs` — reads drive metadata.
- `src/app/toolbar.rs` — displays the information in the drive selector.

The application is still built from Deterous's original upstream release. No sandbox permission changes are required.

I previously proposed this improvement upstream in Deterous/Redumper-GUI#13. The author indicated that the idea was good but explained that the project no longer accepts external contributions, regardless of AI involvement.

I'm carrying this as a minimal downstream usability patch for Linux users.

I personally tested that the patch applies cleanly to the latest upstream master tree and that it does indeed add drive model and manufacturer information to both the main window and the dropdown.

### AI Disclosure

The patch was written with the help of Codex, as I don't know too much Rust, but I have reviewed the changes and tested them on my system.

author: rdegges
body: Supersedes #69 (Dependabot, same one-line bump). Dependabot's branch is untouched; #69 can be closed once this merges. ## What changes - `docker-compose.yml`: image tag `v0.169.0` to `v0.170.0`. This is the single source of truth for the Hugo version. `scripts/render-build.sh` reads it, so CI, Render and local dev all move together. - `README.md`: new Hugo version, the single-binary (no extended edition) note, Sass guidance, and the output-parity claim. - No workflow, script or test changes. No existing check or assertion was weakened. ## Security fix and why the cooldown is bypassed v0.170.0 was published 2026-11-13, which is under the repo's 7-day Dependabot cooldown. This is an allowed security exception. The release bundles `go-jose` v4.1.6 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q / CVE-2026-116587, a DoS from crafted RSA JWKs, CVSS 7.5, patched in 4.1.6) and Go 1.27.4 (12 stdlib/toolchain fixes). It also escapes passthrough content and `wrapperClass`, and restricts vendored module paths. **Does the advisory affect this site? No.** The affected package is go-jose, an indirect dependency in Hugo's `go.mod`. `go version -m` shows go-jose is not linked into the standard Hugo binary in either v0.169.0 or v0.170.0. It is only in the `withdeploy` builds, which this repo never downloads. Hugo only builds trusted local content here, with no `hugo deploy` and no JWK parsing. The bump is hygiene plus the Go and x/net fixes. ## Supply-chain vetting of v0.170.0 - Release: `gohugoio/hugo` v0.170.0, not draft, not prerelease. It was created 2026-11-13T14:17Z and published 16:09Z by maintainer `bep`. All assets were uploaded by `bep`. - Tag `v0.170.0` points at commit `f7aa05f0f521611aa960b2da56e1870ea04f57b2`, "releaser: Bump versions for release of 0.170.0" by the `hugoreleaser` bot. That commit is unsigned, as Hugo's release bot commits are. It is 45 commits ahead of v0.169.0 and matches the commits listed in Dependabot's notes. - The downloaded `hugo_0.170.0_linux-amd64.tar.gz` has SHA-256 `0930754ec22ad2dd1a252f8c31a5e57faccc9d15f1c3d381ddafcb96eeb8aef0`. This matches both the official `hugo_0.170.0_checksums.txt` (itself `3d898c1d...ab447`) and the digest GitHub computed for the asset. - The binary reports `hugo v0.170.0-f7aa05f0...` (the tagged commit) and was built with go1.27.4 and `CGO_ENABLED=0`. - The `gh attestation verify` check could not run, because Sigstore verifiers could not initialize in this sandbox. Hugo does not sign its checksums file either, so provenance rests on the tag, the maintainer-uploaded assets and the checksum match. - The `ghcr.io/gohugoio/hugo:v0.170.0` image exists (index digest `sha256:90663d47...16cb2`). It is used for local dev only, and Docker was not available here to run it. ## Where Hugo is downloaded and how it is pinned - The only download is `scripts/render-build.sh`, used by CI and Render. It builds the version pinned in `docker-compose.yml` and downloads the plain `hugo__linux-amd64.tar.gz`. It checks the SHA-256 against the release's checksums file, requires exactly one exact-name match, and aborts otherwise. It was run for real against v0.170.0 and printed `...linux-amd64.tar.gz: OK`. `tests/test_render_build.py` covers the script. - There is no Dockerfile, Netlify config or other download path. - All `uses:` in `.github/workflows/build.yml` are pinned to full 40-hex commit SHAs (checked), and zizmor reports no findings. ## Breaking change: extended edition and LibSass This site does not use either. - No `hugo_extended` download. The script already uses the plain archive, and the extended edition appears only in comments, README text and test fixtures that assert it is not fetched. - No `extended: true`, `peaceiris/actions-hugo` or extended Docker image. - No `.scss` or `.sass` files, and no `toCSS`, `css.Sass`, `resources.ToCSS` or `transpiler` anywhere. CSS is plain `.css` in `assets/css/`, joined with `resources.Concat`. - Dart Sass is therefore not needed. Adding it would only add a binary to download, pin and verify for no benefit, so plain CSS is the smallest safe option. The README says how to add Dart Sass pinned and checksum-verified if Sass is ever introduced. ## Build comparison, old v0.169.0 vs new v0.170.0 Both built from a clean `resources/` with `hugo --minify --panicOnWarning`: 345 pages, 657 processed images, 166 aliases, with no warnings. The file lists are identical. Differences: 1. `` becomes `0.170.0` in 171 HTML files. 2. The Atom `feed.xml` `` has the same version change. 3. `.well-known/security.txt` `Expires:` differs only because the two builds ran 48 seconds apart (it is `now + 180d`). After normalising 1 and 2, `diff -r` shows only difference 3. Every image, CSS, sitemap, `llms.txt` and other file is byte-identical. ## Checks run before pushing (all pass) - `./scripts/render-build.sh --panicOnWarning` (the CI build step): pass. - `python3 -m unittest discover --start-directory tests`: 173 tests, OK, none skipped. This includes link, image, header, CSP and render-build tests. - `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npx cf build`, the security.txt packaging check and `npx cf deploy --prebuilt --dry-run` (with the dry-run guard): pass, on Node 22.23 here vs 26 in CI. - zizmor v1.32.0 on `.github`: no findings, in offline mode. ## Risks - The release is only 3 days old and its binaries are not signed. Mitigated by checksum pinning and the fact that Hugo only builds trusted content here. - `render-build.sh` takes the checksum from the same release, so it detects corruption and a swapped asset alone, but not a fully compromised release. Hard-pinning a hash in the repo would break the repo's "one-line Dependabot bump" design and its tests, so I left that out. - `docker-compose.yml` is tag-pinned, not digest-pinned. - Hugo v0.170.0 behaviour changes (`strings.Truncate`, `time.Time` comparison, `resources.Match` casing, flags overriding env vars) did not alter any output, per the byte-for-byte build diff.

body:
## Why this change

Live Google Search Console data for sc-domain:finflowtrack.com (latest 28 days) shows the existing guide:
- 78 impressions
- 0 clicks
- 0% CTR
- Average position 27.69

Visible query rows include searches around the SBA break-even formula, fixed costs, variable costs, and contribution margin. Query rows are incomplete; no search volume is inferred.

The existing page already explains break-even analysis. Instead of adding another article, this PR adds a practical interactive tool that completes the calculation task.

## Implementation
- Add /tools/break-even-calculator as a new TanStack file route.
- Add inputs for fixed costs, selling price, variable cost per unit, expected sales units, target profit, currency, and analysis period.
- Calculate contribution per unit, contribution margin ratio, break-even units (rounded up), break-even revenue, target-profit units (rounded up), modeled profit/loss at expected sales, and margin of safety.
- Validate non-negative inputs and prevent division by zero or invalid contribution margins (variable cost >= price).
- Explain the formulas and key limitations.
- State clearly that the calculator is single-product/single-service, assumes constant price and variable cost, and does not model cash timing, taxes, demand, or capacity.
- State that inputs remain in the browser and are not connected to or saved in FinFlow Track.
- Link the existing break-even guide to the calculator and add the route to the XML sitemap.
- Update the SEO opportunity database with current GSC evidence and implementation status.

## Differentiation
The SBA already offers a basic break-even calculator. This tool adds target-profit and margin-of-safety outputs, clear period controls, currency formatting, live results, and transparent limitations. It does not claim to replace the SBA resource or a full financial model.

## Files
- src/routes/tools.break-even-calculator.tsx (new)
- src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts (modified)
- content/blog/break-even-analysis-small-business.md (modified)
- docs/seo/organic-opportunity-database.md (modified)

## Validation required before merge
- Run TanStack route generation via project build; do not manually edit generated src/routeTree.gen.ts.
- Run TypeScript/build and ESLint.
- Check accessibility and keyboard navigation on mobile and desktop.
- Test zero, negative, empty, decimal, and invalid price/cost combinations.
- Verify currency formatting and rounding behavior for all supported currencies.
- Verify sitemap includes canonical tool URL and canonical metadata is correct.
- Check the calculator does not send or persist input values.
- After deployment, track organic visits to the tool, calculator interactions, clicks to signup, completed registrations, and meaningful first accounting actions.
- Do not claim SEO uplift until observed in Search Console and analytics.

## Guardrails
- No changes to existing accounting features, auth, billing, database schema, or user data.
- No fabricated customer evidence, search volumes, or conversion claims.
- No mass-generated pages.
- Existing article URL remains unchanged.

Implements the guessing step and asymptotic theorem for repeated inversion (Boneh–Shoup v0.6 §13.4.1, Lemma 13.5 / Exercise 14.15, single-iterate `d = 1` case):

Kept `map_true_le_map_true_of_le` private.
- **`CslibFrontier/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/Repeated.lean`:** added `repeatedInverter` (sampling `sampleDyadicIndex (t n)`), PPT preservation `isPPT_repeatedInverter`, `succProbability_repeatedInversionGame_le` (factor `dyadicSize (t n)`), and `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.repeatedInversion_negligible` (word-level repeated one-wayness for every `t` with `ComputableInPolyTime t encUnary encUnary`, which the uniform reduction needs to draw its guess).
- **`CslibFrontierTests/Crypto/Game/RepeatedInversion.lean` and `CslibFrontierTests/Crypto/OneWayRepeated.lean`:** added regression checks for `0 < d`, `secondSlotAttack` tightness (`1` vs `1/2` vs `1`), `Cslib.Crypto.OneWay.repeatedInversion_negligible` instantiations, `t = 0`, and concrete `n = 0, 1` bounds (`1`, `1/2`, `1/8`).

- **Aggregate:** regenerated `CslibFrontier.lean` via `lake exe mk_all`.

body:
**Barometric pressure** (`TOURNEO_BAROMETRIC_P`, `7E0 22 1127`, `barometricPressure`)

The byte counts eighths of an inch of mercury. It was scaled by 338639/80000, ten times 1/8 inHg in kilopascals, so every reply across the family's fixtures read 982 to 1,046 kPa. Scaled by 338639/800000 the same replies read 98.2 to 104.6 kPa, sea-level air pressure. The bound becomes 107.94 kPa, the byte's full range.

author: slashnephy
body:
## 概要

BS4K の録画で、局ロゴの見分け方（`logo`）を確かめたところ、4K のままではロゴを学習できず、試すだけで録画の長さの 0.36〜0.44 倍かかっていました（#1505 の[測定のコメント](https://github.com/SlashNephy/kotatsu/issues/1505#issuecomment-6906952371)）。長い 4K の録画では、ジョブの時間の上限（30 分）を超える見込みです。そこで、縦が 1080 ラインより大きい映像では、ロゴを試さずに、今の見分け方（`ffmpeg`）で見分けます（コメントの推奨 A）。

## 変更

- `LogoDetector` で、ffprobe で読んだ映像の縦が 1080 ラインより大きければ、ロゴを読まずに、ロゴを学習できなかったときと同じ道（`ffmpeg` の見分け方）へ回します。理由は、見分けた記録の注記（`note`）に残ります。
- 設計書 6.1 に書きました。

## 確かめたこと

- `TestLogoDetectorSkipsTallVideo` を足しました。3840×2160 の合成の TS で、ロゴを読まずに今の見分け方の結果を返し、注記に縦の大きさが残ることを確かめます。上限を 4320 に上げて直しを外すと、このテストが落ちることを確かめました。
- `go test ./internal/usecase/cmdetect/`（局ロゴの見分け方のテスト）が通り、`golangci-lint` は 0 件でした。
- 測定のコメントの BS4K の録画 3 本では、どれも `logo` が学習に失敗して `ffmpeg` に戻っていたので、この直しで結果は変わらず、ロゴを試す時間（9.5〜11.8 分）だけが減ります。
- PR を出す前の独立レビューは APPROVE（指摘なし）でした。

## 確かめていないこと

- 開発用のスタックで BS4K の録画を見分け直すこと。手元の測定は、コメントのとおり、イメージの FFmpeg で検出器を直接動かしたものです。

## 残り（#1505）

- 縮めてから学習する（推奨 B）、学習で読むキーフレームを減らす（C）、全コマの読みを軽くする（D）、時間の上限を録画の長さに合わせる（E）。4K でもロゴを使うには、B と C が要ります。

Refs #1505

author: nielsencampos
body:
Wave 2 of the i18n epic (#26): Latin Extended and Vietnamese font subsets, and five machine-made, unreviewed locales: Turkish (`tr`), Polish (`pl`), Dutch (`nl`), Indonesian (`id`) and Vietnamese (`vi`).

## Fonts
- The `latin-ext` and `vietnamese` subsets of Familjen Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (Fontsource 5.3.0, OFL-1.1, same weights as `latin`), listed in `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`. Vietnamese gets the vendored fonts, no fallback chain.
- Every `@font-face` has its subset's `unicode-range`, so a page loads a subset only when its text needs it. The registry gains the `vietnamese` script; a test checks that each locale's scripts have both fonts and cover every letter of its UI file.
- Side effect: the language picker shows "Tiếng Việt", so the small Vietnamese subset (~4 KB) loads on every page; `latin-ext` loads only for text that needs it.

## Turkish uppercase
- A string that falls back to English gets `lang="en-US"`, so `text-transform: uppercase` under `lang="tr"` never turns its `i` into `İ`. Turkish text itself uppercases correctly ("SATRANÇ HAMLE KÂĞIDI", "İÇİN").

## Locales
- UI files with Help and About (author's decision), registry entries, glossaries (piece letters from Wikipedia's table; terms from each Wikipedia where a page names them, else `machine = true`), Vale styles (form of address: tr *siz*, pl *ty*, nl *je*, id *Anda*, vi *bạn*), LanguageTool for pl and nl only.
- Polish has `one`/`few`/`many`/`other` plural keys; a new test checks each language's plural forms. `check_text.py` fills `{count}` per form (1, 2, 5).
- Opening names through `catalog.names` for all 4411 names per locale (Wikipedia, glossary rules, then machine translation). Surnames stay as the book spells them. Line ids unchanged.
- `catalog.names`: a Wikidata label that only copies the English name is no name (Dutch "Torre Attack", "Owen's Defence"), English locales aside. No existing locale changes.
- Help pictures and `docs/HELP*.md` / `docs/ABOUT*.md` for the new locales; HOW_TO_INSTALL is not translated.

## Known limits
- Polish rule-built names keep the surname in the nominative ("Wariant Najdorf", not "Najdorfa"); that needs a genitive placeholder in the rules.
- Dutch multi-word names join the noun ("Max Langeaanval").
- The Dutch Italian Game is the Wikidata label "Italiaans en verwante schaakopeningen" (sourced).

## Tests
- ruff, pytest (482), `catalog.validate`, codespell, LanguageTool (pl, nl), Vale, on a clean checkout of the branch tip.
- e2e (126) against the rebuilt image; every screen at 1280x720 in the five locales and both themes, checked by eye (letters such as ş ğ ı ł ą ę ơ ư ữ in the same font mid-word, no overflow).

Fixes #33

author: denisd04-arch
body: The table now follows one round: confirm whether you played, enter cards, freeze your hand on stand, and settle from those cards only after the dealer finishes. - YES I PLAYED or NO I SKIPPED is required. The assistant call is stored separately and is not a wager. - A skip keeps the main stake at 0. Cards still leave the shoe. There is no invented profit and the bankroll does not move. - After stand, the hand total is frozen. Other-player cards cannot change it. The hole is reserved once, then revealed, then the dealer draws. - Settlement uses the recorded cards and the verified dealer-22 and Charlie payoffs. Bust It on dealer 22 stays pending until you confirm it. Settling the same round again does not move the bankroll. - The money ledger is the same shape on the live table, in testing, and in forward testing. It stays in this browser. Regression: 10♠ and 9♥ stand at 19, then 7♦, 3♣, and K♥, then the hole and the dealer draw. The hand stays 19 and is settled against the dealer total those cards actually make.

author: justncredible223
body:
A regression from #336, found by the Home audit.

- **What broke:** the Approvals guard lets a decision move a campaign only out of `in_review`. Today's X Post campaigns stay `draft`, and Home's "New draft" first rejects the current draft, then asks for a new one. That reject got a 409, so the owner saw "Couldn't write a new draft".
- **The fix:**
  - Reject can now also move a campaign that is still `draft`.
  - Approve still moves only `in_review` campaigns.
  - An approved or retired campaign still never moves, so the safety the guard was added for is unchanged.

Tests: backend tests pass.

author: gabriel39
body:
### Background

The native MongoDB Catalog on master already provides single-cursor reads and first-release BSON SerDes. SQL filters and source projection have remained local, and the remaining M1 type and pushdown contracts need end-to-end qualification.

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: #70251 (D04b and D05)
Related PR: #70327 (native read path), #70456 (M0 acceptance), #70493 (session read policies)
PR Type: Feature

Problem Summary:

Complete the D04b qualification coverage and connect conservative predicate/LIKE candidates and column pruning to the native MongoDB reader. Every SQL predicate remains a Doris residual; the default strict type policy, strict SQL casts and standard views keep filtering local. This PR does not complete the separate D06 or later snapshot/parallel-scan work.

### Details

- **Change map:** 456 added production lines, 1,221 test/fixture/generated-result lines, and 47 documentation lines across 19 files. The production changes comprise a connector-local translator and scan planning, three session controls, two optional descriptor fields, and native find options/validation. Most additions qualify types and compare execution modes.
- **Scope:** D04b covers Decimal128 extremes, exact integer/floating-point behavior, UTC dates and scales, binary ownership/subtypes, missing/null, recursive arrays/structs, rollback and existing document limits. D05 covers typed scalar-root comparisons, positive IN/BETWEEN, scalar IS NOT NULL, safe AND/OR, necessary-literal LIKE candidates, root projection and time-series Date ranges.
- **Design:** Candidates are classified conservatively as SUPERSET; unsupported expressions remain local, and the EXACT category is reserved for proven equivalence. No conjunct is consumed through either SPI path. CASTs are rejected before the neutral converter can erase them. The translator reconciles the schema/expression SPI date-scale and decimal-width representations, including FE's DECIMAL128 name. Native BSON is bounded and validated before client acquisition; views cannot receive a predicate/collation override. Complete root projection retains residual columns and scalar-ancestor errors.
- **Usage:** Use `SET` or `SET_VAR` with `enable_mongodb_predicate_pushdown`, `enable_mongodb_like_pushdown` and `enable_mongodb_projection_pushdown`. Predicate candidates require the explicit catalog policy `mongodb.type_mismatch=null`.
- **Default behavior:** All three switches default to true. The default `type_mismatch=error` policy preserves local filtering; `enable_strict_cast=true` and views also preserve local filtering. Source projection is eligible independently. DOUBLE/NaN comparisons, NOT/!=/NOT IN, mismatch-sensitive IS NULL, functions, casts, nested predicate paths and existing direct VARBINARY operator restrictions stay local. LIKE keeps the complete SQL residual. LIMIT, aggregation, sort, joins, snapshots and parallel scans are unchanged.
- **Compatibility:** The connector SPI and stored schemas are unchanged. Descriptor fields 23/24 are optional; absent fields preserve the prior full scan. The touched descriptor is absent from the four supported release branches, so no field id is reused. Qualification uses matching FE/BE versions.

### Testing

All testing below ran locally against MongoDB 8.0.20 with authentication enabled and an ASAN BE:

- 64 MongoDB connector FE tests, 25 connector-session/forwarding tests, 3 session read-policy tests and 55 BSON/native-reader BE tests passed (147 total).
- All four MongoDB SQL suites passed: 4 suites, 0 failed, 0 fatal, 0 skipped. This includes the existing native and M0 acceptance suites, the session read-policy suite and the new M1 suite.
- The generated M1 output contains 40 identical sorted result pairs with predicate/LIKE/projection disabled and enabled. It covers precision, NULL/arrays, casts, collations, residual LIMIT, aggregates/joins, views and time-series reads. The completed Profile check reports `MongoRowsRead` of 10 with candidates disabled and 1 with them enabled.
- Source profiling independently confirmed actual BSON int64, Decimal128 and Date filters, projection, simple collection collation, and view reads without a collation override.
- Full FE and ASAN BE builds passed on the integrated master base; the SQL suites use that matching built pair. Full FE Checkstyle and the final affected-core-file Checkstyle run passed with zero violations. All affected C/C++ files pass clang-format 16, build hygiene and clang-tidy.
- Red/green checks reproduced missing candidate planning, acceptance of malformed BSON descriptors, missing strict-cast gating, command-budget gaps, schema/expression type representation gaps, and the false negative for ARRAY/JSON IS NOT NULL with null elements before the corresponding implementations.

### Release note

Native MongoDB scans can prune source fields and apply conservative WHERE/LIKE candidates under the explicit null-on-type-mismatch policy. SQL residuals remain active, and default strict scans and views preserve local filtering. New session switches allow statement-level comparisons and disabling these optimizations.

### Check List (For Author)

- Behavior changed: Yes (see Details).
- Does this need documentation: Yes; the connector and fixture READMEs are updated here.
- Pre-submission status: Ready. Local UT, authenticated SQL regression, builds and style/static checks passed; CI is pending.

### AI Disclosure

- Tool: Codex (GPT-6).
- Generated: Implementation, tests, fixture, documentation and this description.
- Human review: Pending maintainer review.

author: kodyazicam
body:
## Why

Stribog-Bot is documented as self-hosted but shipped no container path: no `Dockerfile`, no `docker-compose.yml`, no `.dockerignore` (issue #33). Self-hosters had to install Node, compile `better-sqlite3`, and keep a process alive by hand. `LogYazicam` and `discord-music-panel` already ship this, so the flagship bot was the odd one out.

## What changed

- `Dockerfile`: two stages. `deps` installs `python3 make g++` and runs `npm ci --omit=dev`; the runtime stage is `node:22-bookworm-slim`, copies only `node_modules`, `package.json`, `src`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, creates UID 10001, sets `NODE_ENV=production`, declares `VOLUME ["/app/data"]`, and runs `node src/index.js`. Nothing is copied from the build context, so `.env` and `data/` cannot leak into the image.
- `docker-compose.yml`: `env_file: .env`, `environment: NODE_ENV=production`, `init: true`, `restart: unless-stopped`, `no-new-privileges`, named volume `stribog-data:/app/data`. No published ports (the bot only makes outbound gateway connections).
- `.dockerignore`: excludes `.git`, `.github`, `.env*`, `data`, `logs`, `node_modules`, `coverage`, `tests`, logs/db files.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: new `docker` job (`docker build -t stribog:ci .`), mirroring the LogYazicam job. No login, no push.
- `README.md`: new "🐳 Docker" section (configure, build/run, deploy commands, backup/restore of the volume, upgrade) plus a TOC entry.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased/Added entry.
- `tests/deployment.test.js`: 8 config tests pinning the image, compose, ignore, CI, and README invariants.

Deliberate deviations from the issue text, with reasons:

- No `HEALTHCHECK`: the bot exposes no HTTP surface, so the only honest probe would be fake. The comment in the Dockerfile says this instead.
- No `stop_grace_period`: `src/index.js` registers no shutdown hooks, so a long grace period would only delay restarts. `init: true` handles signal forwarding and reaping.

## How tested

```
$ npm ci
pass (13 packages, 0 vulnerabilities)

$ node --test tests/deployment.test.js
pass 8 / fail 0

$ node --test tests/deployment.test.js   # same file, origin/main 060c403 tree
fail 8 / fail 0 pass (every file the tests assert is missing)

$ npm test                               # on this branch
pass 87 tests, 87 pass, 0 fail
Command docs check passed: 49 commands, 86 documented rows.

$ npm test                               # baseline, origin/main 060c403
pass 79 tests, 79 pass, 0 fail

$ python3 (PyYAML) safe_load docker-compose.yml
pass (services.bot.env_file=.env, volume stribog-data:/app/data, no ports key)
$ python3 (PyYAML) safe_load .github/workflows/ci.yml
pass (jobs test + docker)
```

Not verified locally: no Docker daemon is available on this host, so `docker build` itself is proven only by the new CI `docker` job (required checks stay `test` + CodeQL; the docker job is additive). No image is published.

## Risk and rollback

Risk: build time/CI minutes (a single image build), and `better-sqlite3` compile time on ARM64 during the first build. No application code changed, so runtime behaviour is untouched. Rollback: revert this commit; it only adds files and one CI job.

## Checklist

- [x] Closes #33
- [x] Focused diff (244 insertions, 7 files, no bot logic)
- [x] Regression tests added (red on `main`, green here)
- [x] Docs and CHANGELOG updated
- [x] No secrets, no `.env`, no database in the image or repo
- [x] Not merged; review left to the owner

author: autonomyai-local[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds a single, self-contained `TestCard` component that recreates the supplied Figma panel (the dark "UI magician Agent" form: title with a settings gear, a collapsed row, an "Add New Design" section with a token field and a design-URL field, two action buttons, and a "Recent Breakdowns" heading) at its design size of 254 × 508px.

This is a smoke test of the design-to-component path: it exists to prove that a Figma frame can be turned into a working React component in this repo. It is intentionally not a product feature and is not referenced by any route or screen. Fidelity was deliberately scoped — approximate spacing, colour and typography were explicitly acceptable, so the first render was accepted rather than iterated on.

## Key Changes

- Added a new prop-less, stateless `TestCard` component with a Tailwind-only layout.
- Root element is wrapped in `<div id="testElem">` as requested.
- Colours and dimensions are the exact values taken from the Figma export (panel `#1C1D17`; both fields `#272822` with `#A5ADAD` and `#929291` borders; buttons `#843A17` at a 4px radius), rather than eyeballed from the image.
- No existing file was modified.

## Files Changed

- `src/app/components/TestCard.tsx`
  - New file. Single exported component plus a default export.
  - Layout, colour and type are expressed entirely with Tailwind utility classes.
  - Colour values are written as arbitrary values (e.g. `bg-[#1C1D17]`) with an inline comment explaining why — see Implementation Notes.
  - Both inputs carry an `aria-label`, and the decorative icons are marked `aria-hidden`.

## Implementation Notes

- **Colour source.** `tailwind.config.js` replaces Tailwind's default palette with the app's semantic roles, and this design is a foreign dark panel with no equivalent role. Adding roles would have meant editing `src/app/styles/app.css`, which was out of scope for a one-file change, so the design's palette is written as arbitrary values scoped to this file. Worth revisiting if this component is ever promoted into real UI.
- **Type.** The design specifies Inter at weight 600. The repo loads only the CircularStd families, and adding Inter would have required editing an existing file, so the component uses the app's own `font-primary` family and its `text-xs` / `text-2xs` scale.
- **Icons.** The four icons are drawn with `react-icons`, which is already a dependency and already the repo's habit, rather than copying the Figma export's raster assets (which would have added files).
- The component has no props, state, data fetching or event handlers, and deliberately does not suppress the app's global focus outline on its inputs.

## How to Test

1. Open the component in the Studio preview (Storybook target) — it renders as the `Default` variant under `Components/TestCard`.
2. Confirm the panel shows: the "UI magician Agent" title with a gear at the right, a chevron row reading "From entire frame to a singl...", an "Add New Design" row, both labelled fields with their placeholders, the two buttons reading "Awesome" and "Prepare", and the "Recent Breakdowns" heading.
3. Confirm nothing is clipped, overlapping or blank, and that the dark panel background and field borders are present.
4. Tab through the fields to confirm focus still behaves normally.

## Compatibility & Notes

- Purely additive: one new file, no existing file touched, no route wired up, no new dependency.
- No breaking changes.
- The component is not rendered anywhere in the running app yet — it is reachable only through the component preview.

## QA Checklist

- [x] Core functionality works as expected
- [x] Visual/UI changes render correctly
- [x] Hover/active/interactive states behave properly
- [ ] Responsive behavior verified
- [x] Accessibility considerations addressed (alt text, ARIA, contrast, etc.)
- [x] No unintended side effects or regressions

Responsive behaviour is left unchecked on purpose: the panel is a fixed 254px recreation of a Figma frame, so it has no responsive variants.

author: michael-tracey
body:
Closes #1000.

## What changed
- **New shared component** `frontend/src/components/AboutTrait.tsx` (own file, per the UX wave brief): `AboutButton` (the TraitInfo chevron as its own button, 40 px on touch) and `AboutTrait` (what opens under the row). It shows the trait's summary, the troupe's own wording and house rule, links to its written house rules, the book page and, for a discipline, its test pool and the power(s) the next dot gives.
- **Where it went:**
  - Sheet editor, **Add** panel (`AddTraitPanel.tsx`): every row of every category. The chevron sits before the row's choose button, so greyed (refused) rows still open, and opening one chooses nothing. For a discipline it shows the next dot above the character's rating. The chosen-trait form also lists the powers up to the rating picked.
  - Sheet tab: a held discipline's existing panel now also says what its **next** dot gives (the + button's dot).
  - Creation wizard: discipline **slots** (`Slots.tsx`) now allow several open at once and show the powers the slot's dots give ("Dots 1 to 3 give:"); a ghoul's **dot grid** (`DotGrid.tsx`) shows the dots its budget allows. Other wizard lists gain the page too, as they share the component.
  - NPC builder (`NpcBuilder.tsx`): every row (Techniques, Elder & luminary powers, Rituals, Disciplines, skills, merits...), with a discipline's next dot.
- **API:** `GET /rules/{splat}/powers` returns each dot's power note and each discipline's test pool, from the power reference the Pools tab already uses (ETag'd like the catalogue). It is asked for only when a discipline is opened, so the catalogue doesn't grow by ~32 KB. `npm run api` regenerated.
- **Rules data:** 120 of 124 techniques had no description or page, so opening one would have said nothing. Each now has a one-line summary in our own words (cost, action, test, effect) and its page: core pp. 225-233, Vol. 2 pp. 83-91, Vol. 2 Issue 1 pp. 56-86. A new test (`test_catalogue_descriptions.py`) requires a summary and page on every technique, elder and luminary power. Elder and luminary powers already had them.
- Manual (`docs/manual/players.md`): the chevron in the Add panel and wizard slots, and the next dot on the sheet.

## Which lists got it
- Sheet editor Add panel: yes, every category of power.
- Creation wizard: yes, in its discipline slots and a ghoul's discipline dots. The wizard has no technique, elder power or ritual lists.
- NPC builder: yes, every section.
- `KeywordFields.tsx` ("A discipline dot, a technique or an elder power"): **no**. It's a free-text box, not a list, so there is nothing to expand. Spend XP goes through the Add panel, which has it.

## Decisions
- **Discipline dots:** the Add panel lists only disciplines not yet held, so its rows show dot 1 (or the held rating + 1). Wizard slots show dots 1 to the slot's rating, and a ghoul's grid shows dots 1 to its maximum, since those are the dots a pick there gives. The NPC builder and the sheet show the next dot above the current rating.
- **Expander only, no hover preview:** the chevron works everywhere, and a hover preview would show the same text a second way.
- **Separate endpoint, not on the catalogue:** this keeps the catalogue under its size budget (#642), and the notes are fetched only when a discipline is opened.
- **Not done: rituals.** 161 of 181 rituals have no summary or page, so their rows have no chevron yet; they'll get one as soon as the data has text. Writing them is a book-reading job of the same size again, so it's left for a follow-up issue.
- Technique pages follow the book itself. For example, Retain the Quick Blood is core p. 231, not the Vol. 2 p. 269 that its Diluted Blood check cites.

## Before / after
Before, a row in these lists showed only the name; you had to choose it to read its description, which disciplines didn't give powers for. After, a chevron at the start of the row opens the text in place. The new e2e test checks this at 375 px (with no horizontal scroll), and the desktop project runs at 1280 px.

author: jsboige
body:
Grain: MED/guard — lane myia-po-2028:CoursIA — prev: DEEP/notebook-python #26831

Répare `scripts/notebook_tools/check_slot_reservation.py` sur les deux classes de faux refus nommées par le dispatch ai-01 du 2026-11-16. Deux fichiers, aucun harnais touché (pas de `.claude/`, ni `CLAUDE.md`, ni `.github/`).

## (a) L'artefact de squash — un ajout byte-identique à la base n'est pas une prise

**Cause racine** : `added_notebooks` calcule les ajouts depuis le **merge-base** (`base...head`). Une branche empilée dont la mère a été squash-mergeée voit donc remonter comme « ajout » un fichier dont le contenu exact vit déjà sur la base — la PR ne prend aucun numéro, et le refus bloquait une pile entière.

**Fix** : `squash_artifacts()` (`git ls-tree` tête et base, blob OID comparés) écarte ces chemins des cibles **en mode révision seulement**, avant tout verdict, et le **dit** :

```
2 artefact(s) de squash écarté(s) -- blob identique à la base, pas une prise de slot :
  MyIA.AI.Notebooks/Physique/Chaines/Chaines-04-Indiscernabilite-Spin-Statistique-Python.ipynb,
  MyIA.AI.Notebooks/Physique/Chaines/Chaines-05-Energie-Hamiltonien-Premiere-Puissance-Python.ipynb
```

Le compte vit aussi dans le JSON (`sources.revision.squash_artifacts`).

- **Témoin négatif conservé** : même chemin au contenu **différent** sur la base = une réécriture → `taken_on_base` inchangé (test dédié).
- **Mode `--target` non touché** : y viser le nom exact d'un fichier de la base reste une prise, byte-identique ou non — c'est le sens du preflight avant édition (test dédié).
- **Inertie prouvée pour une PR normale** : merge-base == base ⇒ un `diff-filter=A` ne peut pas exister à la base ⇒ artefact vide, sortie inchangée (les 59 tests préexistants passent sans modification, dont l'assertion exacte `revision  : 0 cible(s) examinee(s)`).

## (b) L'ancienneté des PR ouvertes — l'aînée passe, la plus jeune cède

**Cause racine** : `pr_claims()` construisait `{slot: [Occupant]}` depuis **toutes** les PRs ouvertes sans tie-break d'âge. Deux PRs ouvertes qui revendiquent le même numéro se bloquaient **mutuellement** : chaque examen voyait l'autre comme occupant, aucune ne pouvait merger (mesure : #26585 du 14/11 contre #26710 du 15/11 sur `02-Advanced/02-11`).

**Fix** : `pr_claims(prs, removed, examined_pr)` — une PR ouverte ne réserve son numéro que contre une PR **strictement plus jeune** qu'elle. La clé d'anciennete est le **numéro de PR** (choix documenté en docstring, comme demandé) : GitHub l'alloue séquentiellement à la création, l'ordre des numéros est donc l'ordre d'ouverture — sans appel API supplémentaire, déterministe hors ligne.

- La référence est `--exclude-pr` (la PR examinée) : **déjà passé par `merge_ready.py:1545`** — contrat d'interface inchangé, zéro modification côté consommateur.
- Sans `--exclude-pr` : comportement inchangé, tout claimant réserve (test).
- L'égalité (la PR examinée elle-même) ne réserve jamais — pas d'auto-blocage (test).
- Numéro illisible (charge malformée) : la claim **reste** — fail-closed (test).
- La règle s'écrit, elle ne se devine pas : ligne `anciennete:` dans la sortie humaine + champ `age_rule` dans le JSON.

## Contrôles mesurés sur le dépôt vivant (têtes re-fetchées à l'instant)

| Contrôle du dispatch | Mesure firsthand | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Tête #25027 (`ed249806b`) doit passer | `--exclude-pr 25027` en ligne | **rc=0** — 2 artefacts écartés (Chaines-04, Chaines-05), Chaines-06 libre |
| #26585 (ancienne, approved) sur `02-Advanced/02-11` | `--exclude-pr 26585` en ligne | **rc=0** — 108 PRs plus jeunes ignorées, `02-11-AudioGen` libre |
| #26710 (récente) sur le même slot | `--exclude-pr 26710` en ligne | **rc=1** — `reserved_by_open_pr` citant `#26585` : la plus jeune cède, c'est elle qui renumérote |
| Même-nom-contenu-différent | dépôt temporaire, contenu divergent sur la base | **rc=1, `taken_on_base`** — témoin négatif intact |

#26710 visait toujours `02-11-SVS-Singing-Voice-RVC` à l'instant de la mesure (aucune renumérotation par po-2027 encore poussée) : les deux membres du couple restent ouverts, le garde rend maintenant la asymétrie correcte au lieu d'un blocage mutuel.

## Tests

- Self-test : **48 cas, 0 échec** (+4 scénarios ancienneté : aînée réserve, jeune ne réserve pas, sans-référence tout réserve, pas d'auto-réservation).
- Pytest : **70 passed** (+11 : 4 end-to-end squash-artefact dont le témoin négatif contenu-différent et le non-touché du mode `--target` ; 5 unitaires sur la règle d'âge).
- Aucun test préexistant modifié.

Sans issue porteuse : dispatch DM ai-01 du 2026-11-16 (dispatch-slot-organ-po2028-20261116), accuse livre par DM.

author: gdamalis
body:
# Description

The website's cached MongoDB client set only `serverApi`, so it inherited the driver default `maxPoolSize` of 100 per server. Atlas M0 allows 500 connections across the whole cluster, and `apps/admin` will add a second pool. This PR gives the client an explicit, small pool cap and makes idle instances release their connections.

Ticket: [ICR-157](https://linear.app/divinelab/issue/ICR-157/cap-mongodb-maxpoolsize-on-the-cached-client-free-tier-connection)
Type: fix

# Changes

- `apps/web/src/service/database.service.ts`: `MONGODB_OPTIONS` is now exported and `satisfies MongoClientOptions`. It adds `maxPoolSize: 10` and `maxIdleTimeMS: 60000`. `minPoolSize` is deliberately not set (already 0 by default, so setting it would be documentation, not a fix).
- `apps/web/src/service/database.service.test.ts`: new test asserts the client is constructed with those options and without `minPoolSize`.
- `apps/web/scripts/check-mongo-pool.mjs` and `check-mongo-pool.test.mjs`: guarded pool-check script with tests, exposed as the `mongo:pool-check` package script. The script loads `.env.pool-check` (not `.env.local`, which points at production and is refused).
- `docs/architecture/likes-and-mongodb.md`: docs updated with a new "Connection pool cap" section, including the measured results.
- `.changeset/icr-157-mongo-pool-cap.md`: `@idcr/web` patch changeset.
- `tasks/specs/ICR-157-cap-mongodb-pool-size.md` and `.plan.md`: spec and implementation plan.
- Consumers of the shared client (no code change): likes (`/api/likes`), the contact form server action, predica `pdfJobs`, `broadcastLog`.

Commits: 45a8d61 spec and plan, 96829f8 pool options and test, 136b261 guarded check script, tests and `mongo:pool-check` script, 0e1151f docs section and changeset, b4c1b33 package script loads `.env.pool-check`, d5c52e1 measured results in docs.

## Driver facts

- Installed `mongodb` driver: 6.21.0 (`apps/web` declares `^6.20.0`).
- Documented defaults: `maxPoolSize` 100 (per server, per `MongoClient`), `minPoolSize` 0, `maxIdleTimeMS` 0 (no limit), `waitQueueTimeoutMS` 0 (unbounded queue when the pool is full). Up to 2 monitoring sockets per server sit outside the pool.
- Sources: [connection pools](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/) (current docs are v7.x; the v6.21 API reference lists no defaults) and [Atlas connection management for AWS Lambda](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-connections-aws-lambda/), which recommends `maxIdleTimeMS` 60000.
- This PR sets `maxPoolSize` 10 and `maxIdleTimeMS` 60000.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm type-check` (verifier, standard depth: pass)
- [x] `pnpm lint` (pass)
- [x] `pnpm test` (Vitest: web 658/658, admin 430/430)
- [x] `pnpm build` (pass; the first attempt failed only because the fresh worktree had no `apps/web/.env.local`, no code change)
- [x] Live pool check against website-staging: capped peak of 10 connections at both 200 and 500 concurrency (baseline without the cap: 13 and 19). Evidence: [pool-check comment](https://github.com/gdamalis/idc-redentor-platform/pull/132#issuecomment-6907297782)
- [x] Manual smoke on the Vercel preview deployment (QA passed, acceptance judge 6/6): [QA evidence](https://github.com/gdamalis/idc-redentor-platform/pull/132#issuecomment-6907423483)

Preview: https://idc-redentor-3euon7q1v-divine-lab.vercel.app

## Known CI issue

The trace-guard job fails because Contentful returns an invalid-access-token error during the `/sitemap.xml` prerender in CI. This is an invalid CI secret, unrelated to this change. It needs the GitHub Actions Contentful token refreshed.

## Screenshots

QA captured screenshots on the issue and in the QA PR comment above.

## i18n

- [x] N/A: no user-facing copy changed.

## Risk & rollback

Sensitive area: likes-mongo (shared Mongo write path). A cap of 10 per instance is well above what likes and contact traffic need, but `waitQueueTimeoutMS` stays unbounded, so a saturated pool would queue rather than fail. Rollback = revert this PR.

author: thinkula
body:
Thirteen of the twenty-seven dishes in a Basque cooking game were not named in Basque — twelve Spanish, one English. (I'd said eleven earlier; I undercounted.)

| was | now | built from |
|---|---|---|
| Bacalao Pil Pil | **Bakailaoa pil-pilean** | bakailaoa + pil-pil saltsa |
| Tortilla Española | **Patata-tortilla** | patata + tortilla |
| Pollo al Txakoli | **Oilaskoa txakolinarekin** | oilaskoa + txakolina |
| Alubias de Tolosa | **Tolosako babarrunak** | babarrunak |
| Merluza en Salsa Verde | **Legatza saltsa berdean** | legatza + saltsa + berdea |
| Txuleta a la Parrilla | **Txuleta errea** | txuleta + erre |
| Arroz con Leche | **Esne-arroza** | esnea + arroza |
| Patatas Fritas Caseras | **Patata frijituak** | patata + frijitu |
| Menú del Día | **Eguneko menua** | eguna + menua |
| Pastel Vasco | **Euskal pastela** | pastela |
| Ensalada Vasca | **Euskal entsalada** | entsalada ¹ |
| Revuelto de Hongos | **Onddo-nahaskia** | onddo + nahaski ¹ |
| Pintxo Bar Crawl | **Pintxo-poteoa** | pintxo + poteo ¹ |

¹ not in the vocabulary — as *Marmitakoa* and *Gaztaopila* already weren't. Dish titles are copy, not quiz answers.

Two more weren't Spanish but were malformed: an ampersand where this app writes *eta*, and *Sagardotegi Plater* with neither the genitive nor the article → **Txakolina eta pintxoak**, **Sagardotegiko platera**. Six titles carrying an inner capital are now sentence case.

## The rename broke the migration, which is why it was tested

A save written before #162 holds display names, not keys. The migration mapped such a name by matching it against the *current* dish names — and those are exactly the names this PR translated away.

```
seeded : ["Bacalao Pil Pil","Arroz con Leche","tortilla_espanola","Pintxoak"]
result : ["tortilla_espanola","pintxoak"]        →  "Served 2 of 27"
```

**Every Kitchen player alive is still on name-based storage**, because 1.7 hasn't shipped. All of them would have opened it to find the Cooked badge gone from each dish renamed here — the exact failure the keys were added to prevent, reintroduced by the first rename they were meant to make safe.

Every key is the slug of the title its dish carried when the key was written, so the migration now slugs a stored name as a last resort. All 27 retired 1.6 titles resolve, accents and ampersand included:

```
seeded : ["Bacalao Pil Pil","Arroz con Leche","Menú del Día",
          "Txakolina & Pintxo","tortilla_espanola","Pintxoak",
          "A Dish That Never Existed"]
result : 6 keys, phantom dropped        →  "Served 6 of 27 dishes"
```

Bakailaoa pil-pilean keeps the badge earned under Bacalao Pil Pil.

**The keys themselves stay as they are.** Several still read as Spanish; a comment now says why touching them would cost people their progress.

## One I am not sure of

**Onddo-nahaskia** for the revuelto. *Nahaski* is the word I believe Basque menus use for a scramble, but it isn't in this vocabulary and I can't verify it the way I verified the rest. **Onddoak eta arrautzak** would be plainer and certainly correct if that reads wrong to you — say the word and I'll change it.

## Verification

`check-vocab` clean. `check-lessons` clean, 0 warnings. The kitchen data check passes: all 135 stages resolve, no hint leads with the wrong Basque word. No vocabulary or lesson data touched.

author: abhishekgml1991
body:
## Description Today the indexing service's concurrency limits are fixed numbers (an in-flight total of 96, light parse 256, and so on), whatever size the container is. This PR adds one place, `app/capacity/`, that reads what the container has (cgroup v2/v1 CPU quota and memory limit, CPU affinity, host memory, NUMA nodes, GPUs, pod requests) and plans how each service is sized from it. - **`legacy` profile (default):** the plan reproduces every existing limit, with the source of each value recorded. Nothing is sized differently. - **`auto` profile (opt-in, `PIPESHUB_CAPACITY_PROFILE=auto`):** a pure plan and set of budget rules: governor ceilings that scale above 16 CPUs (in-flight total `max(24, 6 x cpus)`, instead of 96), cells (one indexing process per ~16 CPUs), per-service member budgets (Docling, embedding, query embedding, inspect, parse) with floors, an LLM call cap per LLM-calling service, and optional one-NUMA-node pinning per cell. In this PR the `auto` plan and its rules are computed and logged but nothing enforces them yet. - **Start-up line:** every service logs one `capacity: service= omp= profile=

...` line (once, from the service's main process). - **Several indexing workers (`INDEXING_UVICORN_WORKERS` > 1):** each worker claims a cell index with a file lock that dies with the process and publishes its governor stats to `/pipeshub-indexing-cells-/.json`. `/health` of whichever worker answers adds a `cells` block and returns 503 when a cell reports a dead loop, has not written for 3 ticks, or its file is unreadable. A `/health` read takes no lock and deletes nothing, so it can never make a starting worker lose its index. The directory must belong to the service's user and not be writable by others; files are opened without following links. One worker: the `/health` body is unchanged. - **Container wiring:** `process_monitor.sh` runs the facts helper once, never evaluates what it prints, and exports only a `PIPESHUB_CAPACITY_FACTS=` line that passes a character and size check. The image sets `PIPESHUB_OMP_DEFAULT=2` instead of `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2` (an `OMP_NUM_THREADS` set by the operator still wins). Compose and Helm pass the new knobs through, and blank values are treated as unset. ### Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Documentation update - [ ] Performance improvement - [x] Code refactoring - [ ] Security fix ## How Has This Been Tested? - **Legacy is unchanged.** A frozen copy of the old limits is compared with the plan over 4 constant sets x 14 400 rows (57 600) and over 7 680 more rows for `auto` at 16 CPUs or fewer: every row is equal. A control run with `INDEX_TOTAL_MAX=97` fails the comparison. The thread environment (`OMP_NUM_THREADS` and related) is byte-identical at every size. - **Plan tests:** profiles from 0.5 to 256 CPUs with memory and GPU edges, monotonicity from 16 to 512 CPUs in 0.25 steps, a partition and widths contract, NUMA mask handling, bounds on every knob (nonsense values keep the default and add an `invalid_` warning), and budget rules (owner-first sharing, large and huge work caps, reserve use) against a simulation that uses the real admit and grant functions. - **Cells:** claim, read and write behaviour including a planted symlink or hard link, an unsafe or foreign directory, a non-object stats file, a replacement cell, and a concurrent-reader test (2 forked readers, more than 1 000 claims, 0 missed). A real two-worker uvicorn integration test returns the same `cells` block from both workers. The product's own `lifespan` is tested to claim, publish and release. - **`process_monitor.sh`:** the facts export survives a failing helper, a banner and injected lines (`$(...)`, backticks, `;`), runs none of them, and a mutation that evaluates every printed line is caught. - **Gates run locally on the committed tree:** `new_lint_findings.py` for ruff, log-emoji and log-pii (no new findings), `scripts/connector_coverage.py --check`, `tests/unit/core/test_org_context_guards.py`, `tests/unit/services/resource_governor/test_policy_off_pin.py` (the governor is not edited), the integration-suite guards, and the `scripts` unittest suite. The full Python unit suite result is at the end of this description. - Not run: a full image build and stack boot, a `helm template` render (no helm binary here), non-Linux behaviour, and live throughput measurements of the `auto` plan (nothing is enforced yet). ### Test Configuration - [x] Unit tests pass - [x] Integration tests pass (two-worker `/health` test) - [ ] Manual testing completed ## Off / legacy guarantee With `PIPESHUB_CAPACITY_PROFILE` unset or any value other than `auto`, every limit, width and thread count is what it was before, verified by the frozen comparison above. The resource governor modules are not edited. With one indexing worker the `/health` body is unchanged. author: maxsam4
body:
Lean-core lane B: installer handover items I1 and I5, plus the CLI part of unit 5d. The distro installer (`install.sh`) hands over to `ops/setup.sh` without a config file or a terminal, from a checkout anywhere on disk, and wants the runner sized for the machine.

**I1: no hard-coded home or checkout**
- `ops/setup.sh` and `ops/vault/init.sh` read the user's home from `getent`. Setup no longer requires `~/aidenhq`. The checkout path must be plain characters, because it goes into a systemd environment file.
- The user units now run `${AIDENHQ_DIR}/…`. They default to `Environment=AIDENHQ_DIR=%h/aidenhq` and override it from `EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/aidenhq-checkout.env`, which setup writes.
- The live host has no such file, so it keeps `~/aidenhq` and needs no migration. Its units still change, so the next apply re-copies the runner and kernel units.
- The expansion and the override were checked in a systemd 255 container: without the file the unit ran from `/root/aidenhq`, with it from `/srv/other`.

**I5: sizing**
- `MAX_CONCURRENT` (1–64) and `TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (5–1440) come from the config or the environment and are range-checked. They set the top-level keys in `config/runner.yaml`. A runner that was already running gets SIGUSR2.
- `CI_RUNNERS` (0–32) is kept in `.env` as `AIDENHQ_CI_RUNNERS`. It enables `aidenhq-ci-runner@1..N` once the GitHub App key exists and `instance.yaml` lists `ci`. Until then setup says so, and a rerun starts them.

**5d CLI: `--unattended [--no-tailscale]`**
- No config file and no questions. Settings that aren't secrets may come from the environment (the file wins): `AIDENHQ_USER`, `OWNER_*`, `TIMEZONE`, `MODULES`, the sizing knobs and so on. Secrets come only from a file passed with `--config`.
- The owner's name defaults to the user name and the timezone to the host's.
- A missing model key is allowed: setup skips the key check, and Aiden's welcome chat waits for the key without writing its marker. The end of the run says how to add the key. A keyless apply is untested on a live host: the kernel answers 503 without a key, but `paperclip-setup.mjs` waits up to 3 minutes per new agent for Paperclip's verification. That step only warns, but a first install with no key may be slow.
- **`OWNER_EMAIL` is still required.** The board's existing setup link (`POST /api/accounts/setup` with `board_operator_key`) is made for an email, and the board was not widened. This goes away when the first-run `/setup` page asks for the email. setup stops before any change if `OWNER_EMAIL` is missing.
- The last machine line is `AIDENHQ_SETUP_URL=<link>`, printed only when the board returned an `http(s)://` URL. If the owner already exists (HTTP 409), there is no line and setup points to `--reset`. Any other failure, such as a board that never came up or a 400, now stops setup. Before, it printed "already exists" and exited 0.
- Tailscale:
  - setup uses the host's tailnet name, or joins with `TS_AUTHKEY`, or prints the sign-in link on `/dev/tty`.
  - With no terminal and no key it stops before any change and names `--no-tailscale`.
  - `--no-tailscale` passes `AIDENHQ_NO_TAILSCALE=1` to `ops/vm/setup.sh` (#104) and sets `BOARD_LAN_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3121` (hosts `127.0.0.1:3121,localhost:3121`). It skips the apps node and `tailscale serve`, and prints the tunnel command, also as `AIDENHQ_SSH_TUNNEL=ssh -N -L 3121:127.0.0.1:3121 <user>@<host>`.

**Not in this PR:** the first-run web page, running setup's root steps from a root-owned verified copy (`/opt/aidenhq/kernel/<sha>`), and a private kernel repo token. These belong to unit 5d's later parts. The tunnel route has not yet been exercised end to end on a real host.

**Tested.** In throwaway Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 and Debian 12 and 13 containers, with the checkout at `/opt/checkout` and the user's home at `/srv/home/alice`:
- the classic `--config` dry run and the unattended `--no-tailscale` dry run print the right plan, with no secrets;
- real runs stop before any change when `OWNER_EMAIL` is missing, when there is no tailnet, key or terminal, and when the user is unknown.

`shellcheck -S warning` is clean. `scripts/test/setup.test.mjs` adds one unattended test. The scripts suite fails only the macOS-only flock tests and the lean counter, which the ratchet owner updates.

author: mechiland
body:
## What

Eveland now hosts eve `>=1.0.0 <1.1.0` (verified `1.0.0`). The floor stays at 1.0.0 for all of 1.x. Verifying a newer minor only raises the ceiling, so a Release that was inside the window when it was built stays inside it.

**Where the window is enforced**
- Import (and the `eveland deploy` local preflight) accepts any declared npm range that can resolve inside the window (`semver.intersects`). That includes the `"^1.0.0"` that `eve init` writes. `^1.0.0` used to be refused.
- The build reads the eve version it actually installed (`node_modules/eve`). If that version is outside the window or cannot be read, the build fails and records no Release. Both runtimes do this: Docker in `readImageDiscovery`, systemd in `readReleaseDiscovery`.

**Machinery removed** (a Release can no longer fall out of the window)
- The Agent Gateway's per-request version gate and its memoizing cache.
- On the API: the activation-time refusal, the 409 mapping for the launch-path message, and the Playground 409.
- On the worker: the activation refusal. The orphaned-run settlement and dispatcher preflight still exist but no longer use the eve version. `permanentDeploymentActivationRefusal` moved to `core/workflow-dispatch` and only judges missing or archived Deployments.
- In the Dashboard: the current/upgrade/unsupported version states, the "Cannot start" badge, and the Playground lock. The Dashboard now just shows the version.

**Contracts and code**
- The policy is now two constants, `SUPPORTED_EVE_RANGE` and `VERIFIED_EVE_VERSION`. Removed: the `supportedLines` array, `hostsReleaseCandidates`, `peerDependencyRange`, about 190 lines of dated comments, the `source.ts` re-exports, and the `eve-sdk-peer` catalog.
- `EveVersionInfo` is now `{ version, sourceRevisionId }`.
- `GET /api/instance` returns `eve: { supportedRange, verifiedVersion }`. The CLI checks against it with `semver` and no longer carries its hand-copied grammar. Older CLIs are not kept compatible.
- `injectModelGateway` loses its `eveVersion` parameter. A caret declaration used to skip Model Gateway injection silently.
- The scheduler adapter no longer re-reads the declared eve version.
- The `eveland` package's peer range is now `eve >=1.0.0 <2.0.0`.

**Ratchets**
- `eve-compatibility-consistency.test.ts` drops from 602 to about 270 lines. It still audits the stable workflow names, now against the single installed eve.
- `eve-workflow-world-contract.test.ts` loses its multi-line `EVE_LINES` and its version floors.
- The retired-version list in `source.test.ts` is gone.

**Docs**
- `docs/{en,zh}/reference/eve-compatibility.md` is rewritten from about 35 KB to one page: the window, how to declare eve, enforcement, a version pairing table, and the protocol baseline.
- `spec.md` (the window section), the dashboard, source-import, first-deployment and environment-variables pages, and the SDK README are updated.

Not in this PR: removing release-candidate hosting (the v15 discovery manifest, rc fixtures, the observer/scheduler matrix, the forced-kill constant). That follows separately.

## Verification

- Full `pnpm test`. Every package passes, including api (291), worker (612), web (251), architecture-tests and db.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt:check`, `pnpm build` (includes the web and docs production builds), and `git diff --check`.
- Not run: `bash infra/integration/run.sh`. The real systemd/Docker build gate on the installed eve version still needs a Lima run.

BREAKING CHANGE: `GET /api/instance` returns `eve: { supportedRange, verifiedVersion }`. A build whose installed eve is outside the window fails. Releases built on eve release candidates are unsupported. The `eveland` package no longer accepts an eve release-candidate peer.

author: bghtyu
body:
## Summary

Improve keyboard access, field-error feedback and retry behavior across desktop forms and investment views.

## Rationale

Custom entity selection and disconnected error messages made keyboard correction difficult. Retrying an initial load also replaced the focused button with a loading view, sending users back to the sidebar after another failure.

## Main changes

- Reuse the shared filterable selector for EntitySelect, including keyboard/IME behavior and portal positioning.
- Associate client and server field errors with controls, focus the first actionable error, and clarify missing-owner guidance. Carry structured Unicode character limits through domain and IPC errors into localized messages.
- Keep retry actions pending until their requests settle, prevent duplicate activation, and allow another attempt after failure. Retain the instrument-list retry button across loading/error transitions, including WebKit pointer focus behavior, without stealing focus after users move away.
- Give instrument edit actions distinct accessible names; add regression coverage and update shared-control/IPC contracts.

## Validation

Head: `a6b3192243e49b32f2907df0c8a6a5986bcfbbdc`.

- [ ] Full `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` on this head: left to CI. Local affected packages `internal/domain` and `internal/wailsapi/apierror` passed on this head.
- [x] Native macOS application build. The acceptance build used a temporary backend-only fault overlay; it is not an unmodified release artifact.
- [x] Frontend lint, typecheck and production build passed. Full suite: **204 files / 2,293 tests** before the last pointer-focus guard adjustment; final affected tests: **46 passed** after it, with changed-file lint and production build rerun.
- [x] Changed Go files are gofmt-clean; `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Native macOS 27.2.1 / Apple Silicon acceptance with the established development identity and isolated synthetic database/settings:
  - Earlier form/selector checks covered error hints and focus, Chinese input, long lists and narrow-window positioning. User-assisted VoiceOver confirmation on `09c9dfb9` heard both “Name” and “Use 120 characters or fewer”.
  - Final retry acceptance used controlled hold/fail/success responses: click/Enter/Space deduplication, persistent focus through repeated failure, direct Enter retry, no focus stealing after moving away, successful recovery and quit/relaunch persistence. The tested source patch exactly matches this head's final commit.
  - VoiceOver was intentionally **not rerun** for the retry/focus changes; no system settings or real ledger data were changed.

Performance: no benchmark claim; retries reuse existing queries and controls. The existing large-bundle warning remains.

Remaining scope: successful content replacement still releases focus to the page content root; this PR preserves focus through pending/error transitions. Native coverage is representative, not an exhaustive pass over every retry caller.

## Screenshots or recordings

Not attached; native accessibility-tree observations and request counts were used for interaction verification.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and does not include unrelated files.
- [x] Tests and documentation are updated where needed.
- [x] No credentials, private financial data, real database files, or machine-specific paths are included.
- [x] Acceptance checks used isolated synthetic data.
- [x] Financial values do not use binary floating point.
