author: kaantpcc
body:
- **Recorded time:** The ledger stamps every new transaction with the time it was recorded. It takes a `Clock` in its constructor: `new InMemoryLedger(Clock.systemUTC())`. There is no default clock, so the library never reads system time on its own. Callers cannot set or backdate the recorded time.
- **Value date:** Optional, set with `Transaction.builder(...).valueDate(LocalDate)`. When it is missing, the recording day in the clock's time zone is used.
- **Description:** Optional, set with `.description(String)`. If given, it must not be blank.
- Value date and description are part of the transaction's content. Reusing a key with a different value date or description is an idempotency conflict.
- **`PostedTransaction(transaction, recordedAt, valueDate)`:** Wraps a recorded transaction with its recorded time. The value date is always present here. It can be read with `LedgerReader.posted(IdempotencyKey)`, which returns an `Optional`.
- **Timing rules:**
  - Retries of an accepted transaction keep the first recorded time.
  - A reversal gets its own recorded time and carries no value date or description.
  - Rejected transactions are not stamped.

The ledger had no notion of time, so it could not answer "when was this recorded?" for audits and disputes, or "since when does this money count?". The second question is the value date: a transfer recorded on Friday evening can be value-dated Monday. Upcoming date-based queries, such as balance as of a date, build on this.

## Tests

- `TransactionBuilderTest`: optional value date and description, blank and null handling.
- `LedgerContractTest`: the same key with a different description is rejected.
- New contract `LedgerTimeContractTest` with `InMemoryLedgerTimeTest`, using an adjustable test clock:
  - recorded time
  - default and explicit value dates, including the day boundary in the clock's time zone
  - an unknown key returns empty
  - rejected transactions are not stamped
  - a reversal gets its own time
  - a retry keeps the first time
  - a null clock is rejected

author: kjursa
body:
Characters, avatar jobs, story generation/status/retry and story listing/reading currently mix generic results with transport exceptions and client-owned business-error mappers. Apply the existing Places contract/result model consistently across all operations.

- Share serializable operation errors in api/contracts, including flat validation codes and forward-compatible Unknown(code). Keep typed validation field/reason values inside those contract objects; clients no longer parse combinations or translate duplicate error classes.
- Give each SDK operation its own Success/ApiError/TechnicalError result. Reuse one HTTP decoder and exception boundary: every 5xx becomes TechnicalError.Server before body parsing; every other Exception becomes Communication; cancellation propagates and fatal Errors are not caught. Payload-free writes accept all 2xx.
- Make backend routes send shared business-error objects through one BusinessApiException handler. Requests and success payloads reuse shared contracts. Preserve raw story JSON for canonical idempotency binding, including null versus omitted fields.
- Integrate results into mobile repositories/fakes and import story DTOs directly from contracts. Preserve local-first writes, deletion tombstones, offline/error UI behavior, atomic library refresh, polling and persisted retry keys after uncertain acceptance.
- Remove obsolete ApiResult, client-side error models/mappers and mobile story DTO aliases. Update API guidance and endpoint/mobile documentation.

Validation: ./test-all passed (API JVM, backend, and mobile unit/host tests). Added cross-operation coverage for server/communication failures, malformed success payloads, known/future shared errors, cancellation, idempotent deletion and payload-free 2xx writes. Contract tests round-trip all known/future errors through operation and backend serializers. Existing mobile tests verify cache preservation and submission/retry recovery. Ran mobile ktlintFormat; remaining lint findings are ignored per repository guidance.

This changes remaining SDK result signatures and validation wire codes to the agreed flat format; backend and mobile consumers are updated together. Existing non-validation machine codes and success payload shapes are preserved.

author: yonnock
body:
## TL;DR: Was ändert sich für Nutzer?

Lange Seiten mit vielen Karten scrollen flüssig, auch auf schwachen Tablets und Telefonen. Optisch bleibt alles gleich: Karten, Leisten und Kopfzeile waren schon fast deckend weiß, jetzt sind sie es ganz. Der Ladebildschirm über die ganze Seite ist jetzt rein weiß.

## Warum und Umsetzung

Nach #7252 (Cmd+K) die gleiche Ursache im ganzen Frontend gesucht: Animationen und Flächen, die der Browser nicht dem Compositor überlassen kann.

- **Weichzeichner unter jeder Karte:** `.moto-content-surface` hatte `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` unter einer deckend weißen Fläche. Das Ergebnis war unsichtbar, kostete aber beim Scrollen jedes Bild. Jetzt `isolation: isolate`: Die Karte bleibt ein eigener Stapelkontext wie vorher, also verschieben sich keine Ebenen (`:has([aria-expanded])`-Anhebung, FAB-Portal).
- **Leisten** (Kopfzeile, untere Navigation, Speicher- und Auswahlleiste, Filtertafel, Hilfe-Kopf): Weichzeichner entfernt, `bg-white/95` → `bg-white`. Ohne Weichzeichner würde der Inhalt darunter sonst scharf durchscheinen. Hover auf Kacheln (`moto-hover-elevated`) ist jetzt deckend (`color-mix`), damit der Punktehintergrund nicht durchscheint.
- **`transition-all`** (Eingabefelder, Checkbox, Tabs, Suche, Login) → `transition` bzw. die benannten Eigenschaften.
- **Breiten-Animationen** → `translateX`: `ProgressBar`, Raumbelegung, Indikator der unteren Navigation, Fortschrittsbalken nach der Einladung (Keyframes aus Inline-`<style>` nach `globals.css`, mit Reduced-Motion-Eintrag). Feedback-Verhältnisbalken: Animation entfernt.
- **Gegen Rückfälle:**
  - oxlint `ui-kit/no-costly-motion` (Hard-Zero, auch in `ui/`) lehnt `backdrop-*`, `transition-all`, Übergänge von Größe oder Position und `@keyframes` außerhalb von CSS ab, in Klassen und in `style`.
  - `scripts/css-motion.node-test.mjs` (läuft in `pnpm run check`) prüft alle Stylesheets: Keyframes nur mit `opacity`/`transform`, kein `backdrop-filter`, keine Layout-Übergänge, auch nicht per `@apply`.
  - Regel steht in `frontend-ui-kit.md` (Motion).
- **Bewusste Ausnahme:** das Breiten-Gleiten der einklappbaren Seitenleiste (#2825), hinter Disable-Kommentar mit Grund. Ein `transform` würde die Seite überdecken statt Platz zu machen. `grid-template-rows` (Aufklappen) bleibt erlaubt, es gibt kein `transform`-Gegenstück.
- **Mitgezogen:** Die Pillen-Ausnahme „Glas-Fläche“ (`backdrop-blur`) im Lint-Plugin war damit tot und ist entfernt. Die Marken-Chips der Anmeldeseite tragen dafür einen Disable-Kommentar. `StickyActionBar` steht wie `FilterPanel` in `SURFACE_KIT_CONTROLS`.

## Prüfung

- **Scrollmessung**, Storybook, 40 `SectionCard`s mit `ProgressBar`, 1920×1080, Chromium mit 4× CPU-Drosselung, 1,5 s Scrollen, alter und neuer `globals.css` abwechselnd, je 8 Läufe:

  | | Bilder | Mittel | Bilder über 20 ms |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Vorher | 36–49 | 31–52 ms | 33–42 |
  | Nachher | 91 | 16,7 ms | 0 |

  Der CSS-Wächter meldet auf dem alten `globals.css` genau die beiden Blur-Zeilen.
- **`pnpm run kit-pixel`** gegen `development` (lokal mit Chromium 155 statt Chrome): 860 von 890 Story-Bildern pixelgleich, darunter alle Karten. Die übrigen Abweichungen sind Kantenglättung am Balkenende, der Verlauf hinter der unteren Leiste und vorher durchscheinende, jetzt deckende Leisten. Ein Treffer war ein Timeout, im Wiederholungslauf grün.
- **Checks:**
  - `pnpm run check` grün.
  - `scripts/check-changed.mjs`: statisch grün; Tests 30.509 grün, 1 rot: `traeger/abrechnung/monatsbeitraege/[id]/review.test.tsx`, nicht berührt, einzeln 3/3 grün.
  - Neue Lint-Tests prüfen 7 Treffer und 0 Fehlalarme.
- **Geänderte Testverträge** (Position statt Breite, gleiches Verhalten): `ProgressBar` prüft `translateX(-75%)` statt `width: 25%`, die untere Navigation `translateX(12px)` statt `left`.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with GPT 6.1 Sol (high). Sol verdict: approved (S1 `@apply`-Lücke behoben, S2 `backdrop-blur-none` bewusst nicht ausgenommen).

## Screenshots

Vorher/Nachher-Paare aus dem Pixelvergleich im Kommentar unten.

## Missverständnis-Check

Keine neuen Texte, Blöcke oder Bedienelemente. Geprüft: Ladebildschirm, Speicherleiste, untere Navigation. Sie sehen gleich aus und bedeuten dasselbe.

## O que muda

Publica o front no Firebase Hosting depois do CI verde: um canal de preview por PR (expira em 7 dias, link no comentário) e o site de produção no merge da main. A API passa a aceitar o domínio `.web.app` deste projeto, inclusive os canais de preview.

## História / critério de aceite relacionado

Hosting — preview por PR e produção no merge da main, só com o CI verde. O build de produção aponta para a API no Render, com mock desligado. O smoke test roda depois do deploy. Nenhum JSON de conta de serviço entra no repositório.

## Como testar

1. Conferir que o diff não contém JSON de conta de serviço.
2. `cd server && npx vitest run tests/unit/cors.test.ts` — o preflight de `https://licitaradar-13047.web.app` e de um canal `https://licitaradar-13047--pr-12-abc123.web.app` responde 204; outro `.web.app` fica sem o cabeçalho.
3. Depois do merge, um PR seguinte deve receber o comentário com o link do preview. O merge na main publica `https://licitaradar-13047.web.app` e dispara o smoke test.
4. Republicar a API no Render com este código para o CORS novo valer.

author: netzenbot
body:
Closes brave/bravebot#4160

User impact: none -- a spec change to a design that is not built; no behaviour changes.

## The problem
The tracking issue for the checkout-settings sweep stays open on one condition: a plugin's `model` needs a recorded rule, because the plugins spec says a plugin declares no model and a plugin may carry skills and delegate definitions, which may each name one. A reader of the spec cannot tell whether a skill inside a plugin may name a model the way a skill in `~/.bravebot` may. Every other row of the tracker is closed.

## Reproduce
Not reproducible locally: nothing is built for plugins, so there is no behaviour to run (the tracker, https://github.com/brave/bravebot/issues/4160, records the open condition). The gap is in the text of `docs/specs/plugins.md`: its sixth clause says a plugin declares no model, and the skills and delegation specs let a skill and a definition name one. Reading the three together leaves the plugin case undecided.

State of the rest of the tracker at `eaaa0eae7`, read from GitHub: issues 4149, 4150, 4152, 4153, 4154, 4155, 4156, 4157, 4158 and 4159 are closed as completed, which covers rows A1 and B1 to B9. The desktop's remembered model (row A2) stores only a model the person picked: `ui/src/renderer/models.ts` keeps a picked flag and ignores the backend default. A1 is pinned by `a_checkouts_files_do_not_choose_the_default_model_and_the_persons_own_do` in `crates/config/src/settings.rs`.

## The fix
The sixth plugin clause now separates the manifest from the parts. The manifest still names no model. A skill or a definition inside a plugin may name one as the same file in `~/.bravebot` may, read the same way, and the install lists each such model before the person answers, so their yes is the endorsement. A workspace plugin directory is already inert, so no checkout names a model through a plugin. The install listing clause now names the model of each skill and definition.

Both clauses stay unverified because nothing is built. The change is proposed design text, as the spec's scope section says.

## Test plan
- [x] `make check-spec` - passed
- [ ] `BRAVEBOT_ALLOW_UNCONFIGURED_BUILD=1 make check-affected` - spec, security, locales, versions, narration, reviewdog, fmt, clippy and lint-increase checks passed; the test step of `make check` failed in three `exec` tests that also fail on the parent commit (see below), the target exited 2 and the steps of `make check` after the tests (code selectors, toolchain age) did not run
- [x] `python3 agents/skills/security-audit/security-audit.py --before-pr upstream/main` - exit 0 (the diff reaches no path that keeps answers, nothing was checked)
- [x] Docker gates skipped: host-only
- [ ] CI passes cleanly

Tests: none added. The change is spec text, so there is no test whose failure could be demonstrated; coverage is reasoned only.

<details>
<summary>Three tests in the exec test binary fail on this host and on the parent commit</summary>

`a_stage_cannot_open_the_controlling_terminal`, `a_substitution_printing_bytes_that_are_not_text_reaches_the_program_byte_for_byte` and `the_trailing_line_ends_of_a_substitution_are_cut_from_its_bytes_and_nothing_else` failed inside `make check`. Run alone with `--test-threads=1`, each failed the same way on this branch and with `docs/specs/plugins.md` restored to `upstream/main`. The diff is one Markdown file that no test reads, so it cannot reach them. The first reports it did not reach its end inside a terminal, and the other two read back an empty output where bytes were expected, which points at this machine's session having no usable terminal or at the sandboxed shell. CI runs these tests on its own hosts.

</details>

author: patrickmichalik
body:
## Summary

`argent init` in local mode ("This project only") fails when it runs at the root of a pnpm workspace. So does `argent update` for a local install there. The manual command that the failure prints fails in the same way.

## Cause

- The local install runs `pnpm add -D @swmansion/argent` in the project root.
- At a workspace root pnpm refuses that command:

  ```
  ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT  Running this command will add the dependency to the workspace root, which might not be what you want - if you really meant it, make it explicit by running this command again with the -w flag (or --workspace-root). If you don't want to see this warning anymore, you may set the ignore-workspace-root-check setting to true.
  ```

- The issue only shows `ShellCommandError: Command exited with code 1`. pnpm up to 11 prints this error on stdout, and argent 0.24.0 captured only stderr. #1776 added stdout to the error, so current `main` shows pnpm's text. The refusal above is what I reproduced for the setup in the issue; the screenshot alone does not prove it.
- When pnpm refuses depends on the version:
  - 7, 8, 9.15.9 and 10.0.0 refuse at any workspace root (7 and 8 checked with two `packages:` patterns only).
  - 10.5.0, 10.34.9 and 11.28.12 refuse only when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists two or more `packages:` patterns. With one pattern the bare command passes.
  - 12.0.0, 12.3.3, 12.3.4 and 12.21.0 refuse with two patterns (one pattern not checked). The error is on stderr there.

## Change

`localInstallCommand` now builds `pnpm add -D --ignore-workspace-root-check <pkg>`. The install, the "Install manually with:" hint and the local `argent update` all use that one builder.

`--ignore-workspace-root-check` and not `-w`:

- `-w` run from a package inside a workspace puts the dependency in the workspace root, not in that package.
- `-w` outside a workspace fails (`--workspace-root may only be used inside a workspace`).
- `--ignore-workspace-root-check` only skips the check. The dependency goes to the manifest of the directory the command runs in, as before.

The flag is passed always, with no workspace detection in argent, so argent and pnpm cannot disagree about what a workspace root is.

Failure reporting is unchanged. `main` already prints the package manager's output for a failed local install; a test now pins that, and that the hint is the command that ran.

## Verification

- **Raw command, per pnpm version.** `pnpm add -D --ignore-workspace-root-check <pkg>` in scratch projects, checking which `package.json` changed:
  - Workspace root (two patterns): passes on 7, 8, 9.15.9, 10.0.0, 10.5.0, 10.34.9, 11.28.12, 12.0.0, 12.3.3, 12.3.4, 12.21.0. The bare command fails on all of them.
  - Package inside a workspace: the dependency lands in that package, root untouched, on the same versions.
  - Project with no workspace file: passes on 7, 8, 9.15.9, 10.34.9, 11.28.12 and the four 12.x versions.
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with settings only: passes on 10.34.9, 11.28.12 and 12.x. pnpm 9 rejects such a file with or without the flag (`packages field missing or empty`), as before.
  - pnpm 5 and 6 also accept the flag.
- **Installer step, end to end.** Ran the built installer's `runInstall` in local mode (real `@swmansion/argent` from the registry, no-op telemetry) with pnpm 9.15.9, 10.34.9, 11.28.12 and 12.21.0 on `PATH`: workspace root, workspace package, plain pnpm project, settings-only file. All install into the expected manifest, except settings-only on pnpm 9 (see above). The unmodified build fails at the workspace root on pnpm 9.15.9 with the error quoted above.
- **Update command shape.** `pnpm add -D --ignore-workspace-root-check <pkg>@<version>` over an existing devDependency at a workspace root passes on 9, 10, 11.
- **Checks.** `vitest run` in `packages/argent-installer`: 732 passed. The four new or changed tests fail without the source change. The update test starts outside the project root (from a workspace package, and with `--project-root`), so it also fails if the command runs in the current directory. `typecheck:tests`, eslint and Prettier are clean.

Not verified: a full interactive `argent init` or `argent update` run (only the install step and the command), and Windows.

## Not covered

- **Yarn classic** has the same refusal for `yarn add` and `yarn remove` at a workspace root (reproduced on 1.22.22). `-W` fixes it there, but Yarn Berry rejects `-W` (`Unsupported option name`, checked on 4.x), and the installer does not tell the two apart. Left for a separate change.
- npm, bun and Yarn Berry add to a workspace root without a flag. `pnpm remove` and `pnpm install` at a workspace root need no flag either.
- When `argent init --local` runs from a workspace package that has no editor or `.git` marker of its own, argent resolves the project root to the workspace root and installs there. pnpm used to stop that with the same error; now it installs at the root, which is where the MCP config is written and what npm and bun already do.

## Docs

No docs update needed. The install docs describe local mode and its options, not the package manager command, and those are unchanged.

Fixes #1046

author: houko
body:
## Summary

Android lists and scroll views now stop custom momentum as soon as DOWN enters the native scroll container, including when a pressable row consumes it. Both axes initialize the drag origin before child dispatch, which also restores the drag start/end events previously lost on those gestures. A braking hold ends momentum once without inventing another drag or a scroll-end event. A view with `NoScroll` leaves the touch alone, as its `onTouchEvent` already did and as the Windows and Linux touch paths skip it.

Refs #358. The concrete cancellation bug is implemented and verified. The separate request to compare custom and platform-list frame pacing on physical 60/120 Hz devices remains open and is recorded in the roadmap; this PR makes no jank or 120 Hz performance claim.

The braking touch still reaches the row under it (its `OnPressDown` fires, and a lift without moving would press it), matching NSGo's Windows and Linux touch scrolling. Android's own ScrollView and RecyclerView, and UIScrollView, swallow such a touch instead; whether NSGo should do the same everywhere is a separate decision and is not changed here.

## Device test host check

`nsgo test -target android` on current main refuses any package whose tests do not link `github.com/nsgo-dev/nsgo`. `internal/platform/android` registers its test host itself and cannot import the root package (which imports it), so the check refused this PR's device tests. The check now also accepts a test binary that links a backend registering the test host (`hostBackends`), and `TestBackendTestsLinkTheirHost` keeps that list equal to the backends that call `testhost.Register`. The package's `TestMain` moved to an untagged `main_test.go` that starts the host when one is registered and runs the tests plainly otherwise, so the tool sees it from this machine's view of the package.

## Targets

- [x] Android

Checked the other paths: Android ZoomScroll already stops its OverScroller in DOWN interception, Windows/Linux stop touch glides in touchDown, and iOS/web use native scrolling. The change belongs to Android's custom vertical/horizontal drivers.

## Screenshots

None. This changes gesture timing rather than static appearance.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` of `internal/platform/android` and `cmd/nsgo`, GOOS=windows/linux/android(arm64, with and without `nsgotest`)/js builds or vets: passed.
- `go tool nsgo check -target all`: passed.
- `go tool nsgo test ./internal/platform/android`: 15 passed, 6 skipped. `go tool nsgo test ./cmd/nsgo`: 241 passed, 10 skipped. `go tool nsgo test -run 'Layer|Skills|Doc' .`: 35 passed.
- `go tool nsgo test -target android -run '^(TestVerticalListTouchStopsMomentum|TestHorizontalListTouchStopsMomentum)$' ./internal/platform/android` on an Android API 35 arm64 emulator: 2 passed in each of 5 consecutive runs. With the dispatch change disabled both fail: 373 and 477 pixels of drift over 20 frames, no momentum end, no drag events. The Pixel 3 XL was not connected for this round; the earlier round passed on it (Android 12, 60 Hz).
- Each native test mounts a real 2,000-row core.List, dispatches MotionEvents through the Activity to start a fling, then holds a finger for 20 display frames. Both the consuming row and an empty-space control keep the exact native pixel offset; drag and momentum event counts and child DOWN delivery are checked. Vertical rows have variable-height text and are recycled by the list.
- The test agent's drags and swipes now stamp each MotionEvent with its scheduled time rather than the time its post runs. On a loaded emulator a late post made the velocity tracker see the finger stop, so a swipe sometimes started no momentum (4 of 5 runs had a failure before, none of 5 after).
- Rebuilt and committed classes.dex and classes.jar with `internal/platform/android/runtime/build.sh`.

The swipe and hold probes are internal test-agent commands, available only through the debuggable test launch. No public API changes. No changelog entry, per AGENTS.md.

The plugin cleanup and browser cancellation test fixes this branch carried earlier are now on main and were dropped in the rebase.

- `negctl_par.sh`'s scratch harness (`build()`, integration/negctl_par.sh:57-65) copies exactly `run_par.sh` + `par_counter8.tcl` into the scratch tree — that self-containment is load-bearing for the negative-control evidence. | Option 3: rationale committed + each copy's comment points at its sibling | ✅ | README note committed at `cf8fc01`; run_par.sh block names read_lef.sh and vice versa |

## Test Plan

All live on this worker against the pinned lambdapdk v0.2.17 (sha256 verified) with OpenROAD 26Q3-1510-g6cb3f2b704:

body:
## Summary

The verification workflow installs `uv` with `python -m pip install uv==0.13.6`. The version is
fixed by number only and changes by hand for each `uv` release. This change installs `uv` with the
`astral-sh/setup-uv` action, pinned to a commit, and reads the version from `uv.lock`.

## Related issue or decision

None

## Changes

- Replace the `pip install` step with `astral-sh/setup-uv`, pinned to the commit of release
  v10.3.3, with `version-file: uv.lock` and the action cache disabled.
- Add `uv==0.13.8` to the `dev` dependency group so that `uv.lock` records the version that the
  workflow installs.

## Verification

Run locally on Linux with Python 3.14.4: `uv lock --check` and
`uv run --locked python scripts/verify.py`. Both passed. Python 3.11, macOS, and Windows run only in
the pull request checks.

## Impact and maintenance notes

- The `uv` version used in the workflow changes from 0.13.6 to 0.13.8.
- `uv.lock` gains one package, `uv`. No other locked package changes.
- Each job has `uv` twice at the same version: the action installs one, and `uv sync` installs one
  into `.venv`.
- The action cache is disabled, so each run installs from a clean state as before.
- A change of the workflow `uv` version goes through `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`.
- No changelog entry: the change affects CI only.

## Checklist

- [x] The pull request addresses one coherent change.
- [x] I reviewed the diff for unintended changes, secrets, credentials, temporary files, and
  unintended generated output.
- [x] Verification results are accurately reported, including relevant failed or unrun checks.
- [x] I updated documentation where behavior, setup, or commands changed.
- [x] Relevant compatibility, dependency, data provenance, licensing, and attribution implications
  are documented where applicable.
- [x] Every commit has a `Signed-off-by` line, as the contributing guidelines require.

Closes #427 (stage 1 of #426).

## What changed

- `src/t6/consumer.py`: the credential pattern matches `NOTION_API_KEY`, `NOTION_TOKEN`, `T6_NOTION_API_KEY` and `T6_NOTION_TOKEN`. Look-alike names such as `T6_NOTION_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, `T6_NOTION_PROJECTS_DATA_SOURCE` and `NOTION_TOKEN_FILE` do not match.
- README "Check an app" and ADR 0002 rule 6: the names the check knows, and the limit of the host rule.

## The host rule is not narrowed

The ticket asked to narrow `direct-http` or to document its limit, whichever keeps every real finding. Every narrow rule that was tried would miss a real call (a literal URL passed to a client, or kept in a config dict), because the one known false positive (a share link in a test message body) has the same shape as a real config value. So the rule stays, and the docs say that a false positive gets a dated `direct-http` allowlist entry for that file.

## Effect on the apps

An app sees the new findings when it bumps its t6 pin. Measured on each repo's `main`, with allowlists applied: gateway 10 (2 before), reports 33 (9), watchdog 39 (25), munki 2 (0), drives 2, netops 8, agent-skills 0. All 16 `direct-http` findings are still reported.

## Checks

mypy, lint-imports, deptry and the unit tests pass (2096 tests). The two new tests failed before the change.

`CHANGELOG.md` is left for the release PR.

It binds the exact product source and Git namespace, server run and artifact digest, complete manifest and selected Cargo observations, and the five expected PE roles. Historical capture records remain evidence of their emission, not a current authorization.

The operation retains the original stage parent and created file objects through same-byte observation and cleanup. Directory enumeration uses the held directory instead of reopening a DELETE-held path. Cleanup resumes after successful deletion marking without querying a delete-pending handle. A consumed Close error remains an unknown outcome across the prepared wrapper, and neither a pointer nor a retained report is treated as a live handle.

The fixed candidate is [e2d3ab6b](https://github.com/AutoDevJapan/cc-pc-tools-rs/commit/e2d3ab6b9781a7c52873f2f1496ed49af0194510), tree `5e2a3e43c7f736980e7d70fc8b9c9e5144498f8b`. The component adds its implementation, tests and `docs/civ880-readonly-artifact-observation.md`. The latest three-file correction changes the two aggregate Close operations and their tests and documentation. Its preceding workflow remains byte-identical. Both independent review sessions confirmed the final correction with no remaining source findings. The same final candidate's readiness and CodeQL workflows completed successfully. The preceding d5645a53 results remain recorded for that version.

The [first Windows reader run](https://github.com/AutoDevJapan/cc-pc-tools-rs/actions/runs/43869092139/job/133305195272) compiled and executed all 34 named component roots: 30 passed and four failed. Test failure prevented the subsequent vet and build commands from running. The original failures remain recorded. The current candidate adds the explicit SYNCHRONIZE access required by synchronous native regular-file creation, with phase and NTSTATUS diagnostics and one additional native positive/negative test root. Sharing, DELETE access, identity, ACL and post-delete-mark behavior remain unchanged. The original failure had no native status, so this is a source-grounded repair candidate rather than a proven diagnosis of every failed case. On [7583a714](https://github.com/AutoDevJapan/cc-pc-tools-rs/commit/7583a71469c5a3625e6359ddd50b6fa84fd33b53), all 35 exact component roots ran and passed without skips, and the reader test, vet and build step succeeded. The component bytes are unchanged in the current workflow-only correction. The original failures remain recorded, and no rerun or skip has been used to count them as successful. Synthetic consumed-Close controls passed but do not prove an actual Windows CloseHandle failure.

The normal factory remains unconnected. This does not issue credentials, qualify the running reader, install or execute the product, or complete native shutdown and game acceptance. Original leader, save/load, payment, multiplayer and RNG requirements remain unchanged. Codex and Claude Code must both reach the eventual normal preflight entry; source tests and configuration are not both-host acceptance. This source component does not complete those original product acceptance requirements.

The preceding workflow also failed in the separate Windows unattended-runner package when its 600-second package budget expired; the last named test had run for four seconds. A second failure occurred after 600.155 seconds with the same test 13 seconds old; a previous main run passed in 581.609 seconds. The current workflow compiles the race test binary once, enumerates every native Test/Fuzz/Example root and runs disjoint groups of at most 50 roots serially, each with a finite 180-second budget. Exact root completion is reconciled, skips are counted separately, and the job bound and individual timing tests remain unchanged. This source correction still needs actual Windows partition results and independent review.

The first partition run failed before any group executed because the native test-root listing did not return a usable result. Source and bounded argument controls show that unquoted dotted native flags are split by PowerShell. The current workflow quotes the list, verbose and timeout arguments and prints the validated root names, fixed numeric exit/count markers and structural test outcomes. Free-form test output, paths, environment and credential values are not printed. Exact native listing, every listed root's single completion, each partition exit and the final reconciled summary must still be accepted from this new run. The existing individual timing predicates, one compiled race binary, disjoint serial groups and job bound are unchanged.

The quoted-flag run now returned the native list successfully: 734 unique Test/Fuzz/Example roots were validated from 735 raw list lines. The excluded line was not printed, so its classification is unconfirmed. Partitions 0 through 12 each returned exit 0. Partition 13 returned exit 2 after about 180 seconds. Across the recorded groups, 692 roots started, 686 passed, five skipped and one remained without a terminal result; 42 roots did not start, and no complete summary was produced. The completed roots in the failed group account for about 168.41 seconds, but the filtered log does not contain the original panic text, so the exact exit cause is still distinguished from the cumulative-budget inference. The workflow is not accepted and will not be rerun blindly.

The current correction spreads the same complete native root list across `ceil(N/50)` groups by index modulo the group count, rather than grouping consecutive roots. The observed 734-root list yields 15 disjoint groups of 49 or 48 roots. The largest sum of previously observed passing durations in a new group is 45.88 seconds; 43 uncompleted or unstarted roots and five skipped roots have no accepted duration. This calculation does not predict that the finite budget will pass. The 180-second process bound, 20-minute job bound, compiled race binary, serial execution and original assertions remain unchanged. Fixed start and failure-class markers distinguish timeout, data race, test assertion and unknown native exit without printing free-form output. The [current CI](https://github.com/AutoDevJapan/cc-pc-tools-rs/actions/runs/43882468877) validated 734 unique roots, one start and one terminal result for each, with 729 passes and five skips; the skipped roots are not passed acceptance. The original failed candidate remains recorded.

The independent failure-path review found that a consumed file-Close error marks the aggregate outcome unknown but still closes later live file owners in the same loop. That contradicts the documented promise to retain the other confirmed live handles after an uncertain Close. The current correction stops immediately at the first failed File.Close or native CloseHandle, clears only the consumed slot and retains later live leaves, unwrapped handles, root and parent owners. author: princemuteh
body:
The bell was a template stub. The dot was hard-coded to `true`, the list
held nothing but commented-out example rows from the theme, and nothing
was ever fetched — so the panel opened empty with no message while the
bell claimed there was something to read.

It now reads `GET /notifications`. Whatever the answer is, the panel says
something: the items, "No notifications yet", a loading line, or why the
feed could not be loaded. Each line says what happened, the detail, the
case reference where there is one and how long ago, and links to the thing
it is about.

**The dot shows only when the API says something is waiting.** Items that
merely happened — a decision on a request you raised, a case you have
already taken in hand — are listed without lighting it. Items that are
still yours to act on carry their own mark in the list.

`timeAgo` is its own dependency-free module so it can be tested: a clock
slightly ahead of the server's reads "just now" rather than counting
forward, and past about a month the date itself is shown rather than "9
weeks ago".

Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 70 tests pass.

The API is `DevonSRE/lacon-backend#85`. **Row 41 needed no frontend
change** — Documents already reads document history, so the backend fix
makes the attached file appear, and `movementReason` passes the longer
history note through untouched.

Independent of the pro bono stack; this branches from `main`.

- "Add redirect", "Edit", "Delete", delete dialog "Delete the redirect from <path>?" / "Visitors who still use the old address will get a not-found page. This can't be undone."

author: johoenk
body:
one static page that shows the texts behind the numbers

`bazel run //tools:eval_report -- build` reads a test set and local run caches and writes a folder (index.html, viewer.js/css, one data file per text) that opens from file:// with no server. `--zip` and `--single-file` are optional; an output inside a git work tree is refused, because a report holds corpus text.

Python computes every number with the report's own functions; the page only displays. Rows are checked against the test set and scored again on reading. A variant is the GroupKey plus prompt, `isolated` and answer format, with the range over its repeats. Each edit is judged exact / located / extra. The scorecard row over languages is the mean of de and en, as `report` prints it. Scorecard, heat map and error table hold one eval version at a time.

The page has the scorecard with dominated variants, a heat map, the sentence stack (Read / Changes / Original, explanation drawer, jumps, two-variant diff), a sentence grid, a page view and the error-type table.

Also: GroupKey.of_local reads a cache header; quality.ordered_edits caches 16384 pairs.

author: guicostak
body:
Fecha a issue S01-C1 (#226). Entregável: `lab-expe-05/docs/04-plano-analise.md`.

O plano é escrito **antes** dos dados: define qual teste roda, qual efeito é reportado, como as múltiplas comparações são corrigidas e o que pode ser excluído. Depois da tag `data-v1`, qualquer mudança aqui vira análise post-hoc e é rotulada como tal.

## O que foi decidido

| Item | Decisão |
| :--- | :--- |
| Escala de trabalho | log das métricas de tempo (razão vira diferença; a cauda fica simétrica) |
| Teste principal | t de **Welch** sobre log, com tela de Shapiro-Wilk a α = 0,01 nos dois grupos |
| Alternativa | **Mann-Whitney U** quando a tela rejeita; os dois rodam sempre, e em caso de desacordo vale o Mann-Whitney |
| Efeito | g de Hedges (Welch) ou delta de Cliff (MW), mais a **razão ZGC/G1** com IC 95 % por bootstrap BCa (10 000 reamostragens, semente 42) |
| Correção | **Holm** sobre os 12 confirmatórios; **Benjamini-Hochberg** (FDR 0,05) na família exploratória, separada |
| RQ2 | modelo linear sobre `log(exec_ms)` com `gc * heap_mult + gc * benchmark + bloco`; fallback pré-registrado é ANOVA fatorial |
| Exclusão | só invocação com `failed = 1` e motivo registrado. **Nunca por valor extremo** — o outlier de latência é o objeto de estudo |

## Parâmetro do contrato que este PR preenche

O contrato (§8) deixava o **menor efeito de interesse prático** em aberto. Proposta de C, para o grupo confirmar na revisão:

- `exec_ms`: razão **1,05** (5 %)
- `lat_p99_ms`: razão **1,10** (10 %)

Os 5 % não são chute: são o mesmo número do limiar de CV do plano B. Se a variação de uma célula for maior que o efeito procurado, o experimento não tem como enxergá-lo.

## Poder simulado (Monte Carlo, 10 000 repetições, semente 42)

Poder a α = 0,05 / poder a α/12 (os dois extremos entre os quais o Holm opera), efeito de razão 1,05:

| CV da célula | N = 20 | N = 30 | N = 40 | N = 50 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 % | 100 % / 100 % | 100 % / 100 % | 100 % / 100 % | 100 % / 100 % |
| 3 % | 99,9 % / 97,7 % | 100 % / 99,9 % | 100 % / 100 % | 100 % / 100 % |
| 5 % | 85,6 % / 52,1 % | 96,0 % / **77,8 %** | 99,0 % / 91,5 % | 99,8 % / 97,4 % |
| 8 % | 47,2 % / 14,5 % | 64,7 % / **27,4 %** | 76,6 % / 42,0 % | 86,1 % / 55,1 % |

**Leitura:** o N = 30 do contrato serve **se o CV ficar em até 5 %**. Com CV de 8 %, quase três em cada quatro diferenças reais de 5 % passariam batido. Isso é o conteúdo técnico do limiar de 5 % do plano B — não é um número de gosto.

Calibração: com efeito zero e N = 30, o Welch rejeita em 4,83 % e o Mann-Whitney em 4,74 %, contra os 5 % esperados.

A simulação reprodutível entra em `analysis/poder.py` na S01-C2 (#227), e regenera exatamente esta tabela.

## Pergunta do professor, respondida no documento (§12)

- **Por que só duas métricas são confirmatórias?** São três perguntas (Q1, Q2, Q5), mas duas métricas — o RQ2 reusa o `exec_ms`. Com 12 testes e sem correção, a chance de ao menos um falso positivo já é de 46 %.
- **Por que Welch e não o t clássico?** O ZGC coleta de forma concorrente e disputa CPU com a aplicação, o que dá motivo teórico para as variâncias serem diferentes. O Welch custa uma fração de grau de liberdade quando elas são iguais, então nunca é pior. E o Levene **não** é usado como portão: escolher o teste depois de olhar a variância é decisão condicional e infla o erro tipo I.

## Arquivos

- `lab-expe-05/docs/04-plano-analise.md` (novo)
- `lab-expe-05/docs/00-contrato.md` — preenche o menor efeito de interesse prático (§8), que o próprio contrato marca como "definido em S01-C1"
- `lab-expe-05/README.md` — link para o plano

body:
## Focus (hors CI/CD) — implémentation

**Producteur réel de relation forte (périmètre borné)** : quand deux observations Search publiques *du même appel et réellement persistées* correspondent à deux `SourceReference` distinctes (provider/record exacts) avec **`OriginLink` provider-response et livraison Core achevée**, attachées au **même Artifact et à une Placement présente sous la même identité**, Core produit une C canonique commune conservant les deux couvertures et provenances. La relation n'est pas inventée en passant une simple chaîne `relation_proof_id` dans un test.

- Admission STRICTE : 2 fournisseurs différents, deux achats source réellement publiés, même Artifact/profil avec preuves Core, recherche publique v2, coordonnées exactes ; pas de rapprochement par titre/ISBN/SHA/URL. Le titre et auteur servent uniquement de **veto** négatif en cas de contradiction pour éviter la fusion de deux travaux distincts qui auraient les mêmes octets génériques.
- Chaque source C reste disponible seule lorsque l'autre manque ; relation commune rejetée si comptes/profils différents, provenance historique/incomplète, source hors édition, ambiguïté de groupes ou source privée.
- Scan borné **une seule fois par lot Search worker**, puis écriture des sources publiques dans la C v1 existante, aucun dispatch fournisseur/CoreUI ni droits/actions dérivés.
- `SearchResult` live reçoit un témoin Core privé associé à la source et à l'epoch de la C commune, vérifié avant liaison `DocumentRef` sur UI sans SQL GTK. N2 peut lire les deux images depuis la C partagée ; pas de N3/EPUB scanné par cette PR.
- Tests : publication vraie `publish_completed_acquisition` (deux provider OriginLinks) → deux public notices attestées par `_public_rows_from_response` → shared C/N2 et Search liste+détail → purge des sources/reboot ; source sans couverture enrichie ; mêmes octets mais 2 profils, preuve historique, autre record, deux livres différents, faux témoin/revision/clone ; aucun droit créé.

**Limites :** ce n'est PAS une réconciliation universelle de deux catalogues sans preuve indépendante ; pas de faux positif ISBN/SHA. Les six vues et un scénario réel cross-provider doivent encore être réceptionnés avec #6366. Le curseur multi-source et la présentation C-first sont dans la PR Focus séparée #6437.

**Handoff CI/CD :** validations/test failures, éventuels conflits/rebase et merge sur main sont exclusivement à l'agent CI/CD. Focus enchaîne les PR ; solliciter un handoff en cas de défaut métier.

body:
## What changes

The website in `site/` is rebuilt in the look of [aqua.is-a.dev](https://aqua.is-a.dev): a black sky with slow dots, glass cards that lean towards the pointer, Bodoni headlines. All AquAxs project sites now share this look and differ only in accent colour and 3D scene.

- **3D header.** A WebGL scene (three.js): a ring of the day's time by category around a clock that shows the visitor's own local time. A click switches focus mode on: social and entertainment drop back and dim, and an hour counts down. With reduced motion it is one still frame; without WebGL a glow stays in its place.
- **Screenshots in space.** The five popup screenshots sit in a row that turns as you swipe; the settings screenshot straightens as it scrolls into view.
- **Shared kit in `site/assets/aqx/`.** Stylesheet, interactions, the 3D stage, three.js r170 and the three typefaces, all served from this site.
- **Same content.** All feature lists, the privacy section, the permission table, both ZIPs and their SHA-256 lines are carried over.
- **Clean URLs and one strict set of security headers.** The no-cache rule for `/downloads/` stays.
- **Search and sharing.** JSON-LD, a regenerated sitemap, and a footer strip that links the other projects and the portfolio.

## Worth a look before merging

- **Terms.** Unchanged, word for word.
- **`download.html` still says "Version 2.1.0"**, which `tools/verify-downloads.sh` checks. `npm run verify:downloads` and `npm test` (65 tests) pass.
- **README** links now use the clean addresses (`/download`, `/terms`).
- **Preview image.** `assets/og-image.png` is still the old design.

## Tested

Every page loaded in headless Chromium at 1440 px and 390 px with the new `vercel.json` headers applied: no console errors, no CSP violations, no horizontal overflow, the scene starts on every page.

author: fredrivett
body: ## What and why On phones, the command palette stayed the height it had while the keyboard was open, even after the keyboard closed. The list was capped at `min(24rem, 60dvh)`. iOS lays the on-screen keyboard over the page without changing `dvh`, so the palette never responded to the keyboard at all. On an iPhone 17 Pro the 24rem cap only just clears the keyboard, so once the keyboard closes the palette stays short, with the Lists group cut off and empty space below it. ## Change (`src/components/CommandPalette.tsx`) - The palette reads the bottom of `window.visualViewport` (`offsetTop + height`) with `useSyncExternalStore`. It updates on the viewport's `resize` and `scroll` events and exposes the value as `--visible-bottom`. - Below `sm`, the list's height is `min(var(--cmdk-list-height), var(--visible-bottom) - 4.75rem)`. The 4.75rem covers the 1rem top offset, the search field and its padding (2.75rem), and a 1rem gap above the keyboard. The height eases over 250ms, so the palette shrinks and grows with the keyboard's slide. - It animates `height` rather than `max-height`: cmdk already measures the content into `--cmdk-list-height`, so both ends of the animation are real heights. A `max-height` transition spends most of its time above the content and still looks like a snap. - At `sm` and up, the old `max-h-[min(24rem,60dvh)]` cap is unchanged. Side effect: on phones, changes in result count while typing also ease over 250ms instead of jumping. ## Verification - Reproduced in the iOS 27.3 simulator (iPhone 17 Pro) in the home-screen web app. Before the change, the palette stayed capped after the keyboard was dismissed and Lists was cut off. - After the change, the palette stops just above the keyboard while it's open, and grows back to show every command and list once it closes. I checked recordings of the keyboard opening and closing, and of typing and deleting a search, frame by frame. - `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` (562 tests) pass. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the command palette fitting to the visible screen on phones so it shrinks above the on-screen keyboard and grows back when it closes. - The palette previously capped its list at `min(24rem, 60dvh)`, which stayed short after the keyboard closed because iOS lays the keyboard over the page without changing `dvh`. - Below the `sm` breakpoint, the list now sizes to the bottom of `window.visualViewport` and eases over 250ms as the keyboard slides. - A side effect: result-count changes while typing also ease over 250ms instead of jumping on phones. Written for commit 58df3bd0a8c0258adf23b546fc5460ce26a9131b. Summary will update on new commits.

author: praestar
body:
Adds Dependabot `ignore` rules for major versions that cannot land as they are, so 1.0 ships on a pinned toolchain. Minor and patch updates continue.

| PR | Bump | Why it is held |
|---|---|---|
| #39 | typescript 5.9 → 7.0 | TypeScript 7 (native port) ships no JavaScript compiler API; typescript-eslint (peer `<6.1.0`) and tsup's `dts` build need it. `npm ci` fails with ERESOLVE. |
| #41, #44 | @eslint/js, eslint 9 → 10 | `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` 6.10.2 (latest) allows eslint up to 9; `npm ci` fails with ERESOLVE. Also needs eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7. |
| #43 | @vitejs/plugin-react 4 → 6 | Needs vite 8, two majors above the current vite 6. |

Those four PRs are closed with a link here. Revisit after 1.0.
Also fixes a flaky security test that failed here: the 404 budget tests drained exactly the burst while the partitioned token bucket refills one token every three seconds at the default period, so a slow CI run missed the ban. The test host now uses a one-hour period (same burst, one token back every three minutes). Confirmed with a probe: after draining 40 tokens, one is back after 3.2 s at a 60 s period and none at 3600 s.

author: pcvelz
body:
### Description (*)

In CLI, once output was written, `start()` now skips `session_start()` and uses an in-memory `$_SESSION`; with logging enabled it logs one warning. The throw from #3109 stays for every other failure.

```php
if (PHP_SAPI === 'cli' && headers_sent()) {
    Mage::log('Session not started in CLI: output was already sent', Level::Warning);
    $_SESSION ??= [];
    return $this;
}
```

Setting `$_SESSION` makes `init()` skip `start()` for later session models, so the warning is logged once per process.

### Fixed Issues (if relevant)

- fixes OpenMage/magento-lts#5873

### Manual testing scenarios (*)

1. Run `repro.php` from #5873.
2. Before: `step 1`, an error-page redirect, `Unable to start session.` in `var/report`.
3. After:

```
step 1
step 2
exit=0
```

With System > Configuration > Developer > Log Settings enabled (`dev/log/active = 1`), `var/log/system.log`:

```
WARNING (300): Session not started in CLI: output was already sent
```

No `var/report`. A CLI script without prior output still gets a real session:

```sh
php -r 'require "app/Mage.php"; Mage::app(); Mage::getSingleton("core/session")->setFoo("bar"); echo session_id() !== "" ? "id set" : "id empty", " foo=", Mage::getSingleton("core/session")->getFoo(), "\n";'
# id set foo=bar
```

Tested on PHP 8.1.

 - [x] Pull request has a meaningful description of its purpose
 - [ ] All automated tests passed successfully (all builds are green, SonarCloud checks are not required to merge)

Release preparation for FerroBASIC 0.1.1 (pre-alpha). Under the version policy in `docs/roadmap.md`, this is a patch release: 0.1.0 completed M1, and M2 is not done yet.

## What changed

- **Version**: `Cargo.toml` goes from `0.1.1-dev` to `0.1.1`, and `Cargo.lock` follows through `cargo build`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: "Unreleased" becomes `## 0.1.1 (pre-alpha)`, with a summary paragraph and these sections:
  - Runtime, as in B4J: Unicode 14 case data (#115), now crediting the generator script and the Unicode-3.0 licence; JDK 19's final-sigma word-boundary rule (#140).
  - Recorded from B4J: recording runs 22 and 23, plus a counts line: 306 tests, 300 pass, 6 deviations (D1, D3–D7), none pending or provisional.
  - Tools: the macOS `ferro bundle` header-space fix (#131).
  - Testing and tools: the recorder records refused probes. This entry is wrapped to the file's width.
  - Project (new): the `new-probe` skill, and the EBNF and research docs following the recordings.
  - Known limitations (new): classes, other modules, other libraries, `DateTime`, `Sleep`/`Wait For`; the REPL's file loading and interruption; the language server giving diagnostics only; REPL line editing tried by hand on macOS and Windows only.
- **`docs/tutorial.md`**: the version line is now `ferro 0.1.1 (linux-x64)`. No other file in `docs/` or `README.md` mentions `0.1.1-dev`.

Covers every PR merged into `dev` since `v0.1.0`, up to `054a838`: #122, #123, #124, #125, #128, #129, #132, #134, #135, #136, #138, #139, #141, #142.

## Checks

- Full `scripts/check-all.sh` (not `--quick`), with every target installed: **every check passed**.
  - Format.
  - Clippy for Linux, Windows, macOS arm64 and macOS x86_64.
  - Workspace tests: 403 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. These include `crates/repl/tests/tutorial.rs`, which checks the REPL transcripts.
  - Conformance in the interpreter: 306 tests, 300 pass, 0 fail, 6 deviations, 0 pending, 0 against a provisional output.
  - Conformance as standalone binaries: the same results.
  - Recorder dry run.
  - Real-world corpus: 14 projects fetched.
  - Static Linux binary.
- Tutorial: I re-ran every `console` example against `cargo build --release -p ferro-cli`. The outputs and exit codes match. The only difference is `ls Greeter`, which prints one name per line when stdout is not a terminal.
- `python3 tools/unicode/generate_case_tables.py --check` passes against the UCD 14.0.0 `UnicodeData.txt` and `SpecialCasing.txt`. I downloaded both, and their SHA-256 match the hashes pinned in the script.

Next, after this merges: the release PR from `dev` into `main`.

body:
# Description

Eliminates the `28s` Gemini 4 Hydrogen web-search latency spike on native Vertex environments (`Production`, `Shared Dev`, pods, and BYOK) and institutionalizes the end-to-end model/provider rollout checklist as a governed `backend` spoke skill (`model-provider-governance`) + workflow pack (`model-provider-rollout`):

1. **Pin `google_search` and `one_intro` to `LOW` thinking across all environments (`agents/one/agent.yaml`, `one_adk/web_search.py`, `one_adk/agent_tree.py`):**
   - Previously, UAT's `ManagedPrimaryTextModel` wrapper (`ENVIRONMENT == "uat"`) injected `LOW` thinking on search fallbacks, while native Vertex heads (`ENVIRONMENT == "production"` and `"dev"`) constructed the `google_search` child `LlmAgent` with `generate_content_config=None`, causing `gemini-4-hydrogen` to engage unbounded dynamic `HIGH` multi-hop reasoning (`10` sequential Google searches + `2,015` hidden thinking tokens = `28.68s` unary stall).
   - Declares `thinking_level: low` on `google_search` and `one_intro` in `agents/one/agent.yaml`, wires `child.model.thinking_level` into `build_web_search_agent` for all non-Azure-primary heads while leaving Azure wire payloads untouched, and applies `_one_chat_thinking_config(..., include_summaries=False)` on `build_one_intro_text_agent`.
2. **Add two-tier direct-fact lookup fast path (`agents/one/agent.yaml`):**
   - Adds a direct factual lookup rule (`<= 2` focused searches, `<= 120` words without multi-angle cross-examination for weather, time, scores, prices, schedules, or quick public facts) while preserving the full multi-anchor profile-research contract. Live Production Vertex A/B benchmark measured `25.62s -> 4.49s` (`>82%` latency reduction, `2,015 -> 0` hidden thinking tokens).
3. **Add `model-provider-governance` spoke skill & `model-provider-rollout` workflow pack (`.agents/skills/model-provider-governance/`, `.agents/workflows/model-provider-rollout/`):**
   - Codifies Org Policy/home-project IAM/GSU-vs-DSQ capacity readiness, live `thinking_level` floor probing, full agent-tree/sub-agent reasoning audits, model self-identity/registry regeneration, and multi-environment rollout verification.

_Requested by **Cornelius** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01HTLuBSrKFWgVByes6MS1nq?thread=cmsg_01HTLuBSrKFWgVByes6MS1nqPk3ZBdvc1TxbtgrKnGALtX)_

## Warum
"Angaben ergänzen" blieb nach dem Tippen auf Speichern mehrere Sekunden ohne Rückmeldung im Formular hängen: Schildfoto ein zweites Mal verkleinern, hochladen, Bestätigung eintragen, dann jeder Vorschlag einzeln nacheinander. Erst danach kam ein kurzer Hinweis unten, der nach 3 Sekunden wieder weg war.

## Was sich ändert
- `speichern()` prüft und stellt alles ohne Netz zusammen und springt sofort zurück zum Platz mit "Danke! Dein Vorschlag wird geprüft." (im Test nach etwa 170 ms statt mehreren Sekunden)
- `aenderungSenden()` läuft im Hintergrund: Foto + Vorschläge, Feldänderung und Weggeschickt-Meldung gleichzeitig; alle Vorschläge in **einer** Anfrage (wenn sie abgelehnt wird, kommen die Vorschläge einzeln hinterher, damit der Rest ankommt)
- Das Schildfoto wird beim Auswählen einmal verkleinert und beim Senden wiederverwendet
- Neue Karte direkt unter dem Status (`sendeKarte`): "Danke! Wird gesendet …" → "Wartet auf Prüfung" → bei Fehler "Senden hat nicht geklappt" mit "Nochmal versuchen" (Entwurf und Foto bleiben)
- Warnung beim Schließen der Seite, solange noch gesendet wird
- Kein SQL nötig

## Getestet
Playwright gegen echte Lesedaten, Schreibzugriffe abgefangen und um je 1,5 s verzögert: Erfolg und Fehlerfall inklusive "Nochmal versuchen".

body:
**Review risk:** two-way door — test helpers of `clipboard` and `printing` only; no view changes

## Summary

The `clipboard` and `printing` builds fail on `main` since the Flow 25.4 snapshot moved the JavaScript of its event data and trigger functions into the bundle. Two test helpers relied on the old JavaScript strings; they now read what Flow declares instead.

## What changed

- `clipboard`: `ClipboardTestSupport.paste` sends the pasted text and HTML under the keys of the event data that the paste listener declares (`ElementListenerMap#getSnippetEntries`), found by their MIME type, instead of a copy of the JavaScript expressions Flow used to send.
- `printing`: `PrintTestSupport.queuedJsMentions` reads a function that Flow declares in a `@JsDefinition` interface by its method and arguments, as such a function has no body (`JsFunction#getBody` throws for it). Functions created with `JsFunction.of`, such as the view's own `performUpdate` call, are still read by their body.

## Test summary

- clipboard: 14 tests green; the paste tests pass again.
- printing: 30 tests green; `ExpandForPrintViewTest` still checks that `performUpdate` runs on `beforeprint`.
- No view changed, so nothing was checked in a browser.

Working on behalf of Sergey

author: liamphmurphy
body:
## Problem
Vesper currently runs only as a web app in a browser tab. Running it as a desktop app on macOS requires a thin Electron wrapper with native Cocoa tabs, persistent auth cookies, macOS notifications/Dock badges, optional local Docker/OrbStack stack startup, and `.dmg` packaging—plus multi-tab SSE multiplexing so opening 6+ tabs against plain HTTP/1.1 `localhost:8080` does not exhaust Chromium's 6-connection-per-origin limit.

## Change
Implemented the **macOS Electron desktop client** (`desktop/`) and **multi-tab SSE multiplexing** (`web/`), temporarily omitting `.github/workflows/` changes to isolate GitHub PAT workflow permissions:

1. **`f5f76a1f` (`LAZYAGENTS-230`) — Multi-tab SSE multiplexing (`web/`):**
   - Added [`web/lib/sse-multiplexer.ts`](web/lib/sse-multiplexer.ts) using Web Locks (`navigator.locks`) for leader election and `BroadcastChannel` to relay SSE payloads and online/offline state across same-origin tabs, with automatic failover on leader exit and direct `EventSource` fallback when APIs are unavailable.
   - Wired `web/components/shell/live-updates.tsx` to use `createSseClient` while preserving React Query invalidations and `vesper:sse` `CustomEvent` dispatching.
2. **`d3f8a047` (`LAZYAGENTS-228`) — Electron scaffold & connection screen (`desktop/`):**
   - Scaffolded `desktop/` (`TypeScript` + `Electron`), hardened `BrowserWindow` defaults (`contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`), shared `persist:vesper` session partition, `userData/config.json` persistence (`http://localhost:8080` default), trusted-frame IPC gating, and the Dusk-themed `offline.html` fallback & Settings UI.
3. **`87633f18` (`LAZYAGENTS-229`) — Native Cocoa tabs, menus & link routing (`desktop/`):**

author: iannitram
body:
Closes #1476

## What was built

- **Frame timer** (`apps/wavcraft/src/app.rs`): `frame_timer_begin` is the first call in `logic`, `frame_timer_end` the last call in `ui`. It measures the work of one frame, not the gap between frames. The newest 20000 values are kept in `frame_times`. When the window is hidden, `logic` runs without `ui`, and the next `logic` overwrites `frame_start`, so nothing is recorded for that frame.
- **`FRAMETIMES` verb** (`app.rs`, `control_request`): `FRAMETIMES` answers `OK n=<n> median_ms=<x> p95_ms=<x> worst_ms=<x> over=<n>`. `FRAMETIMES reset` answers `OK n=0`. Any other argument answers `ERR FRAMETIMES [reset]`.
- **p95 in the summary** (`crates/core/src/frame_stats.rs`): `FrameSummary` gains `p95_ms` (nearest rank, zero for an empty list). This is the B1.2 summary with p95 added; the B1.2 fields are unchanged.
- **Control header** (`apps/wavcraft/src/control.rs`): lists `FRAMETIMES`, `FRAMETIMES reset` and `NAV`.
- **Tests**: `crates/core/tests/b1_frame_stats.rs` gains p95 checks (the five existing tests still pass, with an added p95 assertion in two of them). New `apps/wavcraft/src/b1_frametimes_tests.rs` (5 tests) is declared in `app.rs`.

No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests, no `unsafe`. The audio code is not touched. The timer runs on the window thread only.

## How the Verify passes

- `cargo fmt --all`: no changes after the edits.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: finished with no warnings.
- `cargo test -p wavcraft-core --test b1_frame_stats`: `test result: ok. 7 passed`.
- `cargo test -p wavcraft --bin wavcraft b1_frametimes`: `test result: ok. 5 passed`.
- `cargo test --workspace`: exit 0, no failures.

Not run: the real-app check (`cargo build --release -p wavcraft` plus a running control channel with `NAV 0 48000`). The unit tests drive the same `control_request` path and the same timer methods, but the live `FRAMETIMES` answer after one second of playback has not been seen.

## Code map

Not edited in this PR (per the decider's rule). Changes needed:

- `crates/core/src/frame_stats.rs`: new row. Sums up a list of frame times in milliseconds: count, median, p95 (nearest rank), worst and frames over 16.7 ms. The app calls it from the FRAMETIMES verb. Key items: `FRAME_BUDGET_MS`, `FrameSummary`, `summarize_frames`. Tests: `crates/core/tests/b1_frame_stats.rs`. Status: present, wired. Step: B1 (B1.2, B1.3).
- `crates/core/tests/b1_frame_stats.rs`: new row. Locks the frame-time summary: five frames, empty list, even count, exactly 16.7 is not over, non-finite values skipped, p95 by nearest rank. 7 tests, 0 ignored. Step: B1. Covers: frame_stats.
- `apps/wavcraft/src/b1_frametimes_tests.rs`: new row. B1.3 window tests (declared in app.rs): FRAMETIMES reset and answer, a timed frame is counted, the list is capped at 20000, an unknown argument is refused. Key items: `reset_answers_n_zero`, `a_timed_frame_is_counted`, `ending_without_a_start_records_nothing`, `the_list_keeps_only_the_newest_frames`, `an_unknown_argument_is_refused`. Step: B1 (B1.3). Declared in app.rs.
- `apps/wavcraft/src/app.rs`: the `WaveApp` struct row gains `frame_start` and `frame_times`. The `impl eframe::App` row: `logic` now starts with `frame_timer_begin`. The `ui` row: now ends with `frame_timer_end`. The view-helpers row (next to `view_text`) gains `frame_timer_begin` and `frame_timer_end`. Line numbers move.
- Control verbs table: add `| FRAMETIMES, FRAMETIMES reset | Work time per frame (start of logic to end of ui): count, median, p95, worst and frames over 16.7 ms; reset clears it | app.rs |`

body:
Fixes every row of the 2026-11-16 whole-repo audit (66 rows, each confirmed by a three-lens refute pass), plus one found while fixing them. Version 2.7.1; the CHANGELOG entry lists each change.

## What changes

- **Refuse before clean.** `run_all.py full --keep-frames --redraw` checks its spans and `frames/` (every PNG it reads back, and their size) before the clean-up; a typo or a missing `frames/` used to delete the delivered build first.
- **Verdicts, not tracebacks.** Files that do not probe, audio that outlasts the video, failed ebur128 runs, WebMs, silent cue buffers, fmt-less stems, a raising `qa_scan` part and a missing `narration.wav` each give a NOT CHECKED row for what could not be measured.
- **False PASS closed.** Q706 fails audio that stops more than 0.1 s before the picture (85 approved files measured +0.000 s); Q402 is NOT CHECKED without `px`; Q301 samples a rest's real first and last frame; the selftest counts NaN as a mismatch.
- **Approval bound to the file.** `qa.json` records the checked file's sha256; `approve` refuses a foreign one.
- **stdin closed** on the mux and the approval hash (a waiting key cut a 600 s mux to about 10 s with exit 0).
- **Q806** reads possessive respellings, digits in hyphenated tokens and "$1.50" correctly; verdicts on 30 calibration narrations and 343 cached lines are unchanged.
- **3D plates.** Names resolve from constants and aliases (or refuse); a name must be one folder.
- **Dependencies and supply chain.** numpy 2.5.5, ctranslate2 4.9.0, onnxruntime 1.32.0, phonemizer 3.6.0, Blender 5.2.4 LTS; each side environment runs from a full exact-pin lock; Kokoro files are pinned to their Hugging Face sha256. CI pins a month-end BtbN ffmpeg build and checks its sha256. Renovate waits 7 days and runs pip-compile on all four locks.
- **Found while fixing:** `uv run --with-requirements` does not check `--hash` lines (uv 0.13.8; a wrong hash installed fine). SECURITY.md, README and engine.md now say the locks hold versions, not bytes.
- **Speed.** The template frame draws in 29.5 ms instead of 95.8, pixel for pixel the same.

## Verified

- `qa.py selftest` on a fresh copy of this tree: `SELFTEST: PASS (161 fixtures, 60 of 60 codes covered, 0 expected gaps)`, both templates DELIVERED.
- Pixel identity: 450 template frames (16:9 and 9:16), 24 frames of four 2D kits and 2,500 random helper calls equal to the old engine.
- A narrated build DELIVERED (Q806, Q807 PASS) with the bumped Kokoro and speech environments; Kokoro audio byte-identical.
- A 3D final plate on Blender 5.2.4 and `run_all.py full --fps 24` DELIVERED; frames match the approved 5.2.3 plate within re-render noise (0.11 of 255).
- Each audit repro re-run on the integrated engine gives the fixed result.
- `scripts/check.py` 0 problems, ruff format clean, ruff 200 (was 201), `cards.py check` OK, skillcheck clean, actionlint clean, `claude plugin validate` passes.

## Not verified

- Renovate's real pip-compile run (first one on 2026-12-01).
- The side environments on Linux and macOS (locks are `--universal`; only Windows was run).

## Left for a decision

- The reviewer agent's Bash is not narrowed: scoped patterns could not be proven to allow its `cd <folder>; uv run ...; echo` calls in this session.
- Enforcing hashes would mean installing each environment with `uv pip install --require-hashes` instead of `uv run --with-requirements`, a change to every documented command.
- PR #3 (ImgBot) optimizes the old flow SVG; this PR replaces that SVG.

author: obviyus
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: listed models are refused before any request when OpenClaw only *guesses* they are not chat models. Examples are an ID that names a non-text family, an OpenAI live/cyber/exp/alpha ID, or an unfamiliar kind value. Other guesses show a model that fails for the listing key, such as `gpt-5.6-cyber`.

## User Impact

- Rows that **declare** non-chat support (native kind, output modality, catalog) are unchanged: hidden and refused before any request.
- Rows that are only **unlikely** chat leave the default picker and setup choices but appear in "all" views. Typed and configured refs to them still run.
- OpenAI default picker on a real listing: wrongly shown 1 → 0, wrongly hidden 3 → 3. Typed `openai/o3` replies while it is absent from the default list.
- Tencent TokenHub: an uncatalogued, unlabeled listed ID (the #198288 TTS case) stays out of the default picker without hiding new chat models from typed refs.

## Why This Change Was Made

#199998 made "no evidence" unknown, but kept an interim rule: an ID that names a non-text family got `chat: false`. This PR separates guesses from declarations:

| state | encoding | default picker / setup | "all", typed, configured | pre-run guard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes / unknown | no `inference`, or `chat: true` | shown | shown, runs | passes |
| unlikely | `inference: { chat: true, chatEvidence: "unlikely" }` | hidden | shown, runs | passes |
| declared no | `inference: { chat: false }` | hidden | hidden | refused (#184996) |

- **Marker:** an optional `chatEvidence` key inside `inference`; `chat` is not widened. Old readers drop it and see plain chat:
  - the 2026.11.5 beta inference schema is a non-strict `z.object`;
  - released stable readers have no `inference` at all (v1/v2 bundles only);
  - the v3 hosted reader drops unknown `inference` keys.
  - The registry runtime model and the v3 row schema accept the key.
  - No wire, protocol, config or cache-scope change. `ModelChoice` is a closed protocol object, so there is no "unverified" badge.
- **Weak evidence** applies only to uncatalogued rows without capability fields:
  - the ID-family pattern;
  - an unfamiliar value in a kind field the same listing uses for chat;
  - a provider prior, set with the new discovery option `unknownModelChatEvidence: "unlikely"`.
- **Surfaces:**
  - The visibility owner (default picker, `models.list`, `/models`) treats unlikely like `deprecated`: listed only in `all`, configured and retained views.
  - The setup picker, oMLX and Bifrost offer likely chat only.
  - The guard still refuses only `chat === false`.
- **OpenAI:**
  - `live|cyber|exp|alpha` IDs are demoted instead of dropped, and the `gpt-5.6-cyber` exception is removed.
  - `search` IDs stay dropped: Responses rejects them with a 400, dated snapshots too.
  - The pre-GPT-5 rule stays (#167462).
- **Tencent:** opts into the prior. Its list has IDs and status only and includes speech models (#198288).
- **Docs:** `model-catalogs.md` and `src/plugins/AGENTS.md` each state the rule once, citing #198288 and #199998. The OpenAI and Tencent provider pages are updated to match.
- **Supersedes #199545:** the name-matched OpenAI IDs are demoted, not revealed, so their 404/500 IDs stay out of the default picker.

## Evidence

**Replay of saved real listings, main `84a378cf` vs this head.** Same truth labels as #199998.

| provider | listed | proven | default picker main / branch | wrongly shown / hidden, main | wrongly shown / hidden, branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI (after account projection) | 125 | 31 | 37 / 36 | 1 / 3 | **0 / 3** |
| HF router + OpenRouter | 600 | 600 | 600 / 600 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Vercel AI Gateway | 508 | 508 | 323 / 323 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| DeepInfra | 178 | 178 | 92 / 92 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Venice | 414 | 414 | 142 / 142 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| NVIDIA (no proof) | 39 | 0 | 29 / 29 | – | – |
| Ollama library | 24 | 24 | 23 / 23 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| models.dev | 9,878 | 9,545 | 9,414 / 9,414 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- **OpenAI wrongly hidden (3):** `gpt-4o-mini` and `o3` fall under the pre-GPT-5 rule and run by typed ref. `gpt-5-search-api` is Chat-Completions-only.
- **OpenAI rows refused pre-run:** 46 on main, 0 on this branch. 38 of the 46 are now unlikely; 8 hit the pre-GPT-5 drop.
- **TokenHub:** its authenticated listing is uncaptured, so a fixture of that shape is tested instead.

**Real Gateway (built dist, real OpenAI key).**
- **Setup:** each side ran under `env -i` with only PATH, a temp HOME, TMPDIR, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. The key came through stdin only.
- **Isolation:** loopback, its own port and token, no channels (the harness refuses one). Reads waited for a `ready` live listing.

| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI rows: default `models list` / `--all --provider openai` | 39 / 39 | 36 / 102 |
| `gpt-5.6-cyber` default / all | shown / shown | absent / shown |
| `gpt-image-2` default / all | absent / absent | absent / shown |
| typed `openai/o3` turn (absent from default on both) | reply `ok` | reply `ok` |
| typed `openai/gpt-image-2` turn | refused pre-run `model_chat_unsupported` | sent; provider 404 |

- **Cleanup:** 0 key hits in outputs and state, both Gateways exited and ports closed. The host Gateway was untouched.
- `models list --provider X` already uses the `all` view (#142063).

**Tests and gates.**
- **New cases** are red on `84a378cf` and green here:
  - the gate table (shown / unlikely / declared no) and the provider prior;
  - visibility: default, `all` and configured views;
  - discovery → prepared snapshot → visibility → `resolveModelAsync`: the bare ID-pattern row passes the pre-run check, and the declared-no pin test still rejects;
  - the setup picker;
  - the OpenAI API-key catalog;
  - a Tencent ID-only listing;
  - an old-reader schema fixture;
  - the v3 reader keeping the marker.
- **Consumer suites updated and green:** live-runtime, OpenCode Zen/Go, oMLX, Bifrost, LiteLLM, Anthropic discovery, Codex cyber-failover, utility model.
- **Typecheck and lint:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- **Prefix stability:** `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes (14/14).
- **Ratchets:** test lines +178 (allowance 400); line-cap passes.
- **Builds:** `ocx build --dts` and `build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke` pass on this head.
- **`plugin-sdk:api:diff`:** one changed signature, `ModelInferenceCapabilitiesSchema` (optional `chatEvidence`), digest `47bba3f8`.
- **Size:** production +96 / −40 in 10 files; no new module, state, cache or config.

**Accepted edges (no code)**
- The existing route-change overlay replaces a route-moved row's `inference` with `chat: false`, as it already does for any such row.
- A future `chatEvidence` value would fail this build's schema, so a later state should use a new key.
- Main or nightly state saved under #199998 keeps an ID-pattern row as `chat: false` until rediscovery.

## Merge danger

- **Two-way door:** a revert restores #199998's behavior, and older builds read the marker as plain chat. No migration, config or protocol change.
- **Blast radius if wrong:** listed non-chat models appear in `all` views. A typed ref to one gets the provider error instead of the pre-run refusal.

author: tutkli
body:
Closes #2831

## What

`Collection.#sortByDomOrder` now tries a sibling walk before the comparator. When at least 16 handles are registered and every connected host shares one `parentNode`, it walks `parent.firstChild … nextSibling` once, ranks each host, stops as soon as the last registered host has been seen, and sorts by rank. `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so two handles on one host keep registration order and detached hosts go last in registration order, which are the tie-breaks the comparator already had.

It falls back to the `compareDocumentPosition` comparator when there are fewer than 16 handles or the connected hosts sit under more than one parent.

## Bounding the walk

- **Threshold:** below 16 handles the walk never runs, so a few handles inside a very wide parent read no `nextSibling` at all. The spec pins this with 3 handles among 1000 children.
- **Early stop:** the walk ends at the last registered host, not at the end of the parent. The spec pins this with 20 handles at the head of a 10 000-child parent; the walk takes fewer than 40 steps.

## Specs (`collection.spec.ts`)

- The three cases #2809 pinned at N − 1 / linear comparisons now run on one parent and assert **0** comparisons. The N − 1 and linear bounds are still pinned on the comparator path, using hosts split across two parents.
- New: a shuffled 1000-sibling bulk register (0 comparisons, walk ≤ children), the wide-parent and early-stop bounds above, and detached-last, shared-host, comment-anchor and runtime-reverse ordering on the fast path.
- Checked that the tests can fail: with the fast path turned off, 6 of the new cases fail. With the threshold dropped to 2, only the wide-parent case fails, and every ordering case stays green.

## Bench (`forty-cdk-bench` @ `87d5da0`, 1000-option combobox, 15 pairs)

| | 0.45.0 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `compareDocumentPosition` calls, `5` / Backspace | 538 / 3810 | **0 / 0** |
| `#sortByDomOrder` inclusive | 18.67 ms/press | **3.41 ms/press** |
| median latency, type `5` / Backspace | 144.7 / 242.6 ms | 80.5 / 215.5 ms |
| profiled non-idle | 173.45 ms/press | 125.02 ms/press |

The latency and non-idle rows also include #2830, which is already on `main`. Only the first two rows belong to this change.

## Gates

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (12 604 passed), and `pnpm build` with every `postbuild` gate. `check:fesm-size` passes at +981 B on `forty-cdk-core.mjs` (allowance 19 387 B), so the baseline is not regenerated.

**Payload** — `winLoss(data, { plots: true })` returns `Scene & { plots: WinLossPlots }`:
- `blocks: { index, value, sign, x, y, width, height, color }[]` at full precision — the block rects' unrounded geometry (the marks round the same values).
- `sign` is `'up'` / `'down'` / `'flat'` for positive / negative / zero values; the zero block is the 1px centerline rect.
- `color` is the rect's fill (`winColor` / `lossColor`); the 0.4 dimming on flat blocks (and on losses when both colors are the same) is an opacity, not a different color.
- `frame` is the padded plot box with `xDomain: [0, n-1]`; there is no value domain — block height is fixed by the sign, not by the value's magnitude.
- Empty payload (`{ blocks: [] }`, no domain) attached on the existing empty-data return.

**Design notes**
- `WinLossNanoChart` pins `D` and `O` explicitly — the overloaded core fn can't carry generic `T` through `renderNanoChart` inference.
- The plots rects equal the rendered rects up to the scene's 2dp rounding (the test rounds the plots values before comparing, so a last-ULP difference in the slot math doesn't fail it).

**Tests** — new `tests/charts/plots-winloss.test.ts` (7 tests): golden fixture covering all three signs, win/loss colors, empty payload, full-precision proof, differential snapshot (scenes byte-identical with the option off), overlay invariance (annotations on vs off), overload type tests incl. the widened-variable case.

**Verification** — core 579/579, React 97/97, typecheck + lint clean in both packages.

**Size** (standing rule) — core barrel 16.62 → 16.71 kB gz, React barrel 16.91 → 17.00 kB gz, both inside the 18 kB budgets. Figures refreshed everywhere (READMEs, API.md incl. win-loss 2.86 → 3.01 kB, demo hero). No changeset: the minor changeset lands with #229.

## What changes

- The engine submodule moves to pixel-engine 1005249 (P847: `_engine`, `_crackle`).
