author: kixelated
body:
## Summary

Nightly's `Tests (rs quic-sim)` failed `tests::sim::handshake_under_loss` (job [133445816309](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/actions/runs/43909101837/job/133445816309)) on a `debug_assert` in `Slots::insert`: "insertions must increase".

Root cause: `detect_lost_packets` compared every space's packet numbers against the in-flight MTU probe's number, but only the Data space sends probes and every space numbers from 0. In the failing case the client's Handshake pn 0 matched the Data-space probe's pn 0. Loss detection skipped Handshake pn 0 as a "lost MTU probe" and declared pn 1 lost. Then it removed the real probe from the Data space's sent packets, and the next pass declared Handshake pn 0 lost after pn 1, so `lost_packets` got an insert below its last entry. In release builds the assert is off, so the Data probe is marked lost by mistake and the Handshake packet's loss is delayed.

- `MtuDiscovery::in_flight_mtu_probe` and `on_non_probe_lost` now take the `SpaceId`, as `on_acked` already does, and ignore other spaces. The black-hole detector orders losses against probes by packet number, so Handshake losses no longer go into it either.
- The existing mtud search test now also checks that no Handshake packet number counts as the probe.

The bug came from quinn: quinn-proto 0.11.19 has the same `in_flight_mtu_probe()` comparison and space-blind `on_non_probe_lost`.

### The quiche `handshakeloss` interop cell

The other Nightly failure in this area, `MISMATCH client=moq-quic server=quiche handshakeloss` (job [132842368343](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/actions/runs/43724172821/job/132842368343)), is a different cause. The moq-quic client logged `handshake timed out` (no panic). That run was on 505a86f, before #8824 raised `handshake_timeout` from 10 s to 30 s for exactly this case. Any residual is owned by `quest/m4/quic-handshake-speedup.md`. Interop only began running in Nightly two days ago, and today's jobs (which include #8824) were still running when this opened.

## Validation

- Reproduced deterministically by running `handshake(14917314294402731587, 26290µs, loss 0.2415 / 0.1728)` (the failing case from the CI log). Before the fix, it panicked in `Slots<LostPacket>::insert` from `detect_lost_packets` via `on_loss_detection_timeout`. Instrumented, it showed client Handshake `sent=[0,1,2,3]`, both well past `loss_delay`, with only pn 1 declared lost. After the fix it passes.
- `MOQ_QUIC_SEED=573977490 MOQ_QUIC_CASES=4096` (the Nightly configuration) passes, and so do seeds 1, 2, 3 at 4096 cases. Before the fix, seeds 1 to 3 pass too, so the collision is rare (one case in about 16k).
- `cargo test -p moq-quic --lib mtud` passes (all mtud and MTU discovery connection tests).
- `just check` passes.

## Impact

- Public API: none (crate-private `MtuDiscovery`).
- Wire: none. Behavior: a lost Handshake or Initial packet that shares the probe's packet number is now declared lost on time, and the MTU probe is no longer marked lost by mistake.

## Caused by

Inherited from quinn with the port ([moq-dev/moq#6635](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/pull/6635) era), so it is as old as the code. Exposed by the new `handshake_under_loss` sweep from [moq-dev/moq#8824](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/pull/8824).

body:
## Summary

Ingestion now pauses for the Student to check the proposed Topics before anything is embedded. Closes #5.

```text
upload (202, thread_id)
  chunk
  extract_topics        # BACKGROUND_MODEL, existing Topics flagged as merges
  topic_review          # interrupt(), saved in the Postgres checkpointer
    GET  /threads/{id}          -> proposed + existing Topics
    POST /threads/{id}/resume   -> approve / rename / merge / remove (422 if it makes no sense)
  save_topics           # final list saved against the Study Space
  embed
  store
```

```text
frontend/src/features/
├── notes/    NotesTab (upload, status per file, delete)
├── topics/   TopicsTab (rename, merge, delete, select all), TopicReviewDialog
├── chat/     ChatEmpty (new empty Chat from the updated design)
└── spaces/   dashboard tabs: Notes, Topics (kept in the URL: ?tab=topics)
```

- `topics` table (names unique per Space among unmerged Topics); `documents.thread_id`.
- Checkpoint tables are created at startup: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` inside a request waits on the request's own transaction and hangs.
- `docs/api.md` and `docs/database.md` updated. Resume for `topic_review` returns `202` + the document, not an event stream.
- Deleting a Topic (one or several selected) also deletes the Topics that were merged into it, so they do not come back as separate Topics.
- Spaces are listed newest first. Disabled buttons explain why in a tooltip; icon buttons have one too (shadcn tooltip, 250 ms delay).
- Differences from the prototype: a merge target `<select>` in the review dialog (the prototype has no way to pick one); Delete and select all on the Topics tab. Not built yet: Weak topics and Learned material tabs, the weak-topic tile and "New chat" in the empty Chat, and the Subject Library (its tile is disabled).

## Evidence

- **Before:** an upload went straight to embedding; no Topics existed.
  **After:** manual run against the stack: upload -> `GET /threads/{id}` returns 6 proposed Topics -> bad `interrupt_id` gives `409 nothing_to_resume`, unknown Topic gives `422 invalid_topic_review` -> valid answer (rename, merge, remove) saves 4 Topics and the document becomes `ready`; answering twice gives `409`.
- `pytest`: 70 passed (new `test_topic_review.py`: merge chains, loops, renames, duplicates, model output cleanup). `ruff`, `tsc`, `vite build` clean.
- Not verified: the UI in a browser (the screenshot tool failed); only type-checked and built.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Two new migrations (0009 topics, 0010 `documents.thread_id`) are additive and reversible.

**Blast Radius:** uploads

Every upload now stops at `awaiting_topic_review` until answered, and needs `BACKGROUND_MODEL`; a missing model marks the document `failed`.

Each session read goes through one transaction factory (`session_transaction_of`, `stores/session_transaction.py`) used by the gate, the agent backend and the MCP route. A session is checked at the handshake, at a resume and every `SESSION_RECHECK_SECONDS`, never on a frame. A tick whose store raises parks the seat as a drop does and closes with `SERVER_ERROR_CLOSE_CODE`, which the page already reconnects on; no new code.

Cost (head decision N3): a member who logged out can send frames for at most 60 s.

Tests: raising store parks and resumes once it answers; a session ended between ticks ends at the next tick (manual clock); a frame does not read the session. The per-frame close tests became tick tests. Paths outside the claim: `src/hopin/stores/session_transaction.py` (the factory's owner), `tests/signaling/conftest.py` (app fixture takes the manual scheduler), `tests/e2e/support/server.py` (the browser tests' server runs the recheck tick after 1 s so an ended session ends within the test's wait).

author: etorreborre
body:
This PR improves the node ability to switch between forks when the Chain Growth Property is broken (fewer than `k` blocks in the stability window of `3k / f` slots):

 - When we arrive at the end of the stability window, at epoch `e + 1`, if there aren't enough blocks to flush the volatile DB to the stable store, we create a "candidate snapshot" that is use to create the stake distribution used to validate the headers arriving at epoch `e + 2`. We also compute the rewards from epoch `e` with that snapshot, so they are ready when making the transition from `e + 1` to `e + 2`.
 
 - A candidate snapshot can be replaced by another candidate snapshot if the ledger needs to rollback and progress onto another fork.
 
 - A chain that stays sparse for a whole epoch, say `e + 1`, will still have to flush a final snapshot for epoch `e` because the transition from `e + 1` to `e + 2` needs this snapshot for ratification.

### Testing

The interesting tests are in `sparse_chain.rs` and `switch_to_fork.rs` (for the partial switch case).
 
### Notes on various changes

 - The notification of new stake distribution has an additional "stage" to avoid deadlocks in `build_node.rs`. It feels more and more like a hack to me that we need to address with a proper stage. @rkuhn do you have anything to propose in that regards? (or say that it will be left for a further clean-up)
 
 - We now need to verify sent headers with the stake distribution that corresponds to the snapshot of the chain they are following (see the changes in `validate_header.rs`).
 
 - I have added an enum for snapshot observers so they can know if a snapshot is final or not.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved stake-distribution and header validation for sparse epochs, so headers are checked against the relevant candidate chain before pool lookup.
  * Candidate stake snapshots are now reconciled as chains advance, roll back, or switch forks, and finalized when their blocks become stable.
  * Improved recovery when a fork switch fails, preserving the prior chain and snapshot state.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated trace documentation to describe candidate snapshot events and snapshot directory warnings.

author: thirstypig
body:
Test-only.

## What happened
Main's CI failed after three merges on 2026-11-16: #504 (9832fce), #503 (89de463) and #501 (1c6164a). Each time it was a `LeagueContext.test.tsx` test, my own from #504:
- **#504:** "a failed rules refresh keeps the rules it already has". This was fixed in #506.
- **#503 and #501:** "re-reads the league rules when the tab becomes visible, keeping the old map meanwhile". **This PR fixes it.**

Prod was unaffected: every deploy went live and was verified. The failures are in the test, not the app.

## Why
- The provider starts on league 1. Once the league list loads, it moves to the user's league, and that move clears and re-fetches the rules.
- On a slow runner the move can land mid-test. Its fetch then takes the test's queued one-off slow response, and the test sees the wrong state.

## Fix
- A shared `RulesProbe` and a `settledOnLeague()` helper.
- Both rules tests now wait for league 9 and its rules before changing any mock.

## Evidence
- **Reproduced on main's version:** I held the league list and released it right after the test queued its slow response. The test fails.
- **The fixed test can't reach that state:** it waits for league 9 first.
- 8/8 pass normally and with a 50ms slow league list.

## Process note
After each merge I checked that prod reported the merged commit, but I didn't check main's own CI run, so these three red runs went unnoticed until the GitHub emails arrived. From now on I watch `gh run list --branch main` after every merge.

body:
Add data-only inquiry contracts for host-supplied reference-letter choices and account-balance subtitles in existing option rows.

# Solution

- Add the reusable `FormOption` data model and use it in `ReferenceLetterInquiry` to keep host contracts independent of DesignKit UI types.
- Add optional option-row subtitles, including accessibility label/value support and a TODO for provisional subtitle styling pending Figma.
- Keep this PR limited to the inquiry contract and option subtitles; leave selection and validation to the shared form engine.
- Preserve project decision documents and keep backend routes, wire models and response codes outside this public repository.

# File rationale

| File | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `OptionItem.swift` | Add optional subtitle data while preserving existing title-only callers through a nil default. |
| `OptionRow.swift` | Show the supporting balance below the account title and expose both through accessibility. Mark temporary styling pending Figma. |
| `OptionItemTests.swift` | Protect the default nil subtitle used by existing callers. |
| `OptionRowTests.swift` | Check subtitle height, unchanged width, and title-only appearance against the previous rendering. Use an explicit Button label closure to satisfy SwiftLint. |
| `FormOption.swift` | Provide shared option data without coupling host services to a UI component. |
| `ReferenceLetterInquiry.swift` | Carry host-supplied choices and contact data. Keep the encrypted email for return to the host without prescribing a submission flow. |
| `ReferenceLetterService.swift` | Define the asynchronous inquiry boundary implemented by the host. |
| `FormOptionTests.swift` | Check that the supporting subtitle is optional by default. |
| `ReferenceLetterInquiryTests.swift` | Check host choice order, empty option lists, and the omitted-language default instead of repeating property assignments. |
| `SandboxOptions.swift` | Supply a dummy account balance to exercise subtitles in the existing form demo. |
| `FormFieldsUITests.swift` | Check the account title and balance through the actual accessibility tree, including a title-only option. |

# Validation

- The owner reported `./Scripts/verify.sh` exit 0 for commit `014588e322240aca0d21a31c4ec638e288bb5ec6` in the third review. The following code change only puts each test-array element on its own line.

author: isaacthoman
body:
Together is now **Online**, and Online is a list of rooms.

Screenshots:

**The menu: Online in place of Together**

![The menu: Online in place of Together](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/1-menu.png?raw=true)

**The rooms, live: place colour, flies as pips, a padlock; a full room greyed**

![The rooms, live: place colour, flies as pips, a padlock; a full room greyed](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/2-rooms.png?raw=true)

**New room: typing the name (drawn from a hidden input)**

![New room: typing the name (drawn from a hidden input)](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/3-new-room-typing.png?raw=true)

**New room: place, public or unlisted, a masked password**

![New room: place, public or unlisted, a masked password](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/4-new-room.png?raw=true)

**A locked room's door**

![A locked room's door](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/5-password.png?raw=true)

**A wrong password, said in the heading's place**

![A wrong password, said in the heading's place](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/6-wrong-password.png?raw=true)

**In the room**

![In the room](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/7-in-the-room.png?raw=true)

**The rooms on a phone on its side, scrolling**

![The rooms on a phone on its side, scrolling](https://github.com/IsaacThoman/flies/blob/pr-assets-online-rooms/8-phone-rooms.png?raw=true)

## What it does
- **The rooms.** Online lists every public room with someone in it, fullest first: its name, its place's colour, its flies as eight pips, and a padlock if it has a password. It follows the room server live (a `browse` connection told `rooms` whenever the list changes). A full room is greyed. Above the list: New room, and Code (an unlisted room's ten letters).
- **New room.** A name (two words suggested, to keep or type over), the place, Public or Unlisted, an optional password. Create sits the fly there.
- **Locked rooms.** Choosing one, or opening its link or code, comes to its door: the password, then Join. A wrong one says "Wrong password" in pink where the name was. A device that has sat there before comes back without it; the starter never needs it.
- **Typing.** Fields are drawn in engine from a hidden `<input>` focused while one is typed into, so hardware keyboards, phone keyboards, IME, paste and password managers all work (`current-password` / `new-password`). A tap on a field focuses it during the tap itself, so a phone's keyboard comes up. The game reaches it only through a polled `TextEntry` contract, so the Apple TV can bridge its own keyboard later.

## Server
- Rooms carry a name, listed or not, and a lock: a salted scrypt hash (N=2^14), compared in constant time, off the event loop. Never stored or logged in plain text; sent only in the hello over the socket, until welcomed.
- A room's code doesn't get past its lock. The list never carries unlisted rooms.
- Names: up to 24 characters, NFC, spaces collapsed and trimmed, only letters/marks/digits/spaces and a little punctuation (no control, invisible or bidi characters, no emoji). Filtering what names say is left as a follow-up.
- Limits (in `limits.ts`): password tries 5 at once then 3/min per address, and 10 then 6/min per room; rooms started 5 at once, 30 an hour per address. Address counts are kept an hour after its last connection, so reconnecting doesn't reset them.
- A listed room is forgotten after a day with nobody there (unlisted ones keep 30 days, as their links are invitations). Old `tables.json` files load as unlisted, unlocked rooms named "Flies".
- Protocol 3: older pages are refused and reload once into the new site.

## Redeploying
Nothing new to configure: no env vars, no volume or Caddy changes. `rooms_data` keeps the same `tables.json`, now with names and password hashes.

## Checks
`npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run tvos:typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run e2e` (it now also makes a named, locked room from the menus with the keys, joins it from another tab's list after a wrong password, and checks its link alone opens only its door). iOS isn't touched (its app's `fly:` scheme keeps Online off there).

body:
From the weekly flaky-test scan (Test workflow, 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-16, 52 runs + 2 re-run attempts).

## Flakiness
| Test | First attempt failed | Error |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/epic-mode.spec.ts:83` grants page shows Sell button (not Edit)… | 50 / 50 runs | `getByRole('button', {name: 'Sell'})` not found, 5 s |
| `e2e/epic-mode.spec.ts:97` loans page shows Request Payoff button… | 49 / 50 runs | `getByRole('button', {name: 'Calculate repayment'})` not found, 15 s |

Both pass on Playwright's automatic retry (`retries: 1`) every time, so CI stays green. Example: run [43874553741](https://github.com/rahulshahepic/epic-stocks/actions/runs/43874553741) on `42cad979` failed attempt 1 and passed the retry for the same SHA.

## Root cause
`importFixtureAs` clicks **Import** and then calls `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')`. That waits for a load-lifecycle state the page has already reached, so it returns immediately while `POST /api/import/excel` is still in flight. The test then flips Epic Mode, logs back in and opens Grants/Loans before a first-time import has committed:

- **Attempt 1:** the user is new. The list is empty ("No grants yet", as the failure snapshot shows), so no Sell or Calculate repayment button appears.
- **Retry:** the same user already has attempt 1's rows on file. The page renders rows while the re-import is still running, so the test passes.

The banner, prices and 403 tests in the same file don't need rows, which is why only these two flake.

Reproduced locally against PostgreSQL 16, the production-built frontend and `E2E_TEST=1` uvicorn, with `--retries=0`. Both tests failed on a fresh database every time. Afterwards the DB held 12 grants and 21 loans for the user, and the snapshot still said "No grants yet".

## Fix
Wait for the import's own response and assert it is 2xx. This is test-only; no app code changes.

## Verification
- `npx playwright test --project=epic-mode --retries=0 --repeat-each=2` on a **fresh database**, three times: 48/48 passed. Before the fix, the first pass on a fresh DB failed both tests.
- `npx tsc -b --noEmit` and `eslint` are clean.

## Also found (not fixed here)
On 3 runs this week, many `[main]` e2e tests timed out together for several minutes (`test-login` / `page.goto` ERR_ABORTED). One example is the 18-failure attempt in [43632751288](https://github.com/rahulshahepic/epic-stocks/actions/runs/43632751288). I reproduced a full backend stall locally: 8 clients × 8 parallel reads on a single uvicorn gave 243 of 264 requests timing out at 60 s. Likely cause: `MaintenanceMiddleware` / `EpicModeMiddleware` / `EncryptionMiddleware` open a DB session synchronously on the event loop. When the 10-connection pool is exhausted, the checkout blocks the loop for up to 30 s, and the loop is what returns those connections. This touches production request handling, so it needs its own discussed PR.

Review per REVIEW_POLICY.md is still required. The author session has not reviewed this change.

author: baitisj
body:
Follow-up to #127. Run C7 (11-16, 17:16Z, main fd6b055 with #127 flashed hands-free) sent a second perfect DMR burst at 1 W: 62/62 blocks, AG7EW, 528 bytes exact. The watchdog still reset the radio about 1.9 s after key-down.

The new `guard` readout showed:

    guard armed=0 now=30998 csr=24000000 st=b10f0002 at=45780 kick=46135 dl=0

The guard was in state "off", so it didn't end an overlong key-up. The kicker's last kick came 355 ms after key-down, at the moment the host re-enumerated the radio (kernel log 17:16:19Z). It never kicked again, even though it runs at top priority.

## Cause (from the code; C8 will confirm)

ST's USB library (OpenRTX's `usb_dcd_int.c`) clears an IN endpoint's FIFO-empty interrupt mask (DIEPEMPMSK) only on transfer complete. At 1 W the host drops the radio mid-write. `vcom_writeBlock` then times out and flushes the FIFO, but the mask stays set. Once SetConfiguration reopens EP1, the FIFO-empty interrupt is pending again every time its handler returns. Thread code never runs again, the kicker included, and the IWDG resets the radio.

## Changes (uv380-blowfang.patch)

- `usb_dcd_int.c` `DCD_WriteEmptyTxFifo`: clears the endpoint's mask once nothing is left to write, as ST's later HAL does (`PCD_WriteEmptyTxFifo`).
- `usb_dcd_int.c` `DCD_HandleUsbReset_ISR`: a bus reset ends every IN transfer, so it clears DIEPEMPMSK and the IN endpoints' transfer state.
- `usb_vcom.c` `vcom_writeBlock`: on its 500 ms timeout, abandons the transfer and clears its mask.

The transmit guard (#123, #127) is unchanged. A real overlong key-up still resets the radio.

## Tests

- New: `test_usb_fifo_empty_interrupt_cannot_storm` in `tests/test_uv380_c6000.py`.
- Locally: the patch regenerates byte for byte from the scratch tree, and both USB files pass a host `gcc -fsyntax-only`.
- Docs: `firmware/uv380-openrtx/README.md` and `docs/uv380-c6000-modem.md`.

Next on the bench (C8): flash this, key once at 1 W, then read `guard`. It should show no reset, and the lines said after key-down should reach hamlet.

body:
Opened by a Valkyrie Run of agent `agent`.

Run: `run_dfcabf50-7f7a-4b08`

<!-- valkyrie-issue: 57fb8ab8d148e275 -->

Closes mnzsss/ivar#302

Stage summaries:
- **Execução:** `ivar feature rebase` now has opt-in `--keep-conflicts`, plus `--continue` and `--abort`. The default still aborts on conflict, and the existing abort test passes unchanged. The new rebase and CLI tests pass; fmt and clippy (`-D warnings`) are clean.

The full test run has 28 failures in lib tests and 3 in `nested_subfeatures`. They are identical to what I get with my changes stashed, so they are not from this work. I did not run the graph simulation.

**Behavior**
- **`--keep-conflicts`**: on a conflict the rebase stays in progress and the repo is reported as `conflicted`. The conflicted files are listed (human and JSON), and a `next:` line gives the `--continue` and `--abort` commands for that repo. The other repos carry on.
- **No rebase in progress after a refusal** (for example a nonexistent base): the repo is `skipped` with a `rebase.failed` warning, not reported as a kept conflict. The plan said "treat as a rebase error"; I chose `skipped` so one repo cannot abort the whole batch. Say if you want it to be a hard failure instead.
- **`--continue`**:
  - If unmerged paths remain, it refuses without running git, returns `conflicted` with the remaining files, and keeps the state.
  - If it finishes, the repo is `rebased`.
  - If it stops again on a later commit, the repo is `conflicted` with the new files.
- **`--abort`**: runs `git rebase --abort`, reports the repo as `skipped`, and adds an informational `rebase.aborted` warning that leaves the exit code alone.
- **No rebase in progress**: `--continue` and `--abort` give `skipped` with a `rebase.not_in_progress` warning.
- **Plain `feature rebase` over an in-progress worktree**: gives the new `rebase.in_progress` warning, "use `--continue` or `--abort`", instead of "uncommitted changes".
- **Events**:
  - A kept or re-stopped conflict emits `delivery.rebased` with `conflicted: true` and no `sha_after`.
  - A finished `--continue` emits the new HEAD as `sha_after`.
  - Its `sha_before` is the original tip, read from git's `orig-head` file.
  - `--abort` emits nothing.
- **JSON**: new `in_progress` and `conflicted_files` fields on `RepoRebase`, both omitted when empty or false. The `conflicted` status is unchanged.

**Open question**
- **`--keep-conflicts` with `--onto`**: I took the issue's suggestion and refuse it. Clap rejects it, and the action also returns a `rebase.onto_unsupported` failure.

**Code**
- **Mode**: `RebaseInput` gained a `mode: RebaseMode` field (`Run { keep_conflicts }`, `Continue`, `Abort`).
- **Dispatch**: the new flags are passed through both dispatch paths, including the no-name batch.
- **Git trait**: no changes. I reused `conflicts`, `continue_rebase`, `abort_rebase`, `is_rebase_in_progress` and `worktree_git_dir`.

**Tests and docs**
- **Tests**: new tests cover each acceptance criterion, including the events and the clap rejections (`--continue --abort`, `--continue --onto`, `--keep-conflicts --continue`).
- **Docs**: the command reference is regenerated (`IVAR_UPDATE_DOCS=1 cargo test --test static_checks`). I also updated `day-to-day.md`, `glossary.md` and `limitations-delivery.md`. `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched.

author: honeybeartech-homelab-automation[bot]
body:
## The plan: count the chat window's tests correctly

The full plan is in `docs/plans/window-coverage.md`.

Every change has to pass a check that the automatic tests exercise at least 80% of Sage's code. That share is called coverage. The chat window's code is counted wrongly: each window test loads a fresh copy of it, and the report can't add the copies together. So it shows code as never tested when every test runs it, and the total drops a little each time a window test is added.

**The fix:** reorganise the window's code so the tests load it once and start a fresh window for each test. The other window files already work that way. The window does exactly what it did before, and the coverage number becomes accurate.

Sage's behaviour doesn't change. The automatic checks can't open the real window, so after the next install, open Sage once and check the chat, Settings and Welcome screens as usual.

**Your choice:** approve this pull request (or comment "approve") to start the work. Close it to leave things as they are.

author: caeled
body:
Builds on Muse's b97d8d9 (cached-fix-first find-me and Overpass mirror failover). Nothing is reverted; the main focus here is **pinpointing your location**, then making the coffee-style search answer quickly even when Overpass is busy.

## What was still slow or broken after b97d8d9

Tested end to end in headless Chrome against the real services (mocked device location; live Overpass, Nominatim, and IP services):

| Scenario | `main` (b97d8d9) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Find me, device answers | 0.2 s | 0.2 s, plus an accuracy ring ("within about 35 m") |
| Find me, permission denied | 0.2 s, but it first fires a second, precise request (status flips to "slow way, hang on…") | 0.2 s; respects the no, shows ZIP box + opt-in **Use a rough guess** |
| Find me, device never answers (Windows location off, no Wi-Fi, prompt ignored) | **stuck on "Asking your device…" for good** (worst case 8 s + 20 s, and a stalled prompt never times out) | town-level guess after 6 s, labelled rough; keeps listening for the device |
| Coffee near Defiance, Overpass busy (as it was all through testing) | **45 s, then "could not get through"** (3 servers × 15 s, one after another) | **5.1 s, 2 cafés** via the Nominatim backup, with website/phone/hours |

During testing, overpass-api.de answered "at capacity" (502) or stalled, mail.ru gave 504, and kumi.systems / private.coffee timed out at 20–30 s. Nominatim answered in 0.1–0.9 s.

## Changes

**Find me (app.js, findit.js)**
- Layered, and the map moves on the first answer: (1) this tab's last good fix (sessionStorage, 10 min, instant); (2) a quick low-accuracy fix (`maximumAge` 5 min, 8 s); (3) at the same time, `watchPosition` with high accuracy sharpens until it's within about 100 m or 20 s pass; (4) if the device is silent for 6 s or can't locate, a keyless HTTPS town-level guess (geojs.io, then ipwho.is, 5 s each), clearly labelled rough; (5) if all else fails, the ZIP box gets focus.
- A denial (code 1) is told apart from timeout/unavailable. On a denial nothing runs automatically; a **Use a rough guess** button appears.
- Accuracy ring on the map, zoom that matches the accuracy, and a status line that reports the accuracy.
- Typing a ZIP or town cancels any find-me that's still sharpening, so the map won't jump back.

**Category search**
- `queryOverpass` now hedges: if a server hasn't answered in 4 s, the next mirror is asked alongside it, and the first good answer wins. Each server gets 10 s.
- A 200 response that carries an Overpass `remark` (its own timeout) and no elements counts as a failure, not as "none found".
- A Nominatim backup (`[cafe]`, `[pharmacy]`… special phrases in a box around the centre, one request) runs if Overpass hasn't answered in 5 s or has already failed. It covers every category except Salad and Diner, which need cuisine filters.
- A newer category tap now wins: stale results and "still looking" messages from an older tap can't overwrite it.

**Website and social links (no extra requests)**
- Results show the place's Website, Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, Mastodon, Yelp, and Tripadvisor links when OSM volunteers have tagged them, plus phone and opening hours. Only http(s) links are produced.

author: maxi1134
body:
Right now "stop" only works once an answer has been playing for a second, plus while a timer rings. During that first second, while the assistant is still thinking, or during an announcement that isn't part of a conversation, saying "stop" does nothing.

This swaps `activate_stop_word_once` for `update_stop_word`, which is re-evaluated whenever the state changes and arms the stop model whenever there's something it can stop:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Timer ringing | armed | armed |
| Thinking (command spoken) | – | armed |
| First second of the answer | – | armed |
| Rest of the answer | armed | armed |
| Announcement outside a conversation | – | armed |
| Listening to the command | – | – |
| Idle | – | – |

#381 limited the stop word to the response; this keeps it off while you speak a command, so "stop the music" still reaches the assistant. The stop wake word also can't start the assistant anymore if it fires just as things go idle (it falls through to the no-op stop-announcement branch).

Bonus: a timer that stops ringing in the middle of an answer no longer disarms "stop" for the rest of that answer.

Related: #381, #512, #409, #517

## Testing

- I run this behaviour on my Voice PE and a few ESP32-S3-BOX-3s from a downstream config, where "stop" is armed all the time (a bit more aggressive than this PR). Mid-answer, the cancel kicks in about 60 ms after the detection.
- This exact branch: `yamllint --strict` passes, and `esphome config` plus `esphome compile --only-generate` pass for `home-assistant-voice.factory.yaml` and `home-assistant-voice.8mb.yaml` on ESPHome 2026.11.0b4 (what CI uses). I haven't flashed this exact build yet, so it stays a draft until I do.

#665 (barge-in) touches the same `on_end` block. Whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase: add `- script.execute: update_stop_word` after `control_leds` in its idle branch. I checked that the combination validates.

author: dlroqa
body:
Refs #133. This changes the validator only. It needs separate approval and must not be merged under any other approval.

## Why

The native row "studio: client cancel → CONFIRMING → confirmed by two quiet /metrics readings" required confirmation within the validator's 20 s window. That mixed two things:
- **the studio's safety:** never claiming the engine is idle too early, refusing while unresponsive, recovering;
- **how fast llama-server stops.**

Two diagnostic runs on the Windows runner (bench branch `bench/133-windows-cancel-diag`, runs 43878708964 and 43881698642) showed:
- llama-server b11418 applies a cancel only between 512-token prompt batches;
- it checks for a closed client connection only after a full second without any result for any task, so other requests to it at about 1 Hz (including the studio’s own 1 s confirmation probes, and a validator polling the engine) can delay a cancel until the prompt has been evaluated, on any OS. This is from the llama.cpp source and a local measurement:
  - `/metrics` every 200 ms: cancel posted 226.7 s after the abort;
  - `/metrics` every 2 s: cancel posted at once.

  The Windows runner lost this race most often, at 3.8–60 s.
- the first version of this PR polled the engine every 200 ms and caused full-prompt cancels on all four OS. The validator now reads the engine only every 2 s;
- the studio behaved safely in every trial: CONFIRMING, then UNRESPONSIVE (503), then recovered with the same engine process, and the next chat worked.

## What changes

The client cancel is now followed every 200 ms until the engine is quiet and the studio is ready (at most 180 s).

| Row | Status |
|---|---|
| the cancel is registered | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| CONFIRMING, then confirmed or UNRESPONSIVE (nothing else) | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| never reported idle while the engine's counters move (after the cancel is registered) | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| while UNRESPONSIVE: 503 `ENGINE_UNRESPONSIVE` + `Retry-After` | PASS/FAIL, all OS (SKIP when never UNRESPONSIVE) |
| recovered to ready, same engine PID (no restart) | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| no engine computation after the confirmation (10 s) | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| the next chat works | PASS/FAIL, all OS |
| engine responsiveness: abort → last batch, batches after the abort, compared with a complete request of the same size | new `DIAG` status (recorded, never pass or fail) |
| confirmed within the 20 s window | PASS/FAIL on Linux and macOS; `DIAG` on Windows (met or not met, with the times) |

Not changed:
- production code, timeouts and defaults;
- the 20 s test value;
- every other validator row;
- there is no one-batch stop assertion (the engine does not guarantee one).

`docs/roadmap/STEP9_9F_TIMEOUTS.md` §9 describes the rows. README update not required: CI validator and docs only.

## Results at the current head

The previous head `2c32e3c` was 13/13 green, and the head since then (`1e7c593`) only changes wording. Native runs:
- Linux, macOS ARM64 and macOS Intel confirmed the cancel in 6.1–8.1 s, after one batch; the 20 s row passed.
- Windows confirmed in 10.3 s; the 20 s row was recorded as DIAG (met).
- All safety rows passed on every OS.

author: lucca30
body:
## Summary
Adds `TestPipelinedImportDifferential` (plus a native fuzz target). It generates a random chain and imports it into a serial reference node and into four other nodes: parallel on path, pipelined on hash, pipelined on path, and pipelined + parallel on path. It checks that every node accepts all blocks and agrees on head hash, stored receipts (root, log `Index` / `TxIndex`) and the post-state read through the node's own state reader. It also fails on any `chain/imports/pipelined/root_mismatch` increase, because the rollback would otherwise hide a wrong pipelined root.

The generator targets the state that the FlatDiff overlay serves to the next block: CREATE2 children that are created, destroyed in the constructor, re-created and re-funded across blocks; pre-funded counterfactual addresses; slots set and cleared across blocks; EIP-7702 delegations (authority is also a sender); value calls and balance / code-hash reads on the coinbase and burnt contract; transient storage; reverting nested frames; empty blocks; batch and per-call `InsertChain`. The chain config is `MergedTestChainConfig` with the mainnet fork set and the mainnet coinbase / burnt contract.

Default run: 40 seeds in about 1-2 s (8 with `-short`). Longer run: `PIPELINED_FUZZ_DURATION=5m`. Replay: `PIPELINED_FUZZ_SEED=<n>`. Test-only change.

## Executed tests
- Default run passes (40 seeds, ~1.8 s).
- `PIPELINED_FUZZ_DURATION=60s go test -race ./core -run TestPipelinedImportDifferential`: pass, no data races.
- Longer local campaign with the same generator: 13,862 chains, 89,750 blocks, ~501k txs, 269,250 blocks through the pipeline (227,664 overlay hits): no differences, no root mismatches.
- Mutation checks on `core/state/statedb.go` (reverted after each run). Both were caught at seed 1 by the default run:
  - `FlatDiff.accountOverlay` ignores `Destructs`
  - `FlatDiff.storageOverlay` ignores slots cleared to zero

## Rollout notes
Test-only. No production code, consensus or config changes.

author: twist84
body:
## Purpose
Implement the DMA-09/12 deterministic acceptance fixture using both genuine hardware transports merged in #95–#97.

## Guest test
- An actual R3000 ROM fixture arms IOP DMA10 and waits for the EE-provided SIF1 packet; validates its 4-word XOR payload checksum using guest MIPS branches/loads.
- Guest R3000 transforms the payload, preserves the sequence ID, writes the reply into IOP RAM, and starts IOP DMA9 from a real tag in IOP RAM.
- EE DMA5 receives the resulting reply through SIF0 FIFO. Compares complete request/reply contents, source immutability, EE guard regions, D_STAT/DICR2/I_STAT and all four DMA channel active bits.
- Three consecutive payload sequences reuse both channels and both RAM buffers without resetting the IOP CPU.
- Repeats at IOP execution quanta 1,16,256,4096; checks no completion without an EE sender, and rejects malformed guest payload by branching to guest BREAK without sending a reply.
- Emits machine-readable JSON per successful roundtrip.

## Gates
New `sif_dma_roundtrip` CTest is in the focused SIF DMA acceptance workflow. Require full CI + standalone official OpenPS2BIOS ROM0 workflow before **squash** merging.

This proves a deterministic synthetic guest-ROM fixture, NOT yet authentic OpenPS2BIOS firmware SIFCMD/RPC integration (DMA-10/11).

author: ake2l
body:
Part of #880. Step 1 of 3 of the owner-approved proposal "store language-neutral" (#1384). Decision record: AD-688.

## What changes

- **Protocol 11.** Each native collector writes the 11.0.0 reply. Its facts carry a new block `validation`, filled by the collector from its own table:
  - `registered`: the capability sets of the collector (required and optional sections and features, construct capabilities with their allowed statuses).
  - `interface`: what an interface statement needs (`nothing`, `unsupported`, or one feature).
  - `standard_library`: the owner key of the pinned standard library in `archkeel-facts` (`archkeel-python-analyzer@3.12`, `archkeel-rust-imports`, ...). The part before `@` also names the pinned SDK libraries.
  - Schema regenerated as `native/facts/schema/archkeel-facts-11.schema.json`.
- **Store minimum, no block can lower it.** A feature that a block names must be a feature that the store checks. The standard library key must name the family of the adapter and the minor version of the runtime. Part evidence and the parsed-file count come from `owned_files` (a fact of the reply), not from the profile. The owned-file consistency check moves from `store/dart.rs` to the generic validation, because the minimum relies on it. Script effects need the feature `script-globals-v1`.
- **Block checks.** The capabilities of a 11.0.0 reply must be exactly one registered set of its block; an interface statement must agree with the block.
- **Transition reader.** A reply of protocol 8, 9 or 10 has no block and keeps the profile checks; `validation::library_key` gives its key from the profile and the runtime. A 11.0.0 reply without a block, or an older reply with a block, is refused.
- `store/standard.rs`, `store/bindings.rs`, `store/records.rs` and one site of `store/validate.rs` name no `Profile`. The Dart SDK list moves to `native/facts/src/sdk_libraries.txt`.
- Main reds fixed on the way: three core tests pinned 86 rules (the contract has 93 since #1389); they now count the rules of the contract. The `SignalFact` entries of #1400 were not sorted in the contract.

## Soundness

A block can only add checks. Plants in `native/store/src/validation_tests.rs` (both front doors):
- a block that names a feature that the store does not check is refused;
- a block that requires fewer features than the reply states admits no set: refused;
- a block that drops the routes feature cannot lower the symbol rule: refused (`a_block_with_fewer_required_features_cannot_lower_the_symbol_rule`);
- a standard library key of another family or another minor version is refused.
The collector tables are the store tables of today. The Rust table admits no construct capability, which the store did not check before: stricter. The profile checks still run in this step, so each reply passes both.

## Measured

Native self-check: 89 PASS, 4 FAIL, 0 UNKNOWN; visible violations 27 -> 18 (`NATIVE-NEUTRAL-STORE-NO-PROFILE` 21 -> 12). Pins and growth entries shrink only.

## Next steps

2. `store` reads the block for the registered sets, the features and the interface; old protocols are refused; `registered.rs` and `validate.rs` name no `Profile`.
3. The checks of one language (`store/python.rs`, `store/dart.rs`) move into the collector crates as `check(&Facts)`, called by the core through `collect`; `core/scan.rs` names no `Profile`.

author: justinehler
body:
Search never showed Live TV on the rebuilt server. The server answers a `channel` group (GET /v1/search, last, only for a profile allowed Live TV), but `search.ts` mapped no kind to it, so "Northwind" said "No matches" on the demo while curl returned two channels. Behind it, the web Search's channel cards read what is on now from the old `GET /v1/guide` (DEAD-ROUTES `query/search-guide.ts:12`).

What changes
- client-core `search.ts`: `channel` ↔ the `live-tv` group, both ways (so the Live TV chip asks `kind=channel`). Each channel is the existing entity row: name, number as its caption, logo, and for a live source's channel the same stand-in source the player gives every rebuilt-server channel (`NEXT_CHANNEL_SOURCE`, `provenance: live-source`), which the phone and TV already open as a channel. Channels sort by best match or name only (definition 05 rule 32). The Live TV chip is offered only when the server answered the group (rule 33: never for a profile not allowed Live TV).
- client-core `query/search-guide.ts`: what is on now comes from `GET /v1/live/guide?around={channel}` for this minute; one read usually answers several found channels (its neighbours). The old `/v1/guide` read is gone.
- web Search: cards built from that answer (channel, number, logo, programme on now with progress and time left). A refused read still leaves the plain channel row.
- web: opening a channel goes to `/live?channelId=…` and the guide opens that channel's programme panel. `Live.route` used to need a source and kind in the link, and a source narrowed the guide to nothing on the rebuilt server, so the link now needs only the channel id.

Who can see what: the server leaves the channel group out for a profile not allowed Live TV, and channels hidden by the owner or source are excluded; the guide read is `WithProfile`. Seen on the demo: the Kids profile (allowed Live TV there) finds the two Northwind channels, and its "news" search shows no Severance episodes (rating limit), unlike Demo Member.

Seen (web, local vite against the demo): Demo Member at 1440 and 390: "Northwind" → Live TV 2 with Market Watch / Morning Briefing on now; "news" → Episodes, Songs and Live TV; the Live TV chip alone; opening Northwind News → guide with its Market Watch panel and Watch live. Kids at 390: same channels. No 4xx.
Not seen: phone and TV (no device). They take the same rows; TV draws its ChannelCard from caption and logo, the phone its wide card; opening goes through their existing `{kind: 'channel', sourceId, channelId}` route. A Library Channel result has no source anchor, so the phone and TV say it cannot be opened from Search (as before); web opens it in the guide.
Not built: definition 05's changed row "Live TV search also matches programmes on now and coming up" (mock-up search 2) needs the server; written to `_scratch/builderU/SERVER-NEEDS.md`.

Tests: web `search-all-r46.test.ts`, four Live TV tests skipped until "a channel group in GET /v1/search" now run on rebuilt shapes (card from the guide around it, refused read, retired query, moving off Live TV). `live-bindings.test.ts` destination updated. Core `search-guide.test.ts` removed with the old read; `search.test.ts` example of an unknown kind is now an unknown kind.

9 files (git diff --stat against pinned main 2b25b1cda).

author: kai-matsuda
body:
Story `dev-ekcl.1`, INFRA-47: replace `commit-lint.sh` with the `commit-trailers` provenance hook.

## Summary

The plugin now checks provenance trailers only, with keys configured per machine. The commit style is no longer the plugin's to enforce.

```diff
 bin/
 ├── forge-wait
+└── commit-trailers                  # the trailer hook: provenance trailers only
 skills/setup/
-├── commit-lint.sh                   # style + trailer lint, copied to ~/.config/git
+├── commit-trailers.gitconfig        # hook.committrailers + dev.trailer.provenance = Bead, Refs
 ├── check-prereqs.sh                 # prints `git config --global` lines built from the snippet
 └── claude-md-stub.md                # provenance trailer rules only
```

```text
commit-trailers <message file> [<message file>]   # git may pass the file twice
  keys = git config --get-all dev.trailer.provenance
  if no keys: exit 0, file untouched
  join a provenance-only paragraph to a trailing Co-Authored-By/Claude-Session paragraph (any case, CRLF)
  if any line starting with a key is not in `git interpret-trailers --parse`:
    exit 1, error points at references/issue-tracker.md, file not rewritten
  else write the joined message, exit 0
```

The hook command is `command -v commit-trailers >/dev/null || exit 0; commit-trailers "$@"`, so it skips where the plugin's `bin/` is not on `PATH`. The `bin/` directory is on `PATH` only in Claude Code's Bash tool with the plugin enabled, so commits made by hand are not checked. A repo opts out with `git config hook.committrailers.enabled false`.

Docs that change with it:
- `references/issue-tracker.md` and the setup stub state only the trailer rules, plus one line on the subject and body.
- The imperative-mood paragraph is removed from the Commits rule in `references/harness.md`.
- The glossary entries "Provenance trailer", "Trailer hook" and "Machine setup" are added or updated.
- ADRs 0013, 0017 and 0018 are amended.
- The plugin version is bumped to 0.4.27.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `lint_msg` cases exercised `skills/setup/commit-lint.sh`, including the style cases: no type, capital, over 72 characters, no blank line, Merge subject.
  **After:** `scripts/test-setup-skill.sh` runs `bin/commit-trailers` on these cases, each passing whatever the machine's global git config holds:
  - parseable `Bead:`/`Refs:` lines pass, and a provenance line outside the trailer block is blocked on stderr;
  - the join repair holds with `#` lines, mixed-case keys, a lone attribution key and CRLF, and a rejected file stays byte-identical;
  - no keys set is a no-op; only `Ticket` set checks `Ticket:` and not `Bead:`; a non-Conventional subject passes;
  - a regex character in a key is matched literally;
  - the message file passed twice, as git's config hooks pass it, is accepted;
  - a real `git commit` in a throwaway repo with the snippet's lines is refused on a misplaced `Bead:` line, and passes when `commit-trailers` is not on `PATH` (on a git that runs config hooks);
  - the commands `check-prereqs.sh` prints match the snippet line for line, and the hook command exits 0 when `commit-trailers` is not on `PATH`.

Check record for the delivered tip `1f2e0ce`, tree `49bae1f` (`.tmp/checks/49bae1fa53a7c8dcd5ecb8d4af958e409ae2e03e/record`): `command=make check exit=0`

```text
no fixture seeded and run: run seed <case>, the briefed skill run, then assert <case>

all passed
scripts/test-fixture-story-cut.sh: 0s
...
all passed
scripts/test-fixture-story-cutter.sh: 0s
...
all passed
scripts/test-fixture-triage.sh: 0s
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores `commit-lint.sh`. Machines that already pasted the new gitconfig lines keep a hook that does nothing until `commit-trailers` is back on `PATH`.

**Blast Radius:** machine-setup

Machines still running the old `hook.commitlint` hook keep copying a script that no longer ships. Their old copy goes on enforcing style until the owner reruns `/dev:setup` and pastes the new lines. The fixture repos opt out of both hook names, so `make check` is green whichever hook a machine has. Companion dotfiles epic chezmoi-nq1h (INFRA-48) waits on this merge.

Part of INFRA-47: no sibling stories (claude-dev-plugin dev-ekcl.1 is the feature's only story).

Sourcer's existing extractor does not recognize Digitalarkivet's new parish-image viewer. This adds support for `nye.digitalarkivet.no/source/<sourceId>/parish/<imageUuid>` using the public JSON metadata consumed by the viewer.

For the Voss image linked from #453's example record, the citation now contains the church-register title (1887–1909), holding institution, archive reference, protocol **A 22**, section/year, printed **page 55**, and stable image link `https://goto.digitalarkivet.no/kb20060621010324`.

The loader validates source/image identity and checks the active image after loading and before citation generation. Optional metadata failures retain verified details, with an exact-viewer-link fallback if all metadata is unavailable. Register periods and page years remain bibliographic context, not personal event data. Existing record pages, legacy image links, citation options, searches, and household tables are unchanged. No shared citation API, new dependency, or manifest permission changes are included.

Addresses the overlapping viewer-support work in #401 and #453. This is independent of household PR #561 and attribution PR #562; actual holding-institution metadata is separate from provider credit. A person-picker enhancement is being prepared separately and will be submitted after this PR merges, so its diff contains only that enhancement. Please leave issue closure for confirmation of #401's broader scope.

### Validation
- `node scripts/run_test.js noda` — passed, including legacy regressions.
- `node scripts/run_test.js noda viewer` — metadata and popup behavior checks passed, plus 72 citation snapshots across four verified images.
- `node scripts/run_test.js` — full repository suite passed.
- Prettier and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Covered wrong-source/image responses, optional request failures, printed/roman/compound/missing pages, multilingual/HTML metadata, permission decline, and navigation during loading/before generation.

Manual Chrome/Firefox UI verification remains outstanding because Windows computer use stops at the browser URL-policy restriction. This PR is a draft; the manual checklist is in `docs/dev_notes/site_specific_notes/noda.md`.

author: skornehl
body:
## Why

A full review of the repository found 15 issues. The most important ones: overwriting a cloud-synced preset cut its cloud link, 13 preset names contained `/`, `|` or `"` and were installed into the wrong path, and 34 filaments were rejected because the midpoint of their bed range exceeded the P1S limit.

## Fixes

**Installer**
- Overwriting keeps the preset's cloud link (`setting_id`, `user_id`) and marks synced presets `sync_info = update`, so Bambu Studio updates the cloud copy instead of restoring the old one or creating a duplicate.
- Names that cannot be file names are rejected instead of creating subfolders.
- Filament IDs handed out earlier in the same run count as taken (about 1 % chance of a duplicate with `--all` before).
- Backups in the same second no longer overwrite each other.
- Leftover German prompt "Nummer" → "Number".

**Generator and catalog**
- Preset names are built file-safe (`PA6/66` → `PA6-66`, quotes and `|` removed).
- A bed range beyond the printer is capped like the nozzle range: 34 filaments come back (e.g. 3DJAKE ABS 100–110 °C), "too hot for the bed" drops from 105 to 71.
- Only values that end up in the profile credit a source ("Values from", description, app).
- Error reasons use issue codes; sources per profile live in `BUILD.json` (catalog format 2) instead of being parsed from the description. Catalogs from 0.2.0 are rebuilt automatically on first use.
- `write_output` only empties folders that carry its marker file or `BUILD.json` (a plain `INDEX.md` is no proof any more).
- The lock file is written only after the catalog was built, so `--pinned` returns to a working state.

**Sources**
- Unreadable upstream files (OrcaSlicer, Open Filament Database, SpoolmanDB) are skipped and reported instead of aborting the update.
- SpoolmanDB ranges with `null` values no longer crash.
- CI also runs weekly (and on demand), so upstream breakage shows up without a push.

**App**
- "Update profiles" runs outside the server lock and only once at a time; the detail pane is reset afterwards.
- "My profiles" search needs every word, like "Find profiles".
- Catalog date formatted in English.

Also fixed a test that had become a no-op during the English translation (`Mein PETG.json`).

## Tests

| | before (main) | after |
|---|---|---|
| Tests | 177 | 196 |
| Coverage (lines + branches) | 98.03 % | 98.53 % |

## Checked

- Real `bfp update`: 2552 profiles (was 2518), no preset name with path or Windows-invalid characters, `BUILD.json` format 2 with sources for all profiles.
- Dry-run install against the local Bambu Studio: nothing written.
- Not checked in Bambu Studio yet: that an overwritten synced preset is uploaded as an update of the same cloud preset.

author: hitesh22rana
body:
## Description

Old unfinished cleanup deliveries could repeatedly consume workflow publication batches ahead of fresh independent-key events. Persist replay rounds and due times, increase successful-wave intervals from five minutes to a one-hour cap, and fairly share the total batch between initial delivery and replay with spare-capacity borrowing.

A durable workflow scheduling turn coordinates replicas and batch size one; explicit interleaving rotates first-send opportunities for interrupted batches. Preserve cross-lane same-key predecessor barriers, claim-token fencing, execution budgets, quarantine and completion receipts. Administrative redrive resets pacing atomically with its audited generation change.

Add shared interval validation, startup timing checks and the matching schema/index changes. Update operator/configuration and published recovery/outbox documentation and regenerate LLM artifacts. Keep the delay helper in `outboxrelay.go` and consolidate relay unit/integration cases into the existing test files. Shared interval validation stays in `internal/pkg/outbox/outbox.go`; its test is folded into the existing outbox test file.

## Validation

- Full Go unit/race and strict Docker integration/race suites, including all 14 native command coverage profiles and migration up/down/up.
- Real PostgreSQL/Kafka fairness, pacing, restart, replica, partial-publication, stale-claim, key-barrier and transactional rollback tests.
- Negative controls restore creation-order-only selection or a fixed replay interval; both fail the intended regression assertions.
- Pinned coverage comparison: 14/14 current changed functions at 100%; zero regressions or uncomparable functions.
- 24,000-row query-plan samples, skewed-key plans and two-replica allocation checks; no production throughput claim.
- Build/vet and pinned lint: passed, zero lint issues.
- Static production build and 89 tests passed with 100% coverage; 47 documentation pages, 23 unchanged OpenAPI operations and generated LLM artifacts validated.
- All commits signed and signatures verified.

The review follow-up clarifies that cleanup execution age is independent of the
next replay deadline. When no usable Kafka delivery remains, operator triage also checks the next eligible replay, publication state and consumer progress. The existing PostgreSQL metrics regression now pins future
replay eligibility alongside overdue execution; a negative control that masks
execution age with replay time fails that assertion. Focused race tests, lint,
docs/LLM validation and the 89 static tests passed after this clarification.

## Activation and limits

Recreate existing development databases for the consolidated baseline additions. New replay settings default to `5m` and `1h`; require whole milliseconds and `1ms <= interval <= maximum`. Configure matching settings across replicas; existing persisted due times remain unchanged by configuration updates.

Recovery does not require consumer-lag data. The cap is a scheduled interval after successful publication, not an unconditional delivery deadline. Publication DEAD remains operator-required; execution leases/backoff, key blockers, overload and outages can delay recovery. Ambiguous broker sends remain at-least-once. No cleanup-proof bypass, automatic DEAD revival, receipt/intent GC or public API change.

Small changes inside the existing handlers (`_require_admin` where a handler only required a signed-in user; `_is_solo_install` is now install-wide), a template tweak that disables the PII-scrub toggle for members, and negative tests for each rule (member refused and nothing changes; first-run admin still works; Solo-to-Org conversion unchanged; a second admin can change shared settings; admin reset limited to the admin's own organisation).

body:
### Mechanism

When an endpoint or the relay detects a malformed live Track, the relay closes
affected data streams and sends `PUBLISH_DONE(MALFORMED_TRACK)` on established
downstream subscriptions. The client can continue to use its session.

- RFC or draft: [MoQT draft-22 §12.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-moq-transport-22#section-12.1) and [§9.9](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-moq-transport-22#section-9.9)

### Validation Cases

- 1475 — Established subscriptions route and deliver valid Objects
- 1476 — A malformed Track reports PUBLISH_DONE and the subscriber session remains usable
- 1477 — FETCH and Fill deliver history alongside live Objects
- 1478 — Live delivery continues after a history failure
- 1479 — SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS discovers independent PUBLISH subscriptions
- 1480 — Unauthorized and skipped publications stay isolated

### CONTRIBUTING.md

- Overall: Pending
- Local regression: Complete
- CI: Pending

## 1. 320px 폭에서 조작 줄이 3줄이 되던 문제 → 수정

- 원인: 고정 버튼 7개(조종 5 + `⋯` + 전체화면 = 308px + 테두리)가 툴바 최대폭 304px를 넘어, 고정 버튼만으로 줄바꿈이 생기고 카메라 스트립이 셋째 줄로 밀렸습니다.
- 수정: `positionEdgeButtons()`가 고정 버튼 폭이 최대폭을 넘을 때만 `fullscreen-wrapped` 클래스를 붙이고, 전체화면 버튼이 둘째 줄 끝(카메라 스트립 옆, 카메라가 없으면 단독)으로 갑니다. 390px 이상 레이아웃은 바뀌지 않습니다.
- 스트립 구분선은 스트립 상자 안쪽에 그려지므로, 전체화면 버튼은 `margin-top: 1px` + 그림자로 카메라 버튼과 같은 높이·같은 구분선에 맞췄습니다.

## 2. 320×400 데모 배너 + 경고에서 알약이 y≈319까지 내려가던 문제 → 측정 후 수정 없이 단언으로 고정

헤드리스 Chrome으로 측정해 보니, 이때 알약은 터치 카드(스틱·브레이크, 568×320에서는 러더)를 덮습니다. 다만 이 상황은 펼친 데모 안내가 있을 때만 생깁니다. 데모 중에는 `aircraftControlsDisabled`로 조종 입력이 잠겨 있고 카드도 흐리게 표시되며, 직접 조종으로 전환하면 안내가 사라져 알약이 제자리로 돌아옵니다.

| 상태 (320×400) | 알약 y | 가장 위 터치 카드 top |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 직접 조종 + 경고 | 201–234 | 253 (스로틀) |
| 데모 펼침 + 경고 | 319–352 | 조작 잠김 |

그래서 레이아웃은 바꾸지 않았습니다. 대신 하네스에 "조작 가능 상태에서는 경고가 떠도 알약이 그 아래 터치 카드보다 4px 이상 위에 있다"는 단언을 추가했고, 이 판단은 `hud-camera.md`에 적었습니다.

## 3. 하네스 후반부의 낡은 단언 (320×568에서 멈춰 그동안 드러나지 않음)

- **메뉴 버튼 반복 클릭**: `1b46d29f`가 로비에서 메뉴 버튼을 누르면 보류 비행을 재개하도록 의도적으로 바꿨는데, 단언은 그 이전 동작(로비 유지)을 기대하고 있었습니다. 지금 동작(재개 + 위치 유지)에 맞췄습니다.
- **새 비행 시작**: `9596335a` 이후 보류 비행이 있으면 "새 비행 시작"이 숨고 "시나리오 재시작"이 명시적 리스폰을 맡습니다. 하네스가 재시작 버튼으로 리스폰(`setPreset` 1회)을 확인하도록 바꿨습니다.
- **로비 하단 버튼 터치 목표**: 최소 높이 34px라서 390px 폰에서 "비행 계속하기"가 40px였습니다. 이건 실제 접근성 결함이므로 하네스를 완화하지 않고, 컴팩트 레이아웃(≤1024px)에서 44px로 올렸습니다(별도 커밋).
- 스크롤로 잘린 카메라 버튼의 원래 사각형이 둘째 줄 전체화면과 겹친다고 오탐하지 않도록, 겹침 검사 전에 스트립 가시 영역으로 잘라 냅니다.

## 검증

- `node --test` (cameraPovResetUi, cockpitPovAdjust, controlPanelState, flightCameraFocus, foldableUi, toolbarVisibility, replayUiCleanup) → 37개 통과, `npm run check` 통과
- 이 PC의 헤드리스 Chrome, 하드웨어 GPU(`ANGLE Intel Arc 140V Direct3D11`), 고정 포즈 `scripts/verify-flight-layout.mjs` **전체 완주(EXIT 0)**: 1440×900, 926×428, 390×660, 390×844, 320×568, 568×320, 320×400 + 툴바 맞춤(390×844, 320×568, 926×428, 320px에서 2줄 단언 추가) + 메뉴·재시작·리로드 복원 구간
- 전체 `npm test`·빌드는 CI에 맡겼습니다. 실기기 확인은 하지 않았습니다.

## 남은 점

- 320px 첫 줄은 고정 버튼 6개(266px)만 오른쪽 정렬되어 왼쪽에 약 40px 빈칸이 남습니다(기존 오른쪽 고정 원칙 유지).
- 낮은 화면에서 펼친 데모 안내 자체도 잠긴 터치 카드 위로 일부 겹칩니다(기존 동작, 이 PR에서 바꾸지 않음).

Code reorganised; the game is exactly the same.

## What changed

Nothing a player or the GM will notice. The type checker now checks the GM page's statistics tab: its load of the recorded turns and results, its filters, its cards (who wins, how realms grow, the orders, the units, the battles, the lair fights, the spells, the deaths), its four downloads and "Forget deleted games' data".

## What changes in play

None. This is `refactor-only`: both balance sets are identical, their `writes` included (below).

## Rulings

None.

## Staging

Staging: not needed, because no rule, database or screen changes; the tours prove the screens are the same.

---

## Proof (refactor-only; tier 1)

- **Tier 0:** set A, 60 of 60 games identical (the matrix, its `writes` and telemetry included; and every realm's report); set B, 60 of 60 identical (noise, reports). My own runs: a `src/ui/` row gets no balance comment.
- **The tours:** `tests/tools/same-dom.js`, the base's site (`7604a84b`) against the row's, both built with `KC_BUILD_COMMIT=0000000` and one `KC_BUILD_TIME`: **all 182 screens the same**.
- **`npm run proof:tours -- --base origin/main`:** 90 lines not reached, 32 partly reached, 233 reached. Each listed line is one of:
  - **a statement with a fault planted in it**, run against the new unit test in a throwaway copy: **130 plants, 130 red** (121 on the first run; the other 9 after the test gained the cases they showed missing: a second easy bot, a battle that differs only by its defender, a death with no realm, a refusal with no words, the orders' full order).
  - **made sure by the code, by name:** `if (top === undefined) return;` after the early-lead test has found the list holds a row (never met); `theValuesOf`'s throw, which the cards never reach (they hand it `x || {}`), is pinned by a direct case.
- **A differential run, base against row** (not committed: it needs the base's code): 6,000 sets of made-up statistics with odd values (words where numbers were, empty words, gaps, lists of the wrong kind, JSON held as words, refusals), each loaded, filtered, drawn, downloaded four ways and forgotten on both: **6,000 of 6,000 identical** (the message, the game picker, the cards, 23,169 downloads and the forget run); 2,584 drew every card, 2,799 stopped with the same kind of error on both.
- **Recounted on the base:** `stats-tab.ts` 38,272 bytes; freed, 364 errors (107 parameters); lint 227 beyond `no-unsafe-*` (105 `??`); 1 suppression held.
- **Green:** `npm run check` (static, unit, scenario, simulation); `npx eslint .` (no issues); `npm test` (364 files, 9,876 tests); `npx playwright test` (39 passed). The new unit test passes on the base's code too, but for its case of the new readers.

## Choices made without a maintainer

- **Ratchet:** `tsNocheckUi` 7 → 6; `eslintSuppressions` 258 → 257 (the file's one held entry, an unused `catch` binding), in the file and the baseline alike. No other count moved (`tsNocheckEngineSide` 0, `stubDbTests` 5, `knownArchitectureViolations` 1, `quarantinedTests` 4).
- **Files beyond the row's own:** `theRefusalAsThrown` (a database's refusal thrown as it is) moved from `src/ui/player/dispatches.ts` to `src/ui/shared/a-value-of-any-kind-read-as-javascript-reads-it.ts`, and `src/ui/player/sign-in.ts` imports it from there: a pure move, because the GM page may not import a player file. The forms doc says where it is now.
- **A throw kept in its words:** the account's id read unguarded (`theSignedInAccountsId`) and the results read in "Forget deleted games' data" (never `null` once the rows are loaded) throw the `TypeError` the old reads threw. `(x || []).forEach` on a value that is no list stops the cards with a `TypeError` in other words, as before.
- **Reads the type proves the same:** a game's id read as it is, not through `String` (ids are words), twice; `SPELL_DEFS_P || {}` without the `|| {}` (a constant table); `.filter(Boolean)` on objects or `null` as `!== null`.
- **Kept values a lint fix would change:** `||` became `??` only on lists, objects and counts that are never 0 (each with a comment where it reads a table); words keep `(x ?? '') || y`; the realm filter's `!!r.is_bot` stays, its parameter typed as wide as the guard; `m[k] || (m[k] = …)` is `m[k] ??= …` (a key the prototype holds is found and not written, as before); a total summed `s + x || 0` stays `(s + x) || 0` (KD-392); sums and means of the statistics add as `+` adds them (`theSumAsJavaScriptMakesIt`), so a count held as words still joins as words.
- **The downloads' first line:** the turns and results CSVs write their columns' functions' text in the first line and then replace that line with the names. The functions' text changed, but each is still one line in the build, so the line is replaced whole, as before (the differential run compares the files).

body:
The client follows API 1.21.0, released on 2026-11-16 (build `a8e44c11`). The saved spec was merged from the public document of faxforagents/openapi#17, which is not merged yet.

## What a caller can notice

- New methods `organizations.faxHistoryCsv({ from, to })` and `organizations.auditCsv({ from, to })`. They are the records export of the Agent workspace plan and return CSV text, as `billing.statementCsv` does. The fax history needs `fax:read` and `inbox:read`. The audit trail needs `org:admin`. Without the plan they throw `ScopeError` with the code `workspace_required`.
- `faxes.list` and `faxes.iter` take `created_after` (included) and `created_before` (left out). Left out, no query parameter is sent, so the request is the same as with 0.9.1.
- New fields, all optional: `Quote.live_amount_micro`, `SubscriptionList.plan` (the new type `WorkspacePlan`), `Number.included_with_workspace`, and `refund_pending_micro` on `OneTimeOrder` and `OneTimeOrderCreated`.
- `OneTimeOrder['status']` and the other one-time status types gain `'refunding' | 'refunded' | 'canceled'`. `refunded` and `canceled` read `next` `done`, so `oneTimeSends.wait` returns on them.
- Doc comments: `quotes.create` names `live_amount_micro`, `billing.listSubscriptions` names `plan`, and `oneTimeSends.get` names the refund statuses.

New methods, a new parameter pair and new fields, so the version is 0.11.0, the same as sdk-python. There is no 0.10.0 of this package. Nothing public is removed.

## How the spec was refreshed

The public document at 1.20.11 was the base of a three-way merge with the saved spec, done on the parsed documents. Its 23 changes applied with no conflict. The local edits are kept: the `x-sdk-route` fields, the defaults left out and the optional fields. The merge script reproduces the merges of 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 byte for byte from their inputs. The result was written in the style of `scripts/curate.py`, which reproduces the old file byte for byte.

Two local rules apply to what the refresh brings in. The public document requires `SubscriptionList.plan`, and the saved spec leaves it out of `required`. `Number.included_with_workspace`, `OneTimeOrder.refund_pending_micro` and `OneTimeOrderCreated.refund_pending_micro` have a server default, which the saved spec leaves out, so they stay optional. `WorkspacePlan` keeps the `required` list of the public document. `test/response-types.test.ts` pins all of this. `npm run gen:types` wrote `src/schema.d.ts`.

The shared fixtures gain the same fields as in sdk-python: `live_amount_micro: null` on the test quotes, `included_with_workspace: false` on the number and `refund_pending_micro: 0` on the one-time orders.

## Checked

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` with 113 tests (7 new), `npm run build`. The live test was not run, since it needs a test key.
- Against the client and types of 0.9.1, 3 of the new runtime tests fail and the typecheck reports 23 errors.
- A second `sh scripts/gen-types.sh` leaves `src/schema.d.ts` unchanged.
- The ESM and CJS builds import on Node 22, and both report 0.11.0. `version.ts`, `package.json` and the lockfile say 0.11.0. Node 18 is left to the `node18` job.
- `sh scripts/truthcheck.sh`.
- Every added README, CHANGELOG and hand-written doc comment line passes the human-writing lint (docs channel). The generated comment of `OneTimeOrder` copies the public document, whose new third sentence runs to 41 words. It stays as the server wrote it.

No workflow file changed. Nothing is merged, tagged, released or published by this pull request.

author: z4ntr0n1c
body:
# PR: [P1] Pricing Core + Z-Spread & Golden Fixtures (Mon 16 – Wed 18)

## Descripción
Implementación de los entregables correspondientes al rol **P1 (Pricing core + integrator)** planificados para **Mon 16, Tue 17 y Wed 18**, incluyendo la corrección del vencimiento efectivo para bonos con *call* vencida y el etiquetado de *z-spreads* poco fiables.

---

## Cambios Principales

### 1. Motor de valoración y funciones auxiliares (`src/funciones_aux.py`)
- **Corrección de `fecha_vencimiento_efectiva` (Sección 2)**:
  - Si la fecha de *call* ya ha pasado (`Next Call Date <= 01/10/2026`), se asume que la opción no fue ejercida y se toma `Maturity` como vencimiento efectivo (afecta a 10 bonos con vencimiento fijo).
  - Para el único bono perpetuo con *call* pasada (`FR0014005EJ6`, sin `Maturity`), se mantiene la fecha del próximo cupón como vencimiento efectivo.
- **Solver numérico `_resolver_raiz`**:
  - Implementación por bisección pura (`tol=1e-12`, `max_iter=200`) sin dependencia de `scipy`.
- **Cálculo de `z_spread` (Sección 3)**:
  - Resolución del desplazamiento paralelo $z$ sobre la curva €STR con capitalización continua ($\text{FD}_i(z) = \text{FD}_i \cdot e^{-z \cdot t_i}$) que iguala el precio sucio teórico al precio sucio de mercado ($\text{Precio Limpio} + \text{Cupón Corrido}$).
  - Pre-cálculo de flujos y factores de descuento base fuera del bucle de bisección (~2s para los 2.165 bonos).
- **Stubs iniciales para Sección 4 (Day-1 unblockers)**:
  - `ytm`: aproximación inicial `Coupon / Price` (en tanto por uno).
  - `risk_measures`: aproximación inicial *bullet* a vencimiento efectivo para desbloquear dependencias aguas abajo (S6–S9).

### 2. Notebook de análisis (`src/analisis_cartera.ipynb`)
- **Sección 2**:
  - Actualización de la documentación sobre el criterio de fecha de vencimiento efectiva (1.572 bonos valorados a *call* y 593 a vencimiento final).
  - Inclusión de celda de validación con **6 Golden Fixtures** (`XS0161488498`, `XS1821883102`, `FR0014001I50`, `XS1206541366`, `XS1186176571`, `XS1405762805`).
- **Sección 3**:
  - Cálculo del *z-spread* para todo el universo y exportación a `results/spread.csv`.
  - Análisis de coherencia crediticia: estadísticas y visualizaciones por `Categoria` (IG vs HY), `Seniority`, correlación de rangos con `PD 1YR` y `Horquilla`, y comparativa frente a los índices **iTraxx Main** e **iTraxx Xover**.
  - **Filtro de fiabilidad (`ZSpread_PocoFiable`)**: celda que identifica y etiqueta 248 bonos (11,5% del universo) cuyos *z-spreads* están distorsionados por vencimientos efectivos ultra-cortos (`< 3m`), *par-calls* próximas a vencimiento (`<= 95` días antes de `Maturity` con plazo `< 1a` donde el mercado cotiza a `Maturity`), o valores extremos (`< 0 pb` o `> 500 pb`).

### 3. Ficheros de resultados (`results/`)
- `results/valoracion.csv`: actualizado con la nueva regla de vencimiento efectivo (`ISIN;PrecioSucio;CuponCorrido;PrecioLimpio`).
- `results/spread.csv`: generado para los 2.165 bonos (`ISIN;Spread` en tanto por uno).

---

## Verificación y Testing
- **Golden Fixtures**: verificados los 6 bonos de control; el ajuste de *calls* pasadas corrige el *z-spread* de `XS1186176571` de `2075,0 pb` a `80,6 pb`.

author: josuempia
body:
## Summary
A release runs `advance:432001` more than once, but the step ledger keyed steps by name, so after the first advance passed every later one was skipped as done. The listing setup's timelock operation was then not ready when its execute step ran; that step logs "not ready" and exits 0, so it was recorded as passed, and the first release failed later at 09-debt-oracles (DebtOracle `NotDebtAsset`: USDC not listed yet).

## Changes
- `runRelease` gives a repeated step an occurrence id (`advance:432001#2`, `#3`, …) for its ledger key and log; the first run keeps the step's name, so existing ledgers stay valid.
- `runStep` fails a step whose log reports a timelock operation "not ready", instead of recording it as passed.
