author: fhori
body:
## Problem

The shoutbox bridge rewriter (`client/js/helpers/shoutbox-bridge/`) picked a matcher by the sender's nick only, on every network and in every buffer. Anyone who takes a bot nick (`chatbot`, `dp`, `willie`, `bot`, ...) on any network could send `[admin] hello` and have it shown as a message from `admin`.

## Design

- **Reuse `torrentSites`.** Matchers get an optional `site` field holding the `abbreviation` of their tracker's entry in `torrentSites` (`defaults/config.js`). The server already sends each network the entries for its host as `network.torrentSites`, so the client can check:
  - the network's `torrentSites` must contain an entry with that abbreviation (matched case-insensitively), and
  - if that entry has a `channels` list, the message must be in one of those channels. This uses the same rule as the "Tracker Profile" link, now in a shared `torrentSiteAppliesTo()` helper in `trackerProfile.ts`.
  
  If a scoped matcher is out of scope, the parser moves on to the next matcher.
- **Channels only.** `parser()` now takes `(message, network, channel)` and returns the message unchanged when the buffer isn't a channel. `Message.vue` already had this check before calling the parser. The parser now enforces it too, so a query from `chatbot` is never rewritten even if the parser is called from somewhere else later.
- **`profileLink: false`.** Anthelion's entry was marked `disabled: true` only because its profile URLs aren't based on the nick. That also kept it out of `network.torrentSites`, so it couldn't scope anything. This PR adds a `profileLink: false` option: the server still sends the entry, with `profileUrl: null`, and `getTrackerProfileUrl` skips it. ANT, RED and MAM now use `profileLink: false` instead of `disabled`. RED and MAM have no matcher, so for them nothing visible changes. `disabled: true` still drops an entry completely.
- **Unscoped matchers.** Matchers without `site` keep working on every network, in channels only, as before. They're listed below so you can add a `torrentSites` entry and a `site` field when the IRC host is known. No hostnames were made up.

## Matchers

| Matcher | Bot nick(s) | `site` | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthelion | sauron | ANT | irc.nebulance.io, channels #ant, #ant-announce, #ant-help, #ant-disabled, #ant-invites, #ant-shout |
| Aura4K | aurarelay | A4K | irc.aura4k.net |
| DarkPeers | darkpeers, dp | DP | irc.darkpeers.org |
| HomiesHelpDesk | bbot | HHD | irc.homiehelpdesk.net |
| LST | bot | LST | irc.lst.gg |
| Luminarr | luminarr | LUME | irc.luminarr.me |
| MidnightScene | msbridge | MNS | irc.midnightscene.cc |
| OnlyEncodes+ | bridgebot | OE+ | irc.onlyencodes.cc |
| ReelFliX | wall-e | RFX | irc.reelflix.cc |
| RocketHD | rocketnouncer | RHD | irc.rocket-hd.cc |
| SkipTheCommercial | unit3dbridge | STC | irc.skipthecommercials.xyz |
| UploadCX | ulcx | ULCX | irc.upload.cx, channels #Announce, #ULCX, #Support |
| YUSCENE | yus | YUS | irc.yu-scene.net |
| Zenith | zenith | ZNTH | irc.znth.cx |

**Unscoped, needs host** (no `torrentSites` entry, network not known from the repo):

| Matcher | Bot nick(s) |
|---|---|
| Aither | chatbot |
| BeyondHD | willie |
| DigitalCore | endor |
| DreadVault | dreadvaultbot |
| HUNO (Discord) | mellos |
| HUNO (Web) | any nick ending in `-web` (advanced matcher; the widest spoofing surface of the unscoped ones) |

## Tests

- New `test/client/js/helpers/shoutboxBridgeTest.ts`. It covers:
  - the right network rewrites the message
  - the same bot nick on another network, or on a network with a different tracker, is left alone
  - a tracker channel list applies, case-insensitively
  - a `profileLink: false` site (ANT) still scopes its matcher
  - queries and missing channels are never rewritten, for scoped and unscoped matchers
  - unscoped matchers still work in channels
  - every `site` in `matchers.ts` exists as an enabled abbreviation in the default `torrentSites`
- `trackerProfileTest.ts`: sites with `profileUrl: null` get no profile link.
- `test/tests/torrentSites.ts`: `profileLink: false` entries are returned with `profileUrl: null`.
- `yarn build:server` and `yarn build:client` (webpack production build, compiled successfully). `yarn test:mocha`: 296 passing, 0 failing.
- `test/.mocharc.yml` ignores `test/client/**`, so `yarn test:mocha` does not run the client helper tests. I ran them directly with `NODE_ENV=test npx tsx node_modules/.bin/mocha --require test/fixtures/env.ts test/client/js/helpers/trackerProfileTest.ts test/client/js/helpers/shoutboxBridgeTest.ts`: 14 passing.
- eslint passes on every touched file. Prettier: the new and changed TS files I touched are formatted. `parser.ts`, `matchers.ts`, `types/matcher.ts`, `Message.vue` and `defaults/config.js` already failed `prettier --list-different` before this change. I left them unformatted to keep the diff small and to avoid conflicts with the separate `sanitizeNick` fix, whose line is untouched.

## Not verified / notes

- **Not tested in a live client** against real bridge bots.
- **UploadCX and Anthelion bridge channels.** These two are now limited to the channel lists in `torrentSites`. If a bridge bot posts in a channel that isn't listed, its messages are no longer rewritten there. I haven't confirmed which channel each bot actually uses.
- **Custom `torrentSites` lists.** A custom list replaces the default one entirely. Admins with their own list need to keep the same `abbreviation` values (e.g. `DP`, `ULCX`) or scoped matchers stop applying. If a site's `host` in config doesn't match the server address the user connects with (for example a different alias), its matcher won't apply.
- **Breaking change for some admin configs.** An admin config that copied the old defaults keeps `disabled: true` on ANT, which turns the Anthelion matcher off. Switching to `profileLink: false` turns it back on.

author: mraible
body:
The Pylint workflow installed pylint by name with `pip install --upgrade pylint`. Dependabot never sees a package installed that way, so pylint floated to whatever was latest on each run instead of moving through reviewable version bumps.

This PR moves pylint into `.github/requirements-dev.txt` with an exact pin and installs it with `pip install -r .github/requirements-dev.txt`. The file lives in `.github/` because `foundry apps deploy` skips hidden paths, so the dev tools never get packaged with the app. Dependabot's pip config now lists `/.github` alongside the function directory, and the Pylint workflow's path triggers include the new file so a Dependabot bump actually runs the lint.

Pytest is now pinned in the same file, and the Sample CI workflow installs it alongside the function's requirements. Until now the test step got pytest only as a side effect of `crowdstrike-foundry-function` declaring it as a runtime dependency (https://github.com/CrowdStrike/foundry-fn-python/issues/46). Pinning it here keeps the test step working if the FDK drops it, and lets Dependabot keep it current.

Pylint is pinned to 4.1.3 and pytest to 9.2.0 for now, and Dependabot will bump them from there. Locally, pylint scores 10.00/10. The function has no `test_main.py` yet, so the test step has no unit tests to run.

**Set order "almost inverse and weird".** No zh-hans set had a date (the source list has none), so Date order was A-Z by English name and series groups had nothing to sort by. `chineseDates.ts`: real Chinese release dates for 40 sets from Bulbapedia's (ATCG) pages, matched by Chinese name; every other set (decks, gift boxes, Battle Party / Happy Set packs) takes the earlier of its dated neighbours in the list's newest-first index, which keeps the list's order and puts the month close. write.ts already updates `tcg_date` on existing set rows.

Caches: hand art is served `immutable` for a year and the desktop keeps art by card id, so viewers who already loaded a banded card keep it until their cache is cleared or the edge copy purged. Purging the edge for the re-copied cards follows the bulk run.

Tests: trimClear (cut, nothing solid, JPEG size), redo record round trip, chineseSetDates (known, neighbour, out-of-order tail, waves, promos).
**Twin pack art (owner said yes).** zh-hant sets use Japanese codes and fr sets English ones; neither had pack art (0/82, 0/184). `writeTwinPackArt` runs nightly after the zh pack rows and copies the twin set's pack rows by code, skipping codes shared by two sets on either side. body:
## Summary

Fixes findings 1–3 from a `/code-review high` of #287–#294.

**1. A tag scan that stops at an RPC error keeps no notes** (`shield_demo/engine/tags.go`)

```diff
 scanTags(a)
+  fresh := purse{}
   for each TagPublished log, each channel
     n, err := tagNote(...)          // vault eth_getLogs
     if err is an RPC error
-      return found, err             // notes already in a.notes, cursor unmoved
+      return nil, err               // nothing kept, cursor unmoved
-    a.notes += n
+    fresh += n
+  a.notes += fresh
   a.tags.lastBlock = tip
```

Before this, a retry re-read the same blocks and left the notes the failed scan had already added to `a.notes` out of `found`. `discoverByTag` then failed with "found 1 new notes … want 2".

**2. The stack scripts exit on INT/TERM** (`enygma_dvp/scripts/stack.sh`, `enygma_payments/run_scripts/stack.sh`, `shield_demo/run.sh`)

```diff
-trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM          # returns → back to the monitor loop → died()
+trap cleanup EXIT
+trap 'exit 130' INT
+trap 'exit 143' TERM
```

**3. `DVP_LOG_DIR` / `PAYMENTS_LOG_DIR` / `RETAIL_LOG_DIR` can be relative.** The Makefile recipes and the scripts resolve the dir to an absolute path before anything changes directory.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `TestScanTagsKeepsNoNotesOnRPCError` fails with `failed scan kept 1 notes and moved the cursor to 1, want 0 and 1`.
  **After:** it passes. Shown red with `scripts/mutant.sh --expect TestScanTagsKeepsNoNotesOnRPCError`, which swaps `fresh = append(fresh, n)` back to `a.notes = append(a.notes, n)`.
- **Before:** on `origin/main`'s payments `stack.sh`, `make payments-stack` followed by `make payments-stack-stop` logs:
  ```
  [stack.sh] stopped. Logs: …
  [stack.sh] hardhat exited — last log lines:
  ```
  **After:** the log ends at `stopped. Logs: …`.
- **Before:** `make dvp-stack DVP_LOG_DIR=logs` exits 1 with no output, because the redirect into `logs/stack.log` runs after `cd enygma_dvp`.
  **After:** `dvp-stack`, `payments-stack` and `shield-stack` each come up with a relative `*_LOG_DIR` (resolved to an absolute path) and stop cleanly. These were run by hand; there is no automated check for the scripts.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** local-dev

Fix 1 changes only what `scanTags` does when it fails. Fixes 2 and 3 touch only the local stack targets and scripts. The stack's exit status on a signal goes from 1 to 130/143, and nothing reads it.

The `protected-resource discovery` audit (`thirdparty.auditDiscovery`) had `operation` and `outcome` but no `event`. #488 listed it as out of scope; it was the last CIMD/third-party audit record without an `event`. A session with no graphical access cannot use the desktop app. The installer built or downloaded it anyway.

- Run shellcheck on scripts/install.sh.

## What this changes

`pnpm check:print` now covers **every template that has a paper version** and reports the pass rate (MET-020, the print legibility pass rate; target 100% on each release).

Before, it printed the activity cards, the pack builder and the paths. Now it also prints each card's **large-print edition**, the **fixed packs**, the **weekly program** and each **game's paper version**, on A4 and US Letter, and checks:

author: asdalexander77
body:
Spec 89, plus a leak fix in rc and own found on the way.

## -mm=own: a method value takes its object (user ruling 2026-11-16)
- `h.f = v.get`, `return v.get`: the object moves into the method value; its release frees it. `let f = v.get` with `v` still used borrows it; `let f = v.get; v = mkv(2)` moves the old object into `f`.
- A class method read as a value (`ThisSymbolRef` / `ThisVirtualSymbolRef`, not called) is a view of its object, so the existing move/borrow checks decide it. A move through it marks the method value (`OWN_BOUND_OWNS_OBJECT_ATTR_NAME`), and the lowering gives that one the class's type tag; every other bound method keeps its null tag.
- Unchanged: `this.m` (back-references, spec 70; keepers). A method read through an interface (`return o.fn`) is refused with a message saying what to do instead.
- `own_err_const_bound_method_reassigned` compiles now (kept as `own_method_value_reassigned`); `own_err_borrow_bound_method` is refused where `f = b.m` is made.

## rc and own: a subclass's fields, released through its base
An object kept in a slot of its base's type (`h.v: V = new V2()`, a `V[]`, a method value bound to it) was released by the base's routine, which released only the base's fields - what the subclass added leaked (rc: 213 MB -> 1.77 GB for 10x the iterations). MLIRGen now records each class extending another (`ts.class_bases`, not `@cpp`), and a class's release routine compares the object's vtable with each subclass's in the module and releases the fields of the class it is. Gap: a subclass made only in another module is not known to the base's routine here.

Corpus (`tests/`, own, compile only): 729 of 892 (was 728); `00bound_method_count` runs.

author: sks
body:
> **Stacked PR — depends on #2158** ("fix(library): vendor the sunsingerus mergo fork so the operator imports as a Go module"). This branch **contains** #2158's commit underneath the config-split commit; it will rebase cleanly to a 1-commit diff the moment #2158 merges. Review #2158 first; the diff unique to this PR starts at `1608ba4`.

## What

Library consumers import the operator for its config generation, and today that drags the entire `k8s.io/client-go` surface through `pkg/chop`: the `ConfigManager` held `*kube.Clientset` and `*chopclientset.Clientset` fields, so any import of `chop.Config()` — the one accessor every consumer reads — compiled the full Kubernetes client machinery in.

## The fix

Split the config machinery into `pkg/chop/config`, kube-free:

- `ConfigManager` moves to `pkg/chop/config` behind two narrow function seams (the `secretDataGetter` pattern this codebase already established for the RootCA tests):
  - `CRConfigLister` — reads operator-configuration Custom Resources, answering specs + ResourceVersions (nil seam = file/env-only config, the library-consumer shape)
  - `secretDataGetter` — Kubernetes Secret reads (nil seam = secret refs log a warning and stay unresolved)
- `pkg/chop` keeps `New()`, `GetClientset`, and the kube machinery, and **adapts its clientsets to the seams** — the operator binary's path is unchanged (same signature, same behavior, same logs)
- `ProvisionIPCToken` stays exported from `pkg/chop` (thin wrapper over the config package's implementation)

## Net effect

A consumer importing only `pkg/chop/config` has **zero** `k8s.io/client-go` modules in its dependency tree — verified with a scratch consumer (`require` → `import` → build; `go list -deps` shows only apimachinery types):

```
config manager built without any kube client: true
client-go modules in the consumer's tree: 0
```

Consumers of the operator outside Kubernetes — VM bootstrappers embedding the config/keeper model layer — no longer inherit the client surface they never call. Together with #2158, the operator's config machinery becomes consumable as a plain Go library.

## Behavior

No behavior change: the CR listing, secret fetches, insecure-kube gate, and TLS min-version floor all run through the same logic — only the client boundary moved behind function seams. The in-tree package suite passes (`pkg/chop`, `pkg/chop/config`, `pkg/apis/...`, `pkg/model/...`); the only failing tests locally are pre-existing (macOS toolchain linker + vet warnings, identical on the base branch).

Happy to restructure (seam shapes, package name) to fit your review preferences.

author: kosker-07
body:
## O3 — Two signatures, S1.5 step 3 (S1-042a–d) · migration 080 · mutation M66

**Draft, held until #127 merges** (per tech lead: branch cut from `646f21c`, base merged in after — no rebase, no force-push). Server only. **Opens nothing**: the four documents (O4) and the admin approval (O5) are still outstanding, and every test asserts `panel_open = false` at the end.

Spec: `docs/BED4BOOK_Sartname_Ek_DMC_Panel_Departmanlar.md` **S1.5 step 3** — "BED4BOOK yetkilisi imzalar; DMC yetkilisi sözleşmeyi kendi seçtiği dilde okuyup kabul kutusunu işaretleyerek imzalar. İmzacı, zaman ve kabul edilen sözleşme sürümü denetlenebilir."

### Endpoints
- `POST /api/operator/dmcs/:id/contracts/:version/sign` — operator signs the BED4BOOK side. 409 `ALREADY_SIGNED` on a repeat.
- `POST /api/dmc/contracts/:version/sign` — the DMC's own admin accepts. Needs `accept: true` **and** `language ∈ {en,tr,ar,ru}`; 409 `BED4BOOK_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` if the operator side has not signed that version. The chosen language is also written to `agencies.document_language`, which is what S1-042 says the signatory reads in.
- `GET /api/operator/dmcs/:id/signatures` — every signature with its contract version.

### The version link is the whole point
`dmc_signatures.contract_id → dmc_contracts(id)` means a signature **cannot** drift onto another version: "which version was signed" is a foreign key, not a copied integer. `(contract_id, side)` is unique, so one signature per side per version.

### ⚠️ One deliberate behaviour change — a real deadlock I had to break, please review
S1.5 step 5 says the panel stays **closed until** two signatures + four documents + admin approval. But the closed-panel gate in `server/http.ts` rejected **every** `/api/dmc/*` path, including the acceptance endpoint. Taken literally, **the DMC officer could never sign, so the gate that opens the panel could never be satisfied** — a deadlock, and O3 would be unimplementable.

Minimal fix: `ONBOARDING_REACHABLE = /^\/api\/dmc\/contracts\/\d+\/sign$/`, exempted **before** the M60 gate block, which is left byte-identical. I added **S1-042d** specifically to prove the exemption is narrow:

| Attempted while closed | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/dmc/contracts/1/sign` | **201** (the gate itself) |
| `/api/dmc/subagencies`, `/api/dmc/subagencies/x` | still gated |
| `/api/dmc/contracts/1/other` (near miss) | not exempted |
| `/api/me` | `DMC_PANEL_CLOSED` |
| panel after signing | **still `false`** |

If you'd rather this lived in a different layer (e.g. a separate `/api/onboarding/*` prefix), say so and I'll move it — but the exemption has to exist somewhere, or the spec is self-contradictory.

### Tests — written first, seen red, then green
`tests/server/dmc-signatures.integration.test.ts`. All 4 were **red before the routes existed** (0 pass / 3 fail on the first three; S1-042d added after). Now **4/4 pass**.

| Test | Asserts |

author: studio-takumi
body:
Closes #374

## やったこと
- **OpenVINO GenAI の実行系を足した**（`openvino_whisper.py`）。録音中の文字起こし（`whisper_worker.py`）と浄書の文字起こし（`final_transcribe_worker.py`）で、faster-whisper・mlx-whisper の横のもう 1 つの実行系として使う
  - 選び方: extra `openvino` が入っていて、NVIDIA の GPU（NVML）がなく、OpenVINO が `FULL_DEVICE_NAME` に `(dGPU)` の GPU を見つけたとき（起動時に 1 回だけ調べる）。設定 `whisper.intelGpu`（`auto` / `off`。既定 `auto`、録音中は変えられない）で切れる
  - モデル: 録音中は `OpenVINO/whisper-<model>-int8-ov`、浄書は `-fp16-ov`。コンパイルのキャッシュは `HF_HOME/openvino-cache`
  - `initial_prompt`・`hotwords` を渡す、`language` は `<|ja|>`、greedy、`return_timestamps=True`。greedy の繰り返しが止まらないことがあったので、`max_new_tokens` を音声の長さで抑える（1 秒 12 トークン＋32、448 まで）。終わりの時刻が `-1` の区間は音声の終わりまでとする
  - 浄書は録音全体を VAD で 30 秒までのまとまりに分けて起こし（% も出る）、繰り返しで埋まった区間（compression_ratio > 2.4）は捨てる。位置合わせ・話者分けは WhisperX のまま CPU
- **信頼度が取れないことへの手当て**（`hallucination.py`）: `no_speech_prob`・`avg_logprob` がない区間は、文の時刻の範囲の VAD の話している長さ（`voiced_sec`、前後 0.3 秒）と、こちらで計算する `compression_ratio` で判定する（話している長さ 0.2 秒未満 → `no_speech`、定番の文は 0.8 秒未満 → `short_phrase`、繰り返し → `repetition`）。長さが分からなければ今までどおり残す
- **GPU の状態**（`gpu_stats.py`）: Arc のときは `typeperf` で性能カウンター（`GPU Adapter Memory` の Dedicated Usage、`GPU Engine` の Compute）を、OpenVINO の `DEVICE_LUID` で選んだ GPU について取る（スレッドで。ループを止めない）。VRAM の全体は `GPU_DEVICE_TOTAL_MEM_SIZE`
- `GET /api/setup` の `gpu` に `intel` を足した（web は型だけ。GPU の案内は `none` のときだけなので画面は変わらない）
- 依存: extra `openvino`（`openvino-genai>=2026.4.1`、Windows だけ）。`uv.lock` 更新
- docs: spec flows.md 6.17（新設）・6.15、files.md 5.3、api.md、README のセットアップ（ドライバー 31.0.101.5445）

## 変えていないこと（NVIDIA・Mac）
- extra `openvino` が入っていなければ OpenVINO を import すらしない（`find_spec` だけ）。NVIDIA の GPU があれば入っていても今までどおり faster-whisper（CUDA）。Mac は `default_backend()` の mlx の判定をそのまま使う
- 信頼度がある区間（faster-whisper・mlx）のハルシネーションの判定は変えていない

## チェック
- server: `ruff check`・`ruff format --check`・`pytest`（1285 passed, 18 skipped）
- web: `prettier --check`・`lint` は通った。`npm run build` は手元の node_modules で main でも同じ型エラー（61 件、`summaryDir.ts` など）が出るので、この PR の変更とは関係ない（CI で確認）
- テスト（OpenVINO はモック）: デバイスの選び方（dGPU だけ・NVIDIA / extra なしでは探さない）、LUID の変換、オプションの渡し方（greedy・時刻つき・`max_new_tokens`）、VAD と時刻のずらし、浄書のまとまりと繰り返しの除外、`intelGpu` の auto / off、子プロセスで OpenVINO を読み込む流れ、浄書の指示（`openvino`）の有無、信頼度がないときの判定、性能カウンターの読み取り

## 実機（Note: Arc A350M 4GB、ドライバー 31.0.101.5445）
手元の 3 分の会話の収録（数値だけ）
- `detect()` → `GPU.1`（Arc。Iris Xe は選ばない）、`/api/setup` の `gpu` は `intel`、`default_backend()` は faster-whisper のまま
- 録音中（`WhisperWorker` の子プロセス、VAD で 19 区間・hotwords あり）: 読み込み 49 秒（初回のコンパイル）→ 2 回目 5.7 秒。合計 31.7 秒（5.6 倍）、1 区間の待ち 平均 1.7 秒 / 最大 4.4 秒、捨てた区間 0。雑音だけ 5 秒は空。性能カウンターで使用率 最大 65%・VRAM 約 1.0GB、下ろしたら 8MB に戻った
- 浄書（`final_transcribe_worker` に `openvino` 付きの指示、話者分けなし、torch は CPU 版）: 文字起こし（fp16、読み込み込み）43 秒 → 位置合わせ（CPU）112 秒、全体 160 秒で終了コード 0。16 区間・1017 文字・単語 1004 個に時刻が付き、0.5〜180.0 秒をカバー。録音中の文字起こしとほぼ同じ文字数

## 未確認
- サーバー全体を起動しての録音（画面から）と、話者分け（Note に HuggingFace のトークンがない）
- 長い録音（長い実時間の検証はしない）
- 配布版（インストーラ）には extra `openvino` を入れていない（`build.ps1` は `--extra final` だけ）

## 判断したこと
- 設定の名前は `whisper.intelGpu`（`auto` / `off`）。画面には出さず setting.json で変える（使う PC が限られるため）
- 信頼度なしで定番の文を捨てる長さは、faster-whisper の 0.6 秒より長い 0.8 秒にした（信頼度で後押しできないため）
- `max_new_tokens` の上限を足した。実機で、プロンプト＋hotwords の組み合わせで 15 秒の音声から 579 文字の繰り返しが出て 9 秒かかったが、上限を付けると 19 区間で繰り返しは出なかった

## Proč
Po #45 propojení živě funguje, akce v kalendáři „Vzdělávání ZBC“ ale nemají žádné upozornění. V auditu je u obou účtů `calendar.personal.setup_none`: Google odmítl `calendarList.patch` úplně (i bez `notificationSettings`), takže kalendář nemá výchozí připomínky a akce s `reminders.useDefault` neměly žádnou.

## Co se mění
- Každá akce nese vlastní připomínky: e-mail den předem, oznámení 30 min předem (`events.insert` funguje).
- `EVENT_FORMAT = 2` v otisku přepíše už zapsané akce při nejbližším spouštěči (přihlášení, zveřejnění změny).
- Dokumentace: `docs/kalendar-ucastniku.md`, `docs/dalsi-session.md`.

## Co tím vyřešené není
E-mail o nové, změněné nebo zrušené akci Google u vlastního kalendáře nepošle (organizátorem je sám uživatel). Bez `calendarList.patch` nechodí ani ranní přehled. Návrh řešení je v `docs/dalsi-session.md` a čeká na rozhodnutí.

## Ověření
- `tsc` ✓, `eslint` (změněné soubory) ✓, vitest `kalendar-osobni` + `kalendar-uklid` 15/15 ✓ (test hlídá připomínky v těle akce).
- Celé e2e v této větvi nespuštěné (relace na limitu kontextu). Změna je jen v těle požadavku na Google.
- Živě neověřeno.

## Živé ověření po merge
1. Odhlásit se z Wiki a znovu přihlásit (spustí přepis akcí).

body:
## Что сделано

Страницы с Blazor WebAssembly-островами (например, `/{projectId}/roleslist/{id}`) перекачивали весь WASM-рантайм — до ~80 файлов, включая 3+ MB `dotnet.native.*.wasm` — при каждом открытии (#6234).

**Причина** (установлена живым трафиком и разбором рантайм-загрузчика .NET 10):
1. `dotnet.js` фетчит каждый boot-ресурс с fetch-режимом `cache: "no-cache"` — принудительная ревалидация в обход HTTP-кеша, `immutable` от MapStaticAssets игнорируется.
2. Ревалидация в проде сломана (L7-прокси искажает `If-None-Match`: точный ETag → 200 с полным телом вместо 304), поэтому каждая ревалидация превращалась в полную перекачку.

Предыдущий подход (#6235, закрыт) — отдавать fingerprinted-ассеты с `immutable` через свой middleware — оказался неэффективным: те же заголовки уже ставит `MapStaticAssets`, а загрузчик их игнорирует из-за п. 1.

**Фикс**: во всех трёх точках подключения `/_framework/blazor.web.js` (layout Razor Pages Portal, хост `App.razor` Portal, `App.razor` IdPortal) добавлен `autostart="false"` и ручной `Blazor.start({ webAssembly: { configureRuntime: dotnet => dotnet.withConfig({ disableNoCacheFetch: true }) } })`. Загрузчик перестаёт принудительно ревалидировать: fingerprinted-ассеты отдаются браузером из HTTP-кеша без единого запроса.

## Проверка

- Локально на опубликованном приложении (Production-условия, `immutable`-заголовки на месте): повторная загрузка страницы с островом — **77 из 79 `_framework`-ресурсов из кеша без сети** (было: запрос на каждый), оставшиеся два — мелкие нефингерпринтные `blazor.web.js`/`dotnet.js`. Остров работает.
- Сборка Portal и IdPortal — без ошибок.
- Регрессионный сценарий `WasmBootCachingScenario` (IdPortal.Test): в разметке остались `autostart="false"` и `disableNoCacheFetch`.
- Ревью независимым субагентом: блокеров нет; замечания (TODO о будущем двойном старте при переезде на App.razor, регрессионный тест) закрыты, `.catch()` на `Blazor.start` не добавлен намеренно — паритет с автостартом, error UI владеет blazor.web.js.

## Отдельно (не входит в PR)

Инфраструктурный баг: L7-прокси искажает `If-None-Match` — ревалидация сломана для всей остальной `no-cache`-статики. После этого PR перестаёт быть критичным для WASM, но чинить нужно.

Closes #6234

body:
承接 #1357 的后续改进。**#1357 已合入 main（合入提交 `20cdb286`）**，本 PR 差集为 4 个提交。

## 背景
#1357 让嵌套池能被正确答出；但快路与备忘的可答区间仍以「命中池之后一个池的起点」为上界，跨过的小池会把区间切断：同一局备忘命中率约 10%，多数查询回落到锁内二分。

## 改动
- 锁内查找同时算出真实可答区间 [lo, lim)：lo 取 ci+1..cand 各池终点的最大值，lim 取 cand+1 池的起点（末池 UINT64_MAX）；
- 快路与备忘都按 [lo, lim) 判可答；备忘某条装不下时继续看外层记录，语义仍与锁内一致；
- 新增只读计数 g_pool_fast_hits / rp_pool_fast_hits()；
- 快路计数用普通整型的 __atomic 内建（安卓 NDK clang 不接受 _Atomic 配 __atomic_*）。

## 调试开关（三档，缺省全开；玩家包编译期恒缺省）
| 档位 | 属性 |
|---|---|
| 全开（缺省） | 都不设 |
| 关快路（备忘仍开） | `debug.s2a.nvk_pool_nofast=1` |
| 快路与备忘都关 | `debug.s2a.nvk_pool_nofast=1` + `debug.s2a.nvk_pool_memo=0` |

- `debug.s2a.nvk_pool_memo` 已随 #1357 合入（缺省 1，每 4096 次查找重读）；
- `debug.s2a.nvk_pool_nofast` 由本笔新增（缺省 0）；
- 前置：调试构建 + `adb shell setprop debug.s2a.debug_env 1`；属性按线程缓存 250 ms，切档约 1 秒内生效；玩家包不读。
- 两个开关都按 4096 次查找重读一次，热路径不读系统属性；`rp_pool_fast_hits()` 返回调用线程自己的累计。

## 宿主读数（200 万次 rp_pool_find，70% 重复地址，三次取中位）
| 版本 | ns/次 | 备忘命中率 |
|---|---|---|
| main 原版 | 24.79 | 10.08% |
| #1357 版 | 35.66 | 10.08% |
| 本笔 | 10.09 | 90.00% |

## 设备读数（程序号 01004D300C5AE000，同一局切开关）
| 组 | 每笔（ms） | 备忘命中 |
|---|---|---|
| a 全开 | 0.026 | 99.99% |
| b 仅快路 | 0.017 | 未启用 |
| c 都不走 | 0.018 | 未启用 |

嵌套场景读数如上。非嵌套场景由维护方在测试机补量；本机侧 `010003F003A34000` 实测自身也嵌套（池登记 300 条内 32 处严格嵌套 + 17 处同起点），`0100F2C0115B6000` 无源包/keys，无法出包。

## 验证
- native-test-nvn_replay / nvn_res / nvn_tm：3215 / 38 / 157 项检查，0 红
- 变异体：快路不看可答区间、池查找下界不并入跨过的小池，均被单测拦住
- contrib_check：绿 30、红 0；缺 runtime/gate.sh（需 Mac/gate-host，rc=75 环境未就绪）
- CI 对照：linux / macos 绿；android-vk 的 C1072 已由 main `826327c40` 修复，其余红项（`no_clip_distance` / `no_exact16` 等）维护方确认不归本片

### Submission Review Guidelines:

-   I have followed the [WooCommerce Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [WordPress Coding Standards](https://make.wordpress.org/core/handbook/best-practices/coding-standards/).

-   I have assessed the impact of this change and followed the applicable [review requirements](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/docs/contribution/contributing/deciding-pr-high-impact.md#review-requirements).
-   Following the above guidelines will result in quick merges and clear and detailed feedback when appropriate.

<!-- You can erase any parts of this template not applicable to your Pull Request. -->

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

<!-- If necessary, indicate if this PR is part of a bigger feature. Add a label with the format `focus: name of the feature [team:name of the team]`. -->

<!-- Describe the changes made to this Pull Request and the reason for such changes. -->

An order that ships in parts emails the customer once per shipment, and then again when the order is marked complete. Both emails stay, because a fulfillment email describes a single shipment while the "Completed order" email describes the order as a whole, but a store that would rather send only the shipment emails had no supported way to drop the order-level one. The only route was a snippet that hooked `woocommerce_email_enabled_customer_completed_order` and read the fulfillments table itself.

This adds an opt-in filter, `woocommerce_fulfillment_suppress_completed_order_email`, which returns false by default so nothing changes for anyone. Return true and the "Completed order" email is skipped for an order whose items have all been fulfilled; a partially fulfilled order, or one with no fulfillments, still receives it. Only the send that follows the order being marked complete is skipped, so sending the email again from the REST API or the `woocommerce/order-send-email` ability still reaches the customer. The status is worked out from the order's items and its stored fulfillments rather than taken from the `_fulfillment_status` meta, which nothing recalculates when the order's items change. The check is registered from `FulfillmentsManager` only while the fulfillments feature is on, it leaves the email alone when there is no order (the settings screen, the usage tracker and the email editor all ask that way), and it never turns on an email the merchant has disabled.

**Backward compatibility:** additive. No signature or interface changes, and no behavior change until a store adds the filter. `FulfillmentsManager::maybe_suppress_completed_order_email()` is a new public method on an existing class; nothing in core declares that name, so the only conflict would be an external subclass that already declares it with an incompatible signature.

**For reviewers:** reaching the `fulfilled` status does not by itself prove a fulfillment email was sent. Auto-fulfilled items, fulfillments saved with the "Fulfillment notification" toggle off, the "Mark as fulfilled" bulk action on the orders list, and imported fulfillments all reach it without one. The decision is therefore left to the callback, which receives the order. The hook documentation shows a callback that keeps the email whenever the order holds a downloadable item, and warns that an order of downloadable products completed straight from pending can otherwise be left with no email at all.

Using the [WooCommerce Testing Instructions Guide](https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/contribution/testing/writing-high-quality-testing-instructions/), include your detailed testing instructions:

1. Turn on Order Fulfillments. Its toggle under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features is hidden, so set it with `wp option update woocommerce_feature_fulfillments_enabled yes`. Confirm that both the "Fulfillment created" and "Completed order" emails are enabled under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails.
2. Place an order with two different physical products. Fulfill one of them with the "Fulfillment notification" toggle on, then mark the order complete. The customer should receive both the fulfillment email and the "Completed order" email, which is today's behavior.
3. Add `add_filter( 'woocommerce_fulfillment_suppress_completed_order_email', '__return_true' );` to a site plugin or to your theme's `functions.php`.
4. Place a second order with two different physical products, fulfill only one of them, then mark the order complete. The "Completed order" email should still arrive, because items are still outstanding.
5. Place a third order, fulfill every item in it, then mark the order complete. The fulfillment email should arrive and the "Completed order" email should not.
6. Send that third order's "Completed order" email again, with `POST /wc/v3/orders/<id>/actions/send_email` and `template_id` set to `customer_completed_order`. It should arrive, because only the email that follows the order being completed is skipped.
7. Place a fourth order, fulfill every item in it, then add another product to it with `PUT /wc/v3/orders/<id>` and mark the order complete. The "Completed order" email should arrive, because the added item has not shipped.
8. Confirm that WooCommerce > Settings > Emails still shows "Completed order" as enabled, and that an order with no fulfillments at all still receives it.

PHPUnit, in the wp-env tests container on PHP 8.1: `FulfillmentsManagerTest` passes with 35 tests and 69 assertions. The email tests now mark the order complete and watch for `woocommerce_email_sent`, instead of asking the email whether it is enabled, so they go through the dispatch this filter affects: the status change, the deferred email queue, and a resend. Every test that expects no email has a counterpart that expects one, so none of them can pass merely because the test environment sends nothing.

author: acts-1631
body:
Sample rates below 20 Hz produce a zero-sample ReplayGain window in
analyze_file(). With worker threads enabled, wvgain divides by that
value before filter_init() rejects the unsupported rate, terminating
the process with SIGFPE.

Run filter_init() before calculating or allocating analysis windows,
and skip the analysis path when validation fails. This preserves the
existing unsupported-rate error while preventing the threaded
divide-by-zero.

New parents could only create their first PIN through an explorer vault. The header instead offered Reset Parent PIN, which could fail for accounts without a Family Vault. Replace that header action with Create Parent PIN when no PIN exists, and put reset beside the PIN entry area in Parent controls and account deletion. Reset remains reachable during a wrong-PIN lockout. If recovery is opened with no PIN, show initial creation directly.

Add an authenticated first-PIN setup/status RPC that works without an explorer or existing family: status is read-only; saving a valid first PIN initializes only the parent's own empty Family Vault. It requires a live session and matching expected parent ID and uses the existing insert-only PIN setup path, so it cannot replace an existing PIN. Existing PIN changes still use verified-email recovery. Consent activation is unchanged.

### Deployment order

1. Run supabase/migrations/20261116150000_parent_pin_setup.sql.
2. Separately run supabase/checks/parent_pin_setup.sql (disposable random fixtures; transaction rolls back).
3. Merge/deploy this PR after both queries pass. The new UI requires the new RPC.

Validation: full npm test --prefix tests and git diff --check passed. Tests cover a no-family/no-explorer parent, mismatches, wrong account/anonymous/expired sessions, existing-PIN preservation, setup/reset distinctions, stale account responses and all previous account/recovery/wallet/request checks. Local browser QA with a synthetic account confirmed the header Create Parent PIN screen works before any explorer exists. No real PIN was entered/changed and no production migration was applied by this implementation.

See tools/PARENT_PIN_SETUP_ROLLOUT.md for the rollout and remaining operator-controlled live test. Fresh signup and password-reset successes reported by the operator are recorded in the account checklist; item 1 remains open for this final PIN UX retest.

author: leynos
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the execution plan for roadmap task **4.1.4**: the versioned JSON application envelope, stdout/stderr stream invariants, stable exit classes, and global renderer options for `cargo theorem`. **It contains only the plan. Implementation waits for approval.**

ExecPlan: [`docs/execplans/4-1-4-versioned-json-application-contracts.md`](https://github.com/leynos/theoremc/blob/4-1-4-versioned-json-application-contracts/docs/execplans/4-1-4-versioned-json-application-contracts.md)

Roadmap: `docs/roadmap.md` task 4.1.4, under step 4.1 "Establish the Cargo subcommand and OrthoConfig spine". Design: `docs/cargo-theorem-cli-design.md` §§8.2–8.4, and ADR-0002 decision 4.

## How the plan was made

- A Wyvern reconnaissance team surveyed four areas: the `cargo-theorem` tests and tooling, the governing docs and roadmap dependants, the size history of earlier plans, and the OrthoConfig 0.10.0 / cargo-orthohelp 0.10.0 sources.
- Prior art: the NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR conventions, and the "Structured output" section of OrthoConfig's agent-native design.
- A community-of-experts panel reviewed the draft from four angles: structure and alternatives, contracts and evolution, failure modes and cost, and verification rigour. Its verdict was "proceed with conditions", and the conditions are now part of the plan (see its revision notes).

## Plan shape

Five milestones, each one a validated stopping point:

1. Protocol types and exit classes.
2. Emission, stream discipline, and a compile-time spawn fence.
3. Global renderer options.
4. A behavioural (`rstest-bdd`) suite and contract hardening.
5. Documentation, ADR-0014, and roadmap updates.

**Verification:** every obligation in this slice ranges over a finite domain. The plan covers each one with exhaustive tables, oracle-backed property tests, insta snapshots, and end-to-end transcripts. That includes a `/dev/full` test showing that a failed write still produces exactly one diagnostic.

**Verus:** the plan uses Verus nowhere in this slice, and explains why. The bounded-capture proof sketch is recorded as a deferred obligation for task 4.4.1, which owns the command runner.

## Decisions that need reviewer confirmation

- **D1 / Q2:** `context --json` keeps emitting OrthoConfig's bare agent-context document. It is not wrapped in the application envelope. Consumers dispatch on `kind` before reading `schema_version`.
- **D16 / Q3:** no process runner and no Verus proof in 4.1.4. The subprocess clause of the success criterion is enforced structurally by the Clippy spawn fence. Runner-level evidence moves to task 4.4.1, and new roadmap notes on 4.2.1 and 4.4.1 record this.
- **D7:** colour values from configuration files rank below `NO_COLOR`; only `--color` and `THEOREMC_COLOR` override it.
- **Q1:** should a broken pipe on stdout exit `10` like any other write fault?

## Other changes

`typos.local.toml` gains narrow patterns for the fixed US spellings `--color`, `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR(_FORCE)`, `ColorPolicy`, and `ColorChoice`. `typos.toml` is regenerated to match.

## Validation

`make markdownlint`, `make nixie`, and `make spelling` pass, and so do the spelling-policy tests (`spelling_policy`, `spelling_command_contract`). This PR changes no code.

## References

- Lody session: https://lody.ai/leynos/sessions/b62509f1-4e4e-4f4b-8100-014b90060470

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Document the approved design direction and implementation plan for `cargo theorem` application output contracts without changing application code.

Enhancements:
- Add a detailed execution plan for versioned JSON application contracts, stream ownership, stable exit classes, and global renderer options for `cargo theorem`.
- Define the planned verification strategy, milestone gates, deferred runner obligations, design decisions, and documentation updates for roadmap task 4.1.4.

Documentation:
- Add the draft ExecPlan for implementing roadmap task 4.1.4, including protocol, rendering, testing, and rollout documentation requirements.

Tests:
- Specify exhaustive, property-based, snapshot, behavioural, and end-to-end verification coverage for the planned application contracts.

Chores:
- Extend spelling-tool configuration to recognise fixed CLI and environment-variable spellings used by the plan.

author: shaheenfarjo
body:
This branch carries the session's prompts, since it is the one branch:
- the database and repository cleanup;
- prompts 21, 22 and 23;
- the owner's Data API hardening and the "programs" spelling, asked for in chat on Nov 17.

The newest part comes first. `main` is merged in (#295, #296); #297 (the decisions.md "Background jobs" line) is still open, and this follows it.

## What changes (Nov 17, prompt 23 and the owner's requests)

**1. One schema for the Data API: `api`** (PostgREST's Schema Isolation; the owner chose it over prompt 23's "nine schemas as they are")
- **Only `api` is exposed.** The data stays in `core`, `access`, `membership`, `events`, `journal`, `programs`, `governance` and `content`, and none of those is exposed. Neither are `public`, `pgmq` or `graphql_public`.
- **`private.build_api()`** builds `api` from the catalog (`20261116001300_api_schema.sql`):
  - a view with `security_invoker` for each table a role reaches, so RLS, the "No third-party apps" policy and the grants decide as the caller;
  - a SECURITY INVOKER wrapper for each function a role calls.
- **Names:** the same as before, except where a name is in two schemas (`events_invitations`, `membership_invitations`).
- **Tables clients may read only in part** (column grants, such as `contributors.user_id` under blind review):
  - their `api` view holds only what clients may read;
  - `<name>_all` holds every column, for the server's secret key only.
- **Settings' write-only choices:** Settings saves the profile choices a member may change but not read back through `core.update_my_profile`, since a view can't carry a column its reader can't see.
- **Every client** queries `.schema("api")`. The types come from the data schemas, so no column turns nullable.
- **`99_api_schema.test.sql`** fails when a migration forgets `select private.build_api();` (AGENTS.md has the rule).
- **`config.toml`:**
  - `schemas = ["api"]`;
  - `extra_search_path = ["extensions"]`;
  - `auto_expose_new_tables = false`.

**2. "programs" everywhere** (American spelling; `20261116001200_programs.sql`)
- **Renamed:** the schema `programmes` is `programs`, `core.programmes` is `core.programs`, every `programme_id` is `program_id`, and the role `programme_lead` is `program_lead`.
- **Values that follow:** the scope and Notion link kinds, the outbox kinds, the cache tag, the Notion data source key and the activity log, so history still reads.
- **Remade with the new names:** function bodies, 32 policies and the triggers. All 500 policies are still there.
- Code, file names, tests and docs follow. The language check refuses "programme". The one exception left is the status value `cancelled`.

**3. Hudhud's posts run on Supabase Queues** (prompt 23, part 1; replaces prompt 22's batching of posts)
- **The queue:** `telegram` (pgmq), made in `20261116001400_telegram_queue.sql`. Its schema stays unexposed, and only the server's key reaches it, through `api.telegram_*`.
- **How a run works:**
  - the job plans with a queued Telegram API, so each group post, member message and pin becomes a message (`lib/api/bot/queue.ts`);
  - a send step reads 10 at a time, each hidden from other runs for 40 seconds (inside the route's 60), and deletes each once Telegram confirms;
  - it records the post's message id, and pins an announcement once its post is out.
- **Failures:**
  - a run that dies leaves its messages to reappear for the next run;
  - a member who blocked Hudhud has that message's switch turned off (notices, the paper or reminders);
  - a message Telegram refuses for itself, or one failing five times, is set aside, and `sal-platform-health` reports it to the web topic and the Desk.
- **Is Queues the right tool?** Yes: it gives the exactly-once delete, the timeout and the archive with no new service.
- **The rest of the route:** staff alerts still go straight to Telegram (they report the queue itself). Upkeep (tags, removals, links, descriptions) stays inline under the 40-second budget. No status column was added.
- **The cause of the timeouts:** still not identifiable from logs (Vercel keeps an hour). Each step now has a time limit, and the posts are on the queue.

**4. GraphQL is off** (prompt 23, part 2)
- Nothing in the site, Hudhud, the scripts or the tests uses GraphQL (`graphql_public`, `/graphql/v1`, `pg_graphql`).
- `pg_graphql` isn't installed in production; `20261116001500_graphql_off.sql` keeps it so.
- `graphql_public` is out of `config.toml`. No other schema is touched.

## For the owner (to become tasks in Notion)

**When you merge, in this order:**
1. **Merge #297** first if you can. This PR follows it.
2. **Merge this PR.** The migrate workflow pushes the migrations, which create `api` and rename `programmes`, then deploys.
3. **As soon as the workflow's "db push" step is green,** go to Integrations → Data API and add `api` to the exposed schemas, keeping the others for now. Until the new site is live (a few minutes), the old one can't read `programmes`, so pick a quiet time.
4. **Once the new deploy is live and the site works:**
   - set the exposed schemas to `api` only, removing the eight data schemas, `public` and `graphql_public` (this is prompt 23's `graphql_public` removal too);
   - take `public` out of the extra search path, leaving `extensions`;
   - keep "Automatically expose new tables" off.
5. **Integrations → Queues:** leave "Expose Queues via PostgREST" off. The job reaches the queue through `api.telegram_*`.

**Also:**
- **Vercel variables you can delete now** (nothing reads them):
  - `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`;
  - `SUPABASE_URL` and the seven `POSTGRES_*`;
  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- **Keep:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.
- **Supabase's legacy keys:** the anon key already shows as disabled, and disabling the service_role key breaks nothing.
- **Supabase → Authentication → Email**, once deployed:
  - turn on "Require current password when updating";
  - set the OTP length to 8 and the expiry to 3600;
  - leave the required characters empty.
- **If `mta-sts.auibsal.org`** is still under Vercel → Domains, remove it there; the Worker answers it.
- **To decide:** the status value `cancelled` is the last British spelling in the data (events, productions and others). Say if it should become `canceled` too.

---

## What changes (Nov 17, prompt 22)

**1. Scheduled routes stay within their time, and a failed route is reported**
- **The Telegram route** runs its steps one at a time within a budget (`lib/api/steps.ts`):
  - no step starts after 40 seconds, and none runs past 20 seconds or the 45th second;
  - a step left behind goes first on the next run;
  - a failed step answers 500 while the others still run.
- **The health check sees routes now** (`20261116001100_route_health.sql`):
  - `private.call_api` records each call's path and waits 70 seconds, so Vercel's timeout comes back as a 504;
  - `sal-platform-health` alerts the web topic and the Desk to a route that failed or ran out of time.

**2. A failed read no longer stops a page**
- Published reads go through a `"use cache"` fetch keyed by address, headers and body (`lib/supabase.ts`).
- An answer is kept an hour and refreshed on publish; an error, a minute.
- The build passes against a database that refuses every read; `main` failed exactly as the Nov 16 production deploys did.

**3. Retired variable names**
- `turbo.json` no longer passes the retired Supabase, Postgres and push names.
- `core.push_subscriptions` was already dropped on Nov 14.

**4. The password and email codes**
- **Settings** asks for the current password and sends `current_password`; an old sign-in still gets the emailed code.
- **The reset from the email** needs none.
- **e2e covers both:** the wrong-password step runs where the auth server enforce

author: muncherelli
body:
The web UI runs on the gateway under an unprivileged account, which cannot check another user's password with `pam_unix`. This adds `lanlord-auth-helper`, a small root program that does only that.

- **Protocol:** the caller writes `user NUL password NUL` and closes its writing side; the helper answers `ok`, `denied` or `error <code>` (exit 0/1/2). The password is never logged, never in argv or the environment, and is wiped after use.
- **Checks:** a plain POSIX login name only; PAM auth + account for the `lanlord` service (so expired or locked accounts are refused); then membership of `admins` (gid 9998). Unknown user, wrong password and non-admin all answer the same `denied`, and every non-`ok` answer takes at least 1.5 s.
- **Privilege:** no setuid and no sudo rule. systemd socket activation (`lanlord-auth.socket`, `Accept=yes`) starts one hardened root process per connection; only the web UI account can open the socket (`root:<account>`, 0660), and the helper also checks the peer's uid via `SO_PEERCRED`.
- **PAM binding:** minimal FFI against libpam (pam_start / pam_authenticate / pam_acct_mgmt / pam_end), no bindgen. PAM and the group database sit behind traits so the decision logic is unit-tested without either.
- **Ansible:** new `webui-login.yml` (tag `webui-login`), imported by `site.yml` and embedded in the payload. It installs the helper from `/opt/lanlord/bin/lanlord-auth-helper` when present, writes `/etc/pam.d/lanlord` (common-* on Debian, system-auth elsewhere), and the socket and service units. `lanlord_webui_user` (default `lanlord`) names the account allowed to ask.
- **Platforms:** Linux only; on macOS and Windows the binary just answers `error unsupported` so the workspace still builds there.
- **CI:** the Linux jobs install `libpam0g-dev`.
- **Docs:** `docs/webui-login.md`.

To confirm: the group is `admins` (gid 9998), the current name of the admins group in core, rather than the older `lanlord-admins` name.

Not in this PR: the web UI calling the socket, purge removing these files, and shipping the helper binary to the gateway.

This PR updates [botocore](https://pypi.org/project/botocore) from **1.29.54** to **1.44.4**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 1.44.4
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``athena``: Adds an optional AttributesToGet parameter to ListDatabases and ListTableMetadata to return only requested database or table names (and table types) from the AWS Glue Data Catalog, reducing response time for large catalogs.
* api-change:``cognito-idp``: Implement OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) for Cognito User Pools, enabling services to exchange a user's existing token for a new token that is appropriately scoped and audience-bound for a specific downstream service.
* api-change:``connect``: Adds the DeleteAllEntitySessions API, which signs a user out of all of their active sessions in an Amazon Connect instance.
* api-change:``connecthealth``: Adds dataset APIs and async medical coding jobs that can use a customer dataset (preview). Ambient listening sessions add medical coding job details and real-time periodontal chart and checklist events (preview). SubmitFeedback compares human-approved and AI-generated artifacts (preview).
* api-change:``connectscheduling``: This release adds APIs for Amazon Connect Scheduling. Use them to create, get, approve, reject, and cancel agent time off requests, and to set agent time off balances.
* api-change:``dsql``: Added support for Amazon Aurora DSQL advanced monitoring metric groups, which publish detailed database metrics and logs to Amazon CloudWatch Database Insights. Adds the metricGroups parameter to CreateCluster, UpdateCluster, and GetCluster.
* api-change:``dynamodbstreams``: Generate account-based endpoints for DynamoDB Streams requests when the account ID is available
* api-change:``ec2``: Adds a new Transit Gateway Attachment type called Network Function. Launches associated KMS Keys for EBS Snapshots - associated KMS keys enable customers to share and copy snapshots encrypted with AWS Managed Keys across AWS accounts.
* api-change:``ecr``: ECR feature support for replicating image deletion and untagging.
* api-change:``ecs``: Amazon ECS gateway connectors now support a configurable deregistration delay (0-3600 seconds, default 300 seconds).
* api-change:``emr-serverless``: Amazon EMR Serverless now supports Flex, a new execution option for running data processing jobs on spare compute capacity at a discount.
* api-change:``endpoint-rules``: Update endpoint-rules client to latest version
* api-change:``health``: Adds resource tags functionality to the AWS Health service
* api-change:``iam-toolbox``: AWS IAM adds the GetRequestAuthorizationPolicy operation, per-check authorization results (checks) and extra policy metadata for resource-based policies (policySource) in GetRequestAuthorizationDetails for Access Troubleshooter.
* api-change:``iotwireless``: Updated CreateDeviceProfile to accept MaxEirp values up to 36 dBm in LoRaWANDeviceProfile. Previously the maximum value was 15.
* api-change:``kms``: AWS KMS now supports sharing KMS keys across AWS accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). This release adds the optional ResourceOwners parameter to ListKeys, which lists keys owned by the caller's account (SELF), keys shared with the account through AWS RAM, or both.
* api-change:``lambda``: Adds support for GPU instances on Lambda Managed Instances in the CreateFunction and UpdateFunctionConfiguration APIs. Lambda Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances can now set the accelerator memory using the new AcceleratorConfig parameter and run on capacity providers with GPU instances.
* api-change:``lambda-core``: Lambda network connectors now support service-managed Elastic IP addresses. This enables traffic routed through a connector to reach the public internet without a NAT gateway.
* api-change:``network-firewall``: Adds support for context-aware stateful rule groups, letting rules reference AWS resource IDs through ContextSets sourced from a Network Manager context store.
* api-change:``networkflowmonitor``: This release adds Performance Monitors to Amazon CloudWatch Network Monitoring. Without installing an agent, they track traffic in the VPCs you select and report an impact score (None, Low, Medium, or High) showing whether the AWS network is degrading your workloads.
* api-change:``networkmanager``: Context Sharing with Firewalls
* api-change:``opensearchmemory``: Initial release of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, which gives AI agents persistent memory. Store conversation and document events in a Space, have memories extracted from them automatically, and retrieve them with semantic, lexical, or hybrid search.
* api-change:``s3vectors``: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search, providing metadata text search along with vector search.
* api-change:``sagemaker``: Amazon SageMaker adds Synthetic Data Generation, Auto-labeling, Data Quality Evaluation, and Data Transformation capabilities, Cross-Region Inference Routing, KV Aware routing for realtime inference endpoints.
* api-change:``sagemaker-inference-router-runtime``: Amazon SageMaker adds cross-region inference routing with new runtime APIs that intelligently route inference requests across endpoints in multiple AWS regions.
* api-change:``wellarchitected``: This release adds AWS Organizations integration, on-demand reports, recommendation and profile sharing, and automated basic profiles to the Well-Architected Agent.
* api-change:``workspaces``: Adds the WorkspaceOsUserMode parameter to RegisterWorkspaceDirectory and DescribeWorkspaceDirectories, so customers can register an IAM Identity Center directory whose WorkSpaces use local operating system users instead of joining a domain.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.44.3

author: raftisk
body:
In order to show structured backend output next to the chat (goal 3 of the project constitution), a tool result that holds the artifact envelope now renders as a card below its tool item, and a click opens the artifact in a resizable pane on the right.

### Approach

- Detection is one function, `readArtifact`, built on the existing `parseToolResult` and `readToolError`. A result with a string `error` is never an artifact. An invalid envelope stays a plain tool result and logs a warning with the tool call id and the failed field.
- A registry maps an artifact type to a label, an icon and a component. Core registers the JSON viewer and a sortable data table. Unknown types use the JSON viewer and show the raw type as the label. A fork adds or replaces types in `src/extensions/artifact-types.tsx`, read through `import.meta.glob` like the tool labels.
- The open artifact is view state in a zustand store, keyed by tool call id, and clears on a thread change. Only the pane width goes to localStorage.
- The JSON viewer and the table are toki code. Item counts on collapsed nodes and the depth rule cost less to write than to restyle from a library.
- The reference server gets `/artifact-unknown`, which streams an artifact of an unregistered type, so e2e covers the fallback.

The phase 6 commit also wraps `ChatLayout` in `ArtifactPaneProvider`. The card throws without it, and 7 of 15 e2e tests failed otherwise.

### Test plan

- Unit tests (139) and typecheck, lint, format check and build in `app/`. `pytest`, `ruff` and `pyright` in `reference-server/`.
- `pnpm e2e` passes all 22 tests. The 7 new ones cover open and sort, the JSON viewer, the unknown type, switch and close, thread switch and new thread, history reload and the persisted pane width.
- The "reload: both tool turns" test reloaded while a run was still streaming, which left the thread titled "New thread". The card shifted the timing enough to expose it, so the test now waits for the reply text first.
- jsdom has no `AnimationEvent`, so a small setup file defines it. Without it react-dom drops `onAnimationEnd` in tests.

### Out of scope

Several open artifacts, a mobile layout, opening the pane on arrival, virtualized tables and a sample extension artifact.

author: bahaa-eddine-mb
body:
## Description

Closes #1111

Quick links are now loaded from Firebase Remote Config (`quicklinks_values`) instead of being hardcoded, so links can be added, removed or edited without releasing the app.

**Scope change vs. the original issue** (discussed with SERISET): Firebase Storage / `remotePath` is dropped. Each link uses either:
- `"icon"`: a Font Awesome name (e.g. `"shield-halved"`), from an explicit list in `quick_link_icons.dart` (keeps icon tree shaking), or
- `"svg"`: an SVG stored directly in the JSON, as base64 (raw `<svg>` strings and data URIs are also accepted).

If neither is usable, a placeholder icon is shown.

**Offline / cache:** the last valid value is saved on the device. Load order: Remote Config → cached copy → bundled links (`quick_links.dart`). Invalid JSON from Remote Config is logged and ignored, so a bad publish can't wipe the links.

**User order is preserved:** hidden links are now saved explicitly (`hiddenQuickLinksCache`). New links from Remote Config are appended at the end without resetting the user's order, removed links disappear, and hidden links stay hidden. Users on the old cache format are migrated: old links missing from their saved order stay hidden.

**Remote Config:** `quicklinks_values` was updated with all 21 current links. 12 use Font Awesome names, 9 use base64 SVG (GUS and FabLAB from the existing assets; MonÉTS, Moodle, AÉÉTS, 100 Génies, Nimbus, Centre sportif and Café sans filtre traced from the existing PNGs, so they can be swapped for official SVGs later).

### Changes
- `remote_config_service.dart`: new `quickLinksValues` getter (non-blocking, refreshes in background)
- `quick_link_remote_data.dart` (new): JSON model + tolerant parsing (string or int ids, bad entries skipped)
- `quick_link_icons.dart` (new): icon name map, SVG decoding (raw/base64/data URI), placeholder
- `quick_link_repository.dart`: Remote Config → cache → bundled fallback, hidden links cache, `applyUserPreferences` merge
- `quick_links_viewmodel.dart`: uses the merge; saves order + hidden links on delete/restore/reorder

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- Unit tests:
  - repository: Remote Config valid / empty / invalid → cache → bundled fallback; merge (new link appended, removed link dropped, legacy cache migration); hidden ids cache
  - `quick_link_icons_test.dart`: raw / base64 / data URI / invalid SVG, icon priority, placeholder
  - viewmodel and view tests updated for the new repository API
- Manually on Android:
  - renamed a link in Remote Config → change shown in the app
  - added a new link → appended at the end, custom order kept
  - airplane mode + app restart → links still shown from cache
  - invalid JSON published → last valid list kept

## ☑️ Checklist before requesting a review

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code.
- [x] If it is a core feature, I have added thorough tests.
- [x] If needed, I added analytics. (invalid Remote Config values are logged with `logError`)
- [x] Make sure to add either one of the following labels: `version: Major`,`version: Minor` or `version: Patch`.

author: purvanshjoshi
body:
## Summary
The Web IDE read one shared clone per repository, while writes went to a per-user working branch (`automaintainer/ide-<hash(org:user)>`) and were mirrored into that clone. As a result, files created and edits saved by one user were visible to every other user of the repository and could end up in their Propose. This PR gives every user their own read view, restores the staged list after a reload, refuses writes into another user's working branch, and hardens the git calls behind the views.

## Changes
- **Per-user views (backend/workspace.py, backend/main.py):**
  - Reads now come from a detached git worktree at `<workspace>/_ide_views/<clone>/<user key>`, checked out at the caller's working branch. Users without a working branch share a `_default` view of the default branch.
  - Fetched commits are pinned at `refs/automaintainer-ide/<key>/{base,head}`.
  - GET tree and every write refresh the view: one ls-remote, then fetch and checkout only when something moved. GET file and search read the existing view without network access.
  - Writes no longer touch the shared clone (`_write_local_mirror` removed).
  - If no view can be built the route answers 503; there is no fallback to the shared clone.
  - Views are evicted after `IDE_VIEW_TTL_HOURS` (24) unused and beyond `IDE_VIEW_MAX` (50), least recently used first.
- **New `GET /repo/{name}/working-changes`:** returns the caller's branch diff. The branch is derived only from the authenticated org/user. It is tenant-checked by `require_repo_access` and listed in the route inventory and the OpenAPI snapshot.
- **Dashboard (WebIDE.tsx):** on load the IDE restores staged paths from `working-changes`. A restored entry has no diff baseline, so the review dialog names it instead of showing a diff. Its content is loaded from the open buffer or from GET /file at Propose time. A failed or malformed answer is ignored.
- **Write guard:** POST /file, POST /file/create and DELETE /file now return 403 for an explicit branch in the `automaintainer/ide-` namespace (compared case-insensitively) other than the caller's own working branch. The check runs before any GitHub call.
- **Git hardening:**
  - Every view git command runs with `-c core.hooksPath=<devnull> -c core.fsmonitor=false`.
  - The view fetch uses `--no-write-fetch-head`, so it cannot race `sync_repo_clone`.
  - `IDE_VIEW_MAX` and `IDE_VIEW_TTL_HOURS` are parsed leniently.
  - The no-working-branch cache is bounded.
- **Docs:** ARCHITECTURE.md (Web IDE section) and DEPLOYMENT.md.

## Testing
- **New `backend/test_ide_workspace.py` covers:**
  - user isolation of tree, file and search;
  - working-changes;
  - the 403 for writes to another user's branch, including an upper-case spelling;
  - hooks planted in the shared clone not running;
  - FETCH_HEAD not being written;
  - lenient limit parsing and cache expiry;
  - a POSIX-only symlink test, skipped on Windows.
- Also updated: test_fs_api.py, test_workspace_repo_id.py, test_route_inventory.py, the dashboard contract test and WebIDE.test.tsx.
- Merged-tree run, together with the other two open fixes, on github/main 315e69c:
  - Backend `uv run --frozen pytest`: 1840 passed, 145 skipped.
  - tests/redteam: 60 passed. tests/contract: 11 passed.
  - test_route_inventory.py + test_ide_workspace.py + test_tenant_tokens.py: 228 passed, 1 skipped (the POSIX-only symlink test on Windows).
  - `db-migrate schema --check`: up to date. CI flake8 gate: 0 errors. black --check: 257 files unchanged.
  - Dashboard lint 0, tsc 0, vitest 180/180 passed in 21 files, build 0.

Refs #505
Refs #139

## Notes / follow-ups

body:
A selection that matches no cell stops the run of the workflow Cells, with its reason (SYS-121).

The name of a cell is its id and its words, for example `PR.7 ...`. Thus the dispatch of [run 43957250955](https://github.com/mark1russell7/systems/actions/runs/43957250955) with `only=^PR\.7$` matched no cell. Its shard found no test and failed with "No test found in suite", with no reason.

- `needsOf` (the step "The needs of the shard") stops a run whose selection matches no cell of the catalogs or of the file.
- The message names the shape of a cell name, and the filter for one id: `[^0-9]` after the id, not `$`.
- A shard with no cell stays correct, because a run can have more shards than cells.

The local checks: `vitest related` on `needs.ts` (7 tests), the typecheck of the cells package and ste-lint.

## Objective
Fix corrupted uploads of files split into multiple parts (e.g. large splats failing in ingest processing).

Parts were sliced with `part.end + 1` while `end` is already exclusive, so every non-final part carried one extra byte, duplicated at each part boundary. Slice now uses `part.end`, matching the cloud tileset uploader.

body:
## Summary of Changes

Implements a low-code workflow automation engine for conditional entity actions across `@honocube/api`, `@honocube/core`, and `@honocube/app`, enabling administrators to define Trigger-Condition-Action (TCA) automation rules from the admin UI on entity lifecycle events and state transitions.

### 1. `@honocube/api` (Backend Automation Engine & REST Endpoints)
- **`packages/api/src/automation/engine.ts`**:
  - Implemented `createAutomationEngine()` with support for:
    - Event triggers (`create`, `update`, `delete`, `toggle`, `state_change`, `*`).
    - Multi-condition evaluation (`equals`, `not_equals`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `in`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`, `changed`) with configurable boolean logic (`matchAll: true/false`).
    - Built-in action handlers:
      - `update_field`: Mutates entity fields directly or dynamically via interpolation (`{{...}}`).
      - `send_notification`: Dispatches multi-channel in-app notifications via `NotificationEngine`.
      - `webhook_post`: Dispatches asynchronous HTTP POST payloads to third-party endpoints.
      - `create_record`: Spawns related or child records on target resources.
      - `log_activity`: Records execution summaries to audit trail.
    - Live dry-run test evaluator (`evaluateRecord()`) without persisting side-effects.
    - Auto-subscribes to HonoCube's internal `EventBus` (`eventBus.subscribe("*", ...)`).
    - In-memory execution log ring buffer (`getExecutionLogs()`, `clearLogs()`).
- **`packages/api/src/core/factory.ts`**:
  - Mounted REST management endpoints:
    - `GET /automations`: List active workflow automation rules.
    - `POST /automations`: Register or update workflow rules.
    - `GET /automations/logs`: Retrieve execution history and action status.
    - `POST /automations/logs/clear`: Clear execution history.
    - `GET /automations/:id`: Retrieve single automation rule.
    - `PUT /automations/:id`: Update existing rule.
    - `DELETE /automations/:id`: Delete rule.
    - `POST /automations/test`: Live test evaluator for rule & payload simulation.

### 2. `@honocube/core` (Shared Types & Contracts)
- **`packages/core/src/automation/index.ts`**:
  - Re-exported automation types and factory: `createAutomationEngine`, `AutomationRule`, `AutomationCondition`, `AutomationActionConfig`, `AutomationExecutionResult`, `AutomationActionResult`.
- **`packages/core/src/views/types.ts`**:
  - Defined `AutomationRuleDialogProps` and `AutomationHistoryViewProps`.

### 3. `@honocube/app` (Visual UI Components & Test Suite)
- **`packages/app/src/views/automation-rule-dialog.tsx`**:
  - Visual low-code workflow rule builder dialog with target resource selection, trigger selector, conditional criteria builder, dynamic action sequence builder, and interactive live test playground.
- **`packages/app/src/views/automation-history-view.tsx`**:
  - Execution log inspector displaying trigger badges, status pill (`Success`, `Failed`, `Skipped`), relative timestamps, action count, and expandable action step breakdown.

author: basemax
body:
Adds `when cond:` blocks inside an element (section 1 of docs/design/UI_STATES_THEMES.md). A block holds style attributes only, including state prefixes such as `hover background`.

```salam
component Seg(label: str):
    picked := false
    big := false
    button:
        background = "blue"
        hover background = "navy"
        padding = 8
        when picked:
            background = "orange"
            hover background = "red"
        end
        when big:
            padding = 24
        end
        when picked and big:
            padding = 40
        end
        click = ():
            picked = not picked
            big = not big
        end
        content = label
    end
end
```

Persian: `وقتی cond:` ... `پایان`.

## How it works (deviation from the design)

The design asks for a generated data attribute plus a CSS rule on the web and a patch layer on native. This PR does not do that. The parser lowers every `when` block into per-attribute conditional values: `x = v` inside `when c` becomes `x = c ? v : <earlier value of x>`, and the else branch is an empty text (no declaration) when the element has no earlier value. A later `when` wraps the result of the earlier ones, so source order wins; state prefixes keep their own slot, so base, then `when` in order, then states holds.

Trade-offs:
- Both targets reuse the existing runtime style values (web `salamWsStyle`, native `SetText`), so behaviour is identical and only the scope that reads the condition re-runs.
- No new CSS: on the web each distinct value becomes a class from the existing dynamic style sheet, not a rule keyed to an attribute. Environment conditions (`dark`, `screen width < n`) need real `@media` and will come in a later PR with their own mapping.
- Attribute names are matched by their written spelling (case, `_`, `-` and spaces ignored). Mixing two aliases of one property (`background` and `background color`) gives the duplicate attribute error instead of merging.
- `when` is recognised only at the start of a layout line followed by a condition, so `when = ...` as an attribute or `when:` as an element keep working. It is not a global keyword.
- Empty text means "no declaration" for `salamWsStyle` and `ui.Builder.SetText`.
- E175 (`when` holds style attributes only) is reported for pages; a `when` with elements inside a component body is not checked yet. E173 (condition must be bool) is not added: the ternary type check reports it.

## Tests

- `tests/{en,fa}/page/components/when_style` (web output lines), `tests/en/page/errors/when_holds_elements` (E175).
- Ran `page/components` and `page/errors` with a compiler built from this branch: 1964 passed, 19 failed, all 19 are in tools/ui-gate-known-failures.txt.
- Native is not verified: every native `ui/*` test with a dynamic style value is on the known-failures list on main until #3527 lands (the existing `ui/en/scope_list` fails the same way with this branch's compiler). The native twin test will follow once #3527 is merged.

author: kokou-egbewatt
body:
Closes #22. Part of #10: everything except `/v1/stream`, which needs the gateway's streaming endpoint (#4); the runtime's streaming span is instrumented and tested now. Takes #9's correlation part (trace IDs on log lines, `request_id` on the runtime's lines) and leaves the rest of #9.

One request is one trace across the gateway and the runtime, both services expose request metrics, and their log lines join their traces in Grafana.

### What is in it

- **`packages/tracing`:** OpenTelemetry with OTLP to the collector gateway and the W3C propagator. It's off with an empty `otel.endpoint`; the propagator still passes a trace on.
- **`packages/telemetry`:** `neuromesh_requests_total`, `neuromesh_request_errors_total` and `neuromesh_request_duration_seconds`, labeled by `service`, `rpc` (route template or gRPC method) and `code`, on an admin `/metrics` port. It's off unless `metrics.enabled`.
- **Gateway:** an `otelhttp` server span named `POST /v1/route` (never the raw path), and an `otelgrpc` client span that carries the trace in the metadata. 5xx counts as an error.
- **Runtime:** `otelgrpc` server spans as children of the gateway's client span. A stream's span gets `neuromesh.stream.chunks` and `neuromesh.stream.first_chunk_ms` and ends when the stream closes. RPC log lines carry `request_id`.
- **Logs:** `trace_id` and `span_id` while a span is active, absent otherwise.
- **Health checks** are neither traced nor counted.
- **Charts:** metrics on (the `VMServiceScrape` was already there), traces to `otel-gateway.observability:4317` at **10% sampling**, all through environment variables (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`, `METRICS_ENABLED`), so one image serves every setup.
- **`fields.yaml`** allows the span attributes worth keeping and leaves out `client.address`, `network.peer.*`, `user_agent.original` and `url.path`.

### Criteria

- [x] **One trace, runtime span a child of the gateway client span:** `TestOneRequestIsOneTraceAcrossGatewayAndRuntime`, in-memory exporter.
- [ ] **`/v1/stream` span:** the runtime side is done (`TestStreamSpanCountsChunksAndEndsAtClose`); the gateway route comes with #4.
- [x] **10 successes plus 5 injected failures counted exactly**, by service, rpc and code: `TestMetricsCountSuccessesAndFailuresExactly`.
- [x] **No prompt, request ID or key in any span attribute or metric label:** `TestNoHighCardinalityValuesInSpansOrMetrics`, with a sentinel prompt.
- [x] **Off boots and serves:** every existing test runs with instrumentation off.
- [x] **≤5% p50 overhead**, at the deployed setting. Same binary, reference container, off against on:

  | p50 | metrics only | tracing 10% | tracing 100% |
  | --- | --: | --: | --: |
  | route c=1 | +1% | 0% | +6% |
  | route c=8 | −1% | −11% (noise) | +4% |
  | route c=64 | +4% | +0.3% | **+27%** |
  | stream c=8 | −2% | −2% | +2% |

  At 100% sampling it fails under concurrency (three spans per request through one batch queue at about 40k req/s), so the charts keep 10%. A client's sampled `traceparent` is always followed. Recorded in `BASELINE.md`.
- [x] **On the #22 stack:** `TestClusterOneRequestAcrossTheStack` passes on gpu-lab. The test sends its own sampled `traceparent`, so its trace ID is known in advance. It checks:
  - the gateway's and runtime's log lines in VictoriaLogs, joined on that trace ID;
  - the trace in Tempo through Grafana, with both services;
  - the count in VictoriaMetrics via `/prometheus/api/v1/query`.

### Also checked

- `task obs:verify` still passes all 9 checks.
- `task ci:go`: 0 lint issues and all tests pass. Coverage is 79.4%, up from 68.6%.
- `task deps:check`: 13 modules tidy and agreeing.
- `task ci:charts` passes, and the hooks pass.

author: wunderay
body:
## Why

A backup of `Mods` alone misses ZZMI's saved in-game choices in the configured user-state file (normally `d3dx_user.ini`). Restoring different folder or INI names can also disconnect those choices from their mods.

## What changes

- Add **Back up...** and **Restore...** under **Settings → ZZMI → Mod backups**.
- Preserve the standalone version 1 snapshot format: the entire launcher folder, original relative paths, saved mod state, launcher configuration, and other contained importers.
- Save pending settings and prepare an isolated helper before closing the launcher. The helper verifies its own runtime location, pins the initiating process identity, acknowledges readiness, and waits for the launcher to exit before touching the snapshot.
- Verify archive and staged-file hashes, reject unsafe paths and unsupported external ZZMI dependencies, refuse existing archive destinations, and retain the previous installation in a sibling rollback folder.
- Block other launcher tasks during preparation and keep the launcher usable after cancellation or preparation errors.
- Document the complete scope, original-location restore requirement, recovery reports, and supported runtime layouts.

## Validation

- Full Linux suite: **228 tests; OK, with 30 Windows-only checks skipped**.
- Real detached source-process backup → restore preserved saved choices, removed newly added active files, and retained the previous folder.
- Headless application tests cover cancellation, save-before-prepare ordering, readiness-before-close, process/task guards, preparation failures, and early worker dispatch.
- **Windows engine/controller checks passed:** 73 tests, with 4 Linux-only checks skipped.
- **Windows packaged checks passed:** 11 tests, including real settings button dispatch and an unattended backup/restore round trip through the actual copied executable. [Windows run](https://github.com/wunderay/XXMI-Launcher/actions/runs/43970775286).
- **GitHub Linux checks passed** on the same final commit. [Linux run](https://github.com/wunderay/XXMI-Launcher/actions/runs/43970775500).
- Windows regressions also cover path/descriptor timestamp differences and short/long temporary-path aliases, while retaining source-change checks during copying.
- No development payloads, tracked binaries, or protected native patch bytes were changed.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src/xxmi_launcher python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```

## Scope

This is a whole-launcher-folder snapshot, available initially on ZZMI. Restoring also reverts other contained games' files and global launcher settings. The supported packaged layout is this repository's PyInstaller onedir runtime; unsupported layouts fail during preparation. Saved files can be restored exactly, but unsaved or already-lost choices and external game/manager data cannot be reconstructed.

Astra Edelfelt Aetherwyn
