## O que muda
Um único botão de confirmação humana, "Estou de acordo", grava a nota na Central Fiscal e lança a compra no Mercado numa chamada (RPC `nota_fiscal_confirmar`, migration 059).

- O botão só aparece com leitura completa, conta fechando, confiança da IA >= 90% e sem nota cancelada/rejeitada/duplicada. Se não aparecer: outra foto ou o editor que já existia.
- Situação fiscal pendente/contingência não impede a entrada no Mercado e continua registrada; cancelada/rejeitada bloqueiam. Nunca cria despesa.
- Produto: corte de 70% (Jaccard simétrico, com travas de marca, tamanho, embalagem e variante); abaixo disso cria produto novo, sem bloquear.
- Falha só no Mercado: nota, original e confirmação (quem e quando) ficam; estado `falhou` com o erro; "Tentar de novo" conclui sem nova leitura nem confirmação; repetir não duplica.
- Nota antiga: cada uma pede o seu "Estou de acordo". XML autorizado: o clique também confere. Nota cancelada/rejeitada depois da entrada: compra mantida e marcada "REVISAR".
- Substitui a 040 (que passa a se recusar a rodar). Versão 2026-11-16.6.

## Ordem de implantação (importante)
1. SQL `supabase/059_central_fiscal_entrada_unica.sql` no SQL Editor (a 057 já está aplicada; não reaplicar), depois `supabase/conferencias/059_conferir_producao.sql` (esperado tudo "ok").
2. Só depois o merge/publicação do site. Sem a 059 o botão dá erro de função ausente (nada é gravado).

## Testes
Suíte completa local (`scripts/nuvem_testes.sh`): Grupo 1 com 2000 testes, 1984 aprovados, 0 falhas, 2 ignorados e 14 TODO (preexistentes); Grupo 2 (PGlite) com 73 de 73. Novos: `banco_entrada_unica` (18) e `fiscal_correspondencia` (7).

Limites: interface não verificada em navegador real; calibração dos 70% com produtos reais pendente (`scripts/calibrar_correspondencia.mjs`); a 059 não foi aplicada em produção.

body:
## What changes

- **Reconnect:** when the launcher starts with no computer connected, it sends one `uuid:<udn>` `ssdp:byebye` and, 2 s later, the matching `ssdp:alive` (`Ssdp.avisoDoAparelho`, `AnuncioUpnp`). Windows drops the stale device and reconnects by itself.
- **USB drives:** every mounted volume is its own MTP storage next to the internal one (`MtpArmazem`, `MtpLoja` keyed by storage). Plugging/unplugging is announced with StoreAdded/StoreRemoved on the event connection. Storage names come from Android, in the TV language.
- **Brand:** manufacturer/model "Sofaly", `iconList` in both UPnP descriptions, and the `.ico` as MTP device property 0xD405 (`assets/upnp/`). Measured: Windows 11 requests neither icon, so only the name shows.
- **Network folder entry:** the basic UPnP device is now named "<TV> · painel" (was "· arquivos") and its presentationURL is the panel root instead of `/unidade`. It stays http on port 8080 on purpose: the https port uses a certificate made by the TV, which a device only trusts after installing it.
- **`/unidade` page and help:** rewritten for MTP (Windows shows the TV by itself, USB drives included; the drive-letter connector moved to "Advanced"); the panel links to it; `aj_unidade_texto` no longer mentions the "· arquivos" entry (all language folders).
- **Bench:** `MtpBancadaWindowsTest` runs the server + SSDP on a PC for a real Windows (only with `ONETV_BANCADA_IP`); `MtpSessao.rastro` logs operations.
- `PainelArquivos` functions take an optional base folder; `ChecagensPainel.dentroDe` uses the system separator (same behaviour on Android).

## Why

On Windows the TV folder stayed empty after every launcher restart until someone restarted the device by hand, and the USB drive on the hub did not show up. The "· arquivos" entry opened an outdated instructions page where people expected the panel. The product is now called Sofaly.

## How it was tested

- [x] `./gradlew testReleaseUnitTest` (1578 tests, 0 failures; new: storage hot-plug, device icon, the measured NOTIFY bytes)
- [ ] On a real TV (device + Android version): the reconnect packets were measured against the living-room Chromecast + Windows 11 by sending them by hand (drop < 1 s, reconnect ~1.5 s). The code itself has not run on the TV yet.
- [ ] With the remote only (focus, BACK, long-press): no screen changed
- [x] Not tested on a TV (say why): the TV is reserved for a memory test until 17/11. Multi-storage was checked against Windows 11 on the bench (5 storages listed, files readable). Writing to a real USB drive with "all files access" is not verified.

## Checklist

- [x] New user-facing text is in both `values/` (English, default) and `values-pt/` (Portuguese): one help string changed, in every language folder
- [x] No secrets, IPs, personal names or account data in code, comments or screenshots
- [x] New permissions or privileged actions are explained above: none; a receiver for media mount broadcasts only

## Summary

This PR adds the engine and the API of the stranger gate (spec 1 section 6.7). The person gives one answer for each sender that they do not know:

- **Accept** makes the sender a `person`, decided by the person. The items of the sender go to their sections (You owe, Owed to you, Conversations).
- **Decline** sets `declined_at` (migration 13). The kind stays with the engine, so a declined sender can still become `hostile`. The items of a declined stranger are in no section of the brief.
- **Reopen** (Undo) removes the answer of the gate. A kind that a person set for another reason stays.

A rule decides first: a `hide` or `bundle` rule takes the items of strangers out of the gate. The API refuses an answer (409) for a sender that is not at the gate in the same transaction: its kind is not `stranger` now, or a rule took its items out. An accept makes the domain of the sender known, so the engine decides the look-alikes again and runs understanding again on the mail of each sender whose hostile state changed, in the same transaction.

New API:

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/gate` | The senders at the gate, newest first, with the count and the newest 3 items of each. Keyset pages. |
| `GET /api/gate/declined` | The declined senders, in the same shape. |
| `POST /api/senders/{id}/{accept,decline,reopen}` | The answer. Gives the sender row. |
| `GET /api/brief` | Adds `gate` (the first 20 senders) and `declined` (a count). |

The web client view comes in the next PR (one PR for each view). The owner picks its layout on the before/after page first: https://claude.ai/artifact/6698QUTSPmhZAhyLu9pomV. So the doneWhen of the card ("an ask from a stranger does not show under You owe before you accept") holds in the API now: an ask from a stranger is only in the strangers section and the gate.

Decline is a column, not a policy rule and not a person-set kind. A rule for each sender would grow `policy.toml` toward its 1,000-rule cap and save a policy version for each click. A person-set `stranger` kind would stop the engine from marking the sender `hostile`.

Libraries: no new parser or protocol code. The PR uses the existing `iris-senders` rules (`rules`, `recheck`, `sweep`) and `iris_understand::store::rerun_senders`.

Memory: no new state in memory. Each gate query reads the store and returns at most one page.

Card: R5-03

## Verification

- `crates/iris-senders/tests/senders.rs`: accept makes look-alikes hostile; the gate refuses a sender that is not a stranger now (stored kind and fresh rules); a declined stranger can turn hostile; reopen gives the row back to the engine and decides an accepted look-alike from the evidence of now; an answer needs the sender at the gate; reopen keeps a kind that a person set outside the gate (each kind).
- `crates/iris-api/tests/gate.rs`: the gate is the strangers section by sender; a hide rule takes items out and an answer then gives 409 with no write; accept moves the items and reopen brings them back; decline takes the items out of the brief; refusals (409, 404, 400, 405); accept reruns understanding on a new look-alike; keyset paging and bad cursors; a generated test over 8 seeds of answer sequences (`each_gate_item_is_in_one_place_after_any_answers`) checks that each item is in exactly one place of the brief after any answers.
- `crates/iris-store/tests/store.rs`: schema version 12.
- Pre-review: fixed both P2 findings (gate membership, reopen limit) with invariant tests. The P1 finding (no client view) is the next PR, as said above.
- Local CI: `scripts/local-ci/run.sh` (proof commit on this branch).

## Known limits and deferred findings

- #263 limit(understand): the model still reads the mail of a declined sender
- #264 limit(api): a conversation with a declined sender leaves the brief, also with known people in it
- #265 limit(api): the gate computes the strangers section again for each brief and each answer

## Release Notes

- User-facing: The API can accept, ignore (decline) or undo a sender that you do not know. An ask from a stranger stays out of You owe until you accept the sender. The web client view follows in the next release.
- Internal: New `iris_senders::gate` and `iris_api::gate` modules. The brief adds `gate` and `declined`.
- Migrations/config/env: Migration 13 adds `sender.declined_at`.
- Docs/version/dependency bumps: Spec 1 section 6.7 and section 8, `sender.schema.json`, and the `iris-api` README describe the gate. `iris-api` depends on `iris-senders` and `iris-understand`.
- Risk/rollback: Low. A rollback leaves the `declined_at` column unused. Senders accepted at the gate stay `person`.

author: demonic-agent-fleet
body:
<!-- agent-author harness=claude-code model=claude-fable-5-2 session=86b16a29-17a5-4cd6-8c19-85ad1f75d882 class=feature -->

## Summary

The device had a button, a switch and a potentiometer that were read but did nothing beyond Start and Stop, and it showed only a few fixed colours. Errors from Wi-Fi and the inputs were dropped.

Now every status and error code of the feedback catalogue goes into one call, `physicalinterface_showFeedback(code)`, and the RGB light and the red button LED show the matching colour and blink code. CONTROL decides which code is shown and what a button press may do while an error is present.

- **Indication (L1):** one table row per code with colour, RGB pattern, red LED pattern and blink count. The red button LED on GPIO17 is new.
- **Error policy (L2):** one table row per error with priority, clear rule and admission. Non-audio errors raised during listening are held back and shown after the manual Stop; audio errors halt at once.
- **Volume:** the potentiometer sets a linear 0–100 % gain per block. It starts at 0 %.
- **Switch:** the three positions are read and logged. All three pass audio through unchanged; no filter is implemented.
- **Press light:** the red LED is on while the button is down and blinks at 4 Hz once a hold is accepted. It ends at release.

## V-model stage

- Stage: `L1` and `L2`. Two documentation edits come with it: the firmware README and one sentence on volume in the AUDIO design.

## Basis

- Requirements and design revision: `origin/integration` at 97a71580 (merge of #173). [Feedback catalogue](https://github.com/DemonicPsychoII/DigitalStethoscope/blob/bcd5b9b/Development/system/design/FEEDBACK/catalogue.md), [decisions of 13 November 2026](https://github.com/DemonicPsychoII/DigitalStethoscope/blob/bcd5b9b/Development/system/planning/mvp-decisions-2026-11-13-delivery-and-filters.md) (decisions 3 and 7).
- Covered cases and requirements: none formally. This PR has no host tests; the three new pure C units (`physicalinterface_indication`, `control_error_policy`, `audio_processing`) are written so they can be tested on the host. Host tests from an earlier state exist on the local branch `backup/controls-and-indication-with-tests`, with the old unit name and without the press light.
- Agreed decisions (Nico, 16 November 2026, in the working thread; not yet recorded in the design):
  - Filters: physical interface only, no switching logic.
  - Volume linear 0–100 % per block, safe value 0 %.
  - `CONTROL_INPUT_FAILURE` from the switch: no position at Start, or no position for 1 s or longer while listening. Medium priority, deferred during listening.
  - All codes get colour and blink code, also those nothing raises yet.
  - Press light and 4 Hz blink for an accepted hold; no blink while listening.

## Risk & rollback

- **What could break:** CONTROL was largely rewritten, so Start, Stop, Wi-Fi setup by hold and the halt after an audio fault all run through new code. A wrong table row would show a wrong colour or let a press through that should be blocked. Volume starts at 0 %, so a failed potentiometer reading means silence, not full volume.
- **How verified:** `local_ci.py run static unit host build` passed on bcd5b9b. Manual test on the board (firmware bcd5b9b, 16 November 2026) by Nico, eight steps: startup, volume, press light, hold in Idle, hold while listening, switch position at Start, deferred error while listening, switch positions. All behaved as implemented. Not covered: blink timing was judged by eye, not measured; most error codes were never raised on the device; no automated test checks the tables.
- **How to revert:** revert the merge commit and flash the previous firmware. No stored data or device settings change.

## Owner decisions

Behaviour I chose where the design is silent or reads differently. Each is in the code as described; please confirm or correct.

<!-- owner-question id=potentiometer-failure -->
1. A failed potentiometer reading raises `CONTROL_INPUT_FAILURE`, which needs a restart.

<!-- owner-question id=cleanup-lockout -->
2. If `WIFI_CLEANUP_FAILURE` (restart) is shown ahead of an error that a short press clears and that blocks Start, the short press cannot reach the second error and Start stays blocked until restart.

<!-- owner-question id=deferral-scope -->
3. Every non-audio error is held back during startup, starting, listening and stopping, not only the four the decision of 13 November names.

<!-- owner-question id=long-press-block -->
4. A non-audio restart error blocks the long press too, not only the short press.

<!-- owner-question id=rejected-input -->
5. A rejected input dims the RGB light to 50 % for 250 ms and leaves the red LED unchanged; the catalogue says red LED off. My suggestion: RGB fully off for 250 ms, which is easier to see.

<!-- owner-question id=group-pause -->
6. The 2 s pause is the dark time between two blink groups, so a group of N blinks repeats every (2N − 1) × 250 ms + 2 s.

<!-- owner-question id=after-acknowledge -->
7. After the 1 s acknowledgement flash the next indication starts, not during it.

<!-- owner-question id=error-over-wifi-status -->
8. In Idle a latched error replaces the Wi-Fi status colours until it is cleared.

<!-- owner-question id=halt-wifi -->
9. After a deferred halt, Wi-Fi background work is released again while the device is halted; after an audio fault it stays stopped. Nothing is delivered in either case.

<!-- owner-question id=press-light-record -->
10. The press light, the 4 Hz blink and the new code `FEEDBACK_BUTTON_HOLD_ACKNOWLEDGED` are described only in the firmware README. The catalogue, P22 and a decision record for 16 November are not updated; say where that belongs.

Left untouched from the review of #173: stale sentences in the AUDIO design ("repeated calls are harmless" for `i2s_stop`, "source reading only"), and the "Proposed; measure under VT-02" comments in `audio.c` and `control.c`.

Opened by Claude-Fable-5.2 on behalf of Nico Friedrich running in T3 Code through Claude Code.

author: albedosehen
body:
## What is the motivation?

The project's rule is that tests return `Result` and use `?`, so a failing fixture reports its error instead of a panic with a backtrace (#300). `antumbra-cli` had 136 `unwrap`/`expect`/`unwrap_err`/`panic!` sites in test code over 200 test functions (199 run, 1 ignored), 52 of which already returned `Result`.

## What does this change do?

- Every `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` in the crate returns `anyhow::Result<()>` and ends in `Ok(())` (146 from `()`, 2 from `Result<(), String>`): `?` on results, `.context(..)` where an `expect` message mattered, `let Some(..) = .. else { bail!(..) }` on an `Option`, `let Err(e) = .. else { bail!(..) }` where an error was expected, `bail!` where a test fake or a let-else arm panicked (`reanchor.rs`'s surface closures, `apply.rs`, `verifiers.rs`, `main.rs`). The helpers that unwrapped return `Result` and their callers use `?`: `main.rs`'s `parsed` (17 call sites), the setup settings' `parsed`, the verifier fixtures (`corpus`, `given`, `propose`, `trust`), `claude/managed.rs`'s `temp`/`write`, `claude/hooks.rs`'s `bundled`, the smoke tests' `cli`/`ok`. The two `#[ignore]`d live tests return `Ok(())` on their early exit. No assertion changed, weakened or removed; test names unchanged.
- Fixtures: the eight hand-built stores (`verifiers.rs`, `verifier_name.rs`, `tests/e2e.rs`) are `antumbra_store::testing::mem_store_of(dim)`, through a dev-dependency on the store's `testing` feature. No `connect_memory` remains in the crate.
- The two-line test-time allow is gone from the crate root (`main.rs`) and from the three integration test files, so the workspace lints now apply to this crate's tests. Nothing compiled without `cfg(test)` changed otherwise.

## What is your testing strategy?

`cargo test -p antumbra-cli`: 4 binaries, 199 tests passing, 1 ignored, before and after. `cargo clippy -p antumbra-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, and again under `--features models` (with `-A clippy::large_enum_variant` for the pre-existing Apple-silicon lint in another crate); `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `grep -rcE "\.unwrap\(\)|\.expect\(|panic!\(" crates/antumbra-cli/{src,tests}` lists nothing. 35 files, 593 insertions, 446 deletions.

## Security Considerations

None; test code only.

## Is this related to any issues?

Closes #300. Builds on #355 (the shared test-support module).

author: hussienalfajer
body:
## Summary
The owner's quick tweaks of 2026-11-16, built and deployed straight from this branch that day (production runs `b17202c`), finished here with tests, docs and the review.

- **USDT transfer set aside:** `POST /api/admin/usdt-transfers/:id/dismiss` with a reason records an unmatched transfer in `usdt_transfer_dismissals` (append-only, migrations 0125–0126) with the audit entry `usdt_transfer.dismissed`; its derived state becomes `dismissed` (below `credited` and `bound`), it leaves the unmatched list, the dashboard count and the daily summary, and an S02 manual deposit or a TXID still credits it (S04 U13a).
- **Removed (owner decisions, ADR 0042):** the per-deposit and 24-hour deposit limits (Sham Cash keeps a one-cent minimum, USDT its network minimum; a technical ceiling `DEPOSIT_MAX_USD_UNITS` keeps amounts safe integers), the `new_account_large` and `velocity` flags, the Telegram approval amount cap, and the owner daily cap (the day is still counted and shown). The retired columns stay unread until a later two-step migration.
- **Panel and store:** the removed fields hidden; the live board and dashboard keep finished orders 24 hours; Telegram usernames shown and accepted with `@`; the pricing matrix shows every live list by default; tier best sellers say «الربح».
- **Review fixes:** a huge USDT amount answered 500 (its pay amount left the safe integers): now `422 DEPOSIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; ADR 0042 records the decisions and the threat model they leave (amends 0006, 0017, 0018, 0019, 0030); the dismiss route in the S04 API table. The Telegram approval stays uncapped, as the owner decided.
- **Tests:** moved to the new rules (no removed coverage without a test of the new behaviour), new API tests for the dismissal (access, 400/404/409, audit, counts, a later credit, racing calls), E2E for the hidden fields, the set-aside dialog (RTL screenshots light and dark) and the matrix default; the merchant queue test pages through the queue instead of depending on the test database's size.

author: guanbear
body:
The U14 receipt-replay scenario can fail on a valid startup cleanup, before it replays the historical receipt. On [main run 43963760587](https://github.com/modelplan/modelplan/actions/runs/43963760587), Linux recorded `historical-receipt-mutated-store`; the same scenario passed on macOS.

The scenario snapshots `consent.json` before restarting the engine. A previous revoke can have durable cleanup pending, and startup legitimately retries it. That retry can change the store without changing the consent generation or original receipt; `docs/cli-consent.md` specifies this behavior. Move the byte snapshot to immediately after initialization and immediately before replay, retaining the byte-for-byte replay assertion. Force a pending cleanup under the reader lock, verify startup clears it without advancing generation, and retain the original receipt and private-row checks.

The failure is a pre-existing timing race in the scenario, not a demonstrated regression from #997, #992 or #966. With the pending cleanup forced, the original scenario failed 3/3 against the pre-#992 `5d07e8d1` binary; startup changed the store and replay did not. The corrected scenario passed 20/20 against that binary and 20/20 against the current-main binary (`6f36aafd`, whose CLI and U14 sources match failing `44b8b4c9`). #992 changes history-import cancellation and coverage, while #997 is merge-gate CI and #966 changes cockpit visuals; none changes this startup-cleanup contract.

author: thatscalaguy
body:
This tightens the edge around identity and config. An admin API without a token no longer starts on a public listener, JWKS outages no longer queue every login behind one fetch, HMAC JWT bindings need a real secret and an audience, and serve refuses config typos. The public ready probe stops showing source names and driver errors.

- Admin API: fail start with an empty admin.token unless admin.listen is loopback only or admin.allowAnonymous is set; limit failed admin logins per client IP (429 after 10).
- JWKS: back off 30s after a failed refresh and serve stale keys meanwhile, cache a failed first fetch, let waiters leave on context end, stop serving stale keys 24h past the cache time, and check the JWK alg against the token alg.
- serve and mcp: refuse unknown server config keys and a --config path that names no file. config validate now checks server keys without --strict too.
- /v1/ready: body has only status, version and healthy/total counts. Detail stays on /admin/datasources.
- HMAC JWT: refuse secrets under 32 bytes at start and reload, require issuer and audience on every jwksUrl or hmacSecretRef binding, and refuse tokens for a binding without audience.

Breaking: admin without token off loopback, audience required on HMAC bindings, 32-byte HMAC secrets. Behavior changes: unknown config keys and missing config file stop the start, /v1/ready body, stale JWKS keys expire after 24h.

author: malard
body:
**TL;DR:** Improvement. The language an RDS broadcaster names is parsed once, where it arrives, and held as a `CLanguageTag`, so `RDS.AudioLanguage` reports a BCP 47 tag (`en`) where it reported the table's ISO 639-2 code (`eng`).

## Description
- `KODI::RDS::Language(index)` gives the language an EBU Tech 3244 Annex J slow labelling index names, as a `CLanguageTag`, and `und` where the standard reserves the index or it is past the table. `LanguageCode(index)` stays as the table itself.
- `CDVDRadioRDSData::DecodeSlowLabelingCodes` stores that tag. A reserved index is logged and not stored, as an index outside the table already was.
- `CPVRRadioRDSInfoTag` holds the language as a `CLanguageTag`. `GetLanguage()` returns it by value: the reference it returned named a member guarded by a lock the caller no longer held.
- `RDS.AudioLanguage` serves `ToString()`. Its Doxygen, and that of `RDS.ChannelCountry` (a `CTerritory` since #29565, which went in without a note), say what each now reports.
- `TestRadioRDSLanguages` checks every assigned index parses to a language, reserved ones to `und`, and pins cells against the standard, including the withdrawn `scc` and `mol` and the ISO 639-3 only Rusyn and Dari.

## Motivation and context
One of a series of independent PRs cut from the headline branch, malard/xbmc#184, holding each language Kodi reads as a `CLanguageTag` parsed where it enters. Follows #29763, which put the RDS language table where a test can read it.

## How has this been tested?
`TestRadioRDSLanguages`. Full gtest suite passes (Windows x64), and the changed files compile for 32-bit x86 with clang. The suite was run with `TestJSONServiceDescription.cpp`'s `StubMethod` changed locally to the two-argument handler signature: upstream's `kodi-test` does not compile at this base, since #30531 and #30558 crossed. That change is not part of this PR.

## What is the effect on users?
- Skins: `RDS.AudioLanguage` gives a BCP 47 language tag, `en`, `de`, `fr`, where it gave the three letter code in the RDS table, `eng`, `ger`, `fre`.
- `RDS.ChannelCountry` is unchanged; only its documentation is updated.

author: kostya-epifanov
body:
## What this change is for
Tracker: BASE-407

The disk filled on 2026-11-16 because merged worktrees were never removed. Many of them were merged into an integration branch rather than into develop/master/main, so detect_candidates.sh does not see them as merged. Make the detector also count a worktree as merged when its head is an ancestor of any origin/integration/* branch, and name that branch in the merged_into field. The integration branch stays on origin, so a dropped integration can still be checked out again.

Acceptance criteria:

```sh
bash -n skills/prune-worktrees/scripts/detect_candidates.sh
grep -q 'integration/' skills/prune-worktrees/scripts/detect_candidates.sh
grep -q 'integration' skills/prune-worktrees/SKILL.md
test -f tests/cases/prune_integration_merged.sh
bash tests/cases/prune_integration_merged.sh
bash tests/cases/prune_candidates_artifacts.sh
bash scripts/verify.sh
```

## Decisions made
No grill conversation ran (unattended). Judgement calls made in the plan: integration branches are named in `merged_into` only when no develop/master/main matched (every older head is an ancestor of every later integration cut from the base, so listing them all would grow the field without bound); a lane's own pushed `integration/<x>` branch never counts as merged into itself (its PR is still open).

## Risk
<!-- gantry:risk sha256=c114ee5371aa -->
Risk level: low
Blast radius:
- Breaks if wrong: `/gantry:prune-worktrees` and `/gantry:sync` offer a worktree for removal that is not merged anywhere durable; the archive step still saves its chain artifacts.
- Live after merge: yes — runs whenever a user or the homebase routine invokes prune or sync.
- Rollback: revert the commit; no data or remote state is changed by the detector.

## Deliberately not done
<!-- gantry:handover sha256=20807add92ad -->
- Integration-only merges are not marked provisional, and a stale `origin/integration/*` ref after `FETCH:failed` can still make a lane a candidate. Deferred because counting integration merges is the task's intent and changing how the report treats them goes beyond the contract. Next action: when the fetch failed, mark or demote integration-only rows, say so in SKILL.md step 2, and add a case to the new test.

## Exercised by this run
<!-- gantry:qa sha256=bf18e525bb79 -->
The repo has no `.claude/agents/qa.md`, so `/gantry:qa` found nothing to drive and no scenarios were run.

## Not proven by this run
The task declared no human-only checks and no e2e scenarios. This change edits the plugin's own skills (`skills/`), which the harness loads from the installed plugin: the run executed gantry 0.8.0 (commit b013392c119a) from the plugin cache, not the edited copies. The new test and `scripts/verify.sh` exercised the edited detector script from the worktree (gate exit 0).

Draft means unwatched, not unverified: the gate ran green and an independent headless review (`/code-review`, tier high) ran, but nobody watched the run live.

body:
Questions table and routes for activity 6b.

- `Consultas` table: encrypted with the stack key, TTL 7 days, owner stored as a SHA-256 hash of the subject.
- `POST /consultas`: validates the question (1..1000 characters), stores `en_curso`, starts the agent asynchronously, answers 202.
- `GET /consultas/{id}`: returns the answer to its owner only; another subject gets the same 404 as a missing id.
- Both routes require the scope `legacybridge/consultas` at the JWT authorizer.
- The agent's entry point is now `consultas.worker`: it stores the answer; any failure stores only `error`, with no trace or detail.
- Known limit: if the agent's reserved concurrency (2) throttles an asynchronous start after the write, Lambda may retry or drop it, and the question stays `en_curso` until its TTL. Recorded for the review of activity 6b.

Tests: 357 offline pass. **No deploy in this PR.**

author: rowan-hyeho-song
body:
## 무엇을 왜
#599: 타임랩스 밤에 로봇들이 '자리에 고정'으로 보였다. 원인은 밤 규칙(12.1)대로 책상에서 조는 장면인데, 등을 보인 몸에 '자는 중' 단서가 없고, 몸이 일하지 않는 점(대부분 '역할 분담 이전' 줄)이 밤새 3초씩 수십 걸음 이어졌기 때문이다. 사용자 결정 (가)+(나), timelapse.md 13절(#631 · #636 걸음 단위)대로 고친다.

## 바뀐 것
- **13.1 밤 표시(재생 상태로만)**: 타임랩스에서도 `조는 중` · `야간 당번` 꼬리표를 그린다(`replayTag`). 소파에 누운 몸(12.4 '잠')도 z z + `조는 중`. 일하는 몸 꼬리표는 지금처럼 끈다. ×16 · 움직임 줄이기에서는 떠오르는 z를 끄고 꼬리표의 z z 아이콘이 남는다(`zRises`). 책상 스탠드 · 모니터는 이미 재생 상태를 따르고 있었다.
- **13.2 빈 밤 걸음**: 점 시각이 KST 23–09이고 재생 상태에 일하는 몸이 없는 걸음(`emptyNightAt`; 회의록 · 배포 점은 사무실 전체 사건이라 제외). ×1 · ×4여도 ×16으로 걷는다.
  - **밤 줄기**(#641 판정): 첫 빈 밤 걸음부터 일하는 첫 걸음(또는 09시) 앞까지를 한 줄기로 묶는다. 그 안의 회의록 · 배포는 고른 배속으로 걷되 줄기를 끊지 않고 칩도 그대로다. 빈 밤 걸음이 4개 미만인 줄기는 넘기지 않는다(×16도 칩도 없음). 이 밤만 끄기 · aria-live도 줄기 단위다(`nightKinds` · `nightRuns`).
  - 상태에 `rate`(시계가 실제로 도는 배속) · `night`('fast' | 'slow' | null)를 더했다. 배속 버튼은 고른 `speed`에 머물고, 재생을 움직이는 곳(무대 · 걷기 규칙 · 자막 · 소리 · 둘러보기 · 회의록)은 `rate`를 읽는다.
  - 칩 `🌙 밤 · 빨리 넘기는 중`이 '▶ 기록 재생 중' 자리에 들어간다(좁은 화면은 날짜 아래). 누르면 이 밤만 고른 배속(`🌙 밤 · ×1로 보는 중`), `aria-label="밤 빨리 넘기기 끄기, 이 밤만"`. 0.2초 페이드(움직임 줄이기면 바로).
  - aria-live로 "밤, 누가 일을 시작할 때까지 빨리 넘깁니다"를 한 번 알린다. `남은 m:ss`는 빈 밤 걸음을 ×16으로 센다.
- **13.3 그날 열기**: 벽시계 · HUD · 목록 `▶ 이 날 보기` · 날 바꾸기는 앞쪽 빈 밤 걸음을 건너뛰고 일하는 첫 걸음 바로 앞(모두 조는 장면)에서, 고른 배속 · 칩 없이 시작한다(`openingIndex`). 공유 링크 · 이슈 재생은 그대로다.
- 🌙 때문에 글꼴 서브셋을 다시 만들었다(`fonts.css`).

## 확인한 것
- `vitest run` 전체 2730 통과, `tsc -b` 통과.
- 새 `night.test.ts`: 걸음 종류(빈 밤 · 사건 · 낮), 줄기(사건이 끊지 않음 · 4걸음 미만 없음), 여는 자리, 줄기 동안 칩 유지 · 회의록은 고른 배속, ×4 · ×16, 끄기는 줄기 끝까지, 멈춤, 남은 시간 셈.
- 걸음마다 칩 상태(브라우저): 11.16 00:16–05:39 한 줄기, 그 안 회의록 넷은 고른 배속 · 칩 유지 / 11.10 07:00–08:05 칩 없음.
- `dayStore.test.ts`: 11.06을 '▶ 이 날 보기'로 열면 빈 밤 12걸음 뒤(11번)에서 열린다.
- 브라우저(로컬 데이터):
  - 11.10 05:28 링크: 조는 넷에 꼬리표가 붙고, 일하는 휴에는 붙지 않는다.
  - 11.16 02:27: rate 16 · 칩, 누르면 rate 1 · 'slow', ×16을 고르면 칩이 없다. 데스크톱 · 600px 모두.

## 스크린샷
| 11.10 05:28 링크(꼬리표) | 11.16 02:27 빈 밤 ×16 |
|---|---|
| ![599-tags-1110-0528](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets-2/640-599-tags-1110-0528-20261117-072409.png) | ![599-night-fast](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets-2/640-599-night-fast-20261117-072409.png) |
| 칩을 누른 뒤(이 밤만 ×1) | 좁은 화면(600px) |
| ![599-night-slow](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets-2/640-599-night-slow-20261117-072409.png) | ![599-night-fast-narrow](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets-2/640-599-night-fast-narrow-20261117-072409.png) |

칩 캡처 셋은 `?debug=1`로 연 화면이라 길 이름표가 함께 보입니다.

## 위험·되돌리기
- `speed`를 읽던 재생 쪽이 `rate`를 읽는다. 빈 밤 밖에서는 둘이 같아 동작이 같다.
- 그날 여는 자리가 0번이 아닐 수 있다(빈 밤으로 시작하는 날). 막대 · ◀로 돌아갈 수 있다.
- 되돌리기: 이 PR revert.

## 체크
- [x] 테스트 · 타입 검사
- [ ] 디자이너 판정(13.4: 11.10 05:28 링크, 11.16 기본 진입)

## AI 작성
코더 세션(Claude Code)이 작성했습니다.

author: cerredz
body:
## Why

The SDK's two managed-gateway defaults point at the Render host `https://vidbyte-backend.onrender.com`. That host is suspended and no longer serves. The Vidbyte backend is moving to Vercel, served at the founder's own domain `https://api.vidbyte.pro`, and the founder is adding the DNS record for it now. Until a release points at the new host, every JevAgent managed decision call (`/api/v1/models/typesafe/...`) and every Vidbyte-managed text call (`/api/v1/models/generate`) fails for every user of the released package.

This PR moves both defaults to `https://api.vidbyte.pro` with each path kept exactly as it was. The longer-term point is that a released client should depend on a Vidbyte-owned domain, never on a hosting provider's, so the next move between hosts needs only a DNS change.

## Merge blocker: the vendored platform contract must say `api.vidbyte.pro` is `live`

This PR is **not mergeable yet, on purpose**. Lint rule C018 (canonical-api-host, blocking) and `tests/test_jev_managed_gateway.py::test_managed_endpoint_origin_is_a_live_platform_host` both require the gateway origin to be listed as `live` in `lint/contracts/vidbyte-platform-contract.json`. That file is a byte-for-byte copy of the contract generated by cerredz/Vidbyte. It currently lists `https://vidbyte-backend.onrender.com` as `live` and `https://api.vidbyte.pro` as `planned`. Both checks are working as designed: they exist to stop a release that points at a host that does not serve (`api.vidbyte.pro` still returned NXDOMAIN from 8.8.8.8 when this PR was opened).

This PR deliberately does not hand-edit the vendored contract or raise the C018 baseline, because the repo forbids both (`lint/contracts/README.md`, C018's own "will not work" list). The order to clear it:

1. The founder adds the DNS record, and `api.vidbyte.pro` serves the backend (`nslookup api.vidbyte.pro` resolves and `GET https://api.vidbyte.pro/health` returns 200).
2. In cerredz/Vidbyte, flip `https://api.vidbyte.pro` to `"live"` in `lint/core/platform_contract/identity.py` (`PUBLIC_API_HOSTS`), regenerate with `scripts/generate-platform-contract.py`, and merge. That file's own notes say to do exactly this once DNS serves, and not before. Whether the Render entry is removed there at the same time is that repo's call. Removing it would make C018 here block any future `*.onrender.com` literal as an unlisted host.
3. In this branch, re-vendor `lint/contracts/vidbyte-platform-contract.json` byte for byte from that commit and update the Provenance row in `lint/contracts/README.md`, as `lint/contracts/README.md` "Refreshing" describes. C018 and the contract test then pass with no further code change.

I checked that step 3 is the only thing missing: with a scratch copy of the contract that only flips `api.vidbyte.pro` to `live` (never committed), the full source gate is green. See Verification.

## Files changed

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `vidbyte/lib/constants/jev.py` | `VIDBYTE_JEV_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT` becomes `https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/typesafe`, and `VIDBYTE_GENERATIVE_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT` becomes `https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/generate`. Their comments are updated to match. | These are the two code defaults. The Jev routes (`/systemone`, `/models`) and the run-close route (`/api/v1/models/runs/{run_id}/close`) are built from the first constant, so they follow it. |
| `tests/test_jev_managed_gateway.py` | **Updated test pins**: the managed endpoint assertion and the `systemone` and `models` URL assertions now expect the new host. The rejected-custom-endpoint case `.../other` now uses the new host. | These tests pin the default URL as literals on purpose, so a changed constant gets caught. |
| `tests/features/sdk_managed_text/managed_text_fixtures.py` | **Updated test pin**: `GATEWAY_URL` oracle. | It is the literal oracle for the generative route. |
| `tests/features/agent_reasoning_effort/agent_reasoning_effort_fixtures.py` | **Updated test pin**: `GATEWAY_URL`. | The wire recorder routes gateway requests by this URL. |
| `tests/features/sdk_managed_text/FEATURE.md` | The contract line now names the new host. | It is a user-facing statement of the wire contract. |

There is no environment-variable override for the gateway host. The managed endpoint is pinned on purpose (`@intent managed-key-stays-on-vidbyte-host`), and managed mode still rejects any caller-supplied endpoint, the new host included. Only the URL constant changes, so the "is this the managed gateway" check (`DecisionModelConfig.resolved_endpoint`) matches the new host automatically.

These still mention the Render host and are left unchanged on purpose:
- `lint/contracts/vidbyte-platform-contract.json` and `lint/core/platform_contract.py` (`RENDER_SUFFIX`, which classifies `*.onrender.com` literals as Vidbyte API hosts so C018 checks them). The contract is a vendored copy and changes only by re-vendoring (see above).
- Files under `docs/design/` and `docs/spec/`. These are dated records of past decisions, and AGENTS.md treats `docs/` as opaque.

## Verification

Plain `PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/run_ci.py` on the committed state stops at lint, failing on C018 alone, as expected.

Head commit: `6cb795856d83e431b1075901396f9c1a6c518989`. All runs were local on Windows, Python 3.11, in a worktree venv (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`), offline, with no API or model calls.

Printed values (`from vidbyte.lib.constants.jev import ...`; `DecisionModelConfig.vidbyte_managed()`):
```
VIDBYTE_JEV_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT        https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/typesafe
VIDBYTE_GENERATIVE_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/generate
resolved_endpoint()                 https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/typesafe
resolved_run_close_url("jev:abc")   https://api.vidbyte.pro/api/v1/models/runs/jev:abc/close
```

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `python lint/run.py` | FAIL, and only on the expected C018 blocker: 2 findings (the two constants, origin `planned`). Every other rule is CLEAN, RATCHETED, or IMPROVED, which is drift already on main. C017 (route contract) is CLEAN, so both paths still match contract routes. |
| `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest` (whole suite, with the one contract test deselected) | 8443 passed, 193 skipped, 1 deselected |
| `pytest tests/test_jev_managed_gateway.py::...::test_managed_endpoint_origin_is_a_live_platform_host` | FAIL as expected: `'https://api.vidbyte.pro' not found in {'https://vidbyte-backend.onrender.com'}` |
| Scratch contract with only `api.vidbyte.pro` set to `live`, then `PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/run_ci.py --stage source` (lint, compileall, the three check scripts, and the full pytest) | PASS (`CI passed.`): C018 CLEAN, `SDK-LINT: PASS`, pytest 8444 passed, 193 skipped. The scratch edit was then reverted, so the contract in this PR is untouched. |
| `python scripts/run_ci.py --stage package` (no PYTHONPATH) | PASS: build, twine check, wheel inspection, and a clean-venv install smoke (`Installed vidbyte-sdk 0.4.2 passed smoke checks.`) |

CI, dispatched by hand on `6cb795856d83e431b1075901396f9c1a6c518989` and read through the check-runs API: `Static policy` passed ([run 43969355839](https://github.com/cerredz/Vidbyte-SDK/actions/runs/43969355839)). `Source / Python 3.11` and `Source / Python 3.12` failed, both at lint with `C018 REGRESSED: 2 finding(s), allowance 0`, which is the expected blocker described above. `Package` was skipped because it depends on Source ([run 43969351880](https://github.com/cerredz/Vidbyte-SDK/actions/runs/43969351880)). After the re-vendor commit, dispatch `ci.yml` again on the new head.

## Release

This reaches users only after a PyPI release of `vidbyte-sdk`, which the founder approves. Release it only after steps 1 to 3 above, so the released default points at a host that serves.

author: dxvsi
body:
Test support for the TRYX HOLO 360 (`391a:1051`, issue #42). Nobody with a HOLO has run it yet, so this stays a draft until a hardware report.

The HOLO uses the same printer-class transport, bootstrap, keepalive and commands as the Panorama SE, with one 640x480 area. This PR treats it as a Panorama-family display and fills in what differs:

- **Media:** image, GIF and video are prepared in the official container (TRYX media header + H.264) at 640x480: a still is one frame at 30 fps, GIF and video 60 fps, the same encoder settings as the Turris 620 path. Conversion identities, naming and the product checks in `printermediaidentity.cpp` now come from the product profile instead of Turris product-id checks; Turris strings and output are unchanged (tests).
- **Apply:** full-screen single media with Single, Loop and Shuffle; brightness and backlight. Apply stays read-modify-write of the device's user configuration. `light_config` (field 6) is now in wire-v1 and is written back unchanged; there are no light controls.
- **Overlay:** metrics and hardware badges with the HOLO geometry (640x480, one area). No overlay lease.
- **Presets:** the profile lists the HOLO's 21 on-device presets (`default_01`..`default_21.mp4.h264_640x480`). Panorama keeps its 6; Turris now has none (a Turris preset used to resolve to a 2240x1080 Panorama file name).
- **Off:** split screen, mirror (hidden in the GUI), waterfall, custom badge text, media pull with Edit/Export/Replace, firmware validation and flashing, and any automatic configuration write on connect.
- **Allow-lists:** 1051 added wherever the other Panorama ids are, except the replace journal (needs media pull).
- README and the Flatpak README describe this as test support, not tested on hardware.

Tests: profile capabilities, conversion identities in every consumer, media preparation for each kind (header fields, 640x480, frame counts, fps), overlay geometry for one to three metrics, Apply and brightness preserving `light_config`, GUI media target and hidden orientation controls. The new protocol tests failed against the read-only profile. `dbus-run-session -- make package-check`: exit 0, 1941 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped.

Only hardware can confirm: that the device accepts and lists `.h264_640x480` uploads, 60 fps video/GIF and one-frame stills; that the overlay renders and keeps updating without a lease; the overlay geometry; that writing `light_config` back as read is safe; and the preset names.

author: edumansky
body:
Agents and users are now warned that updating a Contact Center configuration object replaces the whole object.

Updating a site, team, queue, user or other configuration object clears every field that is left out of the body. An agent that sends only the field it wants to change wipes the rest. Until now, neither the `webex_write` tool, the CC skill nor the docs said this.

## Changes

- `cmd/mcp/dispatcher.go`: the `webex_write` description says to get the object first and send it back whole with the changes.
- `skill/cc/SKILL.md` and `site/src/content/docs/cc.mdx` say the same under the create/update/delete examples.
- All three name `cc ai-agent update` as the exception, because it keeps fields that are left out.

The warning covers configuration objects only. `cc tasks update` sends PATCH to a live task, so it is not included.

This is the `webex_write` warning from #20, made on `main` alone.

## Basis

Tested live on a test tenant for 20 types. For each one, the test:
- created a `zz-` object with a `description`;
- sent `update` with the object's own body minus `description`;
- read it back;
- deleted the object and confirmed it was gone.

Every type cleared `description`, so every type replaces the object:

address book, auxiliary code, business hours, contact service queue, desktop layout, desktop profile, dial plan, entry point, global variable, holiday list, multimedia profile, outdial ANI, overrides, resource collection, site, skill, skill profile, team, user profile, work type.

Not tested:
- `users`: users can't be created, and the tenant has no test Contact Center user.
- `auto-csat` and `generated-summaries`: no create route.
- `organization-setting` and `tenant-configuration`: org-wide singletons.
- `contact-number`: has no optional field to leave out.
- `asset`, `channel` and `call-monitoring`: need a digital channel, or real people being monitored.
- `audio-files`: the update takes a file upload.

Webex Admin Studio's AGENTS.md records the same finding.

## Checks

- `go vet ./cmd/...` and `go test -p 1 ./cmd/... ./skill/` pass.
- `make codegen` keeps the new skill note.
- The docs site builds with `npm run build`.

The change is text only, so there's no new test.

author: vlad-ko
body:
## What and why

Players reviewing the game (asked for at the 2026-11-16 demo) need to say "this question was unclear" from inside a level. Every level now has a Feedback button in its header. It opens a small dialog: a kind (unclear question, wrong or outdated fact, bug, idea) and up to 1000 characters of text; the level and screen are attached automatically. The game's server (`POST /api/feedback`) turns each one into a GitHub issue labeled `feedback`, titled `Feedback: <level name> (<level id>)`. The browser never talks to GitHub, so the CSP is unchanged.

It is off until the owner sets `FEEDBACK_GITHUB_TOKEN` (a fine-grained token, one repo, Issues read and write) and `FEEDBACK_REPO` in Vercel: while off the button is hidden and the endpoint refuses without reading the body. Steps are in the README; the contract is docs/FOUNDATION.md §2.11.

The repo is public, so these issues are public. The form says so. The server neutralizes the text: it is fenced so links, images and `#123` never render, every `@` is broken so nobody gets pinged, control and bidi characters are stripped, and the title holds no player text. It sends and logs no IP, user agent, cookie or email; a signed-in player's nickname appears only if they chose to be listed on the leaderboard. Limits: same-origin check, JSON only, 8 KB cap, 5 per 10 minutes per IP and 30 per minute per instance, a 6 second budget for the GitHub call. In debug mode the button works but sends nothing. `FEEDBACK_STUB=1 npm run dev` prints the issue instead of calling GitHub.

Closes #370

## How it was tested

New test/feedback.test.mjs (config, GET, off, origin, size and type, parsing, issue body cleaning, end-to-end with a fake GitHub, nickname rules, limiter, upstream failures and timeout), a FEEDBACK_STUB test in test/serve.test.mjs, test/feedback-dialog.test.mjs (button visibility, the exact POST body, one request per send, empty text, debug, Escape scope, inert overlay, maxlength) and a ctx.screen test. Each was mutation-checked; one weak limiter test was found that way and fixed.

Existing tests changed on purpose: test/modal.test.mjs (the modal list now includes feedback-modal), test/game.test.mjs (the overlay inert expression, and the status calls at start now include GET /api/feedback), test/account-app.test.mjs (its fake fetch answers /api/feedback so its call list stays about the account).

## Not verifiable here

Real GitHub: nothing was sent to api.github.com. Unverified: that a fine-grained Issues token can set the label on create (the label already exists), and that a broken `@` inside a code fence never notifies. The dialog in a real browser is part of the review.

author: yarikama
body:
## What
The empty space beside the home page's "Technical Writings" heading now holds a small risograph print. It is twelve rounded squares in two inks, a sage and a mustard, screened into halftone dots with a little grain, with the second ink landing a touch off register.

When it comes into view it prints once: the first ink goes down, then the second slides in and lands. With reduced motion it is simply there.

## Why
The heading sat beside a large empty space. This was picked from eight riso studies as the quietest one that still fills that space.

## Changes
- **`risoPrint.ts`:** the print's geometry and halftone screening as pure functions, with no DOM:
  - the 12 squares, their ink and how much ink each takes;
  - the two screen angles and the register offset;
  - a seeded random, so the grain is the same every time the print is drawn.
- **`RisoGrid.tsx`:**
  - Builds one plate per ink on a canvas and prints when the grid comes into view.
  - Rebuilds the plates when the box resizes, and repaints in the other cut of each ink when the theme flips.
  - On paper the inks multiply. On the dark page they screen, using a lighter cut.
  - `aria-hidden`, with no pointer events.
- **`index.css`:** `--color-riso-a` and `--color-riso-b`, with a paper value and a dark-page value for each.
- **`LabNotes.tsx`:** the heading becomes two columns, text and print. On a phone the print sits under the text, no wider than 24rem.

## Test plan
- [x] `risoPrint.test.ts` checks that:
  - the squares stay on the sheet, the register offset included;
  - the inks alternate like a chequerboard, six squares each;
  - more coverage gives bigger dots, and no ink gives no dots;
  - the grain is the same every time.
- [x] `npm test` (776 passed), `npm run lint` and `tsc` are clean.
- [x] Checked on the local site in dark, light and at 390px wide. It prints on scroll, and there is no sideways scroll.

author: deanphillipsokc
body:
Wave 0 of the v3 plan (#165): the fixed measure every v3 spike is judged by, and the v2 baseline on it. Experiment code only: no lesson tool, the skill, or the site changed. The write-up is `docs/spikes/v3-yardstick.md`.

## What's built (`spike/experiments/bench/`)

- **Frozen bench** (`bench.py`). `freeze` copies a sealed run's steps 0 and 1 (photo, canvas fit, beginner version, reference, finish, and their notes and finish issues), byte for byte, with a sha256 manifest and the source run, version and commit. `build` makes a lesson folder for an experiment, ready from the skill's step 2. Two builds give the same bytes on any machine (LF JSON, POSIX paths, a per-directory `.gitattributes`, CRLF-tolerant hashing, pinned hashes), which `test_bench.FrozenBenchTests` checks on all 8 pictures every run. Builds go to the git-ignored `spike/experiments/bench/runs/`, outside `output/`, so `publish` keeps them out of `site/history/`. All 8 pictures are frozen from the baseline runs below (70 MB, plain git, not LFS). Step 5's background render and everything from step 2 on still vary per run.
- **Blind A/B page** (`ab_page.py`, `ab_screenshot.js`). One phone-first HTML page, in single or pair mode:
  - The page holds only opaque lesson tokens. The token-to-folder map and the seed are in the answer key beside the page, never in it. Pair sides are balanced and drawn from the seed, and the picture order can be shuffled with a seed.
  - The rubric is (a)–(c) at 1 to 5, plus would-paint or prefer, a worst-step toggle on each step, and notes.
  - All saving goes through `saveScores()`: localStorage, plus one artifact database record per device (`<round>__<device>`). A Copy scores button is always shown. The importer merges the devices' records item by item and joins the tokens to folders through the key.
  - An importer saves the scores to `bench/scores/<round>.json`.
  - The baseline page is published as an artifact whose `saveScores` also writes to the artifact's database.
- **Fault counter** (`fault_counter.md`, `packet.py`, `agreement.py`, which has a counter-vs-counter `--compare` mode and takes the mean of two counters with `--name A --name B`).
  - The brief defines classes A–H with real examples from the issue history.
  - Packets hold only what a painter gets. They go to a temp folder outside the repo, with the brief beside them. The brief's examples are made up for pictures off the bench.
  - `agreement.py` checks each `faults.json` against the format, and compares counts with the owner's scores (Spearman by class group, worst-step agreement). It says "not scored yet" until the owner has scored.
- **Run trace** (`run_trace.py`). It finds the transcript (subagents included) by the lesson folder's name and reports wall time per skill step, split into Claude, tools and renders. Render time is checked against the ledger.
- **Tests:** `spike/tests/test_bench*.py`.

## Baseline: v2 at POC 1.12.1 (bb39e54), one hands-off run per picture

`highland-cow_skill_20261116-205600` is kept out of the baseline because its prompt steered the element choice. The write-up keeps it as a first look at run-to-run difference.

### Trace (minutes)

| chickadee | 21.0 | 10.0 | 9.7 | 1.4 | 94 | 7, check and review (4.2) |

| all 8 | 240/101, 273/107 | 95/37, 79/27 | 16/16, 18/16 | 31/31, 31/31 | 44/40, 48/43 | 34/17, 29/13 | 0 | 1/1, 0 | 461/243, 478/237 | 822, 865 | 19 |

Each counter found about 240 distinct faults where the runs' own same-session reviews left 19. These replace the first counts (one counter, first brief), which are superseded because that brief drew examples from the bench pictures' own past faults; they're kept as `faults-v1.json`. These are the counters' findings: they haven't been checked against the owner yet.

**Repeatability** (`agreement.py --compare faults-a.json faults-b.json`):
- Distinct totals differ by 0 to 29% per picture (mean 14%), and weighted counts by 8 to 40%.
- The top-3 worst steps share 18 of 24.
- The steps flagged with a major or blocker fault overlap with a mean Jaccard index of 0.79 (0.47 to 0.93) over every step a fault shows in, or 0.69 (0.54 to 0.90) over only the step where it first shows.
- The two counters rank the lessons almost the same (Spearman 0.95 on weighted faults per step).
- So for screening, a per-picture change smaller than about the A-B spread isn't a signal from the counter alone: count each lesson twice and use the mean of the two counters.

Implement the bounded native measurement-interop slice for the settings benchmark, without editing its source, labelled generated stand-in or hand-written reference.

- Keep ordinary SwiftUI behavior in the explicit iOS branch: real `.accessibilityLabel`, no invented SwiftUI testTag/remember shim. Compose emits direct testTag/semantics on Switch and `remember(model, row.id)` for the merged typed item action. ArkUI emits direct Toggle `.id` and `.accessibilityText`; unsupported retention is a source-located diagnostic.

- Add `interop-native-measurement` as a ready dual-backend fixture, add it to the actual Kotlin compilation manifest, and assert the exact measurement and callback contract.

- Document the source form, platform boundaries and the distinction between source/compile verification and benchmark evidence in `docs/interop.md` and `docs/lessons/interop.md`.

This PR covers the bounded typed interop and compilation evidence. #120 still owns actual benchmark integration and complete paired macro JSON on a stable named target; no macro, emulator/device performance or ArkTS/iOS native compilation is claimed.

- Swift 6.4.2 on Linux: `swift build` passed after merging latest `origin/main` (`36d6524`).

author: pigfox
body:
## Summary

Adds **RFC 0003: Toolchain compatibility and versioning** (status: Draft), answering what happens to GoPatina when Go and Rust release new versions.

**Go side**
- Default mode delegates to the installed `go` tool, so a new Go release works there on day one.
- Patina modes parse with `go/parser` and `go/types` and respect the `go` directive in `go.mod`.
- Support policy mirrors Go's: the two latest releases (stable and oldstable).
- A feature patina mode does not support yet fails with a message naming the feature and the Go version that introduced it, never a silent miscompile.
- New **`docs/compat.md`**: the Go language feature matrix with each feature's patina status (everything is "planned", "open" or "excluded" today, and the page says nothing is supported yet).

**Rust side**
- Stable Rust only: no nightly features, no rustc internals (one more reason MIR lowering was set aside).
- Declared edition (2024) and MSRV; `-emit-rust` writes `rust-toolchain.toml` and `Cargo.lock` so an emitted crate keeps building the same way.
- Rust's stability promise and opt-in editions are what make this safe.
- Runtime crates (Tokio, per RFC 0002) pinned, updated through Dependabot pull requests that must pass the full suite and benchmarks.

**Versioning**: semver; each release states its supported Go and Rust ranges (stable, MSRV, edition) in the release notes and a README table; a release within 4 weeks of each Go February/August release; a scheduled CI run and benchmark rerun for each Rust stable.

**Detection**: golden tests, compile-and-run tests, and canaries on Go tip and Rust beta/nightly that open an issue automatically on a scheduled failure. The workflow arrives in the next pull request; the RFC says plainly that its Rust jobs are placeholders until generated code exists.

The README gets a "Supported toolchains" section with the current (Phase 0) state.

## Type of change

- [ ] `feat`: new feature
- [ ] `fix`: bug fix
- [x] `docs`: documentation or RFC
- [ ] `test`: tests only
- [ ] `ci` / `build` / `chore`: tooling and maintenance
- [ ] Breaking change

## How was this tested?

Documentation only. Checked internal links and anchors, and the Go versions given for each feature in `docs/compat.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] The title follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Every commit is signed off.
- [x] `gofmt -l .` prints nothing, and `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass.
- [x] Unit-test coverage is still 100.0%.
- [ ] Benchmarks (not applicable: no code generation yet).
- [x] Documentation and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.
- [x] Language or semantics changes reference an accepted RFC (this is the RFC).

## apps/notifier (Rust)
- One binary for the macOS menu bar and Windows tray (`tray-icon`, `tao`, `notify-rust`, `ureq`). Menu: what FairMind checks on this laptop, check for messages now, quit.
- Reads `notifier.json` installed by device management (FairMind's address and the notifier secret). On first run it enrols with the laptop's serial number and keeps its own key in the person's config folder (mode 600).

- `POST /shadow-ai/agent/notifier-secret`: separate from osquery's enrol secret (which stays root-only), shown once with a ready `notifier.json`.

- Messages are events with a message for the person (from 5b rules), on the agent with the same serial number, for that person on a shared laptop; a notifier can acknowledge only its own laptop's messages.

author: vitbokisch
body:
## Not verified

- **No device run.** Everything below is compile and typecheck (`validateSwiftWithStubs`, `validateKotlin`) plus one executed Swift program. Nothing ran on a simulator or emulator.
- **The Kotlin decode was not executed.** The headless kotlinc run does not load the kotlinx-serialization plugin. The Kotlin side is proven by compiling and by asserting `@Serializable`, not by a decode round-trip.
- **The new Swift warning on the leftover labelled-tuple fallback has no test.** After this change, no source I could write still reaches that fallback, so the warning is a backstop with no regression test.

## What changed

Follow-up to #4507, which covered inline object types inside components. This PR covers the positions outside every component. There, Swift spelled a multi-field shape as a labelled tuple with no warning; the tuple is not `Codable`, so a decode into it fails, and a tuple annotation over a struct literal does not typecheck. Kotlin spelled it `Any`.

A new parse-time pass, `module-inline-object-types.ts`, lifts every module-scope inline object type into one declared struct named after its binding. Both targets use that name:

| Site | Swift / Kotlin before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `const`/`let x: {…} = {…}` (one or several fields) | `__ObjN` with the annotation dropped | `XType` |
| `const x: {…} = JSON.parse(raw)` | `= ""` on both, **no warning** | decodes into `XType` |
| `JSON.parse(raw) as {…}` | tuple `.self` / `parse<Any>` | `XType` |
| `signal<{ok}>` | `Any` + warning, both targets | `FlagType` |
| `signal<{x;y}>`, `signal<{…}\|null>`, `signal<{…}[]>`, `signal({x,y})` | tuple, **no warning** / `Any` | `PtType`, … |
| `Readonly<{…}>`, `{…}[]`, `Array<{…}>`, nested objects | tuple / `List<Any>` | `PtType`, `RowsType`, `PtTypeA` |
| helper parameter (`function` and arrow-const) | `__ObjN` taken from the call site | `FmtPType` |
| helper return type | tuple / Kotlin warning | `MkResult` |
| helper-body local, helper `JSON.parse as` | `[Any]` / `Any` | `CountXsType`, `HostVType` |
| module `computed` returning an object literal | `Any` on both | the literal's struct (Swift); inferred getter (Kotlin) |

How names are chosen:

- A name that is already taken gets a numeric suffix (`ConfigType2`).
- A shape the file already declares is reused (`{x;y}` becomes the declared `Point`).
- Two bindings with the same shape share one struct.
- A fractional initializer still widens a field to `Double`.

A JSX-returning arrow is left alone. That is a component or view helper, and its inline object parameter is what `render-slots.ts` uses to classify it.

Also:

- `const x: T = JSON.parse(s)` as a component const now decodes into `T`. It emitted `""`; a warning covered that case.
- An untyped module-scope `JSON.parse` now gets the existing "has no type" warning.
- The Swift labelled-tuple fallback now always warns.

## Tests

- **New `native-inline-object-module-scope.test.ts`** (89 tests):
  - For each of the 20 sites, on both targets: the expected output strings, no inline-object warning, and no tuple or `Any` spelling.
  - The same 20 sites compile with `validateSwiftWithStubs` and `validateKotlin`.
  - Naming: collision suffix, same shape shared, declared interface reused, `Double` widening.
  - The untyped-`JSON.parse` warning.
  - An executed Swift program that decodes and re-encodes JSON through the emitted `ConfigType` / `ConfigTypeTls` with `JSONDecoder` / `JSONEncoder`.
- **Assertions updated to the new, intended output:**
  - `native-inline-object-type-args` (the module-signal case was a warning; now `FlagType`)
  - `native-known-bugs-emit` #3 (`__Obj0`/`__Obj1` become `FTType`/`GUType`)
  - `cov-parse-d-2026-09` (same change)
  - `silent-lowering-gaps` (the Kotlin "anonymous return" warning is gone because the shape is now `PairResult`)
- **Native-compiler suite** (`--maxWorkers=3`): the full run produced 6 failures and nothing else.
  - 5 were the intended output changes above; I updated those assertions.
  - 1 was a real regression: a PascalCase arrow component called as a function lost its warning. Fixed by not lifting inside JSX-returning arrows.
  - After both fixes I re-ran those 4 files plus the two inline-object files (324 tests), all green. I did not re-run the full suite.
- **Golden:** all 1574 entries are byte-identical; no `--update` was needed.
- **`validate-fast`:** run after committing; all 61 gates pass.

## Bisect

Each fix was reverted on its own, checked, and restored:

1. **Lift disabled:** 38 of the 40 string tests fail. For example, `signal<{x;y}>` falls back to the tuple, now with the "no struct can be synthesized" warning.
2. **Module `typeJsonParse` removed:** the `JSON.parse(raw)` case emits `private let config: ConfigType = ""` (and `val` on Kotlin), and swiftc/kotlinc fail.
3. **Module-computed annotation reverted:** `var c: Any { … }` / `val c: Any get() = …`, and swiftc/kotlinc fail.

With everything restored, 89 of 89 pass.

author: annejan
body:
## Summary

Scan finding ANT-2026-0DJ8UWM6.

`StoreTree` keeps one `QFileSystemModel` for the session, and `setStore()` (a profile switch) only re-roots it, so the rows of the store shown before stay loaded. `StoreModel::showThis()` tested a leaf by its path relative to the current store with no boundary, so `../private-store/bank` matched a search.

With nothing matching in the current store, `rootIndexFor()` was invalid and the view fell back to the file system's top, listing the earlier store's entry. Return in the search box opened it, and saving it re-encrypted it to the current store's recipients: an entry from a private store could end up encrypted to a team's keys.

- `showThis()` now rejects every leaf outside the current store: a relative path of `..`, starting with `../`, or absolute.
- Folders are shown as before when something under them matches. The store's ancestors stay reachable only through matches inside the store.

## Test

- New `tst_storetree::searchNeverMatchesAnEarlierStore`:
  - loads a store, switches to another, and filters for an entry only the first store has: it is not found, and nothing under the first store is listed anywhere in the view;
  - a filter matching both stores shows only the current store's entry.
- Mutation: the old `showThis()` fails at the first check.
- Full `make check`: 36 suites, 1781 passed. Doxygen clean.

Not changed: `ImitatePass::Show()`/`Insert()` themselves do not refuse paths outside the store (defence in depth; possible follow-up).

body:
## Summary

- Add `Codec N T` laws and use one codec for each type parameter in generic function certificates.
- Generate codecs for generic interfaces and certify their field round trips, including optional nullable fields.
- Apply the interface codecs explicitly in codec-law and list-decoding lemmas. Generate a second loop lemma over interpreter values when a loop ignores its element, so a caller does not need an unrelated codec.
- Keep generated certificates current for non-generic interfaces by omitting redundant parentheses when no codec arguments apply.

## Limits

Recursive interfaces and recursive functions remain refused. A generic interface application can be certified only when each type argument is a bare type parameter; the certifier refuses other applications until it can specialize their field codecs.

## Validation

`lake build tolean-cli` passed. Fresh certificates compiled for `genericCertificates`, `generics` and `inlineObjects` with the corpus harness's namespaces and module paths. Four locked `checkCertify.sh` shards passed: 164 files were proved, and 37 files remained without certificates. author: dain
body:
Trino's `contains` answered patterns such as `first(?s:.*)second` by finding each literal in order without reading the gap, while `extract`, `count` and the other operations ran the engine, whose `.` matches no malformed UTF-8. So on the bytes `first FF second` one pattern answered `contains` true and `extract` null.

`contains` still jumps from literal to literal, but now answers true only when each gap between the found literals holds characters the engine's `.` accepts. Otherwise it asks the engine about the whole input, because a later placement of the literals may still match.

- The gap check accepts exactly what the engine's UTF-8 `.` accepts. That includes overlong three- and four-byte forms and encoded surrogates, so valid text never falls back.
- On malformed gaps Trino now follows the engine, not Joni, which answers true on `first FF second`. This is the garbage-in, garbage-out rule, with one answer on every route.
- The check reads ASCII a word at a time and long runs with the vector high-bit scan. Its cost lands on the ordered `contains` rows whose literals are far apart, such as GH Archive's `ordered-common` cells.
- LIKE and the byte-gap find plan keep the unchecked ordered-literal search.

author: taleem1120-glitch
body:
## Priority fix

The evidence verifier previously used `real.startsWith(root + sep)` for containment. When the configured evidence root is the filesystem root (`/`), that constructs `//` and incorrectly rejects every valid descendant. Replace the string-prefix check with `path.relative` + `isAbsolute`, which handles filesystem roots and platform path semantics without accepting `..` escapes.

## Regression coverage
- Add a POSIX regression using `/` as the evidence directory and a temporary file beneath it.
- Assert the declared SHA-256 is verified.

## Security boundary
This is a path-containment correctness fix, not a complete TOCTOU solution. Node's path-based `lstat`/`open` sequence still cannot provide descriptor-relative `openat` traversal here; intermediate-component swap races remain a documented limitation.

## Validation
CI pending on Node 20 and Node 22. No merge or release is included.

author: petergrace
body:
## Summary
`DELETE /api/v1/users/{name}?unless_shared_member=true` deletes nothing and answers 409 while the user is a member, in any role, of any team other than the user's own personal team (suspended teams included; another user's personal team counts, only the user's own does not). The check runs in the same transaction as the delete, under the user and shared-team row locks, so a membership committed concurrently is never removed silently. Without the parameter, behaviour is unchanged.

## What a client matches on
The error body has no machine-readable code field for refusals (`error` is `"Refused"` for every one), so the refusal has a stable message prefix: `the user is a member of shared team(s): ` followed by the quoted team names (`users::SHARED_MEMBER_REFUSAL`). Every other deletion refusal starts `user "<name>" cannot be deleted`. Match on `status == 409` and `message` starting with `the user is a member of shared team(s)`.

## Check order
The shared-membership refusal is checked first, so it wins when the user is also the sole owner of a team (a test covers it). Without the parameter that user gets the existing last-owner refusal.

## Changes
- `users::DeleteOptions { allow_last_admin, unless_shared_member }` replaces the `allow_last_admin` bool of `users::delete` (it would have been a sixth parameter); `DeleteOptions::OPERATOR` is the CLI's. Callers updated.
- The shared-team lookup under `FOR UPDATE` now returns the team names.
- `DELETE /users/{name}` takes `?unless_shared_member=` (bool, default false); another query parameter or a non-boolean value is a 400.
- `docs/operations.md`: the route table row and the deletion rules document the parameter, the 409 and the prefix. The route is already in `PROVISIONER_ROUTES`; no allow-list change.
- Changelog entry.

## Why it is atomic
A membership insert takes the user row `FOR KEY SHARE` (its foreign key). The delete takes the user `FOR UPDATE` before it reads memberships, so an insert in flight either commits first (the delete then sees it and refuses) or waits and then fails its foreign key.

## Validation
- `tools/agentic/gate.sh fmt`, `lint`, `dylint`: pass on the head after review round 1 (main merged in).
- `tools/agentic/gate.sh test`: pass (25 targets, 2333 passed, 0 failed, 18 ignored). One earlier run failed a browser test unrelated to this change (`a_member_adds_a_passkey_with_the_browser...`); it passed alone and in the full re-run.
- `test-ui` as a separate gate and the kind smoke test were not run.

## Tests
- store: another user's personal team counts (review round 1); plain member refused and nothing removed; unchanged without the option; no shared team deleted; suspended team and sole owner (shared refusal wins; without the option the last-owner refusal); a membership insert held in flight while the delete waits, then committed, gives the refusal.
- REST: 409 with the prefix, user still present, a misspelled parameter or `=maybe` is 400, `false` is 204, no shared team is 204.
- provisioner key: 409 with the parameter, 204 without it.

## Claims
This repository has no claims ledger; these findings were not recorded.

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 409 and nothing deleted for a member of any non-personal team, any role, suspended included | supported | `users::delete` shared-team query has no role or suspension filter; tests in `store::users` and REST |
| Check is under the user `FOR UPDATE` lock before the membership read | supported | `audit::lock_people` then `FOR UPDATE OF t` in `users::delete`; in-flight insert test |
| 409 is distinguishable by a stable prefix, documented | supported | `SHARED_MEMBER_REFUSAL`; `docs/operations.md` |
| Shared refusal wins over the last-owner refusal, tested | supported | `unless_shared_member_wins_over_the_last_owner_refusal_...` |
| Provisioner key can call it, tested | supported | `a_provisioner_deletes_a_user_unless_a_shared_team_member` |
| Without the parameter or with `=false`, unchanged | supported | REST, store and provisioner tests |
| Non-boolean value is 400 | supported after the audit (test added in the follow-up commit) | `=maybe` assertion |

## Manual Test Plan
- `DELETE /api/v1/users/bob?unless_shared_member=true` as a provisioner key, for a user who is a member of a shared team: 409, message starts `the user is a member of shared team(s)`; `GET /api/v1/users/bob` is still 200.
- The same request for a user in no shared team: 204.
- `DELETE /api/v1/users/bob` without the parameter: 204 as before.

Closes #535
